purpose: Review evidence only; not automatic gold labels.

items.question_en: What government support programmes are available to farmers in Ghana?
items.answer_en: Key government programs for farmers in Ghana include: Planting for Food and Jobs (PFJ) which provides subsidized seeds and fertilizers; Rearing for Food and Jobs for livestock; Ghana Commercial Agriculture Project (GCAP) for commercial farmers; Youth in Agriculture Program; and the Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) loans. Contact your district MOFA office for current programs available in your area.
items.question_twi: Ɔman boa adwuma bɛn na ɛwɔ ho ma okuafo wɔ Ghana?
items.answer_twi: Ɔman adwuma titiriw a ɛwɔ ho ma okuafo wɔ Ghana ne: Planting for Food and Jobs (PFJ) a ɛde aba ne ferefere a wɔatwa boɔ brɛ; Rearing for Food and Jobs ma mmoa; Ghana Commercial Agriculture Project (GCAP) ma tɔntɔn okuafo; Youth in Agriculture Program; ne Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) ka. Ka kyerɛ wo district MOFA ofisi ma adwuma a ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ wo beae saa ara.

candidates.question_en: Where can I get agricultural loans in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Agricultural loans in Ghana are available from Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) which specializes in farming loans, Rural and Community Banks in your area, the ARB Apex Bank, microfinance institutions, and through government schemes like the Planting for Food and Jobs credit component. The Ghana Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (GIRSAL) provides guarantees to encourage banks to lend to farmers. Always compare interest rates and repayment terms before borrowing.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛhɔ na metumi anya okuafo mfɛdomhyɛw wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Okuafo mfɛdomhyɛw wɔ Ghana wɔ Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) a ɛtaa ma okuafo mfɛdomhyɛw, Rural ne Community Banks a ɛbɛn wo, ARB Apex Bank, microfinance institutions, na aban schemes te sɛ Planting for Food and Jobs credit component. Ghana Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (GIRSAL) de hyɛ banks so sɛ wɔma okuafo mfɛdomhyɛw. Fa interest rates ne repayment ho nsɛm twe ntam ansa na wobɔ mfɛdomhyɛw.

candidates.question_en: What government agricultural support can I access in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Register with your local MOFA office and stay in contact with your extension officer. Subsidies like subsidized fertilizer and seeds under PFJ are distributed through MOFA-registered channels. Have your Ghana Card or voter ID ready and register early as subsidies are often limited.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menya ɔman okuafo adwuma boa?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw wo din wɔ wo MOFA ofisi a ɛbɛn wo na tena wo extension officer ho. Boa te sɛ ferefere ne aba a wɔatwa boɔ wɔ PFJ ase no pue wɔ MOFA mu. Wura wo Ghana Card anaa ɔman nkyerɛwsɛm na kyerɛw wo din ntɛm efisɛ boa no taa yɛ ketewa.

candidates.question_en: What role do women play in agriculture in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Women play a critical role in Ghanaian agriculture — they make up about 52% of the agricultural workforce. Women are primarily responsible for food crop production, post-harvest processing, and marketing. They often face challenges accessing land, credit, and inputs. Programs that specifically support women farmers include Women in Agricultural Development (WIAD) under MOFA, and many NGOs focusing on women's empowerment in agriculture.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mmaa gyina wɔ okuafo adwuma mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Mmaa gyina titiriw pa ara wɔ Ghana okuafo adwuma mu — wɔyɛ bɛn 52% wɔ okuafo adwumafo mu. Mmaa hia aduan nnuaba kura, gye akyi yɛ adwuma, ne tɔn. Wɔtaa hia asase, ka, ne adenneɛ ho nsɛm. Adwuma a ɛhwɛ mmaa okuafo ho pɛ ne Women in Agricultural Development (WIAD) wɔ MOFA ase, ne NGOs bebree a wɔhwɛ mmaa ho wɔ okuafo adwuma mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I get land for farming in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Access farming land in Ghana through several ways including purchasing outright if you have capital, sharecropping where you farm another person's land and share the harvest usually 50 50, leasing land through a written agreement typically 5 to 20 years in peri-urban areas, accessing communal lands through the chief or family head in rural areas, and government land allocations for special farming zones. Always secure a written land use agreement even for sharecropping arrangements to protect your investment.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ menya asase ma okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Nya asase ma okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana de akwan ahorow a ɛka ho de gye to sɛ wo wɔ sika, sharecropping a woto obi asase so na fa nnoa twa mmienu pɛ taa yɛ 50 50, lease asase de nhyiam krataa taa bɛyɛ mfe 5 kɔ 20 wɔ dɔn ho, nya communal asase wɔ ohene anaa abusua panyin nkyɛn wɔ kurow ho, na aban asase kyɛ ma okuafo adwuma zones a wɔayɛ. Hwɛ sɛ wotwerɛ asase de nhyiam krataa bere biara naaso sharecropping nhyiamu ma wo sɛ ɛhwɛ wo sika so.

candidates.question_en: What are the major risks in farming and how can I manage them?
candidates.answer_en: Main farming risks include weather risks from drought or flooding, pest and disease outbreaks, price volatility at harvest time, input price increases, land tenure insecurity, and lack of market access. Manage these risks by diversifying crops so one failure does not ruin you entirely, using drought-resistant varieties, taking out crop insurance where available, joining farmer groups for collective bargaining, storing produce to sell when prices improve, securing formal land documents, and building relationships with multiple buyers.
candidates.question_twi: Aho yɛ den bɛn na ɛwɔ okuafo adwuma mu na dɛn na menyɛ wɔn ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Aho yɛ den kɛse a ɛwɔ okuafo adwuma mu ne: berɛ ho aho yɛ den fi bone anaa nsuo, adwummaker ne yadeɛ ba ntɛm, dwa bo sesa bere a wuyiyɛ, inputs bo kɔ so, asase ho gyinae ankyɛ, na dwa kɔ ho hia. Boa ho de nnuaba ahorow to sɛ baako a atua ho nhia wo a ennye wo ho nyinaa, de drought-resistant varieties to mu, gye crop insurance wɔ hɔ a ɛwɔ, ka okuafo kuo ho ma wobɔ bo kaa bom, guina nnuaba sɛ wotɔ bere a bo yɛ yie, hwɛ sɛ asase ho krataa pa wɔ wo nkyɛn, na kora wo adwene ho buyers kuo mmerantee ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow moringa and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Moringa is one of the most nutritious plants in the world and grows easily in Ghana. Plant seeds directly or use stem cuttings in well-drained soil. It tolerates drought and poor soils. Harvest leaves regularly to keep the tree short and productive. Moringa leaves can be eaten fresh, dried, and powdered. Benefits include: extremely high in iron, vitamins A and C, protein, and calcium. It is used medicinally and sold as a nutritional supplement at premium prices.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura moringa na mfaaso bɛn na ɛwɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Moringa yɛ nnua a ɛwɔ aduan ho nhwiren pa ara wɔ wiase mu na ɛda sor yie wɔ Ghana. To aba tɔtɔ anaa fa tibo cutting wɔ asase a nsuo pue mu yie. Ɛtumi nsuo pa ne asase a enni pa ase hyɛ. Gye nhaban pɛ sɛ ɛkora dua no tia ne adwuma mu. Moringa nhaban wobetumi di foforo, yaw na tutu. Mfaaso ho ne: iron, vitamins A ne C, protein, ne calcium ho yɛ dodo pa ara. Wɔde di dawuro adwuma na tɔn sɛ nutritional supplement wɔ boɔ kɛse.

candidates.question_en: How can I use phone apps to support my farming business?
candidates.answer_en: Several useful apps are available for Ghanaian farmers. The Farmerline Mergdata app provides market prices, weather forecasts and agricultural advice. The ESOKO platform sends SMS alerts about market prices. Plantix app helps diagnose crop diseases using photos. The One Acre Fund app assists with input planning. WhatsApp farmer groups share timely information. Soil Doctor provides soil testing and fertilizer recommendations. Use these apps to make better decisions on planting time, fertilizer application and market timing.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mede phone apps boa me okuafo adwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Apps a ɛboa wɔ Ghana okuafo wɔ hɔ ne: Farmerline Mergdata app a de dwa bo, berɛ nkra ne okuafo nkyerɛkyerɛ to. ESOKO platform de SMS alerts hyɛ dwa bo ho. Plantix app boa sɛ wohunu nnuaba yadeɛ de foto. One Acre Fund app boa inputs siesie. WhatsApp okuafo kuo kyɛ nsɛm a ɛyɛ papa ntɛm. Soil Doctor de asase hwɛ ne ferefere ho nkyerɛkyerɛ. De apps yi ma wo yɛ adwuma pa wɔ to aba bere, ferefere to ne dwa bere ho.

candidates.question_en: Should I register my farm with the government?
candidates.answer_en: Registering your farm with MOFA gives you access to government subsidies, training, extension services, credit, and market linkages. Visit your local MOFA office or District Assembly with your ID and land documents. Registration is free and very beneficial.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mede m'afuo nkyerɛw?
candidates.answer_twi: Wo afuo nkyerɛw wɔ MOFA de tumi ma wo sɛ wunya ɔman ho boa, nyansapɔ, extension nnwuma, ka, ne aguabasa ho kyɛfa. Kɔ wo MOFA ofisi anaa District Assembly a ɛbɛn wo wɔ wo nkyerɛwsɛm ne asase krataa. Nkyerɛw yɛ daa na ɛboa pa ara.

items.question_en: What should I look for in good cowpea seed?
items.answer_en: Use clean, healthy, uniform seed from a reliable source and avoid seed with visible damage or disease symptoms.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ wɔ cowpea aba pa mu?
items.answer_twi: Fa aba a ɛho tew, ɛwɔ ahoɔden na ne kɛse yɛ pɛ, na ɛfiri baabi a wonim. Mfa aba a apira anaa yare ho nsɛnkyerɛnne wɔ ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce aflatoxin risk in groundnut?
candidates.answer_en: Use good-quality seed, manage field stress, harvest carefully, dry pods thoroughly and store them in clean, dry conditions.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate aflatoxin haw so wɔ nkatie mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa aba pa, hwɛ ɔhaw a ɛwɔ afuo mu, gye nkatie no yie, yow wɔn paa na guina wɔ beae a ɛho tew na ɛyɛ yera.

candidates.question_en: How should I handle harvested legumes before storage?
candidates.answer_en: Remove dirt and damaged material, dry the grain thoroughly, cool it before sealing, and keep the storage area dry and clean.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ legumes a magye no ansa na waguina?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi dɔte ne nneɛma a asɛe, yow aba no yie, ma ɛnwunu ansa na woato no mu na ma guina beae no nyɛ yera na ɛho tew.

candidates.question_en: How do legumes improve soil fertility in a mixed farming system?
candidates.answer_en: Legumes can contribute to soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation and can help diversify cropping systems.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na legumes boa ma asase yɛ dɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Legumes tumi de nitrogen boa asase so fa biological nitrogen fixation ho na ɛma nnɔbae ahorow nyɛ baako pɛ.

candidates.question_en: Can legumes be grown with cereals?
candidates.answer_en: Yes. Intercropping some legumes with cereals can use space efficiently and diversify production, but the crops need compatible spacing and management.
candidates.question_twi: Legumes tumi nyin ne cereals bom anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane. Wobetumi adua legumes ne cereals bom ma wɔde beae no di dwuma yie na ɛma nnɔbae ahorow. Nanso ɛsɛ sɛ wɔn ntam ne wɔn nhwɛsoɔ hyia.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve groundnut flowering and pod formation?
candidates.answer_en: Choose well-drained soil, remove heavy weeds and prepare a fine seedbed without excessive compaction.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama nkatie nhwiren ne aba no ayɛ yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw asase a nsuo tumi firi mu, yi nwura a ɛdɔɔso na siesie asase no yie nanso mfa mfrafra asase no dodo.

items.question_en: How do I start a poultry farm in Ghana?
items.answer_en: Decide whether to raise broilers for meat or layers for eggs. Build or rent a poultry house that is well ventilated, predator-proof and has adequate space of 0.1 square metres per broiler or 0.2 square metres per layer. Source day-old chicks from reputable hatcheries. Provide feed, clean water, light and warmth from a brooder for the first 2 weeks. Vaccinate against Newcastle disease and Gumboro disease. Broilers are ready in 6 to 7 weeks and layers start laying at 18 to 20 weeks.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase akoko adwuma wɔ Ghana?
items.answer_twi: Siesie wo tiri ma broilers wɔ nam ho anaa layers wɔ tamma ho. Tu anaa sowa akoko fie a mframa fa mu yie, adwummaker ntumi nkɔ mu, na ahorow teetee wɔ hɔ sɛ 0.1 square metres biara broiler anaa 0.2 square metres biara layer. Gye day-old chicks fi hatcheries a wɔni gyinae. De aduan, nsuo pa, kanea ne berɛhyɛ fi brooder ma nnansa mmienu a ɛdi kan. Hware wɔ so ma Newcastle yadeɛ ne Gumboro yadeɛ. Broilers atwa so nnansas nsia kɔ nson akyi na layers fi ase gu tamma nnansas duodu nwɔtwe kɔ aduonu.

candidates.question_en: How can I start a small poultry farm at home?
candidates.answer_en: To start a small home poultry farm: decide on type (layers for eggs or broilers for meat), build or buy a simple wooden or wire coop with shade and good ventilation, start with 10-20 birds, provide clean water and commercial feed, vaccinate birds at the recommended ages, keep the coop clean, and record feeds, deaths, and egg production. Start small and scale as you learn.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesi akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ si akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie: paw ahodoɔ (layers ma kosua anaa broilers ma nam), si anaa tɔ dua anaa wire fie a ewim brɛ ne mframa pue mu yie, fi akrɔma 10-20, de nsuo horo ne aduan a wɔtɔ ma wɔn, de akrɔma kɔ yadeɛ dawuro bere a ɛsɛ, kora fie no horo, na kora aduan, wuu, ne kosua ho nsɛm. Fi ketewa na fa dodo so bere a wosua.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent Newcastle disease in poultry?
candidates.answer_en: Newcastle disease is the most serious threat to poultry in Ghana. Prevent it through strict vaccination using Lasota vaccine at day 7, day 21 and every 2 months thereafter. Keep visitors away from your poultry house, disinfect equipment and footwear before entering, quarantine new birds for 2 weeks, buy birds from certified sources only, and cull sick birds immediately. There is no treatment for Newcastle disease once birds are infected.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ Newcastle yadeɛ annya me akoko?
candidates.answer_twi: Newcastle yadeɛ ne akoko tia a ɛtaa yɛ den paa wɔ Ghana. Gye wo ho fi mu de Lasota hware aba ahyɛ so mu da 7, da 21 na mprɛn mmienu biara wɔ saa akyi. Ma ahofipa anyɛ kwan kɔ wo akoko fie, hware nneɛma ne nan so ansa na wukɔ mu, kora nnomaa foforɔ wɔ baabi foforo nnansas mmienu, gye nnomaa fi hɔ a wɔakyerɛw so pɛ, na kum nnomaa a wayarɛ ntɛm. Newcastle yadeɛ nni dawuro bere a nnomaa no anya mu.

candidates.question_en: What housing system is best for layer chickens in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: The best housing for layers in Ghana's climate is the open-sided or naturally ventilated house. Use wire mesh or wooden slats on the sides for maximum airflow. Orient the house east to west so the long side faces north and south to reduce direct sunlight. Provide a sloped roof with good overhang. Install battery cages at 3 tiers for commercial production or deep litter floor for smaller flocks. Ensure 0.2 square metres per bird for floor housing and 450 square cm per bird for cages.
candidates.question_twi: Housing nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara ma layers wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Housing a ɛhia pa ara ma layers wɔ Ghana berɛ a ɛwɔ ne open-sided anaa naturally ventilated fie. De wire mesh anaa wooden slats to ho mframa nsa sɛ mframa fa mu yie. De fie no sie east kɔ west sɛ ho tenten so hyɛ north ne south anim sɛ owia ankasa annhyɛ mu. De roof a ɛtɔ yie ne overhang pa si. Si battery cages a tiers mmiɛnsa wɔ mu ma adwuma kɛse anaa deep litter floor ma flocks nketewa. Hwɛ sɛ square metres 0.2 wɔ nnomaa baako ho ma floor housing ne square cm 450 biara nnomaa ho ma cages.

candidates.question_en: How can I increase egg production in layers?
candidates.answer_en: For maximum egg production ensure 16 hours of light daily using artificial lighting, maintain temperature between 18 and 24 degrees Celsius, provide layer mash with 16 to 17 percent protein and added calcium for strong shells, ensure clean water always, control parasites and disease through regular vaccination and deworming, collect eggs three times daily, keep stress low by avoiding sudden disturbances, and cull poor layers that consistently produce below average.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tamma gu akoko sɛ wɔagu pii?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ akoko gu tamma pii a, hwɛ sɛ kanea da wɔ mu dɔn 16 de artificial light, kora berɛ wɔ degrees 18 ne 24 Celsius ntam, de layer mash a protein 16 kɔ 17 percent ne calcium a ɛhia ma tamma ho den na ka ho, de nsuo pa to mu bere nyinaa, boa parasites ne yadeɛ ho de hware ne wia adwummaker bere biara, pam tamma mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa biara da, ma anigyidie sua de gye wo ho fi nka kɔkɔɔkɔ, na kum layers a wɔgu nketewa bere nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: What is the Newcastle disease vaccination schedule for chickens?
candidates.answer_en: The standard Newcastle disease vaccination schedule in Ghana is Lasota live vaccine eye or nose drop at day 7, Lasota booster at day 21, and then Lasota every 2 months thereafter. For layers continue every 2 months throughout the laying period. Use inactivated oil-emulsion Newcastle vaccine at 8 weeks for additional protection especially in high-risk areas. Store vaccines at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and use within the expiry date. Never vaccinate sick birds.
candidates.question_twi: Newcastle yadeɛ vaccination schedule bɛn na ɛhia wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Newcastle yadeɛ vaccination schedule pa wɔ Ghana ne Lasota live vaccine ani anaa afi drops wɔ da 7, Lasota booster wɔ da 21, na Lasota bere biara mprɛn mmienu mu saa akyi. Ma layers tena so mprɛn mmienu mu so wɔ tamma gu bere nyinaa. De inactivated oil-emulsion Newcastle vaccine to ho wɔ nnansas nwɔtwe sɛ ɛboa hwɛ so a ɛhia pii wɔ hɔ a ɛyɛ den. Guina vaccines wɔ degrees 2 kɔ 8 Celsius na de fi mu ansa na bere a wɔakyerɛw so abu. Mma wo mpo hware nnomaa a wayarɛ so.

candidates.question_en: How can I manage heat stress in chickens?
candidates.answer_en: Heat stress is common in Ghana and reduces growth rate and egg production. Manage it by ensuring good ventilation in the poultry house, providing cool fresh water frequently, installing foggers or sprinklers on the roof, feeding in the cooler parts of the day morning and evening, reducing stocking density during hot seasons, adding vitamin C and electrolytes to water during extreme heat, and considering open-sided housing designs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ berɛhyɛ den a ɛba me akoko ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Berɛhyɛ den taa ba wɔ Ghana na ɛhia boɛ a aba nhia na tamma nhia. Boa ho de hwɛ sɛ mframa fa akoko fie mu yie, de nsuo dɛ foforɔ to mu bere biara, si foggers anaa sprinklers wɔ fie no atifi so, didi wɔ berɛ dɛ mu anɔpa ne anwumere, sua akoko a wɔwɔ mu wɔ berɛhyɛ bere, de vitamin C ne electrolytes ka nsuo mu wɔ hyehyɛ den bere, na twe wo adwene ho open-sided housing nhyiamu.

candidates.question_en: What feed should I give broiler chickens?
candidates.answer_en: Feed broilers starter crumbles for the first 2 weeks with 22 to 24 percent protein, then grower pellets with 18 to 20 percent protein from week 3 to 5, and finisher pellets with 16 to 18 percent protein in the final weeks. Provide fresh clean water at all times. Popular feed brands in Ghana include Darko Farms, Akate Wura and Ghana Feedmill feeds. Feed represents 70 percent of your production cost so buying quality feed is critical.
candidates.question_twi: Aduan bɛn na mede ma me broiler akoko?
candidates.answer_twi: De starter crumbles a protein 22 kɔ 24 percent wɔ mu ma broilers nnansas mmienu a ɛdi kan, afei grower pellets a protein 18 kɔ 20 percent wɔ mu wɔ nnansa mmiɛnsa kɔ num, na finisher pellets a protein 16 kɔ 18 percent wɔ mu wɔ nnansas a etwa to. De nsuo fofor pa to mu bere nyinaa. Feed brands a wɔpɛ wɔ Ghana ne Darko Farms, Akate Wura na Ghana Feedmill feeds. Aduan yɛ wo adwuma agyapade 70 percent enti gye aduan pa hia.

candidates.question_en: What are the common diseases affecting poultry in Ghana and how can they be prevented?
candidates.answer_en: Common poultry diseases in Ghana include Newcastle Disease, Gumboro (Infectious Bursal Disease), and Fowl Pox. Prevention includes vaccination, good hygiene, biosecurity measures such as limiting visitors and controlling movement, and proper sanitation of poultry houses.
candidates.question_twi: Yare bɛn na ɛtaa yɛ akokɔ wɔ Ghana na yɛbɛyɛ dɛn atua ano?
candidates.answer_twi: Akokɔ yare a ɛtaa ba wɔ Ghana ne Newcastle Disease, Gumboro (Infectious Bursal Disease), ne Fowl Pox. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wotua ano a, ɛsɛ sɛ wode nnuru bɔ wɔn, hwɛ yiye wɔ ahwehwɛde ho, na wode ahobammɔ ho nhyehyɛe di dwuma te sɛ ahɔho a wobɛtew wɔn so ne akokɔdan mu nnuru a wobɛtwa.

items.question_en: What should I feed growing rabbits?
items.answer_en: Provide a balanced diet appropriate for the rabbit's age, with adequate fibre and clean water.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mede ma rabbits a wɔrenyin no di?
items.answer_twi: Ma wɔn aduane a ɛkari pɛ a ɛfata wɔn mfe, fiber a ɛdɔɔso ne nsuo pa.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce heat stress in rabbits?
candidates.answer_en: Provide shade, ventilation, clean water and protect cages from direct heat during hot periods.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate heat stress so wɔ rabbits mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma sunsuma, mframa kɔ mu, nsuo pa na bɔ cages no ho ban fi ɔhyew tee ho bere a ɛyɛ hyew.

candidates.question_en: How do I start a small rabbit farm?
candidates.answer_en: Begin with healthy breeding stock, suitable housing, reliable feed and water, a cleaning routine and a simple production record system.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahyɛ rabbit kuayɛ ketewa ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi rabbits a wɔyɛ ahoɔden mu ase, nya dan a ɛfata, aduane ne nsuo a wɔde di dwuma daa, ahotew nhyehyɛe ne kyerɛwtohɔ ketewa.

candidates.question_en: What makes a rabbit housing unit suitable?
candidates.answer_en: It should be dry, well ventilated, secure from predators and easy to clean.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma rabbit dan yɛ papa?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɛyɛ yera, mframa kɔ mu, ɛbɔ rabbits ho ban fi mmoa a wɔyɛ wɔn ayayade ho na ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wɔhohoro.

candidates.question_en: Why should rabbits not be kept in dirty cages?
candidates.answer_en: Dirty housing increases odour, parasites and disease risks and can reduce animal performance.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔde rabbits tena cage a ɛho ntew?
candidates.answer_twi: Cage fĩ ma hua bɔne, parasites ne yare dɔɔso na ɛtumi tew mmoa no ahoɔden ne nyin so.

candidates.question_en: How do I identify a sick rabbit?
candidates.answer_en: Watch for reduced feeding, unusual behaviour, diarrhoea, breathing problems, discharge or sudden weight loss.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ rabbit bi ayare?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛ ɔnni aduane, ne suban asesa, ɔyɛ ahonhon, ne ho tumi pue nsuo, anaa ne duru resa ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: What records are useful in rabbit farming?
candidates.answer_en: Keep records of mating, kindling, litter size, growth, treatments, deaths and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛm bɛn na mfaso wɔ rabbit kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw mating, awo, litter size, nyin, ayaresa, owu ne tɔn.

candidates.question_en: How should rabbit manure be handled?
candidates.answer_en: Collect it regularly and compost or manage it appropriately before applying it to crops.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ rabbit dɔte?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye dɔte no daa na yɛ compost anaa hwɛ so yie ansa na wode agu nnɔbae so.

items.question_en: How can I reduce lodging in rice?
items.answer_en: Use suitable varieties, avoid excessive nitrogen, maintain appropriate plant density and manage water and weeds properly.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn atumi atew aburow mu dabere so?
items.answer_twi: Fa aburow ahorow a ɛfata, nma nitrogen dodo, ma nnua no ntam yɛ pɛ na hwɛ nsuo ne nwura so yie.

candidates.question_en: How can I level a rice field before planting?
candidates.answer_en: Remove large clods, fill low spots and reduce high spots so water is distributed evenly. Good leveling helps save water and improves crop establishment.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie aburow afuo no ma asase no yɛ pɛ ansa na madu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase akɛse no, hyɛ mmeae a fam, na brɛ mmeae a ɛyɛ soronko sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a nsuo bɛkyɛ pɛ. Asase a ɛyɛ pɛ boa ma nsuo ntra beae baako na ɛboa aba ma ɛfifi yie.

candidates.question_en: Why is water management important in rice farming?
candidates.answer_en: Rice needs adequate moisture, but uncontrolled standing water can reduce plant health and make field operations difficult. Managing water at the right stages improves growth and efficiency.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na nsuo ho nhwɛsoɔ ho hia wɔ aburow kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Aburow hia nsuo a ɛfata, nanso nsuo a ɛgyina hɔ dodo betumi ama nnɔbae no ayɛ mmerɛ na ayɛ adwuma wɔ afuo mu ayɛ den. Nsuo a wɔhwɛ so wɔ bere a ɛfata ma nyin ne kuayɛ yɛ yie.

candidates.question_en: How should I choose a rice field site?
candidates.answer_en: Choose a site with reliable water, suitable soil, good drainage control, and easy access. Avoid areas that cannot be drained when the crop is mature.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw beae a mɛdua aburow?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw beae a nsuo wɔ no yie, asase no fata, nsuo tumi firi mu, na kwan kɔ hɔ yɛ mmerɛ. Mfa beae a wontumi nnya nsuo mfi mu bere a nnɔbae no awie ase.

candidates.question_en: Why should harvested rice be kept clean?
candidates.answer_en: Clean grain reduces contamination, pest problems and losses during storage and helps maintain quality and market value.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ aburow a magye no tena ahotew mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Aduan a ɛho tew ma fi, mmoawa ne asɛe so te. Ɛboa ma aburow no kɔ so yɛ papa wɔ guina mu na ɛma ne boɔ so.

candidates.question_en: What is the difference between upland and lowland rice farming?
candidates.answer_en: Upland rice is grown without standing water, while lowland rice is grown where water can be managed in low-lying fields. The suitable system depends on rainfall, soil and water availability.
candidates.question_twi: Nsonsonoe bɛn na ɛwɔ upland ne lowland aburow kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Upland aburow nyin a nsuo nnyina asase so, na lowland aburow nyin wɔ beae a wobetumi ahwɛ nsuo so wɔ fam asase so. Nea ɛfata gyina osu, asase ne nsuo a ɛwɔ hɔ so.

candidates.question_en: When should rice be dried after harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Begin drying as soon as practical after harvest. Dry the grain evenly to a safe moisture level suitable for storage or milling.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ meyow aburow akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi ase yow aburow no ntɛm ara sɛnea wubetumi bere a wogye no. Ma ɛyow pɛ na ɛso nsuo nyɛ dodo ansa na waguina anaa wɔayam.

items.question_en: How often should watermelon be watered?
items.answer_en: Provide regular moisture during establishment and fruit development, while avoiding prolonged waterlogging.
items.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ megu watermelon nsuo?
items.answer_twi: Ma watermelon nya nsuo daa bere a ɛrefi ase ne bere a aba reyɛ kɛse, nanso mma nsuo nnyina asase mu akyɛ.

candidates.question_en: When should I reduce irrigation before harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Once fruits are approaching maturity, excessive watering can dilute quality and increase cracking risk. Adjust watering according to soil and crop condition.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mete nsuo so ansa na megye watermelon?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a watermelon rebɛwie ase no, nsuo dodo tumi tew quality so na ɛma aba no paapae. Yɛ nsuo no sɛnea asase ne nnɔbae no tebea te.

candidates.question_en: How should watermelon be handled at harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Cut fruits carefully, avoid dropping them and keep them protected from excessive heat and physical damage.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ watermelon bere a meregye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Twa aba no yie, mma ɛntɔ fam na kora no fi ɔhyew den ne mpirapira ho.

candidates.question_en: How should watermelon be graded before sale?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest at the right maturity, handle fruits carefully and transport them in a way that prevents crushing and excessive heat.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyekyɛ watermelon ansa na matɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye aba a maturity yɛ yie, fa ahwɛyiye na de no kɔ gua so wɔ kwan a ɛremma ɛmpira anaa ɔhyew nka no dodo.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve watermelon fruit size?
candidates.answer_en: Use good seed, maintain balanced nutrition, provide adequate water and manage weeds and pests from early growth.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama watermelon aba no yɛ kɛse?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa aba pa, ma nutrients yɛ pɛ, ma nsuo a ɛfata na hwɛ nwura ne mmoawa so fi ase.

candidates.question_en: Why does watermelon need good drainage?
candidates.answer_en: Its roots perform poorly in prolonged waterlogged soil, which can increase root disease and reduce growth.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na watermelon hia asase a nsuo firi mu yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Ne ntini yɛ adwuma bɔne wɔ asase a nsuo gyina mu kyɛ dodo, na ɛtumi ma root yare dɔɔso na nyin tew.

candidates.question_en: How can I know when watermelon is mature?
candidates.answer_en: Use several maturity signs together, such as changes in the tendril near the fruit, ground spot colour and the fruit's overall appearance.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ watermelon awie ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne pii bom, te sɛ tendril a ɛbɛn aba no, kɔla a asase fã a aba no da so wɔ no yɛ, ne sɛnea fruit no tebea te nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How do I select land for watermelon?
candidates.answer_en: Choose warm, sunny, well-drained land with fertile soil and enough space for vines to spread.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw asase ma watermelon?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw asase a ɛyɛ hyew, owia wɔ, nsuo firi mu yie na ɛyɛ pa, na beae no yɛ kɛse ma vines no trɛw.

candidates.question_en: Why are watermelon fruits cracking?
candidates.answer_en: Sudden changes in water availability, heavy rain after dry conditions and other stress can contribute to cracking.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na watermelon aba paapae?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsuo a ɛsakra ntɛm, osu den akyi ɔpɛ ne ɔhaw foforo bi betumi ama watermelon aba paapae.

items.question_en: What fertilizer is best for maize?
items.answer_en: For maize, use NPK fertilizer (15-15-15) at planting, then top-dress with urea about 4-6 weeks after planting. Apply 2 bags of NPK per acre at planting and 1 bag of urea per acre when top-dressing.
items.question_twi: Ferefere bɛn na ɛyɛ papa ma aburo?
items.answer_twi: Aburo ho, fa NPK ferefere (15-15-15) de to asase mu bere a wode aburow to mu no. Afei fa urea gu so sɛntɔ 4-6 akyi a wode aburow to mu no. Fa NPK bɔtɔ 2 gu acre baako biara mu bere a wode aburow no gu fam, na fa urea bɔtɔ 1 gu acre baako biara mu bere a wode to so.

candidates.question_en: What fertilizer should I apply to maize and when?
candidates.answer_en: Apply NPK 15-15-15 at planting rate of 2 bags per acre mixed into the soil near the seed. At 4 to 6 weeks after planting when the maize is knee high, apply urea (top dressing) at 1 bag per acre. Place urea 5 to 7 cm from the stem and cover lightly with soil to prevent loss through evaporation.
candidates.question_twi: Ferefere bɛn na mede to aburoɔ ho na bere bɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: De NPK 15-15-15 to mu bere a wode aba to mu, bags mmienu biara eka baako mu, na fa ka ho asase a ɛbɛn aba no ho. Nnansa 4 kɔ 6 akyi a aburoɔ aba mu rebɛ kɔsi ntam, de urea (top dressing) to ho, bag baako biara eka baako mu. De urea sie sɛntimita 5 kɔ 7 fi aburoɔ no ho na kata so kakra asase mu sɛ ɛrenyi fi.

candidates.question_en: When is the best time to plant maize in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: In Ghana, the best time to plant maize is at the beginning of the rainy season — March to April in the south, and May to June in the north. Plant when you have received at least 2-3 good rains so the soil is well moistened.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛyɛ ɔkorɔ sɛ wode aburow to mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Wɔ Ghana, bere pa ara sɛ wode aburow to mu ne nsuo bere mfiase — Ɛbɔ kwan so Oforisuo wɔ apuei fam, na Ayɛwohomumo kwan so Mumu wɔ atifi fam. To aba mu bere a wanya nsu mmɛn 2-3 yie na asase no atenante yie.

candidates.question_en: What feed is best for tilapia in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Tilapia does well on commercial pellet feeds with protein content of 25 to 30 percent. Popular brands in Ghana include Raanan, Coppens and Skretting. You can also prepare on-farm feed using locally available ingredients like maize bran, soybean meal, fishmeal and rice bran. Feed at 3 to 5 percent of body weight daily. Reduce feed when water temperature is very high or very low as fish appetite decreases.
candidates.question_twi: Apataa aduan bɛn na ɛhia pa ara ma tilapia wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Tilapia to yie wɔ commercial pellet feeds a protein 25 kɔ 30 percent wɔ mu. Brands a wɔpɛ wɔ Ghana ne Raanan, Coppens na Skretting. Wobetumi nso de aduan a ɛwɔ ho wɔ ɛhɔ yɛ te sɛ aburoɔ bran, soybean meal, fishmeal ne rice bran. Didi bɔ so biara adays 3 kɔ 5 percent. Sua aduan bere a nsuo berɛ yɛ hyehyɛ paa anaa dɛ paa efisɛ apataa nhia aduan da.

candidates.question_en: How many bags of maize can I expect from one acre?
candidates.answer_en: With good management, improved varieties and proper fertilization, you can harvest 20 to 25 bags of 100 kg each per acre. Without fertilizer and using local varieties, expect 8 to 12 bags per acre. The key factors affecting yield are soil fertility, seed variety, timely planting, weed control, pest management and rainfall adequacy.
candidates.question_twi: Sacks aburoɔ ahe na mebetumi anya fi eka baako mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ woyɛ adwuma pa, de varieties pa to mu na de ferefere pa to ho a, wobetumi anya sacks 20 kɔ 25 a nnɔho 100 kg biara wɔ eka baako mu. Sɛ wonni ferefere na wode local varieties to mu a, gyina sacks 8 kɔ 12 biara eka baako ho. Asɛde a ɛma aburoɔ rebɛ yɛ ne: asase no aduan, aba variety, bere pa mu to aba, nhaban foforo yi, adwummaker hwɛ, na nsuo pa.

candidates.question_en: How can I make compost for my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Make compost by layering crop residues dry matter like maize stalks alternating with green matter like grass clippings and kitchen waste. Add a thin layer of soil or finished compost between layers to introduce decomposing organisms. Keep the pile moist but not waterlogged and turn it every 2 weeks. The compost is ready in 8 to 12 weeks when it is dark brown crumbly and earthy smelling. Apply 2 to 3 tonnes of compost per acre before planting to significantly improve soil fertility.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ compost ma me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ compost de layers a nnuaba a ato fɛw aba ntama a wɔatew te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ka ho ne nnuaba foforɔ te sɛ nhawan ne efie ho nneɛma. De asase ketewa anaa compost a ɛawie to ntam biara mu sɛ ɛde organisms a ɛhia kɔ. Ma pile no nsuo ho kakra nanso nsuo nni mu agyina na gyinaso mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas. Compost no atwa so nnansas nwɔtwe kɔ duonum mmienu mu bere a ɛyɛ dark brown, ɛpepee yie na ɛwɔ nhwirɛ pa. De compost tonnes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa to eka baako so ansa na wode aba to mu sɛ ɛboa asase aduan pii.

candidates.question_en: When should maize be planted in southern and northern Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: In southern Ghana, plant maize in March to April for the major season and July to August for the minor season. In northern Ghana, plant from May to June when the rains begin. Planting at the right time ensures the crop gets adequate rainfall during tasseling and silking, which are the most critical growth stages.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛyɛ papa sɛ wode aburoɔ to mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Wɔ Ghana apuei fam, de aburoɔ to mu wɔ Ɔbenem kɔ Oforisuo ma akyi berɛ a na wɔ fam kɛse na bere a ɛtɔ wɔ Kutawonsa kɔ Oforisuo ma akyiri. Wɔ Ghana atifi, de to mu fi Ɔforisuo kɔ Ayɛwohomumo bere a nsuo retoe. Bere pa mu to aba mu kyerɛ sɛ afuom bɛnya nsuo a ɛyɛ papa wɔ bere a aburoɔ reto ahuhuruw.

candidates.question_en: What is Integrated Pest Management for maize?
candidates.answer_en: Integrated pest management for maize combines multiple control methods to reduce pest damage while minimizing chemical use. It includes planting resistant varieties, using certified seeds, planting at the recommended time to escape peak pest pressure, regular scouting to detect pests early, using biological controls like natural enemies, applying chemical pesticides only when pest levels exceed economic thresholds, and crop rotation to break pest cycles. This approach reduces costs and environmental impact compared to calendar spraying.
candidates.question_twi: Integrated pest management yɛ dɛn ma aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Integrated pest management ma aburoɔ de nhyiamu ahorow ka bom sɛ ɛhia adwummaker nsɔre na ɛhia chemicals sua. Ɛka ho to resistant varieties mu, de certified seeds, to mu bere a wɔakyerɛw so sɛ adwummaker atia ktwa, hwɛ so bere biara ma wohunu adwummaker ntɛm, de biological controls te sɛ natural enemies, de chemical pesticides pɛ bere a adwummaker bore so kɛse sen economic thresholds, na sesa adekuo adwuma sɛ ɛbu adwummaker bere. Nhyiamu yi hia sika sua na ɛboa asase mu sen calendar spraying.

candidates.question_en: What is crop rotation and why is it important?
candidates.answer_en: Crop rotation means growing different crops on the same land each season. For example, grow maize in season 1, then cowpea in season 2. This breaks pest cycles, improves soil fertility, and increases yields.
candidates.question_twi: Dea ɛyɛ sɛ wosesa nnuaba gu asase mu na adɛn na ɛyɛ papa?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba sesae kyerɛ sɛ wokura ahorow nnuaba wɔ asase koro so bere biara. Nhwɛso so, kura aburow bere 1 mu, afei kura abɔdweɛ wɔ bere 2 mu. Eyi bubu adwummakers ntam, yɛ asase mu aduan ho nhwiren na ɛma nnuaba da sor dodo.

items.question_en: Why is clean water important when washing food crops?
items.answer_en: Dirty water can contaminate produce. Use water that is suitable for the intended washing purpose and keep washing equipment clean.
items.question_twi: Adɛn nti na nsuo a ɛho tew ho hia bere a yɛhohorɔ nnɔbae?
items.answer_twi: Nsuo a ɛfĩ tumi de nneɛma bɔne kɔ nnɔbae so. Fa nsuo a ɛfata aduan ho tebea di dwuma na ma washing equipment no ho tew.

candidates.question_en: Why should harvested vegetables not be left in direct sun?
candidates.answer_en: Direct heat can increase water loss and shorten shelf life. Move produce to shade and keep it cool after harvest.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛnsɛ sɛ mede nnɔbae a magye no gyaw owia tee mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Owia hyew ma nsuo firi nnɔbae mu ntɛm na ɛtew shelf life so. Fa wɔn kɔ sunsuma na ma wɔyɛ nwunu bere a wogye wɔn akyi.

candidates.question_en: How should farm produce be packaged for market?
candidates.answer_en: Use clean, suitable packaging that protects the product from crushing, contamination and excess moisture.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apakɛ nnɔbae ama gua?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa packaging a ɛho tew na ɛfata a ɛbɔ nnɔbae ho ban fi mpirapira, fĩ ne nsuo dodo ho.

candidates.question_en: Why is traceability useful on a farm?
candidates.answer_en: Simple records can help identify where produce came from, how it was produced and where it was sold if a quality problem occurs.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na traceability ho wɔ mfasoɔ wɔ afuo so?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛwtohɔ ketewa tumi boa ma wohu baabi a nnɔbae no firi, sɛnea wɔyɛe no ne baabi a wɔtɔn no sɛ quality haw bi ba a.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce bruising during produce transport?
candidates.answer_en: Use suitable containers, avoid excessive stacking and handle produce gently during loading and unloading.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpirapira so bere a merekɔfa nnɔbae?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa containers a ɛfata, mma wɔn nsi so dodo na fa ahwɛyiye di dwuma bere a woreload ne unload.

candidates.question_en: What should I do with damaged produce after harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Separate it from sound produce and decide whether it can be safely processed, fed to livestock where appropriate, composted or discarded.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ wɔ nnɔbae a apira akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi no fi nnɔbae pa no ho na hwɛ sɛ wobetumi ayɛ no processed food a ahobammɔ wɔ ho, ama mmoa adi sɛ ɛfata, ayɛ compost anaa ayi afi hɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can I tell if stored grain may have a mould problem?
candidates.answer_en: Look for visible mould, unusual smell, clumping, discolouration or increased moisture. Suspect grain should be isolated and assessed.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ mould wɔ aburow a meguina mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ mould a ɛda adi, hua a ɛnsɛ, grain a ɛbata bom, kɔla a ɛsakra anaa nsuo dodo. Grain a wohwɛ sɛ ɔhaw wɔ ho no yi fi foforo no ho na hwɛ no.

items.question_en: Why should farmers keep weather and planting records?
items.answer_en: Records help farmers compare seasons, understand rainfall patterns and improve planting and management decisions.
items.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ akuafoɔ kyerɛw weather ne planting dates?
items.answer_twi: Records boa ma akuafoɔ toto seasons ho, te rainfall patterns ase na yɛ planting ne farm management gyina nsɛm a wɔakora so so.

candidates.question_en: Why should farmers maintain soil cover?
candidates.answer_en: Soil cover reduces erosion, limits moisture loss and protects soil from intense rainfall and heat.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ akuafoɔ ma asase no kata?
candidates.answer_twi: Asase a covered no tew erosion so, tew nsuo yera so na bɔ asase no ho ban fi osu den ne ɔhyew ho.

candidates.question_en: How can farmers prepare for a late rainy season?
candidates.answer_en: Monitor local weather information, choose suitable planting dates and varieties, conserve soil moisture and avoid planting too early into dry soil.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie m'akuayɛ ma osu bere no akyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ local weather nsɛm, paw bere ne variety a ɛfata, kora nsuo wɔ asase mu na mma wofiri ase dua ntɛm wɔ asase a ɛda so yɛ kusuu mu.

candidates.question_en: How can mulch help during drought?
candidates.answer_en: Mulch reduces evaporation, protects the soil surface and can help conserve moisture around crop roots.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na mulch betumi aboa bere a ɔpɛ wɔ hɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Mulch tew nsuo a ɛyera so, bɔ asase anim ho ban na ɛboa ma nsuo tena nnɔbae ntini ho.

candidates.question_en: What is the benefit of planting windbreaks?
candidates.answer_en: Windbreaks can reduce wind speed, protect crops from wind damage and reduce moisture loss.
candidates.question_twi: Mfasoɔ bɛn na windbreak wɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Windbreak tew mframa ahoɔden so, bɔ nnɔbae ho ban fi mframa sɛe ho na tew nsuo yera so.

candidates.question_en: How can farmers prepare for floods?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid planting in high-risk low areas where possible, improve drainage, protect soil structure and have a plan for moving inputs and livestock to safer areas.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie m'afuo ama nsuyiri?
candidates.answer_twi: Mma wotɔ nnɔbae wɔ mmeae a nsuyiri taa ba sɛ wubetumi akwati, siesie drainage, bɔ asase structure ho ban na nya plan sɛnea wobɛfa nneɛma ne mmoa akɔ baabi a ahobammɔ wɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can water harvesting support dry-season farming?
candidates.answer_en: Stored water can supplement irrigation during dry periods when designed and managed safely.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na nsuo a yɛboaboa ano betumi aboa ɔpɛ bere kuayɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsuo a wɔakora no tumi boa irrigation wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu sɛ wɔayɛ no yie na wɔhwɛ so wɔ ahobammɔ mu.

items.question_en: What diseases commonly affect cassava and how can I manage them?
items.answer_en: Cassava mosaic disease causes yellow mosaic pattern on leaves and reduces yield severely. Cassava brown streak causes brown streaks on stems and rotting of the tuber. Cassava root rot causes tuber decay. Use virus-free certified planting material, plant resistant varieties, remove and destroy infected plants early, and avoid replanting in infected fields for at least one season.
items.question_twi: Yadeɛ bɛn na ɛtaa ba bankye ho na dɛn na menyɛ wɔn ho?
items.answer_twi: Cassava mosaic yadeɛ ma nhaban no yɛ yellow mosaic pattern na nnoa hun. Cassava brown streak ma abɔ no yɛ brown na bua yɛ sɛe. Cassava root rot ma bankye no sɛe. De planting material a virus nni mu a wɔakyerɛw ho, de varieties a wɔagyae so to mu, yi na sɛe nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na nni de to mu wɔ afuom a yadeɛ aba ho mfe baako pɛ.

candidates.question_en: What pests commonly attack cassava and how can I control them?
candidates.answer_en: Major cassava pests include cassava mealybug which causes wilting and stunted growth, cassava green mite causing leaf bronzing, and cassava whitefly which spreads mosaic virus. Control mealybug by releasing natural enemies like the parasitoid wasp Anagyrus lopezi. Remove affected plants and use clean planting material. Spray insecticidal soap or neem extract for mites and whitefly.
candidates.question_twi: Adwummaker bɛn na ɛtaa tu mako bankye na dɛn na menyɛ wɔn ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Adwummaker kɛse a ɛtaa tu bankye mako ne: cassava mealybug a ɛma nnuaba huru na nwa nni, cassava green mite a ɛma nhaban no yɛ bronze, na cassava whitefly a ɛpam mosaic virus. Boa mealybug ho de parasitoid wasp a wɔfre no Anagyrus lopezi guu. Yi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho na de planting material pa. De insecticidal soap anaa neem extract hware mites ne whitefly ho.

candidates.question_en: How do I select healthy cassava stems for planting?
candidates.answer_en: Select stems from healthy mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old. The stem should be firm, not shrivelled, about 2 to 3 cm thick and 20 to 30 cm long with at least 5 nodes. Avoid stems from diseased plants or those showing mosaic virus symptoms. Store cuttings in the shade for no more than 3 days before planting.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick bankye abɔ pa sɛ mede to mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi abɔ fi bankye nnuaba pa a wɔawo akyi mfee 8 kɔ 12. Abɔ no nni yie, mmaadwa gu ho, bɛyɛ sɛntimita 2 kɔ 3 tiawa na sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 tenten a ɛwɔ nodes 5 pɛ. Gye wo ho fi abɔ a ɛfi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho anaa a ɛkyerɛ mosaic virus ho nsono. Guina cutting no wɔ hare ha mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa pɛ ansa na wode to mu.

candidates.question_en: What are the main symptoms of African Cassava Mosaic Disease (ACMD) and how is it managed?
candidates.answer_en: The main symptoms of African Cassava Mosaic Disease (ACMD) include mosaic patterns on the leaves, leaf distortion, and reduced plant growth. Whiteflies and infected planting materials help spread the disease. Management includes using healthy planting materials, resistant varieties, and controlling whitefly populations.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛnkyerɛnne titiriw bɛn na ɛwɔ African Cassava Mosaic Disease (ACMD) ho na yɛbɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ so?
candidates.answer_twi: ACMD nsɛnkyerɛnne ne nhaban a ɛyɛ mosaic, nhaban a ɛyɛ basaa, ne nyini a ɛbrɛ ase. Nnomaa fitaa ne nnuaba a wɔayare na ɛtaa trɛw yare no. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wohwɛ so a, ɛsɛ sɛ wode nnuaba a ɛho tew, nnua a ɛntumi nyare, ne nnomaa fitaa a wobɛtua ano di dwuma.

candidates.question_en: What can I do with cassava peels and other cassava waste?
candidates.answer_en: Cassava peels can be dried and used as animal feed for goats, sheep and pigs, providing a valuable energy source. Fresh peels fermented for 3 to 4 days make good pig and poultry feed. Cassava peel compost improves soil fertility. The starchy water from gari processing can be fermented and used as a fermented cassava drink called pito or as a substrate for mushroom growing. Using cassava by-products reduces waste and adds extra income streams.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ bankye ho ne nsononko ho adwuma yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Bankye ho bɛtumi atew na de ma mmoa te sɛ birekyie, oguan ne prako aduan, de energy toɔ to. Bankye ho foforɔ a wɔde ferment adays mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan yɛ prako ne akoko aduan pa. Bankye ho compost boa asase aduan. Nsuo a starch wɔ mu fi gari yɛ ho bɛtumi aferment na de yɛ nsuo aduan a wɔfre no pito anaa de yɛ substrate ma mushroom noa. De bankye by-products de hyɛ nsono mu hia na ɛhia sika ahoma foforɔ.

candidates.question_en: How does climate change affect farming in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Climate change in Ghana is causing more erratic rainfall, longer dry seasons, increased temperatures, more frequent flooding and drought. Adapt by using drought-tolerant varieties, adopting water harvesting techniques like half-moon pits and tied ridges, diversifying into drought-resistant crops like cowpea cassava and sorghum, using mulching to conserve soil moisture, agroforestry which involves planting trees with crops, joining early warning systems for weather forecasts, and timing planting to match current rainfall patterns rather than traditional calendars.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na climate change yɛ okuafo adwuma den wɔ Ghana na dɛn na menyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Climate change wɔ Ghana ma nsuo tɔ bere sesa daa, bone berɛ tenten, berɛhyɛ tɔ so, nsuo ne bone tɔ so. Siesie wo tiri ho de de drought-tolerant varieties to mu, de water harvesting nhyiamu te sɛ half-moon pits ne tied ridges, sesa kɔ drought-resistant nnuaba te sɛ bɔde, bankye ne sorghum, de mulching sɛ ɛkora asase nsuo, agroforestry a ɛkyerɛ to nnuaba ne nnuaba kaa bom, ka early warning systems ho ma berɛ nkra, na to aba bere sɛ nsuo a ɛtaa tɔ saa ara ho na gye traditional calendars.

candidates.question_en: How should I harvest cassava properly?
candidates.answer_en: Cassava is usually harvested 9-18 months after planting. Cut the stem at 30-40 cm height then loosen the soil around the plant with a hoe and pull up the roots. Handle roots gently to avoid bruising.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye m'bankye yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Bankye taa gye wɔ abosome 9-18 akyi a wode to mu. Twa tibo no wɔ sɛntimita 30-40 so, afei de akɔde fa asase a ɛhyia nnua no ho na twe ntini no sor. De ntini no pɛ efisɛ sɛ ehow a ɛma ɛsɛe ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: How can I add value to my farm produce to earn more money?
candidates.answer_en: Process raw produce into higher-value products: dry and package grains, make tomato paste, gari from cassava, or palm oil from palm fruits. Value addition reduces post-harvest losses and increases income.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mede boɔ ka m'afuo nnuaba ho sɛ menya sika dodo?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ aduan foforo no yɛ aduan a wɔtɔ boɔ kɛse: yaw na paka nnuaba a ayaw, yɛ ntomato paste, gari fi bankye, anaa ngo fi abe aba. Boɔ to so maa mpampa post-harvest mpoano ne ma sika dodo.

candidates.question_en: How many acres of cassava do I need to make a meaningful profit?
candidates.answer_en: To make meaningful profit from cassava you need at least 2 to 5 acres. With improved varieties and good management, 5 acres can yield 40 to 75 tonnes of fresh cassava. At current market rates this translates to GHS 24,000 to 45,000 in revenue. After deducting costs of GHS 6,000 to 10,000 for a 5-acre farm, profit can be GHS 14,000 to 35,000 per season. Processing into gari or starch doubles or triples this profit.
candidates.question_twi: Asase ahe na mɛhia sɛ bankye adwuma ade sika ba?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛnya mfaso pa fi bankye mu a, wohia sɛ eka mmienu kɔ num pɛ. De improved varieties ne adwuma pa, eka num tumi de bankye foforɔ nnɔho 40 kɔ 75 tonne. Wɔ dwa bo a wɔwɔ saa ara, eyi bɛyɛ GHS 24,000 kɔ 45,000. Nnuaha wo costs GHS 6,000 kɔ 10,000 ma eka num afuom akyi, mfaso bɛtumi ayɛ GHS 14,000 kɔ 35,000 bere biara. De yɛ gari anaa starch a ɛde mfaso mmienu anaa mmiɛnsa ba.

items.question_en: What advice would you give a young person starting farming?
items.answer_en: Start small and learn as you grow. Choose one or two crops you understand well for your first season. Keep records of everything. Seek advice from experienced farmers and extension officers. Join a farmer group or cooperative. Do not give up after one bad season. Farming is a dignified and profitable business when done well.
items.question_twi: Adesua bɛn na wobɛma aberantemmaa a ɔresi okuafo adwuma ɛkan?
items.answer_twi: Fi ketewa na sua bere a woda sor. Paw nnuaba baako anaa abien a wohu wɔn yie bere a ɛdi ɛkan. Kora nsɛm nyinaa. Hwehwɛ nnwuma boa fi okuafo a wɔnim adwuma no ne extension officers. Ba okuafo kuo mu. Mma bere koro a aannya yie no amma wo anhuri. Okuafo adwuma yɛ adwuma a ɛwɔ anuonyam na ɛde sika ba sɛ woyɛ no yie.

candidates.question_en: What signs show that cattle may be sick?
candidates.answer_en: Common signs of illness in cattle include loss of appetite and reduced feed intake, unusual posture or difficulty standing, nasal or eye discharge, diarrhoea, bloating, weight loss, reduced milk production, laboured breathing, lameness, and isolation from the herd. Any cattle showing these signs should be separated from healthy animals immediately and examined by a veterinary officer. Early detection and treatment saves lives and prevents spread to other animals.
candidates.question_twi: Nsono bɛn na ɛkyerɛ sɛ nnwan wayarɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsono a ɛkyerɛ sɛ nnwan wayarɛ ne: aduan nhia, gyinae mfa ho anaa ahohia de gyina, hwam fi afi anaa ani, ayamtuo, ahonfuo, nnoa hun, nsuo sua, brɛath a ɛyɛ den, nan ahia, na afi herd no ho. Nnwan biara a ɛkyerɛ nsono yi nni yie sɛ woyiye fi mmoa pa ho ntɛm na vet offisa nhwɛ so. Hunu ntɛm na hu yɛ agyirae anom ne tete nsɛm mmoa foforɔ ho.

candidates.question_en: What pests and diseases commonly affect cocoyam?
candidates.answer_en: Common cocoyam problems include cocoyam root rot caused by Pythium fungi which makes the corm rot from the inside, cocoyam blight which causes lesions on leaves and corms, aphids and mites that suck sap from leaves. Control root rot by planting in well-drained soils, using healthy planting material and avoiding waterlogged conditions. Remove and destroy affected plants.
candidates.question_twi: Adwummaker ne yadeɛ bɛn na ɛtaa ba kɔkɔnte ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Aho yadeɛ a ɛtaa ba kɔkɔnte ho ne: cocoyam root rot a Pythium fungi ma ɛba a ɛma corm no sɛe fi mu, cocoyam blight a ɛma nsono ba nhaban ne corms so, aphids ne mites a wɔnom nhaban no nsuo. Boa root rot ho de to mu wɔ asase a nsuo tew yie, de planting material pa to mu na gye wo ho fi nsuo agyina ho. Yi na sɛe nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I control yam beetles and other yam pests?
candidates.answer_en: The yam beetle is one of the most destructive yam pests, tunnelling into tubers causing rot. Control by treating setts with insecticide before planting, harvesting at the right time without leaving tubers in the ground too long, storing yams properly, rotating crops to break the pest cycle, and applying carbofuran granules around the base of plants. Yam nematodes cause small lesions on tubers. Use certified clean planting material and avoid replanting in infested soil.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ yam beetles ne adwummaker foforɔ ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Yam beetle ne adwummaker a ɛsɛe bayerɛ paa baako, ɛkɔtɔ bua no mu a ɛma ɛsɛe. Boa ho de de insecticide hware setts ansa na wode to mu, yi bere a ɛyɛ papa a womfa bayerɛ na agyina asase mu akyiri, guina bayerɛ yie, sesa adekuo adwuma sɛ ɛbu adwummaker bere, na de carbofuran granules to nnuaba no ase ho. Yam nematodes ma nsono ketewa ba bua so. De certified clean planting material na nni de to mu wɔ asase a adwummaker wɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: When is the best time to plant yam in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Plant yam from February to April before the rains fully begin. Early planting allows the yam to establish roots before the heavy rains and gives a longer growing period. In areas with two rainy seasons, a second planting can be done in September. Yam planted too late misses the best growing period and gives poor yields.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛyɛ papa pa ara sɛ wede bayerɛ to mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: De bayerɛ to mu fi Ebiraw kɔ Oforisuo ansa na nsuo atoe kakra. To mu ediɛ boa bayerɛ no sɛ ɛntena ase wɔ asase mu ansa na nsuo kɛse atoe na ɛma nnɔ berɛ tenten. Wɔ hɔ a nsuo berɛ mmienu wɔ, wubetumi de to mu bio wɔ Ɛbɔ Ɔpɛnimma. Bayerɛ a wɔde to mu akyi sen yi afuom pa bere na ɛde nnoa nketewa ba.

candidates.question_en: How should I store yam properly?
candidates.answer_en: Store yams in a cool, dark, well-ventilated area. Traditional yam barns work well. Avoid contact with soil and keep yams off the ground. Inspect regularly and remove any rotting tubers. Yams can last 4-6 months.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meguina m'bayerɛ yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Guina bayerɛ wɔ bae a ɛhuru, ɛsum na mframa pue mu yie. Amammerɛ bayerɛ guina sukuu yɛ adwuma pa. Bɔ hwɛ asase nka wɔn na ma wɔn na wɔntena asase so. Hwɛ wɔn so pɛ na yi ɔbayerɛ a ɛresɛe. Bayerɛ tumi tena yie abosome 4-6.

candidates.question_en: How should I cure and store yam after harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Curing yams after harvest helps heal minor skin injuries and extends storage life. Place harvested yams in a warm humid location at 29 to 35 degrees Celsius with 90 to 95 percent relative humidity for 4 to 8 days. Traditional yam barns provide natural curing conditions. After curing store yams in a cool well-ventilated barn off the ground. Check stored yams monthly removing any showing rot immediately. Well-stored yams last 3 to 6 months.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛkwan pa bɛn na mede bayerɛ twew na guina yi akyi?
candidates.answer_twi: Bayerɛ twew yi akyi boa sɛ nsono ketewa wɔ ho so sa na aguina bere tenten. De bayerɛ a woyii sie wɔ baabi a ɛhyehyɛ kakra ne nsuo wɔ mu wɔ degrees 29 kɔ 35 Celsius ne relative humidity 90 kɔ 95 percent mu adays nnan kɔ nwɔtwe. Traditional bayerɛ barns de natural curing conditions to. Twew akyi guina bayerɛ wɔ barn a ɛdɛ ne mframa fa mu na ɛfiri asase so. Hwɛ bayerɛ a woguina bere biara na yi a ɛreyɛ sɛe wɔn ntɛm. Bayerɛ a woguina yie tena agyapade mmiɛnsa kɔ nsia mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I control internal parasites in sheep?
candidates.answer_en: Deworm sheep every 3 months using Albendazole or Ivermectin. Rotate between dewormers to prevent resistance. Check for signs of heavy worm burden including pale gums and eyelids which indicate anaemia, bottle jaw from protein loss, poor body condition and weight loss, diarrhoea and rough coat. The FAMACHA method uses eyelid colour scoring to decide which animals need deworming rather than deworming the whole flock unnecessarily. Consult your veterinary officer for a proper deworming schedule.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ internal parasites wɔ oguan ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Wia oguan adwummaker mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa de Albendazole anaa Ivermectin. Sesa dewormers ntam sɛ wɔantumi aho nsɔhwɛ so. Hwɛ nsono a ɛkyerɛ adwummaker pii a ɛwɔ mu te sɛ anom ne ani ho fitaa a ɛkyerɛ mogya hia, bottle jaw fi protein ahunu, ho ba nni yie ne nnoa hun, ayamtuo ne afohyɛ a ɛnte yie. FAMACHA nhyiamu de ani ho bo no sɛ hwɛ mmoa bɛn hia deworming na amma flock nyinaa enni deworm kwa. Bisa wo vet offisa ma deworming schedule pa.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare yam setts before planting?
candidates.answer_en: Cut healthy yam tubers into setts of 100 to 150 grams each. Each sett must have at least one eye or bud. Treat the cut surface with wood ash or a fungicide like Thiram to prevent rotting. Allow the setts to dry in the shade for 2 to 3 days before planting. This healing process called suberization forms a protective layer over the cut surface.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ bayerɛ setts ansa na mede to mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Twa bayerɛ pa setts a biara wɔ nnɔho 100 kɔ 150 gram. Sett biara nni yie sɛ ɛwɔ ani anaa bud baako. De wood ash anaa fungicide te sɛ Thiram hware twa mu no so sɛ ensusu. Ma setts no tew hare ha adays mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa ansa na wode to mu. Ayɛ yi a wɔfre no suberization de twamfo ahwɛ asɔ twa mu no so.

items.question_en: What is citrus greening disease and can it be treated?
items.answer_en: Citrus greening (also called Huanglongbing or HLB) is a deadly bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect. Symptoms include yellowing leaves, misshapen bitter fruits, and tree decline. There is currently no cure — infected trees should be removed and destroyed to prevent spread. Control psyllid insects and use certified disease-free planting material.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na citrus greening yadeɛ yɛ na wobetumi ayɛ dawuro?
items.answer_twi: Citrus greening (a wɔfre no Huanglongbing anaa HLB) yɛ bacterial yadeɛ a ɛkum na Asian citrus psyllid adwummaker de tete. Ahohyenam ho ne nhaban hoho, aba a asɛe ne a wɔn dɛm yɛ den, na nnua hia. Enni dawuro saa ara — yi nnua a wɔayarɛ na seaa wɔn sɛ yadeɛ anntete. Kora psyllid adwummakers ase na fa aba a wɔakyerɛw wɔ ho to mu.

candidates.question_en: What is agroforestry and how can it benefit my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Agroforestry is growing trees alongside crops or livestock on the same land. Benefits include: trees provide shade that reduces water stress, tree roots hold soil and prevent erosion, fallen leaves add organic matter, some trees fix nitrogen improving soil fertility, trees provide fruit or timber as additional income, and trees help store carbon reducing climate change impact. Recommended trees include Moringa, Leucaena, and Acacia.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na agroforestry yɛ na ɛboa m'afuo sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Agroforestry yɛ kura nnua wɔ nnuaba anaa mmoa ho wɔ asase koro so. Mfaaso ho ne: nnua de ewim brɛ ma ɛma nsuo hia nkɔm, nnua ntini kora asase na ɛmma asase nhuru, nhaban a atu de nhwiren foforo ka ho, nnua bi fi nitrogen ma asase ho nhwiren da sor, nnua de aba anaa dua bi ka ho sɛ sika foforɔ, na nnua boa guina carbon na ɛsua katawere mu sɛsae ho ɔkɔm. Nnua a wɔka wɔn ho ne Moringa, Leucaena, ne Acacia.

candidates.question_en: What is minimum tillage and how can it help my soil?
candidates.answer_en: Minimum tillage (also called conservation tillage) means disturbing the soil as little as possible when preparing for planting — using just enough tillage to create a seedbed. Benefits include: preserves soil structure, reduces erosion, maintains soil moisture, protects soil organisms, reduces fuel and labor costs, and helps store carbon in the soil. Use a jab planter or hand hoe to plant directly into the soil with minimal disturbance.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na minimum tillage yɛ na ɛdeɛn na ɛyɛ asase pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Minimum tillage (a wɔfre no conservation tillage nso) kyerɛ haw asase ketewa ketewa bere a wosiesie aba to mu ansa — fa tillage a ɛdodo pɛ sɛ woyi asase aba to mu ansa. Mfaaso ho ne: kora asase mu siesie, sua erosion, kora nsukuro wɔ asase mu, kora asase mu nkwa, sua fuel ne dwumadie ho sika, na boa guina carbon wɔ asase mu. Fa jab planter anaa nsa akɔde to aba tɔtɔ wɔ asase mu na wonhaw dodo.

candidates.question_en: What is damping-off disease in seedlings?
candidates.answer_en: Damping off is a fungal disease that causes seedlings to suddenly collapse and die, usually at the soil level where the stem meets the ground. The stem appears water-soaked and constricted. It is caused by overwatering, poor drainage, overcrowded seedlings, and unsterilized potting mix. Prevent by using sterilized soil, avoiding overwatering, ensuring good air circulation, and treating seeds with fungicide.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na nnuaba-mfoforo wu yadeɛ yadeɛ yɛ wɔ nnuaba mfoforo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba-mfoforo wu yadeɛ yɛ fungal yadeɛ a ɛma nnuaba mfoforo tu ntɛm na wɔwu, titiriw wɔ asase so a tibo ne asase hyia hɔ. Tibo no yɛ sɛ nsuo da mu na ɛhyia. Nsuo dodo, nsuo pue anammɔn a enni pa, nnuaba mfoforo a wɔhyia so, ne potting mix a wonsi amu ama. Kora ase wɔ fa asase a wɔasi amu, bɔ hwɛ nsuo dodo, kora mframa pue mu yie, na de aba ka fungicide ho ansa na woto.

candidates.question_en: What is precision farming and can a small farmer use it?
candidates.answer_en: Precision farming means using data and technology to apply exactly the right amount of inputs at the right time and place. Smallholders can practice basic precision farming by: soil testing different parts of the field and applying fertilizer based on results, using mobile apps to track crop growth, monitoring pest and disease hotspots and targeting treatment, and keeping detailed farm records to identify what works best.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na precision farming yɛ na okuafo ketewa tumi yɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Precision farming kyerɛ fa data ne technology di dwuma sɛ de adenneɛ a ɛfata to bere a ɛsɛ na beae a ɛsɛ. Okuafo ketewa tumi yɛ basic precision farming wɔ: hwɛ asase ahorow afuo mu na de ferefere to wɔ adwuma ho, fa mobile apps di dwuma sɛ kora nnuaba da sor, hwɛ adwumakers ne yadeɛ beae na hyɛ dawuro hɔ pɛ, na kora afuo nsɛm mu yiye sɛ wuhu dea yɛ adwuma pa.

candidates.question_en: What is vermicomposting and how do I start it?
candidates.answer_en: Vermicomposting uses earthworms to break down organic waste into very high-quality compost called vermicompost or worm castings. To start: get a container or build a wooden box, add bedding of moist shredded newspaper or cardboard, add earthworms (red wigglers are best), feed with fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, and eggshells. Avoid meat, dairy, and oily food. Harvest the rich compost from the bottom every 2-3 months.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na vermicomposting yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mesi ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Vermicomposting fa asase nwirɛntwi di dwuma sɛ pɛ nhwiren foforo asennua yɛ compost a ɛwɔ aduan pa pa ara a wɔfre vermicompost anaa worm castings. Sɛ wohwehwɛ si ase: nya nkuku anaa yɛ dua box, de krataa anaa cardboard a wɔatwa twa na wɔapo mu de yɛ mpa, de asase nwirɛntwi hyɛ (red wiggler yɛ pa pa ara), de nnuan ne aba asennua, coffee, ne kosua nkuku hyɛ. Bɔ hwɛ nam, nkyene aduan, ne ngo aduan. Gye compost a ɛwɔ ase hɔ no abosome 2-3 biara.

candidates.question_en: What are nematodes and how do they affect crops?
candidates.answer_en: Nematodes are microscopic worms that live in soil. Some are harmful to crops — they attack roots causing galls (swellings), stunted growth, and yellowing. They are common in sandy soils and warm climates. Control by rotating crops, using resistant varieties, adding organic matter to soil, and solarizing soil (covering with clear plastic to heat it and kill nematodes during the dry season).
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na nematode yɛ na ɛyɛ m'nnuaba dɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Nematode yɛ nwirɛntwi a wɔte asase mu a wɔhunu da. Bi yɛ nnuaba ɔkɔm — wɔtwe ntini ho ma ɛyɛ kɛse, nnuaba nni sor yie, na nhaban hoho. Wɔtaa wɔ asintiɛ asase ne ahuhuro mu. Kora ase wɔ sesa nnuaba, fa aba a ɛtumi hyɛ ase, de nhwiren foforo ka asase ho, na solarize asase (fa plastik fitaa sɛɛ so sɛ ɛhye mu na kum nematode wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu).

candidates.question_en: What is a soil testing kit and how do I use it?
candidates.answer_en: A soil testing kit is a set of chemicals and test strips or color charts that let you test your soil's pH, nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels at home. To use: collect soil from several spots in your field and mix together, take a small sample, follow the kit instructions to mix with testing chemicals, compare the color change to the chart provided, and use results to decide what fertilizer to apply. Kits are available at agricultural supply stores.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na asase hwɛ kit yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Asase hwɛ kit yɛ chemicals ne test strips anaa color charts a ɛma wo tumi hwɛ wo asase pH, nitrogen, phosphorus, ne potassium wɔ fie. Di dwuma eyi: gye asase fi beae ahodoɔ wɔ afuo mu na ka bom, fa sample ketewa, bu kit nhyɛso so sɛ de chemicals ka ho, twe rere sɛsae na ka ho ne chart a wɔde brɛ, na fa adwuma ho sɛ paw ferefere a wohia. Kits wɔ hɔ wɔ agricultural supply adeɛtɔ hɔ.

candidates.question_en: What is Striga and how can I control it?
candidates.answer_en: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches to crop roots. Control includes using Striga-resistant varieties, applying Imazapyr-coated seeds, hand pulling Striga before it flowers, growing trap crops like Sudan grass, and applying fertilizer to help crops outcompete Striga.
candidates.question_twi: Striga nhaban foforo resɛe m'ɔtɛ. Dɛn na metumi yɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Striga yɛ nhaban foforo a ɔkyerɛ ne ho wɔ nnuaba ntini so. Kora ase wɔ de aba a ɛtumi Striga ase hyɛ, de Imazapyr-coated aba, twe Striga wɔ nsa ansa na ɔba abode, kura trap crops te sɛ Sudan grass, na de ferefere to sɛ ɛboa nnuaba no nko ɔkan.

items.question_en: How can I integrate livestock into my crop farm?
items.answer_en: Integrate livestock by using their manure as organic fertilizer for crops. Chickens can help control insects and weeds. After harvest allow animals to graze on crop residues which also helps clear the field. This integrated farming approach reduces costs and improves productivity.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mefa m'mmoa di dwuma ma m'afuo nnuaba?
items.answer_twi: Ka mmoa ho wɔ de wɔn aguare yɛ nhwiren foforo ferefere ma nnuaba. Akrɔma tumi boa kora adwummakers ne nhaban foforo ase. Nnuaba gye akyi, ma mmoa nom nnuaba nsennua a aka no a ɛnso boa hohoro afuo no. Eyi farming anammɔn sua sika na ɛma afuo no nyinaa da sor yie.

candidates.question_en: Can I use animal manure instead of chemical fertilizer?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, animal manure from cows, goats, or chickens is an excellent organic fertilizer. Apply well-composted manure 2-3 weeks before planting. It improves soil structure and provides slow-release nutrients.
candidates.question_twi: Metumi de mmoa dɔteɛ adi dwuma mmom sen nnuru ferefere?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, mmoa aguare fi boo, abirekyi, anaa akrɔma yɛ ferefere papa pa ara. De aguare a ɛawie wo yie no to asase so wiemu 2-3 ansa na wobede aba to mu. Ɛsiesie asase mu na ɛma aduan ho nhwiren ba bebree.

candidates.question_en: How can I start a small poultry farm at home?
candidates.answer_en: To start a small home poultry farm: decide on type (layers for eggs or broilers for meat), build or buy a simple wooden or wire coop with shade and good ventilation, start with 10-20 birds, provide clean water and commercial feed, vaccinate birds at the recommended ages, keep the coop clean, and record feeds, deaths, and egg production. Start small and scale as you learn.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesi akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ si akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie: paw ahodoɔ (layers ma kosua anaa broilers ma nam), si anaa tɔ dua anaa wire fie a ewim brɛ ne mframa pue mu yie, fi akrɔma 10-20, de nsuo horo ne aduan a wɔtɔ ma wɔn, de akrɔma kɔ yadeɛ dawuro bere a ɛsɛ, kora fie no horo, na kora aduan, wuu, ne kosua ho nsɛm. Fi ketewa na fa dodo so bere a wosua.

candidates.question_en: What causes soil to become hard and how can I fix it?
candidates.answer_en: Soil becomes hard from: overuse of heavy machinery which compacts the soil, lack of organic matter, repeatedly plowing at the same depth creating a hardpan layer, frequent flooding followed by drying, and low biological activity. To fix it, add organic matter, practice deep tillage occasionally, and use cover crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma asase yɛ den na ɛhia yiye?
candidates.answer_twi: Asase yɛ den fi: egyapade kɛse ho di dwuma dodo a ɛhia asase, nhwiren foforo aduan ho hia, bere biara boro asase sukyerɛ koro so a ɛyɛ hardpan, nsuo tenten a ɛto akyi na asase yera, ne nkwa a ɛdi asase mu hia. Sɛ wohwehwɛ siesie no a, de nhwiren foforo ka ho, bere bi boro asase mu tenten, na kura asase-bo nnuabas.

candidates.question_en: How can I make low-cost hermetic storage?
candidates.answer_en: You can make low-cost hermetic storage using: triple-layer plastic bags where you place grain in an inner plastic bag, seal it, place in a second bag, seal it, then place in a third outer bag and seal. Or use metal drums with tight-fitting lids sealed with tape. Store off the ground on pallets. This method is very effective for 6-12 months of storage.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meyɛ hermetic guina a ɛboɔ yɛ ketewa?
candidates.answer_twi: Wobetumi yɛ hermetic guina a ɛboɔ yɛ ketewa wɔ: plastik bags mmiɛnsa a wode aduan si plastik bag mu, po so, de si bag abien mu, po so, afei de si bag mmiɛnsa mu na po so. Anoa fa metal drums a wɔn soro yɛ den a wɔde tape po so. Guina wɔ pallet so afi asase so. Anammɔn no yɛ adwuma yie pa ara wɔ guina abosome 6-12 mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I increase egg production in layers?
candidates.answer_en: For maximum egg production ensure 16 hours of light daily using artificial lighting, maintain temperature between 18 and 24 degrees Celsius, provide layer mash with 16 to 17 percent protein and added calcium for strong shells, ensure clean water always, control parasites and disease through regular vaccination and deworming, collect eggs three times daily, keep stress low by avoiding sudden disturbances, and cull poor layers that consistently produce below average.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tamma gu akoko sɛ wɔagu pii?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ akoko gu tamma pii a, hwɛ sɛ kanea da wɔ mu dɔn 16 de artificial light, kora berɛ wɔ degrees 18 ne 24 Celsius ntam, de layer mash a protein 16 kɔ 17 percent ne calcium a ɛhia ma tamma ho den na ka ho, de nsuo pa to mu bere nyinaa, boa parasites ne yadeɛ ho de hware ne wia adwummaker bere biara, pam tamma mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa biara da, ma anigyidie sua de gye wo ho fi nka kɔkɔɔkɔ, na kum layers a wɔgu nketewa bere nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent Newcastle disease in poultry?
candidates.answer_en: Newcastle disease is the most serious threat to poultry in Ghana. Prevent it through strict vaccination using Lasota vaccine at day 7, day 21 and every 2 months thereafter. Keep visitors away from your poultry house, disinfect equipment and footwear before entering, quarantine new birds for 2 weeks, buy birds from certified sources only, and cull sick birds immediately. There is no treatment for Newcastle disease once birds are infected.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ Newcastle yadeɛ annya me akoko?
candidates.answer_twi: Newcastle yadeɛ ne akoko tia a ɛtaa yɛ den paa wɔ Ghana. Gye wo ho fi mu de Lasota hware aba ahyɛ so mu da 7, da 21 na mprɛn mmienu biara wɔ saa akyi. Ma ahofipa anyɛ kwan kɔ wo akoko fie, hware nneɛma ne nan so ansa na wukɔ mu, kora nnomaa foforɔ wɔ baabi foforo nnansas mmienu, gye nnomaa fi hɔ a wɔakyerɛw so pɛ, na kum nnomaa a wayarɛ ntɛm. Newcastle yadeɛ nni dawuro bere a nnomaa no anya mu.

candidates.question_en: How often should I vaccinate my chickens against Newcastle Disease?
candidates.answer_en: Chickens should be vaccinated against Newcastle Disease according to an appropriate schedule. Vaccination may start around day 7, followed by additional doses around weeks 3–4 and 8–10, depending on the vaccine and local disease situation. Farmers should follow the schedule recommended by their local veterinary officer.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mede nnuru bɔ m'ankokɔ tia Newcastle Disease mpɛn ahe?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ wode nnuru bɔ akokɔ tia Newcastle Disease wɔ bere pɔtee bi mu, mpɛn pii no efi da a ɛtɔ so 7, afei wode nnuru foforo bɔ wɔn wɔ dapɛn 3-4 ne 8-10 mu, a egyina nnuru no su ne yare no so. Kɔhwɛ wo mpɔtam hɔ nnuataban sohwɛfo na ɔmma wo nhyehyɛe pɔtee bi.

candidates.question_en: How can I manage heat stress in chickens?
candidates.answer_en: Heat stress is common in Ghana and reduces growth rate and egg production. Manage it by ensuring good ventilation in the poultry house, providing cool fresh water frequently, installing foggers or sprinklers on the roof, feeding in the cooler parts of the day morning and evening, reducing stocking density during hot seasons, adding vitamin C and electrolytes to water during extreme heat, and considering open-sided housing designs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ berɛhyɛ den a ɛba me akoko ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Berɛhyɛ den taa ba wɔ Ghana na ɛhia boɛ a aba nhia na tamma nhia. Boa ho de hwɛ sɛ mframa fa akoko fie mu yie, de nsuo dɛ foforɔ to mu bere biara, si foggers anaa sprinklers wɔ fie no atifi so, didi wɔ berɛ dɛ mu anɔpa ne anwumere, sua akoko a wɔwɔ mu wɔ berɛhyɛ bere, de vitamin C ne electrolytes ka nsuo mu wɔ hyehyɛ den bere, na twe wo adwene ho open-sided housing nhyiamu.

items.question_en: How can I sell my farmed fish at a good price in Ghana?
items.answer_en: Market your fish effectively by selling live fish to restaurants and hotels which pay premium prices for freshness, supplying smoked or dried fish to markets for longer shelf life, building relationships with female fish traders at Kumasi Central Market and Accra markets who buy in bulk, using social media like Facebook to reach direct buyers, selling during festive seasons like Christmas and Eid when demand and prices are highest, and joining fish farmer cooperatives that negotiate group prices.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ metɔ me apataa wɔ bo pa wɔ Ghana?
items.answer_twi: Tɔ wo apataa pa de tɔ apataa a wɔte so kɔ adidibea ne hotels a wɔtua sika pa ma foforɔ ho, de apataa a wɔahye anaa atew to kɔ dwa ma ɛtena mu akyi, kyɛ wo adwene ho okuafo bea a wɔtɔ apataa wɔ Kumasi Central Market ne Accra dwa mu a wɔgye pii, de social media te sɛ Facebook kɔ buyers straight ho, tɔ bere a afenhyia ba te sɛ Bosome Dɔ ne Eid bere a nhia ne bo yɛ so sen, na ka apataa okuafo kuo ho a wɔbɔ bo kaa bom.

candidates.question_en: How can I construct a low-cost earthen fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with clay soil that holds water well, near a reliable water source. Mark out the pond area typically 20 by 25 metres. Dig to a depth of 1.5 to 2 metres with sloping sides for stability. Build an inlet pipe to bring water in and an outlet pipe at the deepest point to drain. Pack the dikes firmly to prevent leaks. Fill with water and leave for 2 weeks to cure and establish algae before stocking. The total cost including excavation for a 500 square metre pond is typically GHS 3,000 to 6,000.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ earthen apataa pond a bo sua?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ clay asase a ɛkora nsuo yie, bɛn nsuo kwan pa. Kyerɛ pond area a ɛtaa yɛ metres 20 ne 25. Boro kɔsi tia metres 1.5 kɔ 2 a ho mfimfini slopes wɔ gyinae ho. Tu inlet pipe sɛ nsuo aba mu na outlet pipe wɔ tia no so sɛ nsuo fa mu. Hyehye dikes no yie sɛ nsuo anyi. Ma nsuo kɔ mu na gyina nnansas mmienu sɛ ɛtena na algae ntua fɔw ansa na wode apataa to. Bo nyinaa a excavation ka ho ma pond a square metres 500 wɔ mu taa yɛ GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000.

candidates.question_en: When should I harvest tilapia?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest tilapia when they reach market size of 300 to 500 grams which typically takes 5 to 6 months from fingerling stage. Monitor growth by sampling fish monthly using a net. Harvest in the early morning when water temperature is cool to reduce fish stress. Partial harvesting at 4 months removes larger fish and allows smaller ones to grow. Sell fresh fish immediately or ice them for transport to market.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na meyiyɛ me tilapia apataa?
