candidates.answer_twi: Yi tilapia bere a wɔkɔ si dwa kɛse a nnɔho 300 kɔ 500 gram a ɛtaa kyɛ mfee 5 kɔ 6 fi fingerling mu. Hwɛ sɛ apataa rebɛbo yie de sample apataa bere biara de net. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo berɛ dɛ sɛ apataa nhunu. Partial yi wɔ mfee nnan mu yi apataa kɛse na ma nketewa bo sɔ. Tɔ apataa fofor ntɛm anaa de ice ka ho ma akɔ dwa.

candidates.question_en: How much does it cost to start a small fish farm in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Starting a small commercial fish farm in Ghana with two earthen ponds of 500 square metres each costs approximately GHS 15,000 to 25,000 including pond construction, fingerlings, feed for one cycle, and basic equipment. A plastic tank fish farm can be started for GHS 8,000 to 15,000. The main ongoing costs are fish feed which accounts for 60 to 70 percent of total production cost. With good management you can make a profit from the first cycle.
candidates.question_twi: Sika ahe na ɛyɛ papa sɛ mefi ase apataa adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apataa adwuma ketewa kɛse fi ase wɔ Ghana de earthen ponds mmienu a square metres 500 biara wɔ mu ho teetee GHS 15,000 kɔ 25,000 a pond yɛ, fingerlings, aduan wɔ cycle baako mu, ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ papa. Plastic tank apataa adwuma wobetumi de GHS 8,000 kɔ 15,000 fi ase. Nneɛma a ɛkyere daadaa a ɛkɔ so pii ne apataa aduan a ɛyɛ adwuma agyapade 60 kɔ 70 percent. Sɛ woyɛ adwuma pa a, wobetumi anya mfaso wɔ cycle a ɛdi kan mu.

candidates.question_en: What is the best way to harvest fish from a pond?
candidates.answer_en: The best harvesting method depends on whether you are doing partial or complete harvest. For partial harvest use a seine net to selectively remove larger fish leaving smaller ones to grow. For complete harvest drain the pond partially then use nets to remove all fish. Harvest early morning when water is cool. Have containers ready with clean water or ice to keep fish alive or fresh. Weigh and record your harvest for business records. Never use chemicals or electricity to harvest as these are illegal and harmful.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛkwan bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ meyiyɛ apataa fi pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛkwan a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wuyiyɛ no kyɛ sɛ partial anaa complete harvest na woyɛ. Ma partial harvest de seine net yi apataa kɛse a wɔbɛ na ma nketewa tena so bo sɔ. Ma complete harvest sua nsuo ketewa fi pond mu afei de nets yi apataa nyinaa. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo dɛ. Ma containers a nsuo foforɔ anaa ice wɔ mu sɛ apataa aguina anaa tena foforɔ. Bu na kora wo harvest ho sɛ adwuma nsɛm. Mma wo mpo de chemicals anaa electricity yiyɛ efisɛ ɛnyɛ nea mmara gyina so na ɛyɛ bɔne.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent overcrowding in a fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Stock according to the pond's capacity and monitor fish growth, water quality and available oxygen.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpataa dodo so wɔ pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa dodow a pond no tumi soa no gu mu na hwɛ mpataa nyin, nsuo quality ne oxygen a ɛwɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: What should I do if fish stop feeding suddenly?
candidates.answer_en: Check water quality, temperature, oxygen, recent weather, feed quality and signs of disease before increasing feed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ sɛ mpataa gyae di aduane ntɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsuo quality, ɔhyew, oxygen, weather a aba foforo, feed quality ne yare ho nsɛnkyerɛnne ansa na woama feed no so.

candidates.question_en: How should a fish farmer keep pond records?
candidates.answer_en: Record stocking date and number, feed used, mortalities, water-quality observations, treatments, harvest weight and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛw fish pond records?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw stocking da ne dodow, feed a wode dii dwuma, mpataa a awuwu, nsuo quality nsɛm, ayaresa, harvest duru ne tɔn.

items.question_en: How can I reduce disturbance around bee hives?
items.answer_en: Keep pathways clear, limit unnecessary activity near hives and use appropriate protective practices when inspecting colonies.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate basabasa so wɔ beehive ho?
items.answer_twi: Ma akwan no ho tew, mma nnipa nyɛ adwuma a ɛho nhia bɛn beehive no na fa ahobammɔ akwan a ɛfata bere a worehwɛ colony no.

candidates.question_en: What should I wear when inspecting bees?
candidates.answer_en: Use appropriate protective clothing and equipment designed for beekeeping, including a veil and gloves where needed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mehyɛ bere a merehwɛ nkyene?
candidates.answer_twi: Hyɛ ahobammɔ ntade ne adwinnade a ɛfata beekeeper, a veil ne gloves ka ho sɛ ɛhia.

candidates.question_en: How often should hives be inspected?
candidates.answer_en: Inspect according to the production system and season, focusing on colony health, pests, food stores and hive condition.
candidates.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ beehive?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛnea production system ne bere no te, na hwɛ colony no ahoɔden, mmoawa, aduane a ɛwɔ hɔ ne hive no tebea.

candidates.question_en: How should honey be stored?
candidates.answer_en: Store honey in clean, food-grade containers in a dry place away from strong odours and excess moisture.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn aguina honey?
candidates.answer_twi: Guina honey wɔ ade a ɛho tew na ɛfata food, wɔ beae yera a hua bɔne ne nsuo dodo nni hɔ.

candidates.question_en: Where should beehives be placed?
candidates.answer_en: Place hives in a quiet, shaded or semi-shaded area with good drainage, access to forage and reasonable protection from disturbance.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛhe na ɛsɛ sɛ mede beehive si?
candidates.answer_twi: Si no wɔ beae a ɛdwo, sunsuma kakra wɔ hɔ, nsuo firi mu yie, nhwiren wɔ ho na nnipa ntɔ no daa.

candidates.question_en: How can a beekeeper estimate honey production from hive records?
candidates.answer_en: Record hive locations, inspections, colony strength, treatments, harvest quantities and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛ honey production dodow afi hive kyerɛwtohɔ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw hive baabi, nhwehwɛmu, colony ahoɔden, ayaresa, honey dodow a woagye ne tɔn.

candidates.question_en: Why are flowering plants important for bees?
candidates.answer_en: Bees depend on flowers for nectar and pollen, so a variety of flowering plants can support colony development.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na nhwiren a ɛbɔ aba ho hia ma nkyene?
candidates.answer_twi: Nkyene gye nectar ne pollen fi nhwiren mu, enti nhwiren ahorow a ɛbɔ aba boa colony no nyin.

items.question_en: How can I calculate the expected cash needed before starting a farming season?
items.answer_en: A farm budget is a plan showing expected income and expenditure for a particular farming activity or season.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛ sika a mɛhia ansa na mahyɛ farming season ase?
items.answer_twi: Farm budget yɛ nhyehyɛe a ɛkyerɛ sika a wohwɛ kwan sɛ wobɛnya ne nea wobɛbɔ wɔ farming adwuma anaa season bi ho.

candidates.question_en: What questions should I ask before investing money in a new farm enterprise?
candidates.answer_en: Include the farm idea, target market, production plan, resources, expected costs, expected sales, risks and a simple implementation timeline.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛmmisa bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mibisa ansa na mede sika ahyɛ kuayɛ adwuma foforo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Susuw kuayɛ adwuma no, gua a wopɛ, production plan, nneɛma a wowɔ, sika a wobɛbɔ, sika a wɔhwɛ kwan sɛ wobɛtɔn no, ɔhaw ne bere nhyehyɛe ho.

candidates.question_en: How do I estimate farm production costs?
candidates.answer_en: List expected costs for land preparation, seed, inputs, labour, water, transport, equipment, packaging and other operating expenses.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛ farm production cost?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw sika a wobɛbɔ wɔ asase siesie, aba, inputs, adwumayɛfo, nsuo, transport, equipment, packaging ne operating expenses ho.

candidates.question_en: Why should I review a farm budget after the season?
candidates.answer_en: Comparing planned and actual figures helps you understand what went well, what went wrong and how to improve the next season.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ farm budget no bio bere a season no awie?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wototo nea wosusuw ho ne nea ɛbaa ankasa a, ɛma wuhu nea ɛyɛɛ yie, nea ɛkɔɔ bɔne ne nea wubetumi asesa season foforo.

candidates.question_en: Why should I calculate break-even before starting a farm enterprise?
candidates.answer_en: Break-even analysis helps you estimate how much you must sell before the enterprise begins to make a profit.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mebu break-even ansa na mahyɛ kuayɛ ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Break-even boa ma wohu dodow a ɛsɛ sɛ wotɔn ansa na kuayɛ adwuma no ahyɛ ase anya mfasoɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can a farmer reduce business risk?
candidates.answer_en: Diversify sensibly, keep records, build an emergency reserve, maintain good production practices and avoid relying on one buyer or one crop alone.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate business risk so wɔ kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyekyɛ kuayɛ nneɛma sɛ ɛfata, kyerɛw records, yɛ emergency reserve, di kuayɛ akwan pa so na mfa wo ho nhyɛ adetɔfo anaa nnɔbae baako so nkutoo.

candidates.question_en: Why is cash flow important in farming?
candidates.answer_en: Farm expenses often happen before income arrives. A cash-flow plan helps ensure money is available when costs are due.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na cash flow ho hia wɔ kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kuayɛ sika pii no wɔbɔ no ansa na sika a ɛfiri tɔn mu aba. Cash-flow plan boa ma sika wɔ hɔ bere a wɔhia tua.

candidates.question_en: Why should I separate household money from farm money?
candidates.answer_en: Separating the two makes it easier to measure whether the farm itself is profitable and reduces confusion in record keeping.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mekye fie sika ne afuo sika mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wokyekyɛ wɔn mu a, ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhu sɛ afuo no ankasa wɔ mfasoɔ anaa enni mfasoɔ na ɛtew basabasa wɔ records mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I decide whether to expand my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Expand only when markets, working capital, management capacity, labour, land and production records show that the enterprise can support growth.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ metrɛw m'afuo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Trɛw no bere a gua, working capital, management, adwumayɛfo, asase ne production records kyerɛ sɛ adwuma no tumi gyina growth no so nkutoo.

items.question_en: Why is good drainage important for groundnut?
items.answer_en: Waterlogging can damage roots and pods and can increase disease problems. Well-drained soil supports healthy pod development.
items.question_twi: Adɛn nti na nsuo firi asase mu yie ho hia ma nkatie?
items.answer_twi: Nsuo a ɛgyina asase mu betumi asɛe ntini ne aba na ɛma yare dɔɔso. Asase a nsuo firi mu yie boa nkatie ma ɛbɔ aba yie.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve groundnut flowering and pod formation?
candidates.answer_en: Choose well-drained soil, remove heavy weeds and prepare a fine seedbed without excessive compaction.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama nkatie nhwiren ne aba no ayɛ yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw asase a nsuo tumi firi mu, yi nwura a ɛdɔɔso na siesie asase no yie nanso mfa mfrafra asase no dodo.

candidates.question_en: How do legumes improve soil fertility in a mixed farming system?
candidates.answer_en: Legumes can contribute to soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation and can help diversify cropping systems.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na legumes boa ma asase yɛ dɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Legumes tumi de nitrogen boa asase so fa biological nitrogen fixation ho na ɛma nnɔbae ahorow nyɛ baako pɛ.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce aflatoxin risk in groundnut?
candidates.answer_en: Use good-quality seed, manage field stress, harvest carefully, dry pods thoroughly and store them in clean, dry conditions.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate aflatoxin haw so wɔ nkatie mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa aba pa, hwɛ ɔhaw a ɛwɔ afuo mu, gye nkatie no yie, yow wɔn paa na guina wɔ beae a ɛho tew na ɛyɛ yera.

candidates.question_en: How should I handle harvested legumes before storage?
candidates.answer_en: Remove dirt and damaged material, dry the grain thoroughly, cool it before sealing, and keep the storage area dry and clean.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ legumes a magye no ansa na waguina?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi dɔte ne nneɛma a asɛe, yow aba no yie, ma ɛnwunu ansa na woato no mu na ma guina beae no nyɛ yera na ɛho tew.

candidates.question_en: Can legumes be grown with cereals?
candidates.answer_en: Yes. Intercropping some legumes with cereals can use space efficiently and diversify production, but the crops need compatible spacing and management.
candidates.question_twi: Legumes tumi nyin ne cereals bom anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane. Wobetumi adua legumes ne cereals bom ma wɔde beae no di dwuma yie na ɛma nnɔbae ahorow. Nanso ɛsɛ sɛ wɔn ntam ne wɔn nhwɛsoɔ hyia.

items.question_en: Which farming businesses are more profitable in Ghana?
items.answer_en: Profitability depends on scale, management and market access. High profit crops include vegetables especially tomatoes, pepper and onion under irrigation, mushroom farming which gives quick returns, snail farming with low inputs, broiler poultry with fast turnover, fish farming especially catfish, and cashew farming for export. The key is to choose something you understand well, have a reliable market for, and can manage consistently. Start with one enterprise before diversifying.
items.question_twi: Okuafo adwuma bɛn na ɛde mfaso ba sen wɔ Ghana?
items.answer_twi: Mfaso no kyɛ sɛ kɛse bɛn na woyɛ, dɛn na woyɛ na dwa kɔ ho. Nnuaba a ɛde mfaso ba sen ne nnuaba ahorow a ɛhia pii te sɛ tomatoes, pepper ne abɔnkɔ wɔ quench ase, mushroom adwuma a ɛde sika ntɛm, snail adwuma a sika ketewa na ɛhia, broiler poultry a ɛde sika ntɛm, apataa adwuma a ɛhia pii ne catfish, na cashew adwuma ma export. Asɛde a ɛyɛ papa ne: yi biribi a wohu mu yie, wowɔ dwa gyinae, na wobetumi ahwɛ so bere biara. Fi ase de adwuma baako ansa na woyɛ pii.

candidates.question_en: What irrigation method is best for tomatoes in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Drip irrigation is the best method for tomatoes in Ghana. It delivers water directly to the root zone reducing disease incidence from leaf wetness, improving water use efficiency, allowing fertigation where fertilizer is applied through the drip system, and reducing weed growth. Furrow irrigation is also acceptable for flat land. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation for tomatoes as wet foliage encourages fungal diseases like late blight. Irrigate in the morning to allow foliage to dry before evening.
candidates.question_twi: Quench nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara ma tomatoes wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Drip quench ne nhyiamu pa ara ma tomatoes wɔ Ghana. Ɛde nsuo kɔ nnɔho asase mu nsɛm a ɛhia yadeɛ a ɛba efisɛ nhaban nsuo, ɛboa nsuo de pa, ɛma fertigation a wɔde ferefere fa wɔ drip system mu to, na ɛhia nhaban foforo. Furrow quench nso yɛ yie ma asase a ɛtee. Gye wo ho fi overhead sprinkler quench ma tomatoes efisɛ nhaban nsuo boa fungal yadeɛ te sɛ late blight. Quench anɔpa sɛ nhaban tew ansa na anwumere aba.

candidates.question_en: How can I make tomato farming profitable?
candidates.answer_en: To make profit from tomatoes, time your production to sell when prices are high which is usually the dry season from November to February. Use drip irrigation for dry season production. Produce in bulk to negotiate better prices, form a farmer group to collectively market your tomatoes, and consider simple processing like tomato paste or puree to add value and extend shelf life. Keep detailed records of all costs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ menyɛ sika wɔ tomatoes adwuma mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛfa sika wɔ tomatoes mu a, siesie wo to aba bere sɛ bɛtɔ bere a bo wɔ so wɔ yiye a ɛyɛ daadaa bone berɛ fi Ɔbenem kɔ Ɔpepon. De drip irrigation ma bone berɛ to aba. To pii sɛ wobɛtumi aho bo mu yie, fa okuafo kuo sɛ wɔde tomatoes bɛtɔ kaa bom, na twe wo adwene ho processing ketewa te sɛ tomato paste anaa puree sɛ ɛbɛde bo kɔso na ɛma ɛtena mu akyi. Kora wo adwuma sika ho nsɛm nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: What is a nursery and when should I use one?
candidates.answer_en: A nursery is a protected area where seeds are germinated and young plants are raised before transplanting to the main field. Use a nursery for: small expensive seeds like tomato, pepper, and onion; crops that need a head start before rains; and crops where seedling survival in the field is uncertain. Nurseries save seeds and improve stand establishment.
candidates.question_twi: Nursery yɛ dɛn na bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛde di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Nursery yɛ beae a wɔbɔ ho ban a wɔde aba gu mu na wɔtete nnua nketewa ansa na wɔde akɔdua wɔ afuo kɛse no mu. Fa nursery di dwuma ma: aba nketewa a ne boɔ yɛ den te sɛ ntomate, mako, ne gyeene; nnɔbae a ɛhia sɛ wofi ase ntɛm ansa na osuo aba; ne nnɔbae a ɛnyɛ awiegye sɛ ɛbɛtena ase wɔ afuo no mu. Nursery boa ma aba no yɛ yiye na ɛma nnua no nyini yiye.

candidates.question_en: Can I grow vegetables during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, you can grow vegetables in the dry season with irrigation. Crops like tomatoes, pepper, onions, leafy vegetables, and cucumbers grow well in dry season with proper watering.
candidates.question_twi: Metumi adua nnɔbae wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, wobetumi kura nnuan wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu sɛ wode nsuo gu so. Nnɔbae te sɛ ntomate, mako, gyeene, nhaban nnɔbae, ne cucumber nyini yiye wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu sɛ wode nsuo gu so yiye a.

candidates.question_en: How should I stake tomato plants?
candidates.answer_en: Staking tomatoes keeps the plant upright reducing soil contact and disease. Use bamboo stakes or wooden sticks about 1.5 metres tall. Insert the stake 15 cm into the soil beside the plant without damaging roots. Tie the plant loosely to the stake using soft twine in a figure-8 pattern at every 20 to 30 cm of growth. Begin staking when plants are 20 to 30 cm tall. Indeterminate varieties need continuous staking as they grow while determinate varieties need staking only once.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tomatoes stake pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Tomatoes stake ma nnuaba gyina straight na ɛhia asase ne yadeɛ nka ho. De bamboo stakes anaa dua bio a ɛtelɛ sɛ metres 1.5. De stake si sɛntimita 15 asase mu bɛn nnuaba no ho a nnɔho nsɔre. Kyekyere nnuaba no de twine mmerɛw wɔ stake no ho wɔ figure-8 nhyiamu wɔ bere biara a nnuaba rekɔ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 so. Fi ase de stake bere a nnuaba bɛyɛ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 tenten. Indeterminate varieties hia stake bere nyinaa a wɔreba mu na determinate varieties hia stake mprɛn baako pɛ.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent tomato late blight?
candidates.answer_en: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans is the most destructive tomato disease. Prevent it by using resistant varieties, avoiding overhead irrigation, ensuring good spacing for air circulation, removing and destroying infected plant material immediately, and applying copper-based fungicides like Ridomil or Champion preventively especially during wet humid weather.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ tomato late blight annya me nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Late blight a Phytophthora infestans ma ɛba ne tomatoes yadeɛ a ɛsɛe paa. Gye wo ho fi mu de varieties a wɔagyae so, gye wo ho fi nsuo wɔ atifi ho quench, hwɛ sɛ ahodɔ pa wɔ hɔ sɛ mframa fa mu, yi na sɛe plant material a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na de copper-based fungicides te sɛ Ridomil anaa Champion hware ansa bere a nsuo ne ahuhuruw wɔ.

candidates.question_en: My harvested tomatoes are spoiling quickly. What can I do?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid harvesting during wet conditions. Handle gently to prevent bruising. Store in cool shaded well-ventilated areas on raised surfaces. Remove and separate any rotting fruits immediately. Consider making tomato paste or drying to reduce losses. Transport in ventilated crates not plastic bags.
candidates.question_twi: M'ntomato a megye wɔn resɛe ntɛm. Dɛn na metumi yɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Bɔ hwɛ gye bere a nsuo wɔ hɔ. De wɔn pɛ sɛ wɔnhow. Guina wɔ bae a ɛhuru, owia ntra mu, mframa pue mu na ɛda sor. Yi na twa ntomato a resɛe ntɛm ara. Fa tomato paste yɛ anaa yaw sɛ mpampa sika kɔ mpoano.

candidates.question_en: When should I transplant tomato seedlings?
candidates.answer_en: Transplant tomato seedlings when they are 4-6 weeks old, have 4-6 true leaves, are 15-20 cm tall, and have a sturdy stem. Seedlings that are too young may not survive transplanting shock. Seedlings that are too old (over 8 weeks) become root-bound and may not establish well in the field.
candidates.question_twi: Mfeɛ bɛn na ɛfata sɛ mesi ntomato nnuaba mfoforo ananmu?
candidates.answer_twi: Si ntomato nnuaba mfoforo ananmu bere a wɔdin nnawotwe 4-6, wɔwɔ nhaban 4-6, wɔn soroɔ yɛ sɛntimita 15-20, na wɔwɔ tibo den. Nnuaba mfoforo a wɔkum dodo betumi ankyɛ si ananmu no ɔkɔm. Nnuaba mfoforo a wɔadin dodo (nnawotwe 8 kenkan) yɛ root-bound na betumi ansi yie wɔ afuo mu.

items.question_en: How can I compare two farming enterprises?
items.answer_en: Compare expected demand, capital required, production time, risks, labour needs, market price and expected return.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn atoto kuayɛ adwuma mmienu ho?
items.answer_twi: Toto nea gua no hia, capital, bere a ɛgye, ɔhaw, adwumayɛ, gua boɔ ne sika a wobɛtumi anya ho.

candidates.question_en: What questions should I ask before investing money in a new farm enterprise?
candidates.answer_en: Include the farm idea, target market, production plan, resources, expected costs, expected sales, risks and a simple implementation timeline.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛmmisa bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mibisa ansa na mede sika ahyɛ kuayɛ adwuma foforo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Susuw kuayɛ adwuma no, gua a wopɛ, production plan, nneɛma a wowɔ, sika a wobɛbɔ, sika a wɔhwɛ kwan sɛ wobɛtɔn no, ɔhaw ne bere nhyehyɛe ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I decide whether to expand my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Expand only when markets, working capital, management capacity, labour, land and production records show that the enterprise can support growth.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ metrɛw m'afuo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Trɛw no bere a gua, working capital, management, adwumayɛfo, asase ne production records kyerɛ sɛ adwuma no tumi gyina growth no so nkutoo.

candidates.question_en: How do I estimate farm production costs?
candidates.answer_en: List expected costs for land preparation, seed, inputs, labour, water, transport, equipment, packaging and other operating expenses.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛ farm production cost?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw sika a wobɛbɔ wɔ asase siesie, aba, inputs, adwumayɛfo, nsuo, transport, equipment, packaging ne operating expenses ho.

candidates.question_en: How can a farmer reduce business risk?
candidates.answer_en: Diversify sensibly, keep records, build an emergency reserve, maintain good production practices and avoid relying on one buyer or one crop alone.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate business risk so wɔ kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyekyɛ kuayɛ nneɛma sɛ ɛfata, kyerɛw records, yɛ emergency reserve, di kuayɛ akwan pa so na mfa wo ho nhyɛ adetɔfo anaa nnɔbae baako so nkutoo.

candidates.question_en: Why is cash flow important in farming?
candidates.answer_en: Farm expenses often happen before income arrives. A cash-flow plan helps ensure money is available when costs are due.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na cash flow ho hia wɔ kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kuayɛ sika pii no wɔbɔ no ansa na sika a ɛfiri tɔn mu aba. Cash-flow plan boa ma sika wɔ hɔ bere a wɔhia tua.

candidates.question_en: Why should I review a farm budget after the season?
candidates.answer_en: Comparing planned and actual figures helps you understand what went well, what went wrong and how to improve the next season.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ farm budget no bio bere a season no awie?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wototo nea wosusuw ho ne nea ɛbaa ankasa a, ɛma wuhu nea ɛyɛɛ yie, nea ɛkɔɔ bɔne ne nea wubetumi asesa season foforo.

candidates.question_en: Why should I calculate break-even before starting a farm enterprise?
candidates.answer_en: Break-even analysis helps you estimate how much you must sell before the enterprise begins to make a profit.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mebu break-even ansa na mahyɛ kuayɛ ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Break-even boa ma wohu dodow a ɛsɛ sɛ wotɔn ansa na kuayɛ adwuma no ahyɛ ase anya mfasoɔ.

candidates.question_en: Why should I separate household money from farm money?
candidates.answer_en: Separating the two makes it easier to measure whether the farm itself is profitable and reduces confusion in record keeping.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mekye fie sika ne afuo sika mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wokyekyɛ wɔn mu a, ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhu sɛ afuo no ankasa wɔ mfasoɔ anaa enni mfasoɔ na ɛtew basabasa wɔ records mu.

items.question_en: How much water do crops generally need?
items.answer_en: Most crops need about 25-50mm of water per week. Signs of water stress include wilting and dry soil. In the dry season, water deeply but less frequently to encourage deep rooting. Early morning watering reduces evaporation.
items.question_twi: Nsuo bɛn na m'nnuaba hia?
items.answer_twi: Nnuaba bebree hia nsuo sɛntimita 25-50 dapɛn biara mu. Nsuo hia ahohyenam ho ne nwonwon ne asase a ɛyera. Ɔpɛ bere mu, de nsuo to asase mu kɛse nanso mmere pii bi no de nsuo to ho sɛ nnua no na wɔde wɔn ntini kɔ ase yie. Owia da ano nsuo guare mma nsukyerɛ yɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow watermelon successfully?
candidates.answer_en: Watermelon needs well-drained sandy loam soil, warm temperatures, and plenty of sunlight. Space 1.5-2 m apart. Water deeply but infrequently. Apply potassium-rich fertilizer during fruiting. Harvest when the tendril near the fruit turns brown.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura watermelon yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Watermelon hia asintiɛ asase a nsuo pue mu yie, owia mu, na owia hye pa. Gyae asukyerɛ mita 1.5-2. De nsuo to asase mu yiye nanso mmere pii bi. De potassium ferefere to so bere a aba reba. Gye bere a ntini a ɛbɛn aba no dan ɛda.

candidates.question_en: How can I conserve water on my farm during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Conserve water by mulching heavily around plants to reduce evaporation, watering early morning or evening only, using drip irrigation which reduces water use by up to 60%, growing drought-tolerant crops, making windbreaks to reduce drying winds, and collecting and storing rainwater during wet season.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora nsuo wɔ m'afuo mu wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora nsuo wɔ de mulch to nnuaba ho papaapa sɛ nsukyerɛ ba sua, de nsuo to owia da ano anaa anwummere pɛ, fa nsuo tete-tete kyɛ a ɛsua nsuo kɔ 60%, kura nnuaba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase, si windbreaks sɛ mframa a ɛma asase yera nkɔ, na gye ne guina osu nsuo wɔ osu bere mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I tell when my crops are lacking nutrients?
candidates.answer_en: Common deficiency signs: Nitrogen deficiency — older leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom of the plant. Iron deficiency — young leaves turn yellow but veins stay green. Phosphorus deficiency — leaves turn purple or reddish. Potassium deficiency — leaf edges turn brown and crispy. Calcium deficiency — new leaves distort and curl. A soil test will confirm which nutrients are lacking.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehunu sɛ m'nnuaba hia aduan?
candidates.answer_twi: Aduan hia ahohyenam a wɔtaa hu: Nitrogen hia — nhaban kedee a wɔwɔ nnua ase hoho fi nnua ase. Iron hia — nhaban foforo hoho nanso nhwiren ho da tuntum-akyen. Phosphorus hia — nhaban dan purpura anaa kɔkɔɔ. Potassium hia — nhaban ho dan ɛda ne den. Calcium hia — nhaban foforo pae ne kyekye. Asase hwɛ bɛkyerɛ aduan a ehia.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm during drought?
candidates.answer_en: During drought, mulch heavily to conserve soil moisture, irrigate if possible, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and avoid adding nitrogen fertilizer which increases water demand. Harvest early-maturing varieties before drought peaks.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ m'afuo so bere a nsuo pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a nsuo pa no, de mulch to asase so yiye sɛ nsukuro wo mu, de nsuo to nnua so sɛ wonya tumi, paw nnuaba aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa so, na bɔ hwɛ de nitrogen ferefere to sɛ ɛma nnuaba hia nsuo dodo. Gye nnuaba a wɔware ntɛm ansa na nsuo pa yɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: What are nematodes and how do they affect crops?
candidates.answer_en: Nematodes are microscopic worms that live in soil. Some are harmful to crops — they attack roots causing galls (swellings), stunted growth, and yellowing. They are common in sandy soils and warm climates. Control by rotating crops, using resistant varieties, adding organic matter to soil, and solarizing soil (covering with clear plastic to heat it and kill nematodes during the dry season).
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na nematode yɛ na ɛyɛ m'nnuaba dɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Nematode yɛ nwirɛntwi a wɔte asase mu a wɔhunu da. Bi yɛ nnuaba ɔkɔm — wɔtwe ntini ho ma ɛyɛ kɛse, nnuaba nni sor yie, na nhaban hoho. Wɔtaa wɔ asintiɛ asase ne ahuhuro mu. Kora ase wɔ sesa nnuaba, fa aba a ɛtumi hyɛ ase, de nhwiren foforo ka asase ho, na solarize asase (fa plastik fitaa sɛɛ so sɛ ɛhye mu na kum nematode wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu).

candidates.question_en: How can I make neem pesticide at home?
candidates.answer_en: Crush 500g of neem seeds, soak in 10 litres of water overnight, strain through cloth, and add a little soap. Spray on crops in early morning or evening. Neem controls aphids, whiteflies, and caterpillars. Reapply after rain.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meyɛ neem adwummakers dawuro wɔ fie?
candidates.answer_twi: Tutu neem aba 500g, da wɔ nsuo litre 10 mu anadwo koro, hun wɔ ntama mu, na de sapo kakra ka ho. Guare nnuaba so owia da ano anaa anwummere. Neem kora aphid, fitaa abowa, ne aborɔnoma ase yie. De to so bio nsuo akyi.

candidates.question_en: How can I manage irrigation efficiently and reduce water waste?
candidates.answer_en: Manage irrigation efficiently by irrigating in the early morning or evening to reduce evaporation losses, using drip irrigation which delivers water directly to the root zone reducing waste by up to 50 percent compared to overhead sprinkler systems, mulching to retain soil moisture, monitoring soil moisture before irrigating rather than watering on a fixed schedule, levelling fields to ensure even water distribution, and fixing leaks in pipes and channels promptly.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mede quench pa yie sɛ me nsa nsuo?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ quench yie de quench wɔ anɔpa anaana anaa awia ansanaan sɛ ɛhia evaporation suas, de drip quench a ɛde nsuo kɔ nnɔho asase mu nsɛm sua nsa suas kɔ 50 percent tia overhead sprinkler systems tia, mulch sɛ asase nsuo agua, hwɛ asase nsuo ansa na woquench na gye wo ho fi quench schedule a ɛte so, siesie fields sɛ nsuo kɔ yie, na sa nsuo kwan mu holes ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow moringa and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Moringa is one of the most nutritious plants in the world and grows easily in Ghana. Plant seeds directly or use stem cuttings in well-drained soil. It tolerates drought and poor soils. Harvest leaves regularly to keep the tree short and productive. Moringa leaves can be eaten fresh, dried, and powdered. Benefits include: extremely high in iron, vitamins A and C, protein, and calcium. It is used medicinally and sold as a nutritional supplement at premium prices.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura moringa na mfaaso bɛn na ɛwɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Moringa yɛ nnua a ɛwɔ aduan ho nhwiren pa ara wɔ wiase mu na ɛda sor yie wɔ Ghana. To aba tɔtɔ anaa fa tibo cutting wɔ asase a nsuo pue mu yie. Ɛtumi nsuo pa ne asase a enni pa ase hyɛ. Gye nhaban pɛ sɛ ɛkora dua no tia ne adwuma mu. Moringa nhaban wobetumi di foforo, yaw na tutu. Mfaaso ho ne: iron, vitamins A ne C, protein, ne calcium ho yɛ dodo pa ara. Wɔde di dawuro adwuma na tɔn sɛ nutritional supplement wɔ boɔ kɛse.

items.question_en: What should I check before buying rice seed?
items.answer_en: Check the variety name, source, purity, germination information and packaging. Prefer seed from a reputable or certified source.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ ansa na matɔ aburow aba?
items.answer_twi: Hwɛ aba no din, baabi a ɛfiri, ne sɛnea ɛho tew, ne germination ho nsɛm ne package no. Prefer aba a ɛfiri baabi a wonim no anaa aba a wɔagye atom.

candidates.question_en: Why should harvested rice be kept clean?
candidates.answer_en: Clean grain reduces contamination, pest problems and losses during storage and helps maintain quality and market value.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ aburow a magye no tena ahotew mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Aduan a ɛho tew ma fi, mmoawa ne asɛe so te. Ɛboa ma aburow no kɔ so yɛ papa wɔ guina mu na ɛma ne boɔ so.

candidates.question_en: When should rice be dried after harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Begin drying as soon as practical after harvest. Dry the grain evenly to a safe moisture level suitable for storage or milling.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ meyow aburow akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi ase yow aburow no ntɛm ara sɛnea wubetumi bere a wogye no. Ma ɛyow pɛ na ɛso nsuo nyɛ dodo ansa na waguina anaa wɔayam.

candidates.question_en: How can I level a rice field before planting?
candidates.answer_en: Remove large clods, fill low spots and reduce high spots so water is distributed evenly. Good leveling helps save water and improves crop establishment.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie aburow afuo no ma asase no yɛ pɛ ansa na madu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase akɛse no, hyɛ mmeae a fam, na brɛ mmeae a ɛyɛ soronko sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a nsuo bɛkyɛ pɛ. Asase a ɛyɛ pɛ boa ma nsuo ntra beae baako na ɛboa aba ma ɛfifi yie.

candidates.question_en: How should I choose a rice field site?
candidates.answer_en: Choose a site with reliable water, suitable soil, good drainage control, and easy access. Avoid areas that cannot be drained when the crop is mature.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw beae a mɛdua aburow?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw beae a nsuo wɔ no yie, asase no fata, nsuo tumi firi mu, na kwan kɔ hɔ yɛ mmerɛ. Mfa beae a wontumi nnya nsuo mfi mu bere a nnɔbae no awie ase.

candidates.question_en: What is the difference between upland and lowland rice farming?
candidates.answer_en: Upland rice is grown without standing water, while lowland rice is grown where water can be managed in low-lying fields. The suitable system depends on rainfall, soil and water availability.
candidates.question_twi: Nsonsonoe bɛn na ɛwɔ upland ne lowland aburow kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Upland aburow nyin a nsuo nnyina asase so, na lowland aburow nyin wɔ beae a wobetumi ahwɛ nsuo so wɔ fam asase so. Nea ɛfata gyina osu, asase ne nsuo a ɛwɔ hɔ so.

candidates.question_en: Why is water management important in rice farming?
candidates.answer_en: Rice needs adequate moisture, but uncontrolled standing water can reduce plant health and make field operations difficult. Managing water at the right stages improves growth and efficiency.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na nsuo ho nhwɛsoɔ ho hia wɔ aburow kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Aburow hia nsuo a ɛfata, nanso nsuo a ɛgyina hɔ dodo betumi ama nnɔbae no ayɛ mmerɛ na ayɛ adwuma wɔ afuo mu ayɛ den. Nsuo a wɔhwɛ so wɔ bere a ɛfata ma nyin ne kuayɛ yɛ yie.

items.question_en: Why should different grades of produce be separated?
items.answer_en: Separating grades helps maintain quality, improves presentation and prevents damaged produce from reducing the value of good produce.
items.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛkyekyɛ nnɔbae no grades mu?
items.answer_twi: Ɛboa ma quality tena hɔ, ma presentation yɛ papa na ɛmma nnɔbae a asɛe no ntew pa no boɔ so.

candidates.question_en: Why should harvested vegetables not be left in direct sun?
candidates.answer_en: Direct heat can increase water loss and shorten shelf life. Move produce to shade and keep it cool after harvest.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛnsɛ sɛ mede nnɔbae a magye no gyaw owia tee mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Owia hyew ma nsuo firi nnɔbae mu ntɛm na ɛtew shelf life so. Fa wɔn kɔ sunsuma na ma wɔyɛ nwunu bere a wogye wɔn akyi.

candidates.question_en: Why is traceability useful on a farm?
candidates.answer_en: Simple records can help identify where produce came from, how it was produced and where it was sold if a quality problem occurs.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na traceability ho wɔ mfasoɔ wɔ afuo so?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛwtohɔ ketewa tumi boa ma wohu baabi a nnɔbae no firi, sɛnea wɔyɛe no ne baabi a wɔtɔn no sɛ quality haw bi ba a.

candidates.question_en: What should I do with damaged produce after harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Separate it from sound produce and decide whether it can be safely processed, fed to livestock where appropriate, composted or discarded.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ wɔ nnɔbae a apira akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi no fi nnɔbae pa no ho na hwɛ sɛ wobetumi ayɛ no processed food a ahobammɔ wɔ ho, ama mmoa adi sɛ ɛfata, ayɛ compost anaa ayi afi hɔ.

candidates.question_en: How should farm produce be packaged for market?
candidates.answer_en: Use clean, suitable packaging that protects the product from crushing, contamination and excess moisture.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apakɛ nnɔbae ama gua?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa packaging a ɛho tew na ɛfata a ɛbɔ nnɔbae ho ban fi mpirapira, fĩ ne nsuo dodo ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce bruising during produce transport?
candidates.answer_en: Use suitable containers, avoid excessive stacking and handle produce gently during loading and unloading.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpirapira so bere a merekɔfa nnɔbae?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa containers a ɛfata, mma wɔn nsi so dodo na fa ahwɛyiye di dwuma bere a woreload ne unload.

candidates.question_en: How can I tell if stored grain may have a mould problem?
candidates.answer_en: Look for visible mould, unusual smell, clumping, discolouration or increased moisture. Suspect grain should be isolated and assessed.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ mould wɔ aburow a meguina mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ mould a ɛda adi, hua a ɛnsɛ, grain a ɛbata bom, kɔla a ɛsakra anaa nsuo dodo. Grain a wohwɛ sɛ ɔhaw wɔ ho no yi fi foforo no ho na hwɛ no.

items.question_en: How can I prevent soil erosion on my farm?
items.answer_en: Plant cover crops or grass along slopes, practice contour farming, build terraces on steep land, and mulch bare soil. Avoid leaving soil uncovered during heavy rain seasons.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mema asase amma ɛnhuru wɔ m'afuo mu?
items.answer_twi: To nnuaba anaa atɛntɛnni wɔ kwantempon ho, yɛ contour farming, si terrace wɔ asase a ɛkwan so, na de mulch sɛɛ asase a ɛda. Bɔ hwɛ asase da ho akyɛ wɔ nsuo tenten bere mu.

candidates.question_en: How should I plant crops on slopes to prevent water erosion?
candidates.answer_en: On slopes, always plant across the slope (contour planting) rather than up and down. Make ridges along contour lines to hold water. Plant cover crops or grasses on the steepest parts. Use tied ridges (ridges with cross-ties every few meters) to capture rainwater. Mulch heavily to protect soil between plants.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn dua nnɔbae wɔ mmepɔw so na nsuo rentwa asase?
candidates.answer_twi: Wɔ kwantempon so, to aba twa kwantempon so daa (contour planting) na mmom kɔ sor na gu ase. Yɛ ntwaho wɔ contour lines no ho na ama nsuo akora. To cover crops anaa atɛntɛnni wɔ beae a ɛkwan pa ara. Fa tied ridges (ntwaho a wɔne kyɛ ɛtɔ so baako biara) sɛ ɛgye osu nsuo. De mulch to so papaapa sɛ ɛkora asase nnuaba ntam.

candidates.question_en: How can I conserve water on my farm during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Conserve water by mulching heavily around plants to reduce evaporation, watering early morning or evening only, using drip irrigation which reduces water use by up to 60%, growing drought-tolerant crops, making windbreaks to reduce drying winds, and collecting and storing rainwater during wet season.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora nsuo wɔ m'afuo mu wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora nsuo wɔ de mulch to nnuaba ho papaapa sɛ nsukyerɛ ba sua, de nsuo to owia da ano anaa anwummere pɛ, fa nsuo tete-tete kyɛ a ɛsua nsuo kɔ 60%, kura nnuaba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase, si windbreaks sɛ mframa a ɛma asase yera nkɔ, na gye ne guina osu nsuo wɔ osu bere mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm from flooding and waterlogging?
candidates.answer_en: Protect your farm from flooding and waterlogging by planting on raised beds or ridges especially for vegetables and root crops, digging drainage channels around the field perimeter to direct excess water away, avoiding farming in flood-prone low-lying areas during heavy rain seasons, choosing flood-tolerant varieties where possible, using cover crops and mulching to reduce runoff, and planting trees or grass strips along slopes to slow water flow and reduce erosion.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me afuom annya nsuo tia?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye wo afuom fi nsuo ho de to mu wɔ beds a ɛtele anaa ridges a ɛhia pii ma nnuaba ne nnɔho, boro drainage channels fa afuom no ho nyinaa sɛ ɛde nsuo a ɛboro so kɔ ho, gye wo ho fi okuafo adwuma wɔ hɔ a nsuo taa tia wɔ nsuo berɛ kɛse mu, yi flood-tolerant varieties wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ, de cover crops ne mulching sua runoff, na to nnuaba anaa nhawan strips wɔ mmepɔ ho sɛ ɛhia nsuo kwan na sua erosion.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm during drought?
candidates.answer_en: During drought, mulch heavily to conserve soil moisture, irrigate if possible, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and avoid adding nitrogen fertilizer which increases water demand. Harvest early-maturing varieties before drought peaks.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ m'afuo so bere a nsuo pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a nsuo pa no, de mulch to asase so yiye sɛ nsukuro wo mu, de nsuo to nnua so sɛ wonya tumi, paw nnuaba aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa so, na bɔ hwɛ de nitrogen ferefere to sɛ ɛma nnuaba hia nsuo dodo. Gye nnuaba a wɔware ntɛm ansa na nsuo pa yɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: How does mulching help my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Mulching covers soil with dry grass, straw, leaves, or plastic and conserves soil moisture reducing watering by 50%, regulates soil temperature, suppresses weed growth, and adds organic matter as it decomposes. Apply 5-10cm thick around plants.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mulching boa m'afuo?
candidates.answer_twi: Mulching sɛɛ asase wɔ atɛntɛnni kraen, tow, nhaban, anaa plastik na ɛkora nsukuro wɔ asase mu ma nsuo to sua 50%, siesie asase osu, kora nhaban foforo ase, na de nhwiren foforo ka ho bere a ɛadwo. De sɛntimita 5-10 to nnuaba ho.

candidates.question_en: What causes root rot and how can I prevent it?
candidates.answer_en: Root rot is caused by soil-borne fungi, mainly when soil stays waterlogged for too long. It causes roots to turn brown and mushy, plants to wilt even when soil is wet, and eventual plant death. Prevent by: improving soil drainage, avoiding overwatering, not planting in low-lying waterlogged areas, using raised beds, treating seeds with fungicide before planting, and rotating crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma ntini sɛe na ɛdeɛn na metumi kora ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Ntini sɛe fi asase fungus, titiriw bere a nsuo da asase mu tenten dodo. Ɛma ntini dan ɛda ne mmerɛ, nnuaba nwo bere a asase nte, na nnua wu. Kora ase wɔ: siesie asase nsuo pue anammɔn, bɔ hwɛ nsuo to dodo, mto nnuaba wɔ asase ase a nsuo hia mu, fa asase-sor afuo, de aba ka fungicide ho ansa na woto mu, na sesa nnuaba.

candidates.question_en: How can I prepare my farm for unpredictable weather?
candidates.answer_en: To prepare for unpredictable weather: grow more than one crop to spread risk, keep records of past planting dates and yields to understand your local patterns, store enough food and seed reserves, install or improve water harvesting systems, use drought and flood-tolerant varieties, maintain healthy soil with high organic matter which buffers both drought and flooding, and join farmer groups that share weather information.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesiesie m'afuo ama ɛwim tebea a ɛntumi nnim?
candidates.answer_twi: Siesie ama ɛwim tebea a ɛntumi nnim: kura nnuaba dodo sɛ mfomso antete, kora aba to bere ne nnuaba a wogye ho nsɛm sɛ wuhu wo beae tebea, guina aduan ne aba ahwɛso, si anaa siesie nsuo guina systɛm, fa aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ne nsuo tenten ase hyɛ, kora asase a enni aho yie ne nhwiren foforo dodo a ɛboa wɔ nsuo pa ne nsuo tenten bere, na ba okuafo kuo a wɔkyɛ ɛwim amanneɛ.

candidates.question_en: What is agroforestry and how can it benefit my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Agroforestry is growing trees alongside crops or livestock on the same land. Benefits include: trees provide shade that reduces water stress, tree roots hold soil and prevent erosion, fallen leaves add organic matter, some trees fix nitrogen improving soil fertility, trees provide fruit or timber as additional income, and trees help store carbon reducing climate change impact. Recommended trees include Moringa, Leucaena, and Acacia.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na agroforestry yɛ na ɛboa m'afuo sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Agroforestry yɛ kura nnua wɔ nnuaba anaa mmoa ho wɔ asase koro so. Mfaaso ho ne: nnua de ewim brɛ ma ɛma nsuo hia nkɔm, nnua ntini kora asase na ɛmma asase nhuru, nhaban a atu de nhwiren foforo ka ho, nnua bi fi nitrogen ma asase ho nhwiren da sor, nnua de aba anaa dua bi ka ho sɛ sika foforɔ, na nnua boa guina carbon na ɛsua katawere mu sɛsae ho ɔkɔm. Nnua a wɔka wɔn ho ne Moringa, Leucaena, ne Acacia.

items.question_en: What is minimum tillage and can I use it for maize?
items.answer_en: Minimum tillage means disturbing the soil as little as possible when preparing for planting. Instead of full ploughing, you make only planting holes or shallow furrows. Benefits include reduced soil erosion, preserved soil structure, lower fuel and labour costs, and better moisture retention. For maize minimum tillage works well especially when combined with mulching of crop residues. However it requires good weed management as weeds can be a bigger problem without full land preparation.
items.question_twi: Minimum tillage yɛ dɛn na ɛtumi yɛ adwuma wɔ aburoɔ afuom?
items.answer_twi: Minimum tillage kyerɛ sɛ wohaw asase ketewa ketewa bere a wosiesie sɛ wode aba to mu. Nti na wonfɛn asase pɛpɛɛpɛ, woyɛ awia pɛ anaa furrows ketewa pɛ. Mfaaso ne: asase erosion nsen, asase nhyiamu aguina, fuel ne adwuma sika sua, na nsuo aguina yie. Ma aburoɔ minimum tillage yɛ adwuma yie a ɛhia pii bere a wode nnuaba a ato fɛw mulch ka ho. Nanso ɛhia nhaban foforo hwɛ pa efisɛ nhaban foforo tumi yɛ den wɔ asase a wonhaw yie mu.

candidates.question_en: What is Integrated Pest Management for maize?
candidates.answer_en: Integrated pest management for maize combines multiple control methods to reduce pest damage while minimizing chemical use. It includes planting resistant varieties, using certified seeds, planting at the recommended time to escape peak pest pressure, regular scouting to detect pests early, using biological controls like natural enemies, applying chemical pesticides only when pest levels exceed economic thresholds, and crop rotation to break pest cycles. This approach reduces costs and environmental impact compared to calendar spraying.
candidates.question_twi: Integrated pest management yɛ dɛn ma aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Integrated pest management ma aburoɔ de nhyiamu ahorow ka bom sɛ ɛhia adwummaker nsɔre na ɛhia chemicals sua. Ɛka ho to resistant varieties mu, de certified seeds, to mu bere a wɔakyerɛw so sɛ adwummaker atia ktwa, hwɛ so bere biara ma wohunu adwummaker ntɛm, de biological controls te sɛ natural enemies, de chemical pesticides pɛ bere a adwummaker bore so kɛse sen economic thresholds, na sesa adekuo adwuma sɛ ɛbu adwummaker bere. Nhyiamu yi hia sika sua na ɛboa asase mu sen calendar spraying.

candidates.question_en: How can I make compost for my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Make compost by layering crop residues dry matter like maize stalks alternating with green matter like grass clippings and kitchen waste. Add a thin layer of soil or finished compost between layers to introduce decomposing organisms. Keep the pile moist but not waterlogged and turn it every 2 weeks. The compost is ready in 8 to 12 weeks when it is dark brown crumbly and earthy smelling. Apply 2 to 3 tonnes of compost per acre before planting to significantly improve soil fertility.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ compost ma me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ compost de layers a nnuaba a ato fɛw aba ntama a wɔatew te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ka ho ne nnuaba foforɔ te sɛ nhawan ne efie ho nneɛma. De asase ketewa anaa compost a ɛawie to ntam biara mu sɛ ɛde organisms a ɛhia kɔ. Ma pile no nsuo ho kakra nanso nsuo nni mu agyina na gyinaso mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas. Compost no atwa so nnansas nwɔtwe kɔ duonum mmienu mu bere a ɛyɛ dark brown, ɛpepee yie na ɛwɔ nhwirɛ pa. De compost tonnes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa to eka baako so ansa na wode aba to mu sɛ ɛboa asase aduan pii.

candidates.question_en: What is intercropping and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Intercropping means growing two or more crops together on the same land. For example, maize with cowpea. Benefits include better land use, the legume adds nitrogen to the soil, reduced pest pressure, and income from two crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛyɛ intercropping na ɛboa?
candidates.answer_twi: Intercropping kyerɛ sɛ wokura nnuaba abien anaa dodo wɔ asase koro so. Nhwɛso so, aburow ne abɔdweɛ. Mfaaso ho ne: asase ho dwuma pa, abɔdweɛ de nitrogen ma asase, adwummakers hia sua, na nnuaba abien firi sika.

candidates.question_en: What is aflatoxin in maize and how can I prevent it?
candidates.answer_en: Aflatoxin is a deadly poison produced by Aspergillus fungi that grows on improperly dried or stored maize. It causes liver cancer and can kill animals and humans. Prevent aflatoxin by drying maize properly to below 13 percent moisture before storage, using hermetic storage bags or metal silos, inspecting stored grain regularly and discarding mouldy grain, using aflasafe biocontrol product, and never feeding visibly mouldy grain to animals.
candidates.question_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ dɛn wɔ aburoɔ mu na dɛn na menyɛ sɛ ɛnnya?
candidates.answer_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ poisons a ɛyɛ den a Aspergillus fungi a ɛso wɔ aburoɔ a wonma no tew yie anaa a wonguina yie ho de ba. Ɛma akokoaa yareɛ na etumi kum mmoa ne nnipa. Gye aflatoxin fi ho de ma aburoɔ no tew yie kɔ 13 percent nsuo ase ansa na woguina, de hermetic storage bags anaa metal silos, hwɛ aba a woguina bere biara na yi aba a mold aba ho, de aflasafe biocontrol de, na mma aba a mold aba ho amma mmoa.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare the soil before planting maize?
candidates.answer_en: Clear the land of weeds and old crop residues. Plough or dig to a depth of 20 to 30 cm to loosen the soil. If possible, apply compost or manure and incorporate it into the soil two weeks before planting. Level the seedbed to ensure even germination. Avoid burning crop residues as this destroys beneficial soil organisms.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ asase no so ansa na meto aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo ne nnuaba a ato fɛw fi asase no so. Boro asase no kosi sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 mu sɛ asase no atete yie. Sɛ wobetumi a, de compost anaa aguare to mu na fa ka ho mprɛnsa mmienu ansa na wode aba to mu. Siesie seedbed no so yie sɛ aba nyinaa retua fɔw yie. Mma nnuaba fidie anhye efisɛ eyi sɛe asase mu adwummaker pa.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Weed at 2 to 3 weeks and again at 6 to 8 weeks after planting. These two weeding operations are critical because early weeds compete directly with young maize for nutrients and water. You can use hand weeding with a hoe or apply pre-emergence herbicides like atrazine before the maize germinates. Mulching between rows also suppresses weeds.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ nhaban foforo a wɔ me aburoɔ afuom mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo nnansa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa akyi na bio wɔ nnansa nsia kɔ nwɔtwe akyi a wode aba to mu. Adwuma nhaban foforo yi mmienu no ho hia pa ara efisɛ nhaban foforo a ɛdi kan no di aburoɔ foforo bere a ɛwɔ ho ferefere ne nsuo ho brε. Wobetumi de nsa ne atia yam yi nhaban foforo anaa de herbicides a wɔfre no atrazine to ho ansa na aburoɔ aba atua fɔw. Mulching nsɛm ntam mu nso boa nhaban foforo ho.

candidates.question_en: What is the Ghana Commodity Exchange and how can farmers use it?
candidates.answer_en: The Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) is a formal marketplace where farmers can sell their produce at transparent, standardized prices. To use it: register as a member through an accredited warehouse operator, store your certified grain in a GCX-accredited warehouse, receive a warehouse receipt that you can sell at the exchange or use as collateral for a bank loan. It is especially good for maize, soya, and sorghum.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Ghana Commodity Exchange yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) yɛ aguabasa a ɛwɔ ho yie a okuafo tumi tɔn wɔn nnuaba wɔ boɔ a wɔada adi ne a wɔasiesie. Sɛ wohwehwɛ fa di dwuma a, kyerɛw wo din wɔ accredited warehouse operator ho, guina wo nnuaba a wɔakyerɛw wɔ GCX-accredited warehouse mu, nya warehouse receipt a wobetumi tɔn wɔ exchange no mu anaa de kɔ ban ho sɛ collateral. Ɛyɛ adwuma yie pa ara ma aburow, soya, ne ɔtɛ.

candidates.question_en: What is contract farming and how can it help farmers in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Contract farming is an agreement between a farmer and a buyer where the buyer agrees to purchase your produce at a pre-agreed price before you plant. In Ghana, companies like Masara N'Arziki for maize, Biase Plantations for sugarcane, various cocoa buying companies and export vegetable companies offer contract farming arrangements. Benefits include guaranteed market, access to inputs on credit, technical support and stable income. The main risk is being locked into a price that may be lower than the open market if prices rise.
candidates.question_twi: Contract farming yɛ dɛn na ɛbɛtumi aboa me wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Contract farming ne nhyiam a ɛwɔ okuafo ne buyer ntam a buyer gyina so sɛ ɔbɛgye wo nnuaba bo a wɔako ka ansa na wode aba to mu. Wɔ Ghana, companies te sɛ Masara N'Arziki ma aburoɔ, Biase Plantations ma sugarcane, cocoa gye companies bebree ne export vegetable companies de contract farming nhyiam to. Mfaaso ne: dwa gyinae, access kɔ inputs wɔ credit so, technical mmoa ne owuo-teetee foforo so. Aho yɛ den kɛse ne sɛ wobɔ bo a ɛtumi yɛ sua sen open market sɛ bo kɔ so.

items.question_en: How should I grow pepper successfully?
items.answer_en: Pepper grows best in warm sunny conditions with well-drained fertile soil. Start seeds in a nursery then transplant 4-6 week old seedlings. Space 45-60 cm apart. Water regularly, stake tall plants, and apply balanced fertilizer.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura mako yie?
items.answer_twi: Mako da sor pa wɔ owia mu na asase a nsuo pue mu yie na ɛwɔ aduan pa. Fi aba fi nursery, afei si nnuaba a wɔdin nnawotwe 4-6 wɔ wɔ beae foforɔ. Gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 45-60. De nsuo to so pɛ, si aduro nnua a wɔreden, na de ferefere pɛ to so.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow bell pepper for high-value markets?
candidates.answer_en: Bell pepper for supermarkets and export requires strict production standards. Use certified hybrid seeds like California Wonder or Yolo Wonder. Start in a nursery and transplant at 60 by 45 cm spacing. Install drip irrigation for consistent moisture. Apply balanced NPK fertilizer and calcium nitrate regularly. Stake plants to prevent lodging. Harvest when fruits reach full size with firm flesh still before colour change for green bell pepper or after colour change for red or yellow. Pack in perforated clamshell containers. Target Accra supermarkets and export companies.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ bell pepper ma dwa a bo wɔ so wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Bell pepper ma supermarkets ne export hia production standards pa ara. De certified hybrid seeds te sɛ California Wonder anaa Yolo Wonder. Fi ase wɔ nursery na transplant wɔ ahodɔ 60 ne 45 sɛntimita. Si drip quench ma nsuo so yie. De balanced NPK ferefere ne calcium nitrate to ho bere biara. De stakes si nnuaba ho. Yi bere a nnuaba bɛbo kɛse pa na flesh yɛ den da ansa na ɛregyina so ma green bell pepper anaa yi akyi bere a bo gyina so ma red anaa yellow. Kura wɔ perforated clamshell containers mu. Tia Accra supermarkets ne export companies.

candidates.question_en: How should I raise pepper seedlings?
candidates.answer_en: Fill seed trays or nursery beds with a mixture of topsoil, compost and sand. Sow seeds 0.5 cm deep and water gently. Cover with transparent plastic or shade netting to retain moisture. Seeds germinate in 7 to 14 days. Water daily in the morning. Seedlings are ready to transplant when they have 4 to 6 true leaves which is about 4 to 6 weeks after sowing.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ pepper seedlings?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma asase a ɛwɔ atifi, compost ne hyerɛn ahohiana kɔ seed trays anaa nursery beds mu. Dware aba 0.5 sɛntimita tia na quench kakra. Kata de plastic transparent anaa shade netting sɛ nsuo agua mu. Aba tua fɔw adays 7 kɔ 14 mu. Quench daada anɔpa. Seedlings atwa so sɛ wɔbɛde transplant bere a wɔwɔ nhaban pa nnan kɔ nsia a ɛyɛ bɛyɛ nnansa nnan kɔ nsia akyi a wɔwui aba.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent pepper root rot?
candidates.answer_en: Pepper root rot caused by Phytophthora capsici causes plants to wilt suddenly and die. Prevent it by planting in well-drained raised beds, avoiding overwatering, using healthy transplants, not planting pepper in the same field two seasons in a row, applying Metalaxyl-based fungicides as a soil drench preventively, and removing affected plants immediately to stop spread.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ pepper root rot annya me nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Pepper root rot a Phytophthora capsici ma ɛba ma nnuaba huru ntɛm na wu. Gye wo ho fi mu de to mu wɔ beds a ɛtele ne nsuo tew, gye wo ho fi quench a ɛboro so, de transplants pa to mu, to mu pepper wɔ afuom koro mfe mmienu so kwa, de Metalaxyl-based fungicides si wɔ asase mu ansa, na yi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm sɛ ɛntete kɔ ho foforɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can I make a homemade chili pesticide spray?
candidates.answer_en: Blend 10-15 hot chili peppers with 1 litre of water. Strain through cloth, add a little liquid soap, and dilute with 5 more litres of water. Spray on affected plants in the morning or evening. The capsaicin in chili repels and kills soft-bodied insects like aphids and mites. Reapply every 3-4 days and after rain.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meyɛ fie nhwiren adwummakers dawuro fi mako?
candidates.answer_twi: Blend mako hye 10-15 ne nsuo litre 1 bom. Hun wɔ ntama mu, de liquid soap kakra ka ho, na fa nsuo litre 5 bio ka ho. Guare nnuaba a wɔayarɛ so owia da ano anaa anwummere. Capsaicin a ɛwɔ mako mu kora adwummakers a wɔn ho yɛ mmerɛ te sɛ aphid ne mite ase. To so bio nnafoa 3-4 biara na osu akyi.

candidates.question_en: How do I harvest pepper without damaging the plant?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest pepper using scissors or a sharp knife to cut the fruit with a small piece of stem — never pull the pepper off by hand as it damages the plant. Harvest when fruits are fully developed and have changed to their final color. Regular harvesting every 3-5 days encourages the plant to produce more fruits throughout the season.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye mako a ɛnsɛe nnua no?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye mako fa scissors anaa sekan tew twa aba no a tibo kakra ka ho — mfa wo nsa twe mako afi nnua no ho da efisɛ ɛsɛe nnua no. Gye bere a aba no awi yie na wɔadan wɔn rere. Gye pɛ mmere 3-5 biara ma nnua no sɛ ɛkɔ ma aba dodo wɔ bere mu nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How can I control vegetable pests using organic methods?
candidates.answer_en: Organic pest control methods for vegetables include: handpicking large insects and caterpillars, using physical barriers like row covers or netting, companion planting with pest-repelling plants, spraying with homemade neem oil, garlic, or chili solutions, attracting beneficial insects with flowering plants, using kaolin clay sprays to confuse insects, and maintaining healthy soil and plants as the best long-term defense.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi kora adwummakers ase nhwiren ho wɔ nnuan afuo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Nhwiren adwummakers kora anammɔn ma nnuan ne: twe adwummakers kɛse ne aborɔnoma wɔ nsa, fa akwantempon a wɔde nnuaba so te sɛ row covers anaa net, ka nnuaba a wɔkora adwummakers ase ho, guare fie neem dawuro, gyene, anaa mako a wɔayɛ, twe adwummakers pa wɔ abode nnuaba ho, fa kaolin clay guare sɛ ɛbue adwummakers no, na kora asase ne nnuaba aho yie sɛ anammɔn pa ara wɔ bere tenten mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I dry and preserve fresh pepper for longer storage?
candidates.answer_en: Dry fresh pepper by washing and removing stems then spreading on clean raised platforms in full sun for 7 to 10 days turning daily. The pepper is dry when it shrivels and rattles when shaken. Alternatively use a mechanical dryer at 60 to 65 degrees Celsius for 8 to 12 hours. Store dried pepper in sealed airtight containers away from moisture and sunlight. Dried pepper lasts 12 to 18 months. You can also grind dried pepper into powder or process into pepper sauce for added value.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ pepper tew na kata so sɛ ɛtena mu akyi?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma fofor pepper tew de hohoro na yi abɔ afei terɛ wɔ platforms a ɛtele na ɛpaa owia so adays 7 kɔ 10 a wogye mu adan bere biara. Pepper tew bere a ɛkɔ yɛ ketewa na ɛkeka bere a woyɛ no. Anaa de mechanical dryer wɔ degrees 60 kɔ 65 Celsius aanos 8 kɔ 12 mu. Guina pepper a ɛatew wɔ containers a wɔato mu paa fi nsuo ne owia ho. Pepper a ɛatew tena agyapade 12 kɔ 18 mu. Wobetumi nso de pepper a ɛatew fɛn yɛ powder anaa yɛ pepper sauce ma ɛbo kɔ so.

candidates.question_en: What pests commonly attack garden eggs and how can I control them?
candidates.answer_en: The main pest of garden eggs is the epilachna beetle which eats large holes in leaves reducing the plant's ability to produce fruit. Control by hand-picking beetles and larvae in the early morning, using neem leaf extract spray, applying spinosad insecticide in severe cases, and destroying heavily infested plants. Aphids and whiteflies also attack garden eggs and can be controlled with insecticidal soap spray. Fruit borers may require systemic insecticides.
candidates.question_twi: Adwummaker bɛn na ɛtaa tu mako ntorɔ na dɛn na menyɛ wɔn ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Adwummaker kɛse a ɛtuu mako ntorɔ ne epilachna beetle a ɛdi nhaban holes kɛse a ɛhia nnuaba tumi nnuaba boa mu. Boa ho de nsa yi beetles ne larvae anɔpa, de neem nhaban extract hware, de spinosad insecticide to ho bere a ɛyɛ yiye, na sɛe nnuaba a adwummaker tuu mako pii. Aphids ne whiteflies nso taa tu ntorɔ mako na wobetumi abo wɔn ho de insecticidal soap hware. Fruit borers bɛtumi ahia systemic insecticides.

items.question_en: How can I measure whether a new farming practice has improved my farm?
items.answer_en: Compare the new practice with your previous method using records such as yield, input cost, labour time, crop losses and income. Review the results over more than one season where possible.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ kuayɛ kwan foforo bi ama m'afuo ayɛ yie?
items.answer_twi: Fa records toto kwan foforo no ne nea wode dii kan ho wɔ yield, input cost, adwuma bere, nnɔbae asɛe ne sika mu. Sɛ ɛbɛtumi a, hwɛ season bɔ nnidisoɔ so bɛyɛ baako pɛ a.

candidates.question_en: How can I use last season's farm records to plan the next season?
candidates.answer_en: Update them as activities happen rather than waiting until the end of the season. Frequent records are more accurate and useful.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn de last season farm records asiesie season foforo?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw records no bere a adwuma no rekɔ so, na mma ntwɛn season no awie. Records a wɔkyerɛw daa yɛ nokware na wɔboa paa.

candidates.question_en: How can a farmer calculate yield per acre?
candidates.answer_en: Divide the total marketable harvest from the plot by the plot area measured in acres, using consistent units.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn abu yield wɔ acre baako so?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyɛ harvest a wotɔn no nyinaa wɔ plot no so mu acre dodow a plot no yɛ, na fa unit koro di dwuma bere nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: What farm records should a beginner start with?
candidates.answer_en: Start with crop area, planting date, seed used, major inputs, labour, harvest quantity, sales and major expenses.
candidates.question_twi: Farm records bɛn na beginner okuafoɔ ɛsɛ sɛ ofi ase de?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi crop area, da a wotɔɔ, aba a wode dii dwuma, inputs titiriw, adwumayɛfo, harvest dodow, tɔn ne sika a wode yɛ adwuma ase.

candidates.question_en: Why should I record planting dates?
candidates.answer_en: Planting dates help you track crop duration, compare seasons and plan future farm activities.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mekyerɛw planting dates?
candidates.answer_twi: Planting dates boa ma wohu nna a nnɔbae no de nyin, toto seasons ho na siesie farm adwuma a ɛbɛba no.

candidates.question_en: How can farmer groups help with information sharing?
candidates.answer_en: Groups can share market information, labour, equipment, experiences, training opportunities and links to extension services.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na farmer groups betumi aboa wɔ nsɛm kyɛmu mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kuo tumi kyɛ market nsɛm, adwumayɛfo, equipment, osuahu, training opportunities ne kwan a wɔbɛfa so anya extension services.

candidates.question_en: Why should I record crop failures?
candidates.answer_en: Recording failures helps identify repeated problems such as pests, poor timing, drought, disease or unsuitable varieties.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mekyerɛw nnɔbae a wɔsɛe?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛboa ma wohu ɔhaw a ɛsan ba bio te sɛ mmoawa, bere a woplant no, ɔpɛ, yare anaa variety a ɛnsɛ.

items.question_en: How can I control tomato leaf miners and reduce leaf damage?
items.answer_en: The tomato leaf miner is a tiny fly whose larvae tunnel inside leaves creating serpentine mines. This weakens plants and reduces yield. Control by removing heavily affected leaves and destroying them, using yellow sticky traps to catch adult flies, releasing the parasitic wasp Diglyphus isaea as biological control, and applying insecticides like Spinosad or Abamectin in severe cases.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tomato leaf miner ho?
items.answer_twi: Tomato leaf miner yɛ nsateaa ketewa a ne larvae tena nhaban mu kotoku yɛ nsɛm a ɛte sɛ nwanwa. Eyi ma nnuaba hunu na nnoa nansen. Boa ho de yi nhaban a yadeɛ aba ho pii na sɛe wɔn, de yellow sticky traps hwe adult flies, de parasitic wasp a wɔfre no Diglyphus isaea guu ma ɛhwɛ so, na de insecticides te sɛ Spinosad anaa Abamectin to ho bere a ɛyɛ yiye.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent tomato late blight?
candidates.answer_en: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans is the most destructive tomato disease. Prevent it by using resistant varieties, avoiding overhead irrigation, ensuring good spacing for air circulation, removing and destroying infected plant material immediately, and applying copper-based fungicides like Ridomil or Champion preventively especially during wet humid weather.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ tomato late blight annya me nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Late blight a Phytophthora infestans ma ɛba ne tomatoes yadeɛ a ɛsɛe paa. Gye wo ho fi mu de varieties a wɔagyae so, gye wo ho fi nsuo wɔ atifi ho quench, hwɛ sɛ ahodɔ pa wɔ hɔ sɛ mframa fa mu, yi na sɛe plant material a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na de copper-based fungicides te sɛ Ridomil anaa Champion hware ansa bere a nsuo ne ahuhuruw wɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can I make tomato farming profitable?
candidates.answer_en: To make profit from tomatoes, time your production to sell when prices are high which is usually the dry season from November to February. Use drip irrigation for dry season production. Produce in bulk to negotiate better prices, form a farmer group to collectively market your tomatoes, and consider simple processing like tomato paste or puree to add value and extend shelf life. Keep detailed records of all costs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ menyɛ sika wɔ tomatoes adwuma mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛfa sika wɔ tomatoes mu a, siesie wo to aba bere sɛ bɛtɔ bere a bo wɔ so wɔ yiye a ɛyɛ daadaa bone berɛ fi Ɔbenem kɔ Ɔpepon. De drip irrigation ma bone berɛ to aba. To pii sɛ wobɛtumi aho bo mu yie, fa okuafo kuo sɛ wɔde tomatoes bɛtɔ kaa bom, na twe wo adwene ho processing ketewa te sɛ tomato paste anaa puree sɛ ɛbɛde bo kɔso na ɛma ɛtena mu akyi. Kora wo adwuma sika ho nsɛm nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How should I stake tomato plants?
candidates.answer_en: Staking tomatoes keeps the plant upright reducing soil contact and disease. Use bamboo stakes or wooden sticks about 1.5 metres tall. Insert the stake 15 cm into the soil beside the plant without damaging roots. Tie the plant loosely to the stake using soft twine in a figure-8 pattern at every 20 to 30 cm of growth. Begin staking when plants are 20 to 30 cm tall. Indeterminate varieties need continuous staking as they grow while determinate varieties need staking only once.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tomatoes stake pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Tomatoes stake ma nnuaba gyina straight na ɛhia asase ne yadeɛ nka ho. De bamboo stakes anaa dua bio a ɛtelɛ sɛ metres 1.5. De stake si sɛntimita 15 asase mu bɛn nnuaba no ho a nnɔho nsɔre. Kyekyere nnuaba no de twine mmerɛw wɔ stake no ho wɔ figure-8 nhyiamu wɔ bere biara a nnuaba rekɔ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 so. Fi ase de stake bere a nnuaba bɛyɛ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 tenten. Indeterminate varieties hia stake bere nyinaa a wɔreba mu na determinate varieties hia stake mprɛn baako pɛ.

candidates.question_en: What is a nursery and when should I use one?
candidates.answer_en: A nursery is a protected area where seeds are germinated and young plants are raised before transplanting to the main field. Use a nursery for: small expensive seeds like tomato, pepper, and onion; crops that need a head start before rains; and crops where seedling survival in the field is uncertain. Nurseries save seeds and improve stand establishment.
candidates.question_twi: Nursery yɛ dɛn na bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛde di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Nursery yɛ beae a wɔbɔ ho ban a wɔde aba gu mu na wɔtete nnua nketewa ansa na wɔde akɔdua wɔ afuo kɛse no mu. Fa nursery di dwuma ma: aba nketewa a ne boɔ yɛ den te sɛ ntomate, mako, ne gyeene; nnɔbae a ɛhia sɛ wofi ase ntɛm ansa na osuo aba; ne nnɔbae a ɛnyɛ awiegye sɛ ɛbɛtena ase wɔ afuo no mu. Nursery boa ma aba no yɛ yiye na ɛma nnua no nyini yiye.

candidates.question_en: My tomato plants are wilting even though I water them. What could be wrong?
candidates.answer_en: Wilting despite watering could be bacterial wilt or fusarium wilt — soil-borne diseases. Cut the stem — if the inside is brown or oozes liquid, it is wilt disease. Remove infected plants and rotate crops for 2-3 years.
candidates.question_twi: M'ntomato nnua rewo na mede nsu hyɛ won. Dɛn na ɛhia?
candidates.answer_twi: Nwonwon a ɛba wɔ nsuo a wode hyɛ won akyi no betumi yɛ bacteria nwiinwii yadeɛ anaa fusarium yadeɛ wilt — yadeɛ a ɛfiri asase mu. Twa tibo no — sɛ mu yɛ ɛda anaa nsuo pue a, ɛyɛ wilt yadeɛ. Yi nnua a wɔayarɛ no fi afuo mu na sesa nnuaba mfe 2-3.

candidates.question_en: How should I store tomatoes without using a refrigerator?
candidates.answer_en: Store tomatoes at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Do not stack heavily. Keep them stem-side down. Tomatoes last 1-2 weeks this way. For longer preservation, dry, can, or make tomato paste. Never refrigerate unripe tomatoes.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meguina m'ntomato a menhyɛ wɔn fridge mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Guina ntomato wɔ fie mu osu a ɛyɛ pɛ sɛ owia ntra wɔn so tɔtɔ. Mfa wɔn si so dodo. De wɔn si wɔn tibo fam. Ntomato tumi tena nnawotwe 1-2 eyi ho. Sɛ wohwehwɛ tena bere tenten a, yaw, kanta, anaa yɛ ntomato paste.

candidates.question_en: What irrigation method is best for tomatoes in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Drip irrigation is the best method for tomatoes in Ghana. It delivers water directly to the root zone reducing disease incidence from leaf wetness, improving water use efficiency, allowing fertigation where fertilizer is applied through the drip system, and reducing weed growth. Furrow irrigation is also acceptable for flat land. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation for tomatoes as wet foliage encourages fungal diseases like late blight. Irrigate in the morning to allow foliage to dry before evening.
candidates.question_twi: Quench nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara ma tomatoes wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Drip quench ne nhyiamu pa ara ma tomatoes wɔ Ghana. Ɛde nsuo kɔ nnɔho asase mu nsɛm a ɛhia yadeɛ a ɛba efisɛ nhaban nsuo, ɛboa nsuo de pa, ɛma fertigation a wɔde ferefere fa wɔ drip system mu to, na ɛhia nhaban foforo. Furrow quench nso yɛ yie ma asase a ɛtee. Gye wo ho fi overhead sprinkler quench ma tomatoes efisɛ nhaban nsuo boa fungal yadeɛ te sɛ late blight. Quench anɔpa sɛ nhaban tew ansa na anwumere aba.

candidates.question_en: My harvested tomatoes are spoiling quickly. What can I do?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid harvesting during wet conditions. Handle gently to prevent bruising. Store in cool shaded well-ventilated areas on raised surfaces. Remove and separate any rotting fruits immediately. Consider making tomato paste or drying to reduce losses. Transport in ventilated crates not plastic bags.
candidates.question_twi: M'ntomato a megye wɔn resɛe ntɛm. Dɛn na metumi yɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Bɔ hwɛ gye bere a nsuo wɔ hɔ. De wɔn pɛ sɛ wɔnhow. Guina wɔ bae a ɛhuru, owia ntra mu, mframa pue mu na ɛda sor. Yi na twa ntomato a resɛe ntɛm ara. Fa tomato paste yɛ anaa yaw sɛ mpampa sika kɔ mpoano.

items.question_en: How should mushroom growing materials be prepared?
items.answer_en: Use a suitable substrate and prepare or treat it according to the production method so that competing organisms are reduced.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie nneɛma a mede bɛyɛ mushroom?
items.answer_twi: Fa substrate a ɛfata na siesie anaa yɛ ho adwuma sɛ production method no kyerɛ sɛnea nneɛma afoforo no bɛso atwa.

candidates.question_en: How should harvested mushrooms be handled?
candidates.answer_en: Handle them gently, keep them clean and cool, and move them to market or appropriate storage quickly.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ mushrooms akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa ahwɛyiye, ma ɛho tew na ɛyɛ nwunu, na de no kɔ gua anaa guina a ɛfata ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: What records should a mushroom farmer keep?
candidates.answer_en: Record substrate quantities, production dates, contamination, harvest weight, sales, losses and operating costs.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛm bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mushroom okuafoɔ kyerɛw?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw substrate dodow, da a wofii ase, contamination, aba no duru, tɔn, asɛe ne sika a wode yɛ adwuma.

candidates.question_en: Why is hygiene important in mushroom production?
candidates.answer_en: Clean equipment and growing areas reduce contamination by unwanted organisms that can compete with the mushrooms.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ahotew ho hia wɔ mushroom kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Adwinnade ne beae a wɔyɛ no ho tew ma nneɛma foforo a ɛho nhia no ntumi nko mushrooms no na ɛtew contamination so.

candidates.question_en: How do I know mushroom substrate is contaminated?
candidates.answer_en: Unusual colours, foul smells or rapid growth of unwanted mould can indicate contamination.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ mushroom substrate no ayɛ contamination?
candidates.answer_twi: Kɔla a ɛnsɛ, hua bɔne anaa mould a ɛnyin ntɛm betumi akyerɛ sɛ contamination aba.

candidates.question_en: What basic conditions do mushrooms need to grow?
candidates.answer_en: Mushrooms need a suitable growing substrate, moisture, appropriate temperature, cleanliness and adequate ventilation for the chosen species.
candidates.question_twi: Tebea bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mushrooms nya na wɔnyin?
candidates.answer_twi: Mushroom hia growing material a ɛfata, nsuo, ɔhyew a ɛfata, ahotew ne mframa a ɛkɔ mu sɛnea species no hia.

items.question_en: How can young people make farming profitable?
items.answer_en: Young people can make farming profitable by: treating farming as a business not a subsistence activity, specializing in high-value crops or livestock products, using technology and innovation, accessing youth-specific agricultural finance programs, connecting to urban markets through digital platforms, forming youth cooperatives for scale and bargaining power, adding value through processing, and combining farming with agribusiness services like input supply or transportation.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mmofra tumi ma okuafo adwuma brɛ sika?
items.answer_twi: Mmofra tumi ma okuafo adwuma brɛ sika wɔ: hwɛ okuafo adwuma sɛ adwuma na mfa sɛ fie aduan adwuma, paw nnuaba anaa mmoa nnuaba ho adwuma a wɔtɔ boɔ kɛse, fa technology ne nnorimde di dwuma, nya mmofra ho okuafo adwuma ka adwuma, ka kɔ akura aguabasa wɔ digital platforms ho, si mmofra cooperative sɛ fa ɔman ne tumi kɛse, de boɔ ka ho wɔ yɛ adwuma mu, na ka okuafo adwuma ho nnwuma te sɛ adenneɛ tɔn anaa kwan so nnwuma.

candidates.question_en: How do I register my farm as a business in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: To register your farm as a business in Ghana: register with the Registrar General's Department as a sole proprietorship or partnership (costs GHS 150-300), get a Tax Identification Number (TIN) from the Ghana Revenue Authority, register with MOFA for agricultural activities, open a business bank account, and get all required operating permits from your local assembly. A formally registered farm business is more credible to banks, buyers, and government programs.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mede m'afuo kyerɛw sɛ adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ kyerɛw wo afuo sɛ adwuma wɔ Ghana a: kyerɛw wɔ Registrar General's Department sɛ sole proprietorship anaa partnership (sika GHS 150-300), nya Tax Identification Number (TIN) fi Ghana Revenue Authority hɔ, kyerɛw wɔ MOFA ho ma okuafo adwuma, bue adwuma ban account, na nya kratafa biara a wohia fi wo local assembly. Afuo adwuma a wɔakyerɛw no yɛ pa ara wɔ ban, adeɛtɔfo, ne ɔman adwuma ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I find buyers for my farm produce before harvest?
