candidates.answer_en: Visit local markets to identify traders. Contact food processing companies and restaurants. Use phone or WhatsApp groups for farmers in your area. Signing contract farming agreements with companies before the season guarantees buyers and sometimes provides inputs on credit.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwehwɛ adeɛtɔfo ma m'afuo nnuaba ansa na megye wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Kɔ aguabasa a ɛbɛn wo sɛ wuhu nnipa a wɔtɔn. Ka kyerɛ aduan yɛ adeɛ kuo ne adidibea. Fa fɔn anaa WhatsApp kuo ma okuafo wɔ wo beae. De contract farming agreement ka adeɛtɔ kuo bere a bere mfiase ansa na ɛma adeɛtɔfo yɛ dada.

candidates.question_en: Which farming apps can help farmers in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Useful apps for Ghanaian farmers include: Esoko for market prices, Farmerline for agricultural advice and services, Hello Tractor for renting tractors, AgroFresh for produce quality management, Google Translate for translating agricultural content, YouTube for farming tutorials, Ghana Met Agency app for weather forecasts, and WhatsApp for connecting with other farmers and extension officers. Most are free or low-cost.
candidates.question_twi: Farming apps bɛn na ɛboa okuafo wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apps a ɛboa okuafo Ghana mu ne: Esoko ma aguabasa boɔ, Farmerline ma okuafo adwuma boa ne nnwuma, Hello Tractor ma tractor asɛ, AgroFresh ma nnuaba ho pa hwɛ, Google Translate ma okuafo nsɛm dan, YouTube ma okuafo adwuma nhyehyɛe, Ghana Met Agency app ma ɛwim amanneɛ, ne WhatsApp ma kasa ne okuafo ne extension officers foforɔ. Wɔn bebree yɛ daa anaa boɔ yɛ ketewa.

candidates.question_en: How can I get certified to sell organic farm produce?
candidates.answer_en: To sell as certified organic you need to farm organically for at least 3 years and pass inspection by an accredited certification body. In Ghana organizations like ENCOT and Control Union offer organic certification.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menya kratafa sɛ metɔn organic nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ tɔn organic nnuaba a wɔakyerɛw wɔn a, ɛsɛ sɛ woyɛ organic okuafo adwuma mfe 3 pɛ na wufa inspection a organic kuo yɛ. Wɔ Ghana, kuo te sɛ ENCOT ne Control Union de organic kratafa brɛ.

candidates.question_en: What is a market information system and how does it help farmers?
candidates.answer_en: A market information system provides farmers with current prices of crops at different markets so they can decide where and when to sell for the best price. In Ghana, services like Esoko, the Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX), and MOFA market information services provide this. Access via phone, radio, or internet. This prevents farmers from being cheated by middlemen who know prices but farmers don't.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na aguabasa nsɛm system yɛ na ɛboa okuafo sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Aguabasa Nsɛm system de nnuaba boɔ a ɛwɔ aguabasa ahodoɔ so ma okuafo sɛ wɔtumi paw beae ne bere a wɔbɛtɔn sɛ wanya boɔ pa. Wɔ Ghana, nnwuma te sɛ Esoko, Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX), ne MOFA aguabasa nsɛm nnwuma de eyi brɛ. Nya ase wɔ fɔn, redio, anaa internet so. Eyi mma okuafo anko ase wɔ middlemen a wɔnim boɔ nanso okuafo nnim ntam.

candidates.question_en: What training opportunities are available for farmers in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Training opportunities for farmers in Ghana include the Farmer Field Schools organized by MOFA where farmers learn by doing in their own fields, training by agricultural NGOs like SEND Ghana, Opportunity International and SNV, agricultural colleges and vocational institutions, online courses through platforms like Coursera and the FAO e-learning academy, cooperative training programmes, and the government-sponsored Youth in Agriculture Training Programmes. Many input suppliers also offer free agronomic training when you buy their products.
candidates.question_twi: Training nhyiamu bɛn na ɛwɔ ma okuafo wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Training nhyiamu ma okuafo wɔ Ghana ne Farmer Field Schools a MOFA de sɛ okuafo sua wɔ wɔn ankasa afuom mu, training de agricultural NGOs te sɛ SEND Ghana, Opportunity International ne SNV, agricultural colleges ne vocational institutions, online courses wɔ platforms te sɛ Coursera ne FAO e-learning academy, cooperative training programmes, na aban-sponsored Youth in Agriculture Training Programmes. Input suppliers bi nso de free agronomic training to bere a wogye wɔn nneɛma.

candidates.question_en: Should I join a farmers' cooperative?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, cooperatives offer many benefits including group purchasing of inputs at lower prices, collective selling for better prices, access to credit, shared equipment, training, and stronger negotiating power with buyers and government.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ meba okuafo kuo mu anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, cooperative de mfaaso bebree brɛ: kuo to adenneɛ ketewa mu, kuo tɔn sɛ wanya boɔ pa, nya ka, fa egyapade bom, nyansapɔ, na kuo tumi yɛ kɛse sen wɔ adeɛtɔfo ne ɔman ho nsɛm mu.

candidates.question_en: Where can I sell my farm produce for a better price?
candidates.answer_en: Sell directly at local markets, to aggregators or food processing companies, or form a cooperative with other farmers. Register with government programs like PFJ which helps connect farmers to buyers.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛhe na metumi de m'afuo nnuaba tɔn na nya boɔ pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Tɔn tɔtɔ wɔ aguabasa a ɛbɛn wo, anaa wɔ aduan yɛ adeɛ kuo, anaa si cooperative ne okuafo foforɔ. Kyerɛw wo din wɔ ɔman adwuma te sɛ PFJ a ɛboa okuafo ayɔnkofa ne adeɛtɔfo.

items.question_en: How can I access land for farming if I do not own land?
items.answer_en: Options for accessing land include: renting from landowners (common in Ghana, negotiate fair terms), sharecropping where you farm and share produce with the landowner, borrowing land from family or community leaders, government allocation programs for young farmers, and cooperative land pooling. Always get written agreements when renting or sharecropping to protect your investment. Contact the Lands Commission or MOFA for guidance on formal land access.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menya asase ma okuafo adwuma sɛ menni?
items.answer_twi: Asase nya anammɔn ho ne: asɛ fi asase wura (taa yɛ wɔ Ghana, siesie nhyɛso yie), sharecropping a woyɛ okuafo adwuma na fa nnuaba bi brɛ asase wura no, de asase fi abusua anaa oman hene ho, ɔman asase brɛ adwuma ma mmofra okuafo, ne cooperative asase ka bom. Kora nhyɛso krataa bere a wasɛ anaa sharecrop sɛ ɛkora wo sika. Ka kyerɛ Lands Commission anaa MOFA sɛ wunya mmoa wɔ asase nya anammɔn mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I get land for farming in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Access farming land in Ghana through several ways including purchasing outright if you have capital, sharecropping where you farm another person's land and share the harvest usually 50 50, leasing land through a written agreement typically 5 to 20 years in peri-urban areas, accessing communal lands through the chief or family head in rural areas, and government land allocations for special farming zones. Always secure a written land use agreement even for sharecropping arrangements to protect your investment.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ menya asase ma okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Nya asase ma okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana de akwan ahorow a ɛka ho de gye to sɛ wo wɔ sika, sharecropping a woto obi asase so na fa nnoa twa mmienu pɛ taa yɛ 50 50, lease asase de nhyiam krataa taa bɛyɛ mfe 5 kɔ 20 wɔ dɔn ho, nya communal asase wɔ ohene anaa abusua panyin nkyɛn wɔ kurow ho, na aban asase kyɛ ma okuafo adwuma zones a wɔayɛ. Hwɛ sɛ wotwerɛ asase de nhyiam krataa bere biara naaso sharecropping nhyiamu ma wo sɛ ɛhwɛ wo sika so.

candidates.question_en: What government agricultural support can I access in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Register with your local MOFA office and stay in contact with your extension officer. Subsidies like subsidized fertilizer and seeds under PFJ are distributed through MOFA-registered channels. Have your Ghana Card or voter ID ready and register early as subsidies are often limited.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menya ɔman okuafo adwuma boa?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw wo din wɔ wo MOFA ofisi a ɛbɛn wo na tena wo extension officer ho. Boa te sɛ ferefere ne aba a wɔatwa boɔ wɔ PFJ ase no pue wɔ MOFA mu. Wura wo Ghana Card anaa ɔman nkyerɛwsɛm na kyerɛw wo din ntɛm efisɛ boa no taa yɛ ketewa.

candidates.question_en: What are the signs of good farming soil?
candidates.answer_en: Good farming soil is dark, crumbly, and has a pleasant earthy smell. Push your finger 5cm into the soil — if it holds shape but breaks apart easily, it is good. You can also send a sample to an agricultural office for a proper soil test.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na ɛkyerɛ sɛ m'asase yɛ yɛ papa ma okuafo adwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Asase pa wɔ okuafo adwuma mu yɛ ɛda, na ɛpepee yie, na ɛwɔ asase hua. Fa wo nsateaa wura asase no mu sɛntimita 5 — sɛ ɛkura ne ho nanso ɛpae yie a, ɛyɛ asase pa. Wobetumi de asase bi kɔ okuafo ofisi sɛ wɔhwɛ so yie.

candidates.question_en: What documents do I need to qualify for an agricultural loan?
candidates.answer_en: To qualify for agricultural loans, banks and microfinance institutions typically require: farm records showing area farmed and crops grown, sales records for at least one season, input purchase receipts, a farm business plan, MOFA registration certificate, land ownership or lease documents, a valid ID, and sometimes a guarantor. Start keeping records now even if you are not currently seeking a loan — it takes time to build a credible financial history that banks trust.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛm bɛn na ɛsɛ mekora sɛ menya okuafo adwuma ka?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ nya okuafo adwuma ka a, ban ne microfinance institutions taa hia: afuo nsɛm a ɛkyerɛ asase asukyerɛ ne nnuaba a wokura, tɔn nsɛm ma bere baako pɛ pɛ, adenneɛ tɔn krataa, afuo adwuma dwumadie plan, MOFA kyerɛwsɛm kratafa, asase wura anaa asɛ krataa, ID a ɛtia, na mmere bi obi a ɔbɛka ho. Fi kora nsɛm saa ara bere a wonhwehwɛ ka da — ɛhia bere sɛ si sika ho nsɛm a wɔgye di a ban tumi gye di.

candidates.question_en: What role do women play in agriculture in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Women play a critical role in Ghanaian agriculture — they make up about 52% of the agricultural workforce. Women are primarily responsible for food crop production, post-harvest processing, and marketing. They often face challenges accessing land, credit, and inputs. Programs that specifically support women farmers include Women in Agricultural Development (WIAD) under MOFA, and many NGOs focusing on women's empowerment in agriculture.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mmaa gyina wɔ okuafo adwuma mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Mmaa gyina titiriw pa ara wɔ Ghana okuafo adwuma mu — wɔyɛ bɛn 52% wɔ okuafo adwumafo mu. Mmaa hia aduan nnuaba kura, gye akyi yɛ adwuma, ne tɔn. Wɔtaa hia asase, ka, ne adenneɛ ho nsɛm. Adwuma a ɛhwɛ mmaa okuafo ho pɛ ne Women in Agricultural Development (WIAD) wɔ MOFA ase, ne NGOs bebree a wɔhwɛ mmaa ho wɔ okuafo adwuma mu.

candidates.question_en: What are the major risks in farming and how can I manage them?
candidates.answer_en: Main farming risks include weather risks from drought or flooding, pest and disease outbreaks, price volatility at harvest time, input price increases, land tenure insecurity, and lack of market access. Manage these risks by diversifying crops so one failure does not ruin you entirely, using drought-resistant varieties, taking out crop insurance where available, joining farmer groups for collective bargaining, storing produce to sell when prices improve, securing formal land documents, and building relationships with multiple buyers.
candidates.question_twi: Aho yɛ den bɛn na ɛwɔ okuafo adwuma mu na dɛn na menyɛ wɔn ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Aho yɛ den kɛse a ɛwɔ okuafo adwuma mu ne: berɛ ho aho yɛ den fi bone anaa nsuo, adwummaker ne yadeɛ ba ntɛm, dwa bo sesa bere a wuyiyɛ, inputs bo kɔ so, asase ho gyinae ankyɛ, na dwa kɔ ho hia. Boa ho de nnuaba ahorow to sɛ baako a atua ho nhia wo a ennye wo ho nyinaa, de drought-resistant varieties to mu, gye crop insurance wɔ hɔ a ɛwɔ, ka okuafo kuo ho ma wobɔ bo kaa bom, guina nnuaba sɛ wotɔ bere a bo yɛ yie, hwɛ sɛ asase ho krataa pa wɔ wo nkyɛn, na kora wo adwene ho buyers kuo mmerantee ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow soybean commercially for profit?
candidates.answer_en: Soybeans are highly profitable legumes. Plant after rains are well established. Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium bacteria before planting (this fixes nitrogen and can triple yields). Space 30-45 cm within rows and 60 cm between rows. Apply phosphorus fertilizer at planting. Weed once at 3 weeks. Harvest when 95% of pods have turned yellow-brown. Dry to 12% moisture before storage. Soybeans have strong demand from oil processors and animal feed manufacturers.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura soya yɛ adwuma sɛ menya sika?
candidates.answer_twi: Soya yɛ abɔdweɛ a ɛde sika ba pa ara. To akyi a osu asi yie. De Bradyrhizobium bacteria ka aba ho ansa na woto (eyi fi nitrogen na ɛtumi ma nnuaba da sor mprɛ mmiɛnsa). Gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 30-45 wɔ ntam ne sɛntimita 60 wɔ nnua so ntam. De phosphorus ferefere to mu bere a wode to. Tia nhaban foforo bere a ɛto so mmiɛnsa no nnawotwe baako. Gye bere a 95% fidie no adan hoho bɔɔ. Yaw kosi 12% nsuku ansa na waguina. Soya hia yɛ kɛse wɔ ngo adwuma kuo ne mmoa aduan adwuma kuo ho.

candidates.question_en: What is a soil testing kit and how do I use it?
candidates.answer_en: A soil testing kit is a set of chemicals and test strips or color charts that let you test your soil's pH, nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels at home. To use: collect soil from several spots in your field and mix together, take a small sample, follow the kit instructions to mix with testing chemicals, compare the color change to the chart provided, and use results to decide what fertilizer to apply. Kits are available at agricultural supply stores.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na asase hwɛ kit yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Asase hwɛ kit yɛ chemicals ne test strips anaa color charts a ɛma wo tumi hwɛ wo asase pH, nitrogen, phosphorus, ne potassium wɔ fie. Di dwuma eyi: gye asase fi beae ahodoɔ wɔ afuo mu na ka bom, fa sample ketewa, bu kit nhyɛso so sɛ de chemicals ka ho, twe rere sɛsae na ka ho ne chart a wɔde brɛ, na fa adwuma ho sɛ paw ferefere a wohia. Kits wɔ hɔ wɔ agricultural supply adeɛtɔ hɔ.

items.question_en: How can I reduce stress when introducing new chickens?
items.answer_en: Provide suitable housing, clean water, feed and a calm environment, and avoid overcrowding during the adjustment period.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate stress so bere a mede nkokoɔ foforo ba?
items.answer_twi: Ma housing a ɛfata, nsuo ne feed pa, ma beae no yɛ dwo na mma wɔn nkɔyɛ overcrowding bere a wɔresiesie wɔn ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I manage heat stress in chickens?
candidates.answer_en: Heat stress is common in Ghana and reduces growth rate and egg production. Manage it by ensuring good ventilation in the poultry house, providing cool fresh water frequently, installing foggers or sprinklers on the roof, feeding in the cooler parts of the day morning and evening, reducing stocking density during hot seasons, adding vitamin C and electrolytes to water during extreme heat, and considering open-sided housing designs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ berɛhyɛ den a ɛba me akoko ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Berɛhyɛ den taa ba wɔ Ghana na ɛhia boɛ a aba nhia na tamma nhia. Boa ho de hwɛ sɛ mframa fa akoko fie mu yie, de nsuo dɛ foforɔ to mu bere biara, si foggers anaa sprinklers wɔ fie no atifi so, didi wɔ berɛ dɛ mu anɔpa ne anwumere, sua akoko a wɔwɔ mu wɔ berɛhyɛ bere, de vitamin C ne electrolytes ka nsuo mu wɔ hyehyɛ den bere, na twe wo adwene ho open-sided housing nhyiamu.

candidates.question_en: How can I choose a reliable poultry feed supplier?
candidates.answer_en: Choose a reputable supplier, check feed labels and dates, and store feed correctly after purchase.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw poultry feed supplier a mewɔ ahotoso wɔ no?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw supplier a ne din ye, hwɛ feed label ne dates na guina feed no yie bere a woatɔ no.

candidates.question_en: What causes broiler chickens to die suddenly?
candidates.answer_en: Sudden death syndrome in broilers is common and caused by metabolic disorders due to fast growth rates. Other causes include Gumboro disease which destroys the immune system, Newcastle disease, infectious bronchitis, ammonia poisoning from dirty litter, water deprivation, heat stress and cardiac arrest. Maintain good ventilation, provide clean water always, vaccinate regularly, manage litter properly and avoid pushing birds to extreme growth rates through excessive feeding.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn ma broiler akoko wu ntɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Broilers wu ntɛm yɛ adwuma a ɛtaa yɛ na ɛba fi metabolic disorders a ɛba efisɛ wɔbo sɔ ntɛm. Aho akyirikyiri ne Gumboro yadeɛ a ɛsɛe immune system, Newcastle yadeɛ, infectious bronchitis, ammonia poisons fi litter fi, nsuo ahia, berɛhyɛ den ne akoko akyikyide. Hwɛ mframa yie, de nsuo pa to mu bere nyinaa, hware so bere biara, hwɛ litter yie na mma nnomaa nbo sɔ akyi sen wɔ aduan a ɛboro so de.

candidates.question_en: How can I start a small poultry farm at home?
candidates.answer_en: To start a small home poultry farm: decide on type (layers for eggs or broilers for meat), build or buy a simple wooden or wire coop with shade and good ventilation, start with 10-20 birds, provide clean water and commercial feed, vaccinate birds at the recommended ages, keep the coop clean, and record feeds, deaths, and egg production. Start small and scale as you learn.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesi akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ si akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie: paw ahodoɔ (layers ma kosua anaa broilers ma nam), si anaa tɔ dua anaa wire fie a ewim brɛ ne mframa pue mu yie, fi akrɔma 10-20, de nsuo horo ne aduan a wɔtɔ ma wɔn, de akrɔma kɔ yadeɛ dawuro bere a ɛsɛ, kora fie no horo, na kora aduan, wuu, ne kosua ho nsɛm. Fi ketewa na fa dodo so bere a wosua.

candidates.question_en: How can I tell if chickens are eating normally?
candidates.answer_en: Monitor feed consumption, activity, droppings, body condition and changes in behaviour rather than relying on one sign.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ akokɔ redi aduane sɛnea ɛsɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ feed consumption, activity, wɔn dɔte, nipadua tebea ne suban nsakrae, na mfa nsɛnkyerɛnne baako so nko ara nnyina.

candidates.question_en: What feed should I give broiler chickens?
candidates.answer_en: Feed broilers starter crumbles for the first 2 weeks with 22 to 24 percent protein, then grower pellets with 18 to 20 percent protein from week 3 to 5, and finisher pellets with 16 to 18 percent protein in the final weeks. Provide fresh clean water at all times. Popular feed brands in Ghana include Darko Farms, Akate Wura and Ghana Feedmill feeds. Feed represents 70 percent of your production cost so buying quality feed is critical.
candidates.question_twi: Aduan bɛn na mede ma me broiler akoko?
candidates.answer_twi: De starter crumbles a protein 22 kɔ 24 percent wɔ mu ma broilers nnansas mmienu a ɛdi kan, afei grower pellets a protein 18 kɔ 20 percent wɔ mu wɔ nnansa mmiɛnsa kɔ num, na finisher pellets a protein 16 kɔ 18 percent wɔ mu wɔ nnansas a etwa to. De nsuo fofor pa to mu bere nyinaa. Feed brands a wɔpɛ wɔ Ghana ne Darko Farms, Akate Wura na Ghana Feedmill feeds. Aduan yɛ wo adwuma agyapade 70 percent enti gye aduan pa hia.

candidates.question_en: How can I increase egg production in layers?
candidates.answer_en: For maximum egg production ensure 16 hours of light daily using artificial lighting, maintain temperature between 18 and 24 degrees Celsius, provide layer mash with 16 to 17 percent protein and added calcium for strong shells, ensure clean water always, control parasites and disease through regular vaccination and deworming, collect eggs three times daily, keep stress low by avoiding sudden disturbances, and cull poor layers that consistently produce below average.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tamma gu akoko sɛ wɔagu pii?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ akoko gu tamma pii a, hwɛ sɛ kanea da wɔ mu dɔn 16 de artificial light, kora berɛ wɔ degrees 18 ne 24 Celsius ntam, de layer mash a protein 16 kɔ 17 percent ne calcium a ɛhia ma tamma ho den na ka ho, de nsuo pa to mu bere nyinaa, boa parasites ne yadeɛ ho de hware ne wia adwummaker bere biara, pam tamma mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa biara da, ma anigyidie sua de gye wo ho fi nka kɔkɔɔkɔ, na kum layers a wɔgu nketewa bere nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: What housing system is best for layer chickens in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: The best housing for layers in Ghana's climate is the open-sided or naturally ventilated house. Use wire mesh or wooden slats on the sides for maximum airflow. Orient the house east to west so the long side faces north and south to reduce direct sunlight. Provide a sloped roof with good overhang. Install battery cages at 3 tiers for commercial production or deep litter floor for smaller flocks. Ensure 0.2 square metres per bird for floor housing and 450 square cm per bird for cages.
candidates.question_twi: Housing nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara ma layers wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Housing a ɛhia pa ara ma layers wɔ Ghana berɛ a ɛwɔ ne open-sided anaa naturally ventilated fie. De wire mesh anaa wooden slats to ho mframa nsa sɛ mframa fa mu yie. De fie no sie east kɔ west sɛ ho tenten so hyɛ north ne south anim sɛ owia ankasa annhyɛ mu. De roof a ɛtɔ yie ne overhang pa si. Si battery cages a tiers mmiɛnsa wɔ mu ma adwuma kɛse anaa deep litter floor ma flocks nketewa. Hwɛ sɛ square metres 0.2 wɔ nnomaa baako ho ma floor housing ne square cm 450 biara nnomaa ho ma cages.

items.question_en: What is a farmer-based organisation and how does it help farmers?
items.answer_en: Farmer-based organisations (FBOs) in Ghana help members access group inputs at lower prices through bulk purchasing, negotiate better prices for produce, access credit collectively, share knowledge and technology, access extension services more easily, participate in government programmes, and market their produce jointly. To find an FBO in your area contact your District Department of Agriculture under MOFA. Joining a recognised FBO also helps you qualify for government subsidies and NGO support programmes.
items.question_twi: Okuafo kuo adwuma yɛ dɛn wɔ Ghana?
items.answer_twi: Okuafo kuo (FBOs) wɔ Ghana boa wɔn members sɛ wɔgye group inputs wɔ bo sua mu de bulk buying, bɔ wɔn nnuaba bo yie, gye credit kaa bom, fa nyansa ne nkyerɛkyerɛ, gye extension services mmerɛw, ka aban programmes ho, na tɔ wɔn nnuaba kaa bom. Sɛ wohia FBO wɔ wo hɔ a, ka wo District Department of Agriculture wɔ MOFA ase ho. Ka FBO a wɔakyerɛw ho ho nso boa sɛ woatwa abo aban subsidies ne NGO mmoa programmes ho.

candidates.question_en: What is a market information system and how does it help farmers?
candidates.answer_en: A market information system provides farmers with current prices of crops at different markets so they can decide where and when to sell for the best price. In Ghana, services like Esoko, the Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX), and MOFA market information services provide this. Access via phone, radio, or internet. This prevents farmers from being cheated by middlemen who know prices but farmers don't.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na aguabasa nsɛm system yɛ na ɛboa okuafo sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Aguabasa Nsɛm system de nnuaba boɔ a ɛwɔ aguabasa ahodoɔ so ma okuafo sɛ wɔtumi paw beae ne bere a wɔbɛtɔn sɛ wanya boɔ pa. Wɔ Ghana, nnwuma te sɛ Esoko, Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX), ne MOFA aguabasa nsɛm nnwuma de eyi brɛ. Nya ase wɔ fɔn, redio, anaa internet so. Eyi mma okuafo anko ase wɔ middlemen a wɔnim boɔ nanso okuafo nnim ntam.

candidates.question_en: Should I join a farmers' cooperative?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, cooperatives offer many benefits including group purchasing of inputs at lower prices, collective selling for better prices, access to credit, shared equipment, training, and stronger negotiating power with buyers and government.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ meba okuafo kuo mu anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, cooperative de mfaaso bebree brɛ: kuo to adenneɛ ketewa mu, kuo tɔn sɛ wanya boɔ pa, nya ka, fa egyapade bom, nyansapɔ, na kuo tumi yɛ kɛse sen wɔ adeɛtɔfo ne ɔman ho nsɛm mu.

candidates.question_en: What training opportunities are available for farmers in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Training opportunities for farmers in Ghana include the Farmer Field Schools organized by MOFA where farmers learn by doing in their own fields, training by agricultural NGOs like SEND Ghana, Opportunity International and SNV, agricultural colleges and vocational institutions, online courses through platforms like Coursera and the FAO e-learning academy, cooperative training programmes, and the government-sponsored Youth in Agriculture Training Programmes. Many input suppliers also offer free agronomic training when you buy their products.
candidates.question_twi: Training nhyiamu bɛn na ɛwɔ ma okuafo wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Training nhyiamu ma okuafo wɔ Ghana ne Farmer Field Schools a MOFA de sɛ okuafo sua wɔ wɔn ankasa afuom mu, training de agricultural NGOs te sɛ SEND Ghana, Opportunity International ne SNV, agricultural colleges ne vocational institutions, online courses wɔ platforms te sɛ Coursera ne FAO e-learning academy, cooperative training programmes, na aban-sponsored Youth in Agriculture Training Programmes. Input suppliers bi nso de free agronomic training to bere a wogye wɔn nneɛma.

candidates.question_en: What is grading and why is it important when selling produce?
candidates.answer_en: Grading means sorting produce into quality categories based on size, color, shape, and freedom from defects. It is important because: buyers pay premium prices for Grade A produce, graded produce has longer shelf life when sorted, it builds trust with buyers and processors, it allows you to sell different grades to different markets, and it makes it easier to negotiate better prices. Grade A goes to supermarkets, Grade B to restaurants, Grade C to processors.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na grading yɛ na ɛsɛ sɛ ɛyɛ papa sɛ wotɔn nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Grading kyerɛ yi nnuaba no mu wɔ aba ho pa ahodoɔ wɔ boɔ, rere, ahofã, ne mfomso a enni ho so. Ɛho hia efisɛ: adeɛtɔfo tua sika dodo ma Grade A nnuaba, nnuaba a wɔasi no mu tena yie bere tenten, ɛkyerɛ adeɛtɔfo ne adwuma kuo sɛ wobetumi de wɔn so, ɛma wo tumi tɔn Grade ahodoɔ wɔ aguabasa ahodoɔ, na ɛboa wo ne adeɛtɔfo siesie boɔ yie. Grade A kɔ supermarkets, Grade B kɔ adidibea, Grade C kɔ adwuma kuo.

candidates.question_en: Which farming apps can help farmers in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Useful apps for Ghanaian farmers include: Esoko for market prices, Farmerline for agricultural advice and services, Hello Tractor for renting tractors, AgroFresh for produce quality management, Google Translate for translating agricultural content, YouTube for farming tutorials, Ghana Met Agency app for weather forecasts, and WhatsApp for connecting with other farmers and extension officers. Most are free or low-cost.
candidates.question_twi: Farming apps bɛn na ɛboa okuafo wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apps a ɛboa okuafo Ghana mu ne: Esoko ma aguabasa boɔ, Farmerline ma okuafo adwuma boa ne nnwuma, Hello Tractor ma tractor asɛ, AgroFresh ma nnuaba ho pa hwɛ, Google Translate ma okuafo nsɛm dan, YouTube ma okuafo adwuma nhyehyɛe, Ghana Met Agency app ma ɛwim amanneɛ, ne WhatsApp ma kasa ne okuafo ne extension officers foforɔ. Wɔn bebree yɛ daa anaa boɔ yɛ ketewa.

candidates.question_en: How do I register my farm as a business in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: To register your farm as a business in Ghana: register with the Registrar General's Department as a sole proprietorship or partnership (costs GHS 150-300), get a Tax Identification Number (TIN) from the Ghana Revenue Authority, register with MOFA for agricultural activities, open a business bank account, and get all required operating permits from your local assembly. A formally registered farm business is more credible to banks, buyers, and government programs.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mede m'afuo kyerɛw sɛ adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ kyerɛw wo afuo sɛ adwuma wɔ Ghana a: kyerɛw wɔ Registrar General's Department sɛ sole proprietorship anaa partnership (sika GHS 150-300), nya Tax Identification Number (TIN) fi Ghana Revenue Authority hɔ, kyerɛw wɔ MOFA ho ma okuafo adwuma, bue adwuma ban account, na nya kratafa biara a wohia fi wo local assembly. Afuo adwuma a wɔakyerɛw no yɛ pa ara wɔ ban, adeɛtɔfo, ne ɔman adwuma ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I find buyers for my farm produce before harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Visit local markets to identify traders. Contact food processing companies and restaurants. Use phone or WhatsApp groups for farmers in your area. Signing contract farming agreements with companies before the season guarantees buyers and sometimes provides inputs on credit.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwehwɛ adeɛtɔfo ma m'afuo nnuaba ansa na megye wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Kɔ aguabasa a ɛbɛn wo sɛ wuhu nnipa a wɔtɔn. Ka kyerɛ aduan yɛ adeɛ kuo ne adidibea. Fa fɔn anaa WhatsApp kuo ma okuafo wɔ wo beae. De contract farming agreement ka adeɛtɔ kuo bere a bere mfiase ansa na ɛma adeɛtɔfo yɛ dada.

candidates.question_en: How can I get certified to sell organic farm produce?
candidates.answer_en: To sell as certified organic you need to farm organically for at least 3 years and pass inspection by an accredited certification body. In Ghana organizations like ENCOT and Control Union offer organic certification.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menya kratafa sɛ metɔn organic nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ tɔn organic nnuaba a wɔakyerɛw wɔn a, ɛsɛ sɛ woyɛ organic okuafo adwuma mfe 3 pɛ na wufa inspection a organic kuo yɛ. Wɔ Ghana, kuo te sɛ ENCOT ne Control Union de organic kratafa brɛ.

items.question_en: Can I intercrop maize with other crops?
items.answer_en: Yes, maize intercropping is common and beneficial in Ghana. You can intercrop maize with cowpea, groundnut, cassava or beans. Cowpea and groundnut fix nitrogen into the soil which benefits the maize. Cassava can be planted at the same time but needs wider spacing. Avoid intercropping with crops that are too tall or spread wide as they will shade the maize.
items.question_twi: Metumi de aburoɔ ato mu ne nnuaba foforɔ?
items.answer_twi: Aane, aburoɔ ne nnuaba foforɔ to mu yɛ biribi a wɔyɛ na ɛboa wɔ Ghana. Wobetumi de aburoɔ ato mu ne bɔde, groundnut, bankye anaa aduaba. Bɔde ne groundnut de nitrogen ka asase mu a ɛboa aburoɔ. Wobetumi de bankye to mu bere koro nanso ɛhia ahodɔ kɛse. Mma aba to mu ne nnuaba a ɛsua fɛw anaa a ahorow tete yie efisɛ wɔbɛkata aburoɔ no so.

candidates.question_en: What crop rotation plan is suitable for Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: A good crop rotation for Ghana is to plant legumes like cowpea or groundnut after cereals like maize or sorghum. Legumes fix nitrogen into the soil improving fertility naturally. A 3-year rotation could be maize in year one, cowpea in year two, and cassava or vegetables in year three. Avoid planting the same crop family in the same field two seasons in a row as this builds up pests and diseases specific to that crop.
candidates.question_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu pa wɔ Ghana ne de legumes te sɛ bɔde anaa groundnut to mu akyi cereals te sɛ aburoɔ anaa sorghum. Legumes de nitrogen ka asase mu a ɛboa asase aduan pa. Mfe mmiɛnsa rotation bɛtumi ayɛ: aburoɔ mfe a ɛdi kan mu, bɔde mfe mmienu mu, na bankye anaa nnuaba mfe mmiɛnsa mu. Gye wo ho fi de nnuaba nhyiamu koro to mu wɔ afuom koro mfe mmienu so kwa efisɛ eyi ma adwummaker ne yadeɛ a ɛfa nhyiamu no ho kɔ so.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare the soil before planting maize?
candidates.answer_en: Clear the land of weeds and old crop residues. Plough or dig to a depth of 20 to 30 cm to loosen the soil. If possible, apply compost or manure and incorporate it into the soil two weeks before planting. Level the seedbed to ensure even germination. Avoid burning crop residues as this destroys beneficial soil organisms.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ asase no so ansa na meto aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo ne nnuaba a ato fɛw fi asase no so. Boro asase no kosi sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 mu sɛ asase no atete yie. Sɛ wobetumi a, de compost anaa aguare to mu na fa ka ho mprɛnsa mmienu ansa na wode aba to mu. Siesie seedbed no so yie sɛ aba nyinaa retua fɔw yie. Mma nnuaba fidie anhye efisɛ eyi sɛe asase mu adwummaker pa.

candidates.question_en: What is intercropping and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Intercropping means growing two or more crops together on the same land. For example, maize with cowpea. Benefits include better land use, the legume adds nitrogen to the soil, reduced pest pressure, and income from two crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛyɛ intercropping na ɛboa?
candidates.answer_twi: Intercropping kyerɛ sɛ wokura nnuaba abien anaa dodo wɔ asase koro so. Nhwɛso so, aburow ne abɔdweɛ. Mfaaso ho ne: asase ho dwuma pa, abɔdweɛ de nitrogen ma asase, adwummakers hia sua, na nnuaba abien firi sika.

candidates.question_en: How can I start farming in Ghana with little money?
candidates.answer_en: Start small with crops that need minimal investment like vegetables, maize or cassava. Begin with what land you have access to. Use family labour initially to reduce costs. Join a farmer-based organisation for access to group inputs and credit. Apply for the government Planting for Food and Jobs programme which provides subsidized seeds and fertilizer. Reinvest your profits to gradually expand your farm each season.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana a sika ketewa wɔ me nkyɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi ase ketewa de nnuaba a sika ketewa na ɛhia te sɛ nnuaba, aburoɔ anaa bankye. Fi ase wɔ asase a wowɔ ho. De wo fie ho adwuma ansa na ɛhia sika. Ka okuafo kuo ho sɛ wɔde group inputs ne credit nya. Bisa aban Planting for Food and Jobs programme a wɔde subsidized aba ne ferefere to. De wo mfaso no to wo afuom no so bere biara ma ɛkɔ so kɛse tenten tenten.

candidates.question_en: How can I make compost for my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Make compost by layering crop residues dry matter like maize stalks alternating with green matter like grass clippings and kitchen waste. Add a thin layer of soil or finished compost between layers to introduce decomposing organisms. Keep the pile moist but not waterlogged and turn it every 2 weeks. The compost is ready in 8 to 12 weeks when it is dark brown crumbly and earthy smelling. Apply 2 to 3 tonnes of compost per acre before planting to significantly improve soil fertility.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ compost ma me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ compost de layers a nnuaba a ato fɛw aba ntama a wɔatew te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ka ho ne nnuaba foforɔ te sɛ nhawan ne efie ho nneɛma. De asase ketewa anaa compost a ɛawie to ntam biara mu sɛ ɛde organisms a ɛhia kɔ. Ma pile no nsuo ho kakra nanso nsuo nni mu agyina na gyinaso mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas. Compost no atwa so nnansas nwɔtwe kɔ duonum mmienu mu bere a ɛyɛ dark brown, ɛpepee yie na ɛwɔ nhwirɛ pa. De compost tonnes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa to eka baako so ansa na wode aba to mu sɛ ɛboa asase aduan pii.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Weed at 2 to 3 weeks and again at 6 to 8 weeks after planting. These two weeding operations are critical because early weeds compete directly with young maize for nutrients and water. You can use hand weeding with a hoe or apply pre-emergence herbicides like atrazine before the maize germinates. Mulching between rows also suppresses weeds.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ nhaban foforo a wɔ me aburoɔ afuom mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo nnansa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa akyi na bio wɔ nnansa nsia kɔ nwɔtwe akyi a wode aba to mu. Adwuma nhaban foforo yi mmienu no ho hia pa ara efisɛ nhaban foforo a ɛdi kan no di aburoɔ foforo bere a ɛwɔ ho ferefere ne nsuo ho brε. Wobetumi de nsa ne atia yam yi nhaban foforo anaa de herbicides a wɔfre no atrazine to ho ansa na aburoɔ aba atua fɔw. Mulching nsɛm ntam mu nso boa nhaban foforo ho.

candidates.question_en: When is the best time to plant maize in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: In Ghana, the best time to plant maize is at the beginning of the rainy season — March to April in the south, and May to June in the north. Plant when you have received at least 2-3 good rains so the soil is well moistened.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛyɛ ɔkorɔ sɛ wode aburow to mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Wɔ Ghana, bere pa ara sɛ wode aburow to mu ne nsuo bere mfiase — Ɛbɔ kwan so Oforisuo wɔ apuei fam, na Ayɛwohomumo kwan so Mumu wɔ atifi fam. To aba mu bere a wanya nsu mmɛn 2-3 yie na asase no atenante yie.

candidates.question_en: Which crops are most resilient to climate change in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Drought-tolerant crops for Ghana's changing climate include improved NERICA rice, drought-tolerant maize varieties like Obatanpa and Omankwa, cowpea, sorghum, millet, and cassava. Contact CSIR-SARI or MOFA for the latest recommended varieties in your region.
candidates.question_twi: Nnuaba bɛn na ɛtumi wiase tebea sɛsae ase hyɛ yie wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase hyɛ wɔ Ghana tebea sɛsae mu ne NERICA ɔmɔ a wɔayɛ no foforo, aburow a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase te sɛ Obatanpa ne Omankwa, abɔdweɛ, ɔtɛ, ɔtɛ pa, ne bankye. Ka kyerɛ CSIR-SARI anaa MOFA sɛ wunya aba a wɔaka.

items.question_en: How can I improve young coconut seedling survival?
items.answer_en: Plant healthy seedlings when soil moisture is adequate, protect them from weeds and severe heat, and maintain appropriate moisture.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama coconut seedlings nketewa atena ase yie?
items.answer_twi: Dua seedlings a wɔyɛ ahoɔden bere a nsuo wɔ asase mu, bɔ wɔn ho ban fi nwura ne ɔhyew den ho na ma moisture a ɛfata.

candidates.question_en: What soil conditions suit coconut farming?
candidates.answer_en: Coconut generally performs best in deep soils with good drainage, adequate moisture and suitable fertility.
candidates.question_twi: Asase tebea bɛn na ɛfata coconut kuayɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Coconut nyin yie wɔ asase a ɛdɔ, nsuo firi mu yie, nsuo wɔ mu kakra na nutrients wɔ mu a ɛfata.

candidates.question_en: How can coconut farmers reduce damage from strong winds?
candidates.answer_en: Maintain healthy trees, manage the farm so windbreaks are possible and remove dangerous dead material safely.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mframa den sɛe so wɔ coconut mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma nnua no nya ahoɔden, yɛ windbreak sɛ ɛfata na yi nneɛma a awu a ɛyɛ ahobammɔ ho haw no wɔ kwan a ɛyɛ safe.

candidates.question_en: How can coconut husks be used on the farm?
candidates.answer_en: Husks can be used as mulch or processed for fibre and other products, depending on local facilities and demand.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn de coconut husks adi dwuma wɔ afuo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Wobetumi de husks ayɛ mulch anaa ayɛ fibre ne nneɛma foforo sɛ mpɔtam no wɔ facilities ne gua a ɛfata.

candidates.question_en: How should young oil palms be protected from weeds?
candidates.answer_en: Keep a manageable weed-free area around young palms while avoiding damage to the roots or stem.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn abɔ oil palm nketewa ho ban fi nwura ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma beae a ɛbɛn palm nketewa no nyɛ nwura, nanso hwɛ sɛ nwura yiyie no renyɛ ntini anaa dua no ho haw.

candidates.question_en: What should I consider before starting a tree-crop farm?
candidates.answer_en: Consider the long establishment period, land rights, capital, market, labour, climate and when income is expected to begin.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ misusuw ho ansa na mahyɛ tree-crop kuayɛ ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Susuw bere tenten a nnua no de bɛyɛ, asase ho hokwan, capital, gua, adwumayɛ, ewim tebea ne bere a wobɛfi ase anya sika ho.

candidates.question_en: Why should oil palm bunches be harvested on time?
candidates.answer_en: Timely harvesting helps maintain fruit quality and reduces losses from overripe or fallen bunches.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛgye oil palm bunches bere a ɛsɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Gyeɛ a ɛba bere mu ma fruit quality yɛ papa na ɛtew asɛe a ɛfiri bunch a wɔawie dodo anaa aba a atɔ fam ho so.

candidates.question_en: Why is spacing important in oil palm plantations?
candidates.answer_en: Adequate spacing reduces overcrowding, allows better light and airflow, and gives each palm enough growing space.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na plant spacing ho hia wɔ oil palm afuo mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ntam a ɛfata tew overcrowding so, ma owia ne mframa kɔ mu yie na ɛma palm biara nya beae a ɛsɛ.

candidates.question_en: Why is farm sanitation important around oil palms?
candidates.answer_en: Removing or properly managing dead and decaying material can reduce some pest and disease risks and make inspection easier.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na farm sanitation ho hia wɔ oil palm ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wuyi anaa wohwɛ nneɛma a awu ne nea ɛporɔ yie a, ebetumi ate mmoawa ne yare ho haw so na ɛma inspection yɛ mmerɛ.

items.question_en: How can I reduce misshapen cucumber fruits?
items.answer_en: Maintain even soil moisture, provide adequate nutrients and avoid severe stress during flowering and fruit development.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate cucumber aba a ɛnsɛ ho?
items.answer_twi: Ma nsuo a ɛwɔ asase mu yɛ pɛ, ma nutrients a ɛfata na bɔ nnɔbae no ho ban fi ɔhaw den bere a ɛrehuru ne bere a aba reyɛ kɛse.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect cucumber flowers?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid unnecessary disturbance during flowering, maintain adequate moisture and manage pests that attack flowers and young fruits.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn abɔ cucumber nhwiren ho ban?
candidates.answer_twi: Mma nhwiren no ho nnyɛ basabasa bere a ɛrehuru, ma nsuo a ɛfata na hwɛ mmoawa a wɔtow nhwiren ne aba nketewa no so.

candidates.question_en: What causes bitter cucumber fruits?
candidates.answer_en: Stress such as uneven watering, extreme temperatures or variety-specific factors can contribute to bitterness.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma cucumber yɛ nwene?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsuo a ɛnyɛ pɛ, ɔhyew a ɛdɔɔso anaa ɛsua, ne nneɛma a ɛfa variety ho tumi ma cucumber yɛ nwene.

candidates.question_en: How should cucumbers be handled after harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Handle them gently, keep them shaded and avoid excessive heat to preserve freshness and reduce bruising.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ cucumber akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa ahwɛyiye, kora wɔn wɔ sunsuma na mma ɔhyew den nka wɔn sɛnea fresh no bɛtena hɔ na wɔmpirapira.

candidates.question_en: When should cucumber be harvested?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest when fruits have reached the market size and are still firm and tender. Delayed harvesting can reduce quality.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ megye cucumber?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye bere a aba no anya kɛse a gua hia na ɛda so yɛ den na ɛyɛ mmerɛ. Sɛ wotwentwɛn a quality betumi resa.

candidates.question_en: How often should cucumber be picked?
candidates.answer_en: Pick frequently during the production period so mature fruits do not remain on the vines and slow further production.
candidates.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ megye cucumber?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye wɔn daa wɔ bere a wɔrebɔ aba mu sɛnea aba a awie ase renka dua no so na ɛrenkum aba foforo.

candidates.question_en: What kind of site is suitable for cucumber?
candidates.answer_en: Choose a sunny site with fertile, well-drained soil and access to reliable water.
candidates.question_twi: Beae bɛn na ɛfata ma cucumber?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw beae a owia wɔ, asase no yɛ pa na nsuo firi mu yie, na nsuo wɔ hɔ daa.

candidates.question_en: Can cucumber be grown in containers?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, but use a sufficiently large container, good drainage, fertile growing media and support for the vines.
candidates.question_twi: Cucumber tumi nyin wɔ nkuku mu anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, nanso fa kuku a ɛso kɛse, nsuo tumi firi mu, asase pa ne adeɛ a ɛbɛkura vines no.

candidates.question_en: Why do cucumber vines need support?
candidates.answer_en: Supporting vines can improve air circulation, keep fruits cleaner and make harvesting easier.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛma cucumber vines nya biribi kura wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛboa ma mframa fa mu yie, ma aba no ntra dɔte mu na ɛma gyeɛ yɛ mmerɛ.

items.question_en: What is drought-tolerant farming?
items.answer_en: It is an approach that reduces crop losses under limited water by using suitable varieties, moisture conservation, efficient watering and good soil management.
items.question_twi: Dɛn ne drought-tolerant kuayɛ?
items.answer_twi: Ɛyɛ kuayɛ kwan a ɛboa tew nnɔbae asɛe so bere a nsuo sua, fa varieties a ɛfata, nsuo conservation, nsuo a wɔde di dwuma yie ne asase nhwɛsoɔ pa.

candidates.question_en: How can mulch help during drought?
candidates.answer_en: Mulch reduces evaporation, protects the soil surface and can help conserve moisture around crop roots.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na mulch betumi aboa bere a ɔpɛ wɔ hɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Mulch tew nsuo a ɛyera so, bɔ asase anim ho ban na ɛboa ma nsuo tena nnɔbae ntini ho.

candidates.question_en: What is the benefit of planting windbreaks?
candidates.answer_en: Windbreaks can reduce wind speed, protect crops from wind damage and reduce moisture loss.
candidates.question_twi: Mfasoɔ bɛn na windbreak wɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Windbreak tew mframa ahoɔden so, bɔ nnɔbae ho ban fi mframa sɛe ho na tew nsuo yera so.

candidates.question_en: How can farmers prepare for a late rainy season?
candidates.answer_en: Monitor local weather information, choose suitable planting dates and varieties, conserve soil moisture and avoid planting too early into dry soil.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie m'akuayɛ ma osu bere no akyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ local weather nsɛm, paw bere ne variety a ɛfata, kora nsuo wɔ asase mu na mma wofiri ase dua ntɛm wɔ asase a ɛda so yɛ kusuu mu.

candidates.question_en: How can water harvesting support dry-season farming?
candidates.answer_en: Stored water can supplement irrigation during dry periods when designed and managed safely.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na nsuo a yɛboaboa ano betumi aboa ɔpɛ bere kuayɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsuo a wɔakora no tumi boa irrigation wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu sɛ wɔayɛ no yie na wɔhwɛ so wɔ ahobammɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: Why should farmers maintain soil cover?
candidates.answer_en: Soil cover reduces erosion, limits moisture loss and protects soil from intense rainfall and heat.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ akuafoɔ ma asase no kata?
candidates.answer_twi: Asase a covered no tew erosion so, tew nsuo yera so na bɔ asase no ho ban fi osu den ne ɔhyew ho.

candidates.question_en: How can farmers prepare for floods?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid planting in high-risk low areas where possible, improve drainage, protect soil structure and have a plan for moving inputs and livestock to safer areas.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie m'afuo ama nsuyiri?
candidates.answer_twi: Mma wotɔ nnɔbae wɔ mmeae a nsuyiri taa ba sɛ wubetumi akwati, siesie drainage, bɔ asase structure ho ban na nya plan sɛnea wobɛfa nneɛma ne mmoa akɔ baabi a ahobammɔ wɔ.

items.question_en: How can I scout my maize field for pests?
items.answer_en: Scout your maize field weekly by walking in a W or X pattern across the field. Examine at least 20 plants at each of 5 locations. Look under leaves for eggs and larvae, in the whorl for fall armyworm frass, on ears for silk damage, and on stems for borer entry holes. Record the percentage of plants affected. If more than 5 to 10 percent of plants are infested take action. Scout in the early morning when pests are most active. Keep a scouting notebook to track pest trends.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mehwɛ me aburoɔ afuom mu hwɛ adwummaker?
items.answer_twi: Hwɛ wo aburoɔ afuom mu nnansas de kɔ wɔ W anaa X pattern wɔ afuom mu. Hwɛ nnuaba 20 pɛ wɔ baabi 5 mu. Hwɛ nhaban ase ma tammɛn ne larvae, wɔ whorl mu ma fall armyworm frass, wɔ ears so ma silk nsɔre, na wɔ abɔ so ma borer holes. Kora nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho percent. Sɛ nnuaba 5 kɔ 10 percent a adwummaker tuu wɔn mako a, yɛ biribi. Hwɛ anɔpa bere a adwummaker yɛ adwuma pii. Kora scouting notebook ma wo hunu adwummaker trend.

candidates.question_en: How can I identify Fall Armyworm in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Look for ragged holes in leaves with fine sawdust-like droppings inside the funnel of the plant. The worm itself is greenish-brown with stripes along the body and a distinctive Y-shaped marking on the head. Affected plants will have leaves with irregular feeding damage. Check your field early morning when the worms are most active on the surface.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛkyerɛ sɛ fall armyworm atu mako wɔ me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ afifide a wɔatwa mu ne akyɛkyɛɛ teketeke a ɛte sɛ sawdust wɔ nnuaba funnel mu. Adwummaker no ankasa yɛ green-brown na ɛwɔ lines wɔ ne ho so na ɛwɔ nsono a ɛte sɛ Y wɔ ne ti so. Nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho wɔ nsono a wɔatwa mu te ɛnte. Hwɛ wo afuom anɔpa anaana bere a adwummaker no wɔ asase so pefee.

candidates.question_en: How can I make compost for my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Make compost by layering crop residues dry matter like maize stalks alternating with green matter like grass clippings and kitchen waste. Add a thin layer of soil or finished compost between layers to introduce decomposing organisms. Keep the pile moist but not waterlogged and turn it every 2 weeks. The compost is ready in 8 to 12 weeks when it is dark brown crumbly and earthy smelling. Apply 2 to 3 tonnes of compost per acre before planting to significantly improve soil fertility.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ compost ma me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ compost de layers a nnuaba a ato fɛw aba ntama a wɔatew te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ka ho ne nnuaba foforɔ te sɛ nhawan ne efie ho nneɛma. De asase ketewa anaa compost a ɛawie to ntam biara mu sɛ ɛde organisms a ɛhia kɔ. Ma pile no nsuo ho kakra nanso nsuo nni mu agyina na gyinaso mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas. Compost no atwa so nnansas nwɔtwe kɔ duonum mmienu mu bere a ɛyɛ dark brown, ɛpepee yie na ɛwɔ nhwirɛ pa. De compost tonnes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa to eka baako so ansa na wode aba to mu sɛ ɛboa asase aduan pii.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Weed at 2 to 3 weeks and again at 6 to 8 weeks after planting. These two weeding operations are critical because early weeds compete directly with young maize for nutrients and water. You can use hand weeding with a hoe or apply pre-emergence herbicides like atrazine before the maize germinates. Mulching between rows also suppresses weeds.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ nhaban foforo a wɔ me aburoɔ afuom mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo nnansa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa akyi na bio wɔ nnansa nsia kɔ nwɔtwe akyi a wode aba to mu. Adwuma nhaban foforo yi mmienu no ho hia pa ara efisɛ nhaban foforo a ɛdi kan no di aburoɔ foforo bere a ɛwɔ ho ferefere ne nsuo ho brε. Wobetumi de nsa ne atia yam yi nhaban foforo anaa de herbicides a wɔfre no atrazine to ho ansa na aburoɔ aba atua fɔw. Mulching nsɛm ntam mu nso boa nhaban foforo ho.

candidates.question_en: How do I choose the best maize variety for my area?
candidates.answer_en: Choose your maize variety based on the rainfall pattern of your area, the soil type, and your market. For the forest zone with high rainfall, use medium to late maturing varieties like Abontem or Mamaba. For the savanna and transition zones, use drought-tolerant varieties like Obatanpa, Wari or Aburohemaa. For household consumption, choose floury white varieties. For animal feed, yellow varieties like Dobidi have higher energy content. Buy certified seed from licensed dealers.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick aburoɔ aba variety pa wɔ me ɛhɔ ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi wo aburoɔ variety sɛ nsuo a ɛtɔ bere wɔ wo hɔ, asase nhyiamu, na wo dwa so. Ma kwaeɛ zone a nsuo tɔ pii ho, de medium kɔ late maturing varieties te sɛ Abontem anaa Mamaba. Ma savanna ne ntam zones ho, de drought-tolerant varieties te sɛ Obatanpa, Wari anaa Aburohemaa. Ma efie didi, yi floury white varieties. Ma mmoa aduan, yellow varieties te sɛ Dobidi wɔ energy pii mu. Gye certified seed fi licensed dealers.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce feed costs in poultry farming?
candidates.answer_en: Reduce poultry feed costs by formulating your own feed using locally available ingredients like maize, soybean meal, fishmeal, rice bran and mineral premix. This can reduce feed cost by 20 to 30 percent compared to commercial feeds. Buy feed ingredients in bulk when prices are low. Use fermented feed to improve digestibility and reduce feed conversion ratio. Reduce waste by using appropriate feeders and filling them only two-thirds full. Grow fast-growing varieties and slaughter at the right age before feed efficiency declines.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me aduan bo sua wɔ akoko adwuma mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sua akoko aduan bo de yɛ wo ankasa aduan de nneɛma a ɛwɔ ho te sɛ aburoɔ, soybean meal, fishmeal, rice bran ne mineral premix. Eyi bɛtumi asua aduan bo 20 kɔ 30 percent tia commercial feeds. Gye aduan nneɛma pii bere a bo sua. De fermented feed ma digestibility kɔ so na sua feed conversion ratio. Hia adefoforo de feeders pa na ma wɔn mu mprɛnsa mmienu pɛ. To fast-growing varieties mu na kum bere a ɛyɛ papa ansa na feed efficiency huna.

candidates.question_en: My maize leaves have dark areas and insects are eating them. What should I do?
candidates.answer_en: This is likely the Fall Armyworm. Look inside the whorl for worms. Apply insecticides like emamectin benzoate early morning or late evening. Sand mixed with ash applied into the whorl also helps as an organic option.
candidates.question_twi: M'aburow nhaban wɔ tumtum na wɔredidi won. Dɛn na meyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Eyi tumi yɛ Aborɔnoma Adwummaker Kɛse adwummaker. Hwɛ nhaban mu sɛ wɔhwehwɛ adwummakers anaa wɔ ho ntama. De adwummakers dawuro te sɛ emamectin benzoate guare owia da ano anaa nnɔnhwerew mu. Asintiɛ a waka nkamfo ka ho no tumi de gu nhaban mu sɛ nhwiren dawuro.

candidates.question_en: What is maize streak virus and how can I manage it?
candidates.answer_en: Maize streak virus causes yellow streaks running along the leaf veins giving leaves a striped appearance. It is transmitted by the leafhopper insect. There is no cure once a plant is infected. Control by planting resistant varieties like Obatanpa and Mamaba from CSIR, destroying infected plants early, and controlling leafhoppers with appropriate insecticides. Avoid late planting as late-planted fields suffer more leafhopper attacks.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛkyerɛ maize streak virus na dɛn na menyɛ ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Maize streak virus ma nhaban ho yɛ yellow streaks a ɛkɔ wɔ nhaban abɔ ho na ɛma nhaban no yɛ stripes. Leafhopper adwummaker de tete. Yadeɛ no nni dawuro bere a nnuaba nya mu. Boa ho de resistant varieties te sɛ Obatanpa ne Mamaba fi CSIR to mu, yi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na de insecticides hware leafhoppers so. Gye wo ho fi late to mu efisɛ afuom a wɔde to mu akyi sen no nya leafhopper atia sen.

candidates.question_en: What is aflatoxin in maize and how can I prevent it?
candidates.answer_en: Aflatoxin is a deadly poison produced by Aspergillus fungi that grows on improperly dried or stored maize. It causes liver cancer and can kill animals and humans. Prevent aflatoxin by drying maize properly to below 13 percent moisture before storage, using hermetic storage bags or metal silos, inspecting stored grain regularly and discarding mouldy grain, using aflasafe biocontrol product, and never feeding visibly mouldy grain to animals.
candidates.question_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ dɛn wɔ aburoɔ mu na dɛn na menyɛ sɛ ɛnnya?
candidates.answer_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ poisons a ɛyɛ den a Aspergillus fungi a ɛso wɔ aburoɔ a wonma no tew yie anaa a wonguina yie ho de ba. Ɛma akokoaa yareɛ na etumi kum mmoa ne nnipa. Gye aflatoxin fi ho de ma aburoɔ no tew yie kɔ 13 percent nsuo ase ansa na woguina, de hermetic storage bags anaa metal silos, hwɛ aba a woguina bere biara na yi aba a mold aba ho, de aflasafe biocontrol de, na mma aba a mold aba ho amma mmoa.

items.question_en: How can I store dried fish or meat without a refrigerator?
items.answer_en: Dry fish or meat thoroughly until it is very hard and dry. Wrap tightly in cloth or paper, then in a plastic bag. Store in a cool, dry, ventilated area away from moisture and insects. You can smoke the meat or fish to extend shelf life. Inspect weekly and re-dry immediately if any moisture is detected. Properly dried fish or meat can last 2-3 months.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meguina nsuomnam anaa nam a ayaw wɔ afuo so a menwɔ fridge?
items.answer_twi: Yaw nsuomnam anaa nam no yie kosi sɛ ɛyɛ den na yera. De ntama anaa krataa sɛɛ mu yie, na afei de plastik bag sɛɛ. Guina wɔ bae a ɛhuru, yera, na mframa pue mu fi nsuo ne adwummakers ho. Wobetumi bu nam anaa nsuomnam no ewi sɛ ɛma no tena yie. Hwɛ so nnawotwe biara na yaw ntɛm sɛ nsuo wɔ mu. Nam anaa nsuomnam a ayaw yie tena abosome 2-3.

candidates.question_en: What is the best way to harvest fish from a pond?
candidates.answer_en: The best harvesting method depends on whether you are doing partial or complete harvest. For partial harvest use a seine net to selectively remove larger fish leaving smaller ones to grow. For complete harvest drain the pond partially then use nets to remove all fish. Harvest early morning when water is cool. Have containers ready with clean water or ice to keep fish alive or fresh. Weigh and record your harvest for business records. Never use chemicals or electricity to harvest as these are illegal and harmful.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛkwan bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ meyiyɛ apataa fi pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛkwan a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wuyiyɛ no kyɛ sɛ partial anaa complete harvest na woyɛ. Ma partial harvest de seine net yi apataa kɛse a wɔbɛ na ma nketewa tena so bo sɔ. Ma complete harvest sua nsuo ketewa fi pond mu afei de nets yi apataa nyinaa. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo dɛ. Ma containers a nsuo foforɔ anaa ice wɔ mu sɛ apataa aguina anaa tena foforɔ. Bu na kora wo harvest ho sɛ adwuma nsɛm. Mma wo mpo de chemicals anaa electricity yiyɛ efisɛ ɛnyɛ nea mmara gyina so na ɛyɛ bɔne.

candidates.question_en: How can I construct a low-cost earthen fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with clay soil that holds water well, near a reliable water source. Mark out the pond area typically 20 by 25 metres. Dig to a depth of 1.5 to 2 metres with sloping sides for stability. Build an inlet pipe to bring water in and an outlet pipe at the deepest point to drain. Pack the dikes firmly to prevent leaks. Fill with water and leave for 2 weeks to cure and establish algae before stocking. The total cost including excavation for a 500 square metre pond is typically GHS 3,000 to 6,000.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ earthen apataa pond a bo sua?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ clay asase a ɛkora nsuo yie, bɛn nsuo kwan pa. Kyerɛ pond area a ɛtaa yɛ metres 20 ne 25. Boro kɔsi tia metres 1.5 kɔ 2 a ho mfimfini slopes wɔ gyinae ho. Tu inlet pipe sɛ nsuo aba mu na outlet pipe wɔ tia no so sɛ nsuo fa mu. Hyehye dikes no yie sɛ nsuo anyi. Ma nsuo kɔ mu na gyina nnansas mmienu sɛ ɛtena na algae ntua fɔw ansa na wode apataa to. Bo nyinaa a excavation ka ho ma pond a square metres 500 wɔ mu taa yɛ GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent overcrowding in a fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Stock according to the pond's capacity and monitor fish growth, water quality and available oxygen.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpataa dodo so wɔ pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa dodow a pond no tumi soa no gu mu na hwɛ mpataa nyin, nsuo quality ne oxygen a ɛwɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: When should I harvest tilapia?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest tilapia when they reach market size of 300 to 500 grams which typically takes 5 to 6 months from fingerling stage. Monitor growth by sampling fish monthly using a net. Harvest in the early morning when water temperature is cool to reduce fish stress. Partial harvesting at 4 months removes larger fish and allows smaller ones to grow. Sell fresh fish immediately or ice them for transport to market.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na meyiyɛ me tilapia apataa?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi tilapia bere a wɔkɔ si dwa kɛse a nnɔho 300 kɔ 500 gram a ɛtaa kyɛ mfee 5 kɔ 6 fi fingerling mu. Hwɛ sɛ apataa rebɛbo yie de sample apataa bere biara de net. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo berɛ dɛ sɛ apataa nhunu. Partial yi wɔ mfee nnan mu yi apataa kɛse na ma nketewa bo sɔ. Tɔ apataa fofor ntɛm anaa de ice ka ho ma akɔ dwa.

candidates.question_en: How much does it cost to start a small fish farm in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Starting a small commercial fish farm in Ghana with two earthen ponds of 500 square metres each costs approximately GHS 15,000 to 25,000 including pond construction, fingerlings, feed for one cycle, and basic equipment. A plastic tank fish farm can be started for GHS 8,000 to 15,000. The main ongoing costs are fish feed which accounts for 60 to 70 percent of total production cost. With good management you can make a profit from the first cycle.
candidates.question_twi: Sika ahe na ɛyɛ papa sɛ mefi ase apataa adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apataa adwuma ketewa kɛse fi ase wɔ Ghana de earthen ponds mmienu a square metres 500 biara wɔ mu ho teetee GHS 15,000 kɔ 25,000 a pond yɛ, fingerlings, aduan wɔ cycle baako mu, ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ papa. Plastic tank apataa adwuma wobetumi de GHS 8,000 kɔ 15,000 fi ase. Nneɛma a ɛkyere daadaa a ɛkɔ so pii ne apataa aduan a ɛyɛ adwuma agyapade 60 kɔ 70 percent. Sɛ woyɛ adwuma pa a, wobetumi anya mfaso wɔ cycle a ɛdi kan mu.

candidates.question_en: What should I do if fish stop feeding suddenly?
candidates.answer_en: Check water quality, temperature, oxygen, recent weather, feed quality and signs of disease before increasing feed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ sɛ mpataa gyae di aduane ntɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsuo quality, ɔhyew, oxygen, weather a aba foforo, feed quality ne yare ho nsɛnkyerɛnne ansa na woama feed no so.

candidates.question_en: How should a fish farmer keep pond records?
candidates.answer_en: Record stocking date and number, feed used, mortalities, water-quality observations, treatments, harvest weight and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛw fish pond records?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw stocking da ne dodow, feed a wode dii dwuma, mpataa a awuwu, nsuo quality nsɛm, ayaresa, harvest duru ne tɔn.

items.question_en: How can I control tomato leaf miners?
items.answer_en: Tomato leaf miners are larvae that tunnel inside leaves creating winding white trails. Control by: removing and destroying heavily mined leaves, applying spinosad or abamectin insecticides, using yellow sticky traps to catch adult flies, releasing parasitic wasps as biological control, and avoiding planting tomatoes after tomatoes in the same location.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi kora ntomato nhaban miner ase?
items.answer_twi: Ntomato nhaban miner yɛ larvae a wɔkɔ nhaban mu mu na wɔyɛ kwan fitaa a ahwimhwim. Kora ase wɔ: yi ne seaa nhaban a wɔahyia so kɛse, de spinosad anaa abamectin guare, fa yellow sticky traps gye sorɔ a ɛyɛ hogua mu no, de parasitic wasp guare sɛ biological control, na bɔ hwɛ to ntomato akyi ntomato wɔ faako koro.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent tomato late blight?
candidates.answer_en: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans is the most destructive tomato disease. Prevent it by using resistant varieties, avoiding overhead irrigation, ensuring good spacing for air circulation, removing and destroying infected plant material immediately, and applying copper-based fungicides like Ridomil or Champion preventively especially during wet humid weather.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ tomato late blight annya me nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Late blight a Phytophthora infestans ma ɛba ne tomatoes yadeɛ a ɛsɛe paa. Gye wo ho fi mu de varieties a wɔagyae so, gye wo ho fi nsuo wɔ atifi ho quench, hwɛ sɛ ahodɔ pa wɔ hɔ sɛ mframa fa mu, yi na sɛe plant material a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na de copper-based fungicides te sɛ Ridomil anaa Champion hware ansa bere a nsuo ne ahuhuruw wɔ.

candidates.question_en: My harvested tomatoes are spoiling quickly. What can I do?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid harvesting during wet conditions. Handle gently to prevent bruising. Store in cool shaded well-ventilated areas on raised surfaces. Remove and separate any rotting fruits immediately. Consider making tomato paste or drying to reduce losses. Transport in ventilated crates not plastic bags.
candidates.question_twi: M'ntomato a megye wɔn resɛe ntɛm. Dɛn na metumi yɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Bɔ hwɛ gye bere a nsuo wɔ hɔ. De wɔn pɛ sɛ wɔnhow. Guina wɔ bae a ɛhuru, owia ntra mu, mframa pue mu na ɛda sor. Yi na twa ntomato a resɛe ntɛm ara. Fa tomato paste yɛ anaa yaw sɛ mpampa sika kɔ mpoano.

candidates.question_en: How should I store tomatoes without using a refrigerator?
candidates.answer_en: Store tomatoes at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Do not stack heavily. Keep them stem-side down. Tomatoes last 1-2 weeks this way. For longer preservation, dry, can, or make tomato paste. Never refrigerate unripe tomatoes.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meguina m'ntomato a menhyɛ wɔn fridge mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Guina ntomato wɔ fie mu osu a ɛyɛ pɛ sɛ owia ntra wɔn so tɔtɔ. Mfa wɔn si so dodo. De wɔn si wɔn tibo fam. Ntomato tumi tena nnawotwe 1-2 eyi ho. Sɛ wohwehwɛ tena bere tenten a, yaw, kanta, anaa yɛ ntomato paste.

candidates.question_en: How can I make tomato farming profitable?
candidates.answer_en: To make profit from tomatoes, time your production to sell when prices are high which is usually the dry season from November to February. Use drip irrigation for dry season production. Produce in bulk to negotiate better prices, form a farmer group to collectively market your tomatoes, and consider simple processing like tomato paste or puree to add value and extend shelf life. Keep detailed records of all costs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ menyɛ sika wɔ tomatoes adwuma mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛfa sika wɔ tomatoes mu a, siesie wo to aba bere sɛ bɛtɔ bere a bo wɔ so wɔ yiye a ɛyɛ daadaa bone berɛ fi Ɔbenem kɔ Ɔpepon. De drip irrigation ma bone berɛ to aba. To pii sɛ wobɛtumi aho bo mu yie, fa okuafo kuo sɛ wɔde tomatoes bɛtɔ kaa bom, na twe wo adwene ho processing ketewa te sɛ tomato paste anaa puree sɛ ɛbɛde bo kɔso na ɛma ɛtena mu akyi. Kora wo adwuma sika ho nsɛm nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How should I stake tomato plants?
candidates.answer_en: Staking tomatoes keeps the plant upright reducing soil contact and disease. Use bamboo stakes or wooden sticks about 1.5 metres tall. Insert the stake 15 cm into the soil beside the plant without damaging roots. Tie the plant loosely to the stake using soft twine in a figure-8 pattern at every 20 to 30 cm of growth. Begin staking when plants are 20 to 30 cm tall. Indeterminate varieties need continuous staking as they grow while determinate varieties need staking only once.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tomatoes stake pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Tomatoes stake ma nnuaba gyina straight na ɛhia asase ne yadeɛ nka ho. De bamboo stakes anaa dua bio a ɛtelɛ sɛ metres 1.5. De stake si sɛntimita 15 asase mu bɛn nnuaba no ho a nnɔho nsɔre. Kyekyere nnuaba no de twine mmerɛw wɔ stake no ho wɔ figure-8 nhyiamu wɔ bere biara a nnuaba rekɔ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 so. Fi ase de stake bere a nnuaba bɛyɛ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 tenten. Indeterminate varieties hia stake bere nyinaa a wɔreba mu na determinate varieties hia stake mprɛn baako pɛ.

candidates.question_en: When should I transplant tomato seedlings?
candidates.answer_en: Transplant tomato seedlings when they are 4-6 weeks old, have 4-6 true leaves, are 15-20 cm tall, and have a sturdy stem. Seedlings that are too young may not survive transplanting shock. Seedlings that are too old (over 8 weeks) become root-bound and may not establish well in the field.
candidates.question_twi: Mfeɛ bɛn na ɛfata sɛ mesi ntomato nnuaba mfoforo ananmu?
candidates.answer_twi: Si ntomato nnuaba mfoforo ananmu bere a wɔdin nnawotwe 4-6, wɔwɔ nhaban 4-6, wɔn soroɔ yɛ sɛntimita 15-20, na wɔwɔ tibo den. Nnuaba mfoforo a wɔkum dodo betumi ankyɛ si ananmu no ɔkɔm. Nnuaba mfoforo a wɔadin dodo (nnawotwe 8 kenkan) yɛ root-bound na betumi ansi yie wɔ afuo mu.

candidates.question_en: My tomato plants are wilting even though I water them. What could be wrong?
candidates.answer_en: Wilting despite watering could be bacterial wilt or fusarium wilt — soil-borne diseases. Cut the stem — if the inside is brown or oozes liquid, it is wilt disease. Remove infected plants and rotate crops for 2-3 years.
candidates.question_twi: M'ntomato nnua rewo na mede nsu hyɛ won. Dɛn na ɛhia?
candidates.answer_twi: Nwonwon a ɛba wɔ nsuo a wode hyɛ won akyi no betumi yɛ bacteria nwiinwii yadeɛ anaa fusarium yadeɛ wilt — yadeɛ a ɛfiri asase mu. Twa tibo no — sɛ mu yɛ ɛda anaa nsuo pue a, ɛyɛ wilt yadeɛ. Yi nnua a wɔayarɛ no fi afuo mu na sesa nnuaba mfe 2-3.

candidates.question_en: What is a nursery and when should I use one?
candidates.answer_en: A nursery is a protected area where seeds are germinated and young plants are raised before transplanting to the main field. Use a nursery for: small expensive seeds like tomato, pepper, and onion; crops that need a head start before rains; and crops where seedling survival in the field is uncertain. Nurseries save seeds and improve stand establishment.
candidates.question_twi: Nursery yɛ dɛn na bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛde di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Nursery yɛ beae a wɔbɔ ho ban a wɔde aba gu mu na wɔtete nnua nketewa ansa na wɔde akɔdua wɔ afuo kɛse no mu. Fa nursery di dwuma ma: aba nketewa a ne boɔ yɛ den te sɛ ntomate, mako, ne gyeene; nnɔbae a ɛhia sɛ wofi ase ntɛm ansa na osuo aba; ne nnɔbae a ɛnyɛ awiegye sɛ ɛbɛtena ase wɔ afuo no mu. Nursery boa ma aba no yɛ yiye na ɛma nnua no nyini yiye.

items.question_en: Can I grow different crops together on the same farm?
items.answer_en: Yes, mixing vegetables is called companion planting and can be very beneficial. Good combinations include tomatoes with basil (basil repels tomato pests), maize with beans and squash (the Three Sisters method), onions with carrots (they repel each other's pests), and marigolds with any vegetable (repels many insects). Avoid planting crops from the same family together as they share pests.
items.question_twi: Metumi adua nnɔbae ahorow pii wɔ afuo koro mu anaa?
items.answer_twi: Aane, nnɔbae a wudua no bom yɛ companion planting na ɛboa pii. Nnuaba a wɔyɛ adwuma yie wɔ bom ne ntomato ne basil (basil kora ntomato adwummakers ase), aburow ne abɔdweɛ ne squash (Three Sisters anammɔn), gyene ne carrot (wɔkora wɔn ho adwummakers ase), na marigold ne nnuan biara (ɛkora adwummakers bebree ase). Hwɛ yiye na woannua nnɔbae a ɛwɔ abusua koro mu wɔ beae koro efisɛ wɔtaa nya yare koro.

candidates.question_en: What is intercropping and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Intercropping means growing two or more crops together on the same land. For example, maize with cowpea. Benefits include better land use, the legume adds nitrogen to the soil, reduced pest pressure, and income from two crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛyɛ intercropping na ɛboa?
candidates.answer_twi: Intercropping kyerɛ sɛ wokura nnuaba abien anaa dodo wɔ asase koro so. Nhwɛso so, aburow ne abɔdweɛ. Mfaaso ho ne: asase ho dwuma pa, abɔdweɛ de nitrogen ma asase, adwummakers hia sua, na nnuaba abien firi sika.

candidates.question_en: What crop rotation plan is suitable for Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: A good crop rotation for Ghana is to plant legumes like cowpea or groundnut after cereals like maize or sorghum. Legumes fix nitrogen into the soil improving fertility naturally. A 3-year rotation could be maize in year one, cowpea in year two, and cassava or vegetables in year three. Avoid planting the same crop family in the same field two seasons in a row as this builds up pests and diseases specific to that crop.
candidates.question_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu pa wɔ Ghana ne de legumes te sɛ bɔde anaa groundnut to mu akyi cereals te sɛ aburoɔ anaa sorghum. Legumes de nitrogen ka asase mu a ɛboa asase aduan pa. Mfe mmiɛnsa rotation bɛtumi ayɛ: aburoɔ mfe a ɛdi kan mu, bɔde mfe mmienu mu, na bankye anaa nnuaba mfe mmiɛnsa mu. Gye wo ho fi de nnuaba nhyiamu koro to mu wɔ afuom koro mfe mmienu so kwa efisɛ eyi ma adwummaker ne yadeɛ a ɛfa nhyiamu no ho kɔ so.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds on my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Control weeds by timely hand weeding in the first 3-4 weeks after planting, using mulch to suppress weeds, and applying pre-emergence herbicides at planting. The first weeding must be done within 2-3 weeks after crop emergence.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ nhaban a ɛntia asɛm yie a mennya sika koraa?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nhaban foforo ase wɔ nnafoa 3-4 a aburow pue akyi no mu, fa mulch kora nhaban foforo ase, na de herbicide to ansa na nnuaba pue. Nhaban foforo tia a ɛdi ɛkan no yɛ wɔ nnafoa 2-3 mu a nnuaba pue akyi.

candidates.question_en: How can I store maize to prevent aflatoxin?
candidates.answer_en: Dry maize properly to below 13% moisture before storage. Store in clean, dry, well-ventilated structures. Use hermetic bags to prevent insect infestation. Avoid mixing good grain with damaged grain.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meguina m'aburow na aflatoxin dze nka ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Yaw aburow yie na ɛsua 13% nsuku ansa na waguina. Guina wɔ fie a ɛhoro, yera, na ɛwɔ mframa pa. Fa hermetic bags sɛ adwummakers nni mu. Bɔ hwɛ ka aburo pa ne aburo a ɛasɛe no bom.

candidates.question_en: What is crop rotation and why is it important?
candidates.answer_en: Crop rotation means growing different crops on the same land each season. For example, grow maize in season 1, then cowpea in season 2. This breaks pest cycles, improves soil fertility, and increases yields.
candidates.question_twi: Dea ɛyɛ sɛ wosesa nnuaba gu asase mu na adɛn na ɛyɛ papa?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba sesae kyerɛ sɛ wokura ahorow nnuaba wɔ asase koro so bere biara. Nhwɛso so, kura aburow bere 1 mu, afei kura abɔdweɛ wɔ bere 2 mu. Eyi bubu adwummakers ntam, yɛ asase mu aduan ho nhwiren na ɛma nnuaba da sor dodo.

candidates.question_en: How can I start farming in Ghana with little money?
candidates.answer_en: Start small with crops that need minimal investment like vegetables, maize or cassava. Begin with what land you have access to. Use family labour initially to reduce costs. Join a farmer-based organisation for access to group inputs and credit. Apply for the government Planting for Food and Jobs programme which provides subsidized seeds and fertilizer. Reinvest your profits to gradually expand your farm each season.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana a sika ketewa wɔ me nkyɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi ase ketewa de nnuaba a sika ketewa na ɛhia te sɛ nnuaba, aburoɔ anaa bankye. Fi ase wɔ asase a wowɔ ho. De wo fie ho adwuma ansa na ɛhia sika. Ka okuafo kuo ho sɛ wɔde group inputs ne credit nya. Bisa aban Planting for Food and Jobs programme a wɔde subsidized aba ne ferefere to. De wo mfaso no to wo afuom no so bere biara ma ɛkɔ so kɛse tenten tenten.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Weed at 2 to 3 weeks and again at 6 to 8 weeks after planting. These two weeding operations are critical because early weeds compete directly with young maize for nutrients and water. You can use hand weeding with a hoe or apply pre-emergence herbicides like atrazine before the maize germinates. Mulching between rows also suppresses weeds.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ nhaban foforo a wɔ me aburoɔ afuom mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo nnansa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa akyi na bio wɔ nnansa nsia kɔ nwɔtwe akyi a wode aba to mu. Adwuma nhaban foforo yi mmienu no ho hia pa ara efisɛ nhaban foforo a ɛdi kan no di aburoɔ foforo bere a ɛwɔ ho ferefere ne nsuo ho brε. Wobetumi de nsa ne atia yam yi nhaban foforo anaa de herbicides a wɔfre no atrazine to ho ansa na aburoɔ aba atua fɔw. Mulching nsɛm ntam mu nso boa nhaban foforo ho.

candidates.question_en: What is the Ghana Commodity Exchange and how can farmers use it?
candidates.answer_en: The Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) is a formal marketplace where farmers can sell their produce at transparent, standardized prices. To use it: register as a member through an accredited warehouse operator, store your certified grain in a GCX-accredited warehouse, receive a warehouse receipt that you can sell at the exchange or use as collateral for a bank loan. It is especially good for maize, soya, and sorghum.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Ghana Commodity Exchange yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) yɛ aguabasa a ɛwɔ ho yie a okuafo tumi tɔn wɔn nnuaba wɔ boɔ a wɔada adi ne a wɔasiesie. Sɛ wohwehwɛ fa di dwuma a, kyerɛw wo din wɔ accredited warehouse operator ho, guina wo nnuaba a wɔakyerɛw wɔ GCX-accredited warehouse mu, nya warehouse receipt a wobetumi tɔn wɔ exchange no mu anaa de kɔ ban ho sɛ collateral. Ɛyɛ adwuma yie pa ara ma aburow, soya, ne ɔtɛ.

items.question_en: When should groundnuts be harvested for seed?
items.answer_en: Harvest when the pods are mature and the crop shows the expected maturity signs for the variety. Select healthy, well-filled pods for seed.
items.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ megye nkatie a mede bɛyɛ aba?
items.answer_twi: Gye nkatie bere a aba no awie ase na nnɔbae no akyerɛ maturity a ɛfata. Paw nkatie a ɛho tew na aba no ahyɛ mu yie ma aba.

candidates.question_en: How should I handle harvested legumes before storage?
candidates.answer_en: Remove dirt and damaged material, dry the grain thoroughly, cool it before sealing, and keep the storage area dry and clean.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ legumes a magye no ansa na waguina?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi dɔte ne nneɛma a asɛe, yow aba no yie, ma ɛnwunu ansa na woato no mu na ma guina beae no nyɛ yera na ɛho tew.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce aflatoxin risk in groundnut?
candidates.answer_en: Use good-quality seed, manage field stress, harvest carefully, dry pods thoroughly and store them in clean, dry conditions.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate aflatoxin haw so wɔ nkatie mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa aba pa, hwɛ ɔhaw a ɛwɔ afuo mu, gye nkatie no yie, yow wɔn paa na guina wɔ beae a ɛho tew na ɛyɛ yera.
