candidates.question_en: How can I improve groundnut flowering and pod formation?
candidates.answer_en: Choose well-drained soil, remove heavy weeds and prepare a fine seedbed without excessive compaction.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama nkatie nhwiren ne aba no ayɛ yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw asase a nsuo tumi firi mu, yi nwura a ɛdɔɔso na siesie asase no yie nanso mfa mfrafra asase no dodo.

candidates.question_en: Can legumes be grown with cereals?
candidates.answer_en: Yes. Intercropping some legumes with cereals can use space efficiently and diversify production, but the crops need compatible spacing and management.
candidates.question_twi: Legumes tumi nyin ne cereals bom anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane. Wobetumi adua legumes ne cereals bom ma wɔde beae no di dwuma yie na ɛma nnɔbae ahorow. Nanso ɛsɛ sɛ wɔn ntam ne wɔn nhwɛsoɔ hyia.

candidates.question_en: How do legumes improve soil fertility in a mixed farming system?
candidates.answer_en: Legumes can contribute to soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation and can help diversify cropping systems.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na legumes boa ma asase yɛ dɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Legumes tumi de nitrogen boa asase so fa biological nitrogen fixation ho na ɛma nnɔbae ahorow nyɛ baako pɛ.

items.question_en: How can I protect banana bunches from physical damage?
items.answer_en: Use suitable bunch-management practices, avoid rough handling and keep pathways clear during field operations.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn abɔ banana bunches ho ban fi mpirapira ho?
items.answer_twi: Fa bunch management akwan a ɛfata, mfa ahoɔden nyɛ wɔn ho adwuma na ma akwan a wɔfa so yɛ adwuma no ho tew.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce wind damage in plantain?
candidates.answer_en: Use suitable spacing, maintain healthy plants and consider wind protection where strong winds are common.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mframa sɛe so wɔ plantain mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa spacing a ɛfata, ma nnua no nyɛ ahoɔden na susuw wind protection ho wɔ mmeae a mframa den taa ba.

candidates.question_en: How should plantain bunches be transported?
candidates.answer_en: Handle bunches carefully, protect them from crushing and avoid unnecessary dropping during loading and transport.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn de plantain bunches akɔ gua a ɛnsɛe?
candidates.answer_twi: Kura bunches no yie, bɔ wɔn ho ban fi crushing ho na mma wɔntɔ fam bere a woreloading ne transport.

candidates.question_en: How can I control Black Sigatoka disease in plantain?
candidates.answer_en: Black sigatoka is a serious fungal disease causing black streaks on leaves that eventually kill them. Control it by removing and destroying affected leaves regularly, ensuring good drainage, maintaining adequate spacing for air circulation, and applying recommended fungicides like Mancozeb or Dithane every 2 to 3 weeks during wet seasons. Use resistant varieties like Apantu and FHIA-21 where available.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ black sigatoka yadeɛ ho wɔ boɔde ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Black sigatoka yɛ fungal yadeɛ kɛse a ɛma nhaban no yɛ black na ɛkum wɔn awiei pɛ. Boa ho de yi na sɛe nhaban a yadeɛ aba ho daadaa, hwɛ sɛ nsuo tew yie, kora ahodɔ pa sɛ mframa fa mu yie, na de fungicides a wɔagyae so te sɛ Mancozeb anaa Dithane hware mprɛnsa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa mu nsuo berɛ. De varieties a wɔagyae so te sɛ Apantu ne FHIA-21 fa to mu wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can I select healthy plantain suckers?
candidates.answer_en: Choose vigorous, disease-free planting material from healthy mother plants and avoid suckers showing unusual damage or weakness.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw plantain suckers a wɔyɛ ahoɔden?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw planting material a ɛyɛ ahoɔden na yare nni ho, na ɛfiri mother plants a ɛyɛ sehat. Mfa suckers a asɛe anaa ayɛ mmerɛ.

candidates.question_en: What is the difference between plantain farming and banana farming?
candidates.answer_en: Plantain and banana are closely related but differ in use and management. Plantain is starchier, larger and must be cooked before eating. Banana is sweeter, eaten raw and matures faster. Banana requires more water and is more sensitive to drought. Plantain is more tolerant of less fertile soils. Both need similar disease management. Commercial banana farming for export requires higher standards of pest and disease control.
candidates.question_twi: Nte sɛn bɛn na ɛwɔ boɔde adwuma ne kwadu adwuma ntam?
candidates.answer_twi: Boɔde ne kwadu yɛ bɔhyɛ bɔhyɛ nanso wɔyɛ so sɛ wɔde wɔn ho na wɔhwɛ wɔn so nte. Boɔde wɔ starch pii, ɛso sen, na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhyehye ansa na wɔbɛdi. Kwadu dɛ, na wɔdi atoa, na ɛtwa so ntɛm. Kwadu hia nsuo pii na ɛyɛ amrane wɔ bone ho. Boɔde tumi gyina asase a ferefere nni mu pii. Wɔn mmienu hia yadeɛ hwɛ koro. Kwadu kɛse adwuma ma export hia adwummaker ne yadeɛ hwɛ pa sen.

candidates.question_en: How can I export my farm produce from Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: To export farm produce from Ghana register your business with GIPC if it involves foreign investment, obtain an export licence from the Ghana Export Promotion Authority, ensure your produce meets destination country phytosanitary standards by getting certificates from the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate under MOFA, have your produce inspected by Ghana Standards Authority, work with a licensed freight forwarder for logistics, and target markets with high demand for Ghanaian products like the EU for chilli and pineapple and the UK for yam and plantain.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mede me afuom nnuaba tɔ amansan foforɔ fi Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛde wo afuom nnuaba tɔ amansan foforɔ fi Ghana a, si wo adwuma ho wɔ GIPC sɛ obi fi amansan foforɔ wɔ mu, gye export licence fi Ghana Export Promotion Authority, hwɛ sɛ wo nnuaba to country a wɔde kɔ phytosanitary standards mu de certificates fi Plant Protection ne Regulatory Services Directorate wɔ MOFA ase, ma Ghana Standards Authority hwɛ wo nnuaba so, ka licensed freight forwarder ho ma logistics, na tia markets a wɔpɛ Ghana nneɛma pii te sɛ EU ma pepper ne pineapple ne UK ma bayerɛ ne boɔde.

candidates.question_en: What causes small plantain bunches and how can I increase their size?
candidates.answer_en: Small plantain bunches are caused by poor soil fertility, water stress during bunch formation, heavy pest or disease pressure especially black sigatoka, overcrowded suckers competing for nutrients, using inferior planting material, and not removing dead leaves promptly. Improve bunch size by applying NPK and potassium fertilizer regularly, irrigating during dry spells, controlling sigatoka with fungicide, desuckering to one sucker per stool, and using quality sword suckers for planting.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn ma boɔde ntama yɛ ketewa na dɛn na menyɛ sɛ ɛntɔ me?
candidates.answer_twi: Boɔde ntama nketewa ba efisɛ asase aduan hia, nsuo ahia bere a ntama reyɛ, adwummaker ne yadeɛ a ɛhia pii a black sigatoka ka ho, suckers pii a wɔdi ferefere ho brε, planting material mfa ho, na amma wo nhaban a ɛawu asiesie ntɛm. Boa ntama bo kɔ so de de NPK ne potassium ferefere to ho bere biara, quench bone berɛ mu, boa sigatoka ho de fungicide hware, desuckering kɔsi sucker baako biara stool, na de sword suckers pa to mu.

candidates.question_en: How should I manage suckers in a plantain farm?
candidates.answer_en: Manage suckers by allowing only one follower sucker per stool at a time. Remove excess suckers using a sharp spade cutting them off at soil level. Choose the best positioned sword sucker as the follower. After harvest of the main bunch cut the harvested stem down to 1 metre and let it die naturally. A well-managed stool can produce continuously for 5 to 7 years. Fertilize each stool with 100 to 200 grams of NPK twice a year for sustained production.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ suckers sɛ me boɔde afuom ayɛ adwuma yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ suckers de ma sucker baako pɛ tena wɔ stool biara bere koro. Yi suckers a ɛboro so de spade akyer wɔ asase so. Yi sword sucker a ɛtete yie ma ɛyɛ follower. Ntama kɛse yi akyi twa abɔ a woyii no kɔsi metre baako na ma no wu ankasa. Stool a wohwɛ so yie tumi de nnuaba ba daadaa mfe 5 kɔ 7. De NPK gram 100 kɔ 200 to stool biara ho mprɛn mmienu biara afe ma nnoa tena so.

items.question_en: How can I prevent diseases in farmed fish?
items.answer_en: Prevent fish diseases by maintaining good water quality with regular testing and water changes, avoiding overstocking, feeding quality feed without overfeeding, quarantining new fish for 2 weeks before introducing to main ponds, not mixing fish from unknown sources, and removing dead fish immediately. Common fish diseases include ich (white spot), gill diseases and bacterial infections which can be treated with salt baths and approved veterinary medications.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ yadeɛ annyi me apataa ho?
items.answer_twi: Gye apataa yadeɛ fi ho de kora nsuo pa na hwɛ so bere biara na sesa nsuo, gye wo ho fi to pii, didi aduan pa na amma ɛnboro so, de apataa foforɔ sie nnansa mmienu ansa na wode ka ho wɔ ponds kɛse, mma apataa fi hɔ a wonnim fi ka ho, na yi apataa a awu ntɛm. Yadeɛ a ɛtaa ba apataa ho ne ich (white spot), gill yadeɛ ne bacterial infections a wubetumi ahu wɔn ho de salt baths ne nkuru a wɔagyae so.

candidates.question_en: How can I construct a low-cost earthen fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with clay soil that holds water well, near a reliable water source. Mark out the pond area typically 20 by 25 metres. Dig to a depth of 1.5 to 2 metres with sloping sides for stability. Build an inlet pipe to bring water in and an outlet pipe at the deepest point to drain. Pack the dikes firmly to prevent leaks. Fill with water and leave for 2 weeks to cure and establish algae before stocking. The total cost including excavation for a 500 square metre pond is typically GHS 3,000 to 6,000.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ earthen apataa pond a bo sua?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ clay asase a ɛkora nsuo yie, bɛn nsuo kwan pa. Kyerɛ pond area a ɛtaa yɛ metres 20 ne 25. Boro kɔsi tia metres 1.5 kɔ 2 a ho mfimfini slopes wɔ gyinae ho. Tu inlet pipe sɛ nsuo aba mu na outlet pipe wɔ tia no so sɛ nsuo fa mu. Hyehye dikes no yie sɛ nsuo anyi. Ma nsuo kɔ mu na gyina nnansas mmienu sɛ ɛtena na algae ntua fɔw ansa na wode apataa to. Bo nyinaa a excavation ka ho ma pond a square metres 500 wɔ mu taa yɛ GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent overcrowding in a fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Stock according to the pond's capacity and monitor fish growth, water quality and available oxygen.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpataa dodo so wɔ pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa dodow a pond no tumi soa no gu mu na hwɛ mpataa nyin, nsuo quality ne oxygen a ɛwɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: How much does it cost to start a small fish farm in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Starting a small commercial fish farm in Ghana with two earthen ponds of 500 square metres each costs approximately GHS 15,000 to 25,000 including pond construction, fingerlings, feed for one cycle, and basic equipment. A plastic tank fish farm can be started for GHS 8,000 to 15,000. The main ongoing costs are fish feed which accounts for 60 to 70 percent of total production cost. With good management you can make a profit from the first cycle.
candidates.question_twi: Sika ahe na ɛyɛ papa sɛ mefi ase apataa adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apataa adwuma ketewa kɛse fi ase wɔ Ghana de earthen ponds mmienu a square metres 500 biara wɔ mu ho teetee GHS 15,000 kɔ 25,000 a pond yɛ, fingerlings, aduan wɔ cycle baako mu, ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ papa. Plastic tank apataa adwuma wobetumi de GHS 8,000 kɔ 15,000 fi ase. Nneɛma a ɛkyere daadaa a ɛkɔ so pii ne apataa aduan a ɛyɛ adwuma agyapade 60 kɔ 70 percent. Sɛ woyɛ adwuma pa a, wobetumi anya mfaso wɔ cycle a ɛdi kan mu.

candidates.question_en: When should I harvest tilapia?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest tilapia when they reach market size of 300 to 500 grams which typically takes 5 to 6 months from fingerling stage. Monitor growth by sampling fish monthly using a net. Harvest in the early morning when water temperature is cool to reduce fish stress. Partial harvesting at 4 months removes larger fish and allows smaller ones to grow. Sell fresh fish immediately or ice them for transport to market.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na meyiyɛ me tilapia apataa?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi tilapia bere a wɔkɔ si dwa kɛse a nnɔho 300 kɔ 500 gram a ɛtaa kyɛ mfee 5 kɔ 6 fi fingerling mu. Hwɛ sɛ apataa rebɛbo yie de sample apataa bere biara de net. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo berɛ dɛ sɛ apataa nhunu. Partial yi wɔ mfee nnan mu yi apataa kɛse na ma nketewa bo sɔ. Tɔ apataa fofor ntɛm anaa de ice ka ho ma akɔ dwa.

candidates.question_en: What should I do if fish stop feeding suddenly?
candidates.answer_en: Check water quality, temperature, oxygen, recent weather, feed quality and signs of disease before increasing feed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ sɛ mpataa gyae di aduane ntɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsuo quality, ɔhyew, oxygen, weather a aba foforo, feed quality ne yare ho nsɛnkyerɛnne ansa na woama feed no so.

candidates.question_en: What is the best way to harvest fish from a pond?
candidates.answer_en: The best harvesting method depends on whether you are doing partial or complete harvest. For partial harvest use a seine net to selectively remove larger fish leaving smaller ones to grow. For complete harvest drain the pond partially then use nets to remove all fish. Harvest early morning when water is cool. Have containers ready with clean water or ice to keep fish alive or fresh. Weigh and record your harvest for business records. Never use chemicals or electricity to harvest as these are illegal and harmful.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛkwan bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ meyiyɛ apataa fi pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛkwan a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wuyiyɛ no kyɛ sɛ partial anaa complete harvest na woyɛ. Ma partial harvest de seine net yi apataa kɛse a wɔbɛ na ma nketewa tena so bo sɔ. Ma complete harvest sua nsuo ketewa fi pond mu afei de nets yi apataa nyinaa. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo dɛ. Ma containers a nsuo foforɔ anaa ice wɔ mu sɛ apataa aguina anaa tena foforɔ. Bu na kora wo harvest ho sɛ adwuma nsɛm. Mma wo mpo de chemicals anaa electricity yiyɛ efisɛ ɛnyɛ nea mmara gyina so na ɛyɛ bɔne.

candidates.question_en: How should a fish farmer keep pond records?
candidates.answer_en: Record stocking date and number, feed used, mortalities, water-quality observations, treatments, harvest weight and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛw fish pond records?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw stocking da ne dodow, feed a wode dii dwuma, mpataa a awuwu, nsuo quality nsɛm, ayaresa, harvest duru ne tɔn.

items.question_en: How many eggs can a good layer produce in a year?
items.answer_en: A good commercial layer hen like Lohmann Brown or Hy-Line can produce 280 to 320 eggs per year under good management. In Ghana with challenges of heat and disease, expect 200 to 260 eggs per year under average management. Egg production starts declining after 72 weeks of age. After this point, evaluate whether to cull the flock and start with new chicks or continue with the declining layers.
items.question_twi: Tamma ahe na layer akoko gu wɔ afe baako mu?
items.answer_twi: Layer kɛse pa te sɛ Lohmann Brown anaa Hy-Line tumi gu tamma 280 kɔ 320 afe baako mu sɛ wohwɛ so yie. Wɔ Ghana a berɛhyɛ ne yadeɛ yɛ den a, gyina tamma 200 kɔ 260 afe baako mu sɛ wohwɛ so yie kakra. Tamma gu a ɛkɔ so huna wɔ nnansas 72 akyi. Wɔ saa bere no, twe wo adwene ho sɛ kum flock no na fi ase de chicks foforɔ anaa gyina so de layers a ɛhuna no.

candidates.question_en: How can I increase egg production in layers?
candidates.answer_en: For maximum egg production ensure 16 hours of light daily using artificial lighting, maintain temperature between 18 and 24 degrees Celsius, provide layer mash with 16 to 17 percent protein and added calcium for strong shells, ensure clean water always, control parasites and disease through regular vaccination and deworming, collect eggs three times daily, keep stress low by avoiding sudden disturbances, and cull poor layers that consistently produce below average.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tamma gu akoko sɛ wɔagu pii?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ akoko gu tamma pii a, hwɛ sɛ kanea da wɔ mu dɔn 16 de artificial light, kora berɛ wɔ degrees 18 ne 24 Celsius ntam, de layer mash a protein 16 kɔ 17 percent ne calcium a ɛhia ma tamma ho den na ka ho, de nsuo pa to mu bere nyinaa, boa parasites ne yadeɛ ho de hware ne wia adwummaker bere biara, pam tamma mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa biara da, ma anigyidie sua de gye wo ho fi nka kɔkɔɔkɔ, na kum layers a wɔgu nketewa bere nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How can I manage heat stress in chickens?
candidates.answer_en: Heat stress is common in Ghana and reduces growth rate and egg production. Manage it by ensuring good ventilation in the poultry house, providing cool fresh water frequently, installing foggers or sprinklers on the roof, feeding in the cooler parts of the day morning and evening, reducing stocking density during hot seasons, adding vitamin C and electrolytes to water during extreme heat, and considering open-sided housing designs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ berɛhyɛ den a ɛba me akoko ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Berɛhyɛ den taa ba wɔ Ghana na ɛhia boɛ a aba nhia na tamma nhia. Boa ho de hwɛ sɛ mframa fa akoko fie mu yie, de nsuo dɛ foforɔ to mu bere biara, si foggers anaa sprinklers wɔ fie no atifi so, didi wɔ berɛ dɛ mu anɔpa ne anwumere, sua akoko a wɔwɔ mu wɔ berɛhyɛ bere, de vitamin C ne electrolytes ka nsuo mu wɔ hyehyɛ den bere, na twe wo adwene ho open-sided housing nhyiamu.

candidates.question_en: What housing system is best for layer chickens in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: The best housing for layers in Ghana's climate is the open-sided or naturally ventilated house. Use wire mesh or wooden slats on the sides for maximum airflow. Orient the house east to west so the long side faces north and south to reduce direct sunlight. Provide a sloped roof with good overhang. Install battery cages at 3 tiers for commercial production or deep litter floor for smaller flocks. Ensure 0.2 square metres per bird for floor housing and 450 square cm per bird for cages.
candidates.question_twi: Housing nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara ma layers wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Housing a ɛhia pa ara ma layers wɔ Ghana berɛ a ɛwɔ ne open-sided anaa naturally ventilated fie. De wire mesh anaa wooden slats to ho mframa nsa sɛ mframa fa mu yie. De fie no sie east kɔ west sɛ ho tenten so hyɛ north ne south anim sɛ owia ankasa annhyɛ mu. De roof a ɛtɔ yie ne overhang pa si. Si battery cages a tiers mmiɛnsa wɔ mu ma adwuma kɛse anaa deep litter floor ma flocks nketewa. Hwɛ sɛ square metres 0.2 wɔ nnomaa baako ho ma floor housing ne square cm 450 biara nnomaa ho ma cages.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent Newcastle disease in poultry?
candidates.answer_en: Newcastle disease is the most serious threat to poultry in Ghana. Prevent it through strict vaccination using Lasota vaccine at day 7, day 21 and every 2 months thereafter. Keep visitors away from your poultry house, disinfect equipment and footwear before entering, quarantine new birds for 2 weeks, buy birds from certified sources only, and cull sick birds immediately. There is no treatment for Newcastle disease once birds are infected.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ Newcastle yadeɛ annya me akoko?
candidates.answer_twi: Newcastle yadeɛ ne akoko tia a ɛtaa yɛ den paa wɔ Ghana. Gye wo ho fi mu de Lasota hware aba ahyɛ so mu da 7, da 21 na mprɛn mmienu biara wɔ saa akyi. Ma ahofipa anyɛ kwan kɔ wo akoko fie, hware nneɛma ne nan so ansa na wukɔ mu, kora nnomaa foforɔ wɔ baabi foforo nnansas mmienu, gye nnomaa fi hɔ a wɔakyerɛw so pɛ, na kum nnomaa a wayarɛ ntɛm. Newcastle yadeɛ nni dawuro bere a nnomaa no anya mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I start a small poultry farm at home?
candidates.answer_en: To start a small home poultry farm: decide on type (layers for eggs or broilers for meat), build or buy a simple wooden or wire coop with shade and good ventilation, start with 10-20 birds, provide clean water and commercial feed, vaccinate birds at the recommended ages, keep the coop clean, and record feeds, deaths, and egg production. Start small and scale as you learn.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesi akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ si akrɔma afuo ketewa wɔ fie: paw ahodoɔ (layers ma kosua anaa broilers ma nam), si anaa tɔ dua anaa wire fie a ewim brɛ ne mframa pue mu yie, fi akrɔma 10-20, de nsuo horo ne aduan a wɔtɔ ma wɔn, de akrɔma kɔ yadeɛ dawuro bere a ɛsɛ, kora fie no horo, na kora aduan, wuu, ne kosua ho nsɛm. Fi ketewa na fa dodo so bere a wosua.

candidates.question_en: What is the Newcastle disease vaccination schedule for chickens?
candidates.answer_en: The standard Newcastle disease vaccination schedule in Ghana is Lasota live vaccine eye or nose drop at day 7, Lasota booster at day 21, and then Lasota every 2 months thereafter. For layers continue every 2 months throughout the laying period. Use inactivated oil-emulsion Newcastle vaccine at 8 weeks for additional protection especially in high-risk areas. Store vaccines at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and use within the expiry date. Never vaccinate sick birds.
candidates.question_twi: Newcastle yadeɛ vaccination schedule bɛn na ɛhia wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Newcastle yadeɛ vaccination schedule pa wɔ Ghana ne Lasota live vaccine ani anaa afi drops wɔ da 7, Lasota booster wɔ da 21, na Lasota bere biara mprɛn mmienu mu saa akyi. Ma layers tena so mprɛn mmienu mu so wɔ tamma gu bere nyinaa. De inactivated oil-emulsion Newcastle vaccine to ho wɔ nnansas nwɔtwe sɛ ɛboa hwɛ so a ɛhia pii wɔ hɔ a ɛyɛ den. Guina vaccines wɔ degrees 2 kɔ 8 Celsius na de fi mu ansa na bere a wɔakyerɛw so abu. Mma wo mpo hware nnomaa a wayarɛ so.

candidates.question_en: What feed should I give broiler chickens?
candidates.answer_en: Feed broilers starter crumbles for the first 2 weeks with 22 to 24 percent protein, then grower pellets with 18 to 20 percent protein from week 3 to 5, and finisher pellets with 16 to 18 percent protein in the final weeks. Provide fresh clean water at all times. Popular feed brands in Ghana include Darko Farms, Akate Wura and Ghana Feedmill feeds. Feed represents 70 percent of your production cost so buying quality feed is critical.
candidates.question_twi: Aduan bɛn na mede ma me broiler akoko?
candidates.answer_twi: De starter crumbles a protein 22 kɔ 24 percent wɔ mu ma broilers nnansas mmienu a ɛdi kan, afei grower pellets a protein 18 kɔ 20 percent wɔ mu wɔ nnansa mmiɛnsa kɔ num, na finisher pellets a protein 16 kɔ 18 percent wɔ mu wɔ nnansas a etwa to. De nsuo fofor pa to mu bere nyinaa. Feed brands a wɔpɛ wɔ Ghana ne Darko Farms, Akate Wura na Ghana Feedmill feeds. Aduan yɛ wo adwuma agyapade 70 percent enti gye aduan pa hia.

candidates.question_en: What are the common diseases affecting poultry in Ghana and how can they be prevented?
candidates.answer_en: Common poultry diseases in Ghana include Newcastle Disease, Gumboro (Infectious Bursal Disease), and Fowl Pox. Prevention includes vaccination, good hygiene, biosecurity measures such as limiting visitors and controlling movement, and proper sanitation of poultry houses.
candidates.question_twi: Yare bɛn na ɛtaa yɛ akokɔ wɔ Ghana na yɛbɛyɛ dɛn atua ano?
candidates.answer_twi: Akokɔ yare a ɛtaa ba wɔ Ghana ne Newcastle Disease, Gumboro (Infectious Bursal Disease), ne Fowl Pox. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wotua ano a, ɛsɛ sɛ wode nnuru bɔ wɔn, hwɛ yiye wɔ ahwehwɛde ho, na wode ahobammɔ ho nhyehyɛe di dwuma te sɛ ahɔho a wobɛtew wɔn so ne akokɔdan mu nnuru a wobɛtwa.

items.question_en: How do I harvest and process shea nuts properly?
items.answer_en: Collect fallen shea fruits from the ground during the harvest season (May to August). Remove the sweet pulp by soaking and washing. Dry the nuts for 1-2 weeks in the sun. Crack the dried shells to get the kernels. Dry kernels further before storing or processing into shea butter. Never dry shea nuts on bare soil or over fire as this reduces butter quality.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye ne yɛ adwuma wɔ nkuto aba?
items.answer_twi: Gye nkuto aba a atu gu asase so wɔ gye bere mu (Ɔbɛnem kwan so Ɔsannaa). Yi asew a ɛda mu wɔ da wɔ nsuo mu na hohoro. Yaw aba no owia mu nnawotwe 1-2. Bubu nkuku a ayaw no sɛ wunya aba no mu ade. Yaw aba mu ade no bio ansa na waguina anaa yɛ nkuto ngo. Mfa nkuto aba yaw wɔ asase firi so anaa ogya so da efisɛ ɛsua ngo ho pa.

candidates.question_en: When should I harvest groundnuts?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest groundnuts when leaves start yellowing. Loosen the soil with a hoe first then pull the whole plant upward. Shake off excess soil and thresh on a clean tarpaulin. Dry pods in the sun for 3-5 days before storage.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye nkatie a aba bi nko?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye nkatie bere a nhaban no redan sika. Fa akɔde fa asase no ho ansa, afei twe nnua no nyinaa sor. Woso asase a aka no afi na bu wɔ tarpaulin horo so. Yaw aba no wɔ owia mu nnafoa 3-5 ansa na waguina.

candidates.question_en: How should I dry my crops after harvesting?
candidates.answer_en: Spread grains on clean tarpaulins or raised drying platforms in the sun. Stir regularly for even drying. Avoid drying on bare soil which introduces dirt and moisture. Grains are dry enough when a handful feels cool not warm and hard seeds do not dent easily.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meyaw m'nnuaba yie akyi a megye wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: To nnuaba wɔ tarpaulin horo anaa platform a ɛda sor wɔ owia mu. Sane wɔn pɛ sɛ wɔyaw pɛ. Bɔ hwɛ yaw wɔ asase firi so efisɛ ɛde fufuo ne nsuo ba mu. Nnuaba yaw yie bere a wo nsa a wode fa no yɛ huru na aba den nyi wɔ nsateaa ase ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: When are mangoes ready for harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Mangoes are ready to harvest when: the fruit changes color from green to yellow, orange, or red depending on variety; the fruit flesh near the seed turns yellow; the fruit gives slightly when gently pressed; and the fruit smells sweet near the stem. For commercial harvest, pick slightly before full ripeness so they ripen during transport.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na mangoro awie ase sɛ megye?
candidates.answer_twi: Mangoro awie ase bere a: aba no resen rere fi akyen kɔ hoho, ɛda, anaa kɔkɔɔ wɔ aba no ahodoɔ so; aba no nnompe a ɛbɛn aba no dan hoho; aba no tumi pii kakra bere a wode fa so pɛ; na aba no nhwiren foforo pue fi tibo ho. Tɔn ho, gye ansa na ɛawi pɛpɛɛpɛ na ɛware wɔ kwan so.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow soybean commercially for profit?
candidates.answer_en: Soybeans are highly profitable legumes. Plant after rains are well established. Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium bacteria before planting (this fixes nitrogen and can triple yields). Space 30-45 cm within rows and 60 cm between rows. Apply phosphorus fertilizer at planting. Weed once at 3 weeks. Harvest when 95% of pods have turned yellow-brown. Dry to 12% moisture before storage. Soybeans have strong demand from oil processors and animal feed manufacturers.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura soya yɛ adwuma sɛ menya sika?
candidates.answer_twi: Soya yɛ abɔdweɛ a ɛde sika ba pa ara. To akyi a osu asi yie. De Bradyrhizobium bacteria ka aba ho ansa na woto (eyi fi nitrogen na ɛtumi ma nnuaba da sor mprɛ mmiɛnsa). Gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 30-45 wɔ ntam ne sɛntimita 60 wɔ nnua so ntam. De phosphorus ferefere to mu bere a wode to. Tia nhaban foforo bere a ɛto so mmiɛnsa no nnawotwe baako. Gye bere a 95% fidie no adan hoho bɔɔ. Yaw kosi 12% nsuku ansa na waguina. Soya hia yɛ kɛse wɔ ngo adwuma kuo ne mmoa aduan adwuma kuo ho.

candidates.question_en: How do I know if my fertilizer is working?
candidates.answer_en: Signs that fertilizer is working include: darker green leaves, faster plant growth, larger leaves, and higher yield compared to unfertilized plots. If plants remain yellowish and grow slowly after 2-3 weeks of fertilizer application, the fertilizer may not have been applied correctly or the soil may have other problems.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menim sɛ m'ferefere yɛ adwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Ahohyenam sɛ ferefere yɛ adwuma ne: nhaban a wɔyɛ tuntum-akyen pa ara, nnuaba a wɔda sor ntɛm, nhaban kɛse, ne nnuaba a wɔda sor dodo sen beae a wɔanto ferefere. Sɛ nnuaba da hoho na wɔda sor brɛ akyi a ferefere to so wiemu 2-3 a, ferefere no beɛ to so yie anaa asase no wɔ nsɛm foforɔ.

candidates.question_en: What is seed priming and how does it help germination?
candidates.answer_en: Seed priming is soaking seeds in water or a special solution for a specific time before planting to improve germination rate, speed, and uniformity. Methods include: hydropriming (soaking in plain water for 6-12 hours then drying before planting), and salt priming (soaking in dilute salt solution). Primed seeds germinate faster and more uniformly, which helps crops establish better especially in marginal soils or unpredictable rainfall.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na seed priming yɛ na ɛboa aba pue sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Seed priming kyerɛ da aba wɔ nsuo anaa aduru a wɔakyerɛ ho bere mu ansa na woto mu sɛ ɛsiesie aba pue rate, ntɛm, ne pɛ. Anammɔn ho ne: hydropriming (da wɔ nsuo foforo mu dapɛn 6-12 na yaw ansa na woto), ne salt priming (da wɔ ɛwa a wɔasusu mu). Aba a wɔaprime no pue ntɛm ne pɛ, eyi boa nnuaba si yie titiriw wɔ asase a enni pa anaa osu a ɛntumi nnim bere mu.

candidates.question_en: What is vermicomposting and how do I start it?
candidates.answer_en: Vermicomposting uses earthworms to break down organic waste into very high-quality compost called vermicompost or worm castings. To start: get a container or build a wooden box, add bedding of moist shredded newspaper or cardboard, add earthworms (red wigglers are best), feed with fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, and eggshells. Avoid meat, dairy, and oily food. Harvest the rich compost from the bottom every 2-3 months.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na vermicomposting yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mesi ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Vermicomposting fa asase nwirɛntwi di dwuma sɛ pɛ nhwiren foforo asennua yɛ compost a ɛwɔ aduan pa pa ara a wɔfre vermicompost anaa worm castings. Sɛ wohwehwɛ si ase: nya nkuku anaa yɛ dua box, de krataa anaa cardboard a wɔatwa twa na wɔapo mu de yɛ mpa, de asase nwirɛntwi hyɛ (red wiggler yɛ pa pa ara), de nnuan ne aba asennua, coffee, ne kosua nkuku hyɛ. Bɔ hwɛ nam, nkyene aduan, ne ngo aduan. Gye compost a ɛwɔ ase hɔ no abosome 2-3 biara.

candidates.question_en: How do I know if my seeds have germinated properly?
candidates.answer_en: Check germination 5-10 days after planting depending on the crop. Good germination means at least 80% of planted seeds have sprouted uniformly. If germination is poor, check if seeds were planted too deep, soil was too dry or waterlogged, temperature was too extreme, or seeds were old. Replant gaps with fresh seeds immediately.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menim sɛ m'aba apue yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛ aba no afifi nna 5-10 akyi a wode agu fam5. Sɛ aba no fifi yiye a, ɛkyerɛ sɛ aba a wode agu fam no 80% pɛ afifi pɛpɛɛpɛ80. Sɛ aba no mfifi yiye a, hwɛ sɛ wode agu fam dodo, asase no yɛ kusuu anaa nsuo dɔɔso wɔ mu, ewim yɛ hye anaa nwunu dodo, anaa aba no dedaw. Fa aba foforo gu mmeae a ɛda hɔ no ntɛm ara.

items.question_en: What is honey harvesting hygiene?
items.answer_en: Use clean equipment, clean containers and hygienic handling so the honey is protected from dirt, smoke and other contamination.
items.question_twi: Dɛn ne ahotew a ɛsɛ wɔ honey gyeɛ mu?
items.answer_twi: Fa adwinnade a ɛho tew, ade a ɛho tew ne ahotew mu di dwuma sɛnea fĩ, wusi ne nneɛma foforo renka honey no.

candidates.question_en: How should honey be stored?
candidates.answer_en: Store honey in clean, food-grade containers in a dry place away from strong odours and excess moisture.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn aguina honey?
candidates.answer_twi: Guina honey wɔ ade a ɛho tew na ɛfata food, wɔ beae yera a hua bɔne ne nsuo dodo nni hɔ.

candidates.question_en: What should I wear when inspecting bees?
candidates.answer_en: Use appropriate protective clothing and equipment designed for beekeeping, including a veil and gloves where needed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mehyɛ bere a merehwɛ nkyene?
candidates.answer_twi: Hyɛ ahobammɔ ntade ne adwinnade a ɛfata beekeeper, a veil ne gloves ka ho sɛ ɛhia.

candidates.question_en: How often should hives be inspected?
candidates.answer_en: Inspect according to the production system and season, focusing on colony health, pests, food stores and hive condition.
candidates.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ beehive?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛnea production system ne bere no te, na hwɛ colony no ahoɔden, mmoawa, aduane a ɛwɔ hɔ ne hive no tebea.

candidates.question_en: How can a beekeeper estimate honey production from hive records?
candidates.answer_en: Record hive locations, inspections, colony strength, treatments, harvest quantities and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛ honey production dodow afi hive kyerɛwtohɔ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw hive baabi, nhwehwɛmu, colony ahoɔden, ayaresa, honey dodow a woagye ne tɔn.

candidates.question_en: Why are flowering plants important for bees?
candidates.answer_en: Bees depend on flowers for nectar and pollen, so a variety of flowering plants can support colony development.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na nhwiren a ɛbɔ aba ho hia ma nkyene?
candidates.answer_twi: Nkyene gye nectar ne pollen fi nhwiren mu, enti nhwiren ahorow a ɛbɔ aba boa colony no nyin.

candidates.question_en: Where should beehives be placed?
candidates.answer_en: Place hives in a quiet, shaded or semi-shaded area with good drainage, access to forage and reasonable protection from disturbance.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛhe na ɛsɛ sɛ mede beehive si?
candidates.answer_twi: Si no wɔ beae a ɛdwo, sunsuma kakra wɔ hɔ, nsuo firi mu yie, nhwiren wɔ ho na nnipa ntɔ no daa.

items.question_en: How should I safely handle sick animals?
items.answer_en: When handling sick animals: wear gloves and wash hands thoroughly after contact, isolate sick animals from healthy ones immediately, do not move sick animals to other farms, contact a veterinary officer for diagnosis before administering treatment, follow withdrawal periods for medicines before slaughter or selling milk, keep records of all treatments given, and dispose of dead animals by deep burial away from water sources.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ mmoa a wɔayarɛ ho yie?
items.answer_twi: Bere a wuhwɛ mmoa a wɔayarɛ ho: fa nsatea nhoma na hohoro wo nsa yie akyi a woka wɔn, yi mmoa a wɔayarɛ fi wɔn a wɔwɔ aho no mu ntɛm, mfa mmoa a wɔayarɛ kɔ afuo foforɔ, ka veterinary officer ho sɛ ɔhunu yadeɛ no ansa na wode dawuro to, bu dawuro withdrawal bere ansa na wokum anaa tɔn nufuo, kora nsɛm a yɛ dawuro nyinaa ho, na de mmoa a awu sisie wɔ asase mu tenten fi nsuo ho.

candidates.question_en: What are the risks of using untreated human or animal waste as fertilizer?
candidates.answer_en: Using raw (untreated) waste carries serious risks: human and animal waste contains pathogens like E.coli, Salmonella, and parasites that can contaminate crops and cause disease in people who eat them. The WHO recommends composting waste for at least 6-12 months or treating with ash or lime before applying to crops. Only apply to soil, never to the edible parts of plants. Always wash hands and produce thoroughly.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɔkɔm wɔ ho wɔ fa onipa anaa mmoa aguare foforo yɛ ferefere?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa aguare foforo (a wonsi amu) di dwuma wɔ ɔkɔm kɛse: onipa ne mmoa aguare wɔ yadeɛ mu te sɛ E.coli, Salmonella, ne adwumakers a ɛtumi haw nnuaba na yɛ nnipa a wɔdi wɔn yadee. WHO ka sɛ compost aguare wiemu 6-12 anaa siesie wɔ nkamfo anaa lime ho ansa na wode to nnuaba so. De to asase pɛ, mde to nnuaba a wɔdi ho da. Hohoro wo nsa ne nnuaba yie daa.

candidates.question_en: How should I dry my crops after harvesting?
candidates.answer_en: Spread grains on clean tarpaulins or raised drying platforms in the sun. Stir regularly for even drying. Avoid drying on bare soil which introduces dirt and moisture. Grains are dry enough when a handful feels cool not warm and hard seeds do not dent easily.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meyaw m'nnuaba yie akyi a megye wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: To nnuaba wɔ tarpaulin horo anaa platform a ɛda sor wɔ owia mu. Sane wɔn pɛ sɛ wɔyaw pɛ. Bɔ hwɛ yaw wɔ asase firi so efisɛ ɛde fufuo ne nsuo ba mu. Nnuaba yaw yie bere a wo nsa a wode fa no yɛ huru na aba den nyi wɔ nsateaa ase ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare my land before planting?
candidates.answer_en: Clear the land of weeds and old crop residues. Plow or dig to loosen the soil to about 20-30 cm deep. Break up large clods and remove stones. Level the surface and apply basal fertilizer or compost before planting.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesiesie asase aba to mu ansa?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi sare ne nnua funu fi asase no so. Twa anaa hwe asase no mu kɔ sɛntimita 20- 30 mu. Bubu asase akɛse no na yi abo. Siesie fam no yiye na fa basal ferefere anaa compost gu so ansa na wode aba no agu fam.

candidates.question_en: How do I calculate the profit from my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Profit equals Total Sales Revenue minus Total Costs. Track all expenses including seeds, fertilizer, labor, transport, and chemicals and all income from sales. Keep a simple notebook or use your phone to record daily expenses.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na melem m'afuo ho mfaaso?
candidates.answer_twi: Mfaaso yɛ sika nyinaa a wogye fi tɔn no minus sika nyinaa a wode. Kora sika nyinaa a wode ka ho te sɛ aba, ferefere, dwumadie, kwan so sika, dawuro, ne sika nyinaa a wogye fi tɔn. Kora krataa ketewa anaa fa wo fɔn de kora da biara ho sika.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm during drought?
candidates.answer_en: During drought, mulch heavily to conserve soil moisture, irrigate if possible, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and avoid adding nitrogen fertilizer which increases water demand. Harvest early-maturing varieties before drought peaks.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ m'afuo so bere a nsuo pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a nsuo pa no, de mulch to asase so yiye sɛ nsukuro wo mu, de nsuo to nnua so sɛ wonya tumi, paw nnuaba aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa so, na bɔ hwɛ de nitrogen ferefere to sɛ ɛma nnuaba hia nsuo dodo. Gye nnuaba a wɔware ntɛm ansa na nsuo pa yɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: How should I plan my farm season?
candidates.answer_en: Season planning should include: checking your budget and available resources, deciding which crops to grow based on market demand and land suitability, calculating input quantities needed and ordering in advance, arranging labor supply for peak periods, planning irrigation if needed, identifying buyers in advance, and reviewing what worked and what didn't in the previous season. Start planning at least 2 months before the season begins.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesiesie bere a ansa na ɛba?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere siesie sɛ aka: hwɛ wo sika ne adenneɛ a wowɔ, paw nnuaba a wobɛkura wɔ aguabasa hia ne asase ho, lem adenneɛ dodo a wohia na tɔ ansa na bere aba, siesie obi a obɛyɛ adwuma wɔ bere a ɛhia dodo, siesie nsuo to sɛ ɛhia, hwehwɛ adeɛtɔfo ansa na bere aba, na hwɛ dea yɛ adwuma yie ne dea anyɛ yie wɔ bere a edi ɛkan. Fi siesie abosome 2 ansa na bere aba.

candidates.question_en: How should I keep records for my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Keep a simple farm diary or notebook. Record planting dates, inputs purchased and costs, labor hired and paid, crop activities, harvest quantities, and sales. Simple mobile apps or voice memos on your phone can help record activities easily.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora m'afuo nsɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora afuo krataa anaa nsɛmpoma ketewa. Kora aba to da, adenneɛ a wotɔ ne won boɔ, dwumadie a wohwɛ ne sika a wode twaa, afuo adwuma, nnuaba a wogye, ne tɔn nsɛm. Mobile apps ketewa anaa kasa nkrataa wɔ wo fɔn no tumi boa wo kora nsɛm yie.

candidates.question_en: How can I test my soil at home without a kit?
candidates.answer_en: Simple home tests: for pH, mix soil with vinegar — if it fizzes the soil is alkaline. Mix soil with baking soda and water — if it fizzes the soil is acidic. For texture, squeeze moist soil — clay soil holds shape, sandy soil crumbles, and loam soil holds shape then crumbles. For organic matter, dark soil has more organic matter than pale soil.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ m'asase wɔ fie a menwɔ kit?
candidates.answer_twi: Fie hwɛ anammɔn ketewa: pH ho, ka asase ne vinegar — sɛ ɛpɔ a asase no yɛ alkaline. Ka asase ne baking soda ne nsuo — sɛ ɛpɔ a asase no yɛ acidic. Nsusuw ho, hia asase nte — amane asase kura ne ho, asintiɛ asase pae, na loam asase kura ne ho na afei pae. Nhwiren foforo ho, asase ɛda wɔ nhwiren foforo dodo sen asase hoho.

items.question_en: What is cold storage and can a small farmer use it?
items.answer_en: Cold storage is refrigerated storage that keeps produce at low temperatures to extend shelf life. Small farmers can access it through: farmer cooperatives that own shared cold storage facilities, government-run cold storage centers, private cold storage services that charge per crate or kilogram, mobile cold storage trucks, and evaporative coolers which are low-cost non-electrical cooling structures.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na cold storage yɛ na okuafo ketewa tumi nya ase anaa?
items.answer_twi: Cold storage yɛ aduan guina a wɔde ntwene nkuma so ma aduan tena yie bere tenten. Okuafo ketewa tumi nya ase wɔ: okuafo cooperative a wɔwɔ cold storage bom, ɔman cold storage centres, onipa hɔ cold storage nnwuma a wɔsua crate anaa kilogram biara, mobile cold storage trucks, ne evaporative coolers a ɛboɔ yɛ ketewa a wɔhyɛ electricity mu.

candidates.question_en: What are the benefits of joining a farmer cooperative?
candidates.answer_en: Benefits of farmer cooperatives include: collective bargaining power for better input prices and higher selling prices, shared access to expensive equipment like tractors and storage facilities, group loans that may be easier to access than individual loans, collective learning and knowledge sharing, risk pooling among members, access to bulk markets that individual farmers cannot reach, and stronger political voice when advocating for farmer interests with government.
candidates.question_twi: Mfaaso bɛn na ɛwɔ ho wɔ si okuafo cooperative?
candidates.answer_twi: Okuafo cooperative mfaaso ho ne: kuo tumi kɛse ma adenneɛ boɔ sua ne tɔn boɔ kɛse, ka egyapade a wɔboɔ yɛ den te sɛ tractor ne guina fie ho bom, kuo ka a ɛtumi yɛ mmerɛ sɛ nya sen onipa ho ka, kuo suahu ne nyansam kyɛ, mfomso sesae wɔ kuo mu, nya aguabasa kɛse a okuafo baako nntumi nkɔ hɔ, ne kuo mu tumi kɛse bere a wɔka okuafo ho nsɛm kyerɛ ɔman.

candidates.question_en: What is contract farming and how does it benefit farmers?
candidates.answer_en: Contract farming is an agreement between a farmer and a buyer before the season starts. The buyer agrees to purchase your produce at a fixed price after harvest. Benefits include guaranteed market, sometimes free inputs on credit, and technical support.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na contract farming yɛ na ɛboa me sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Contract farming yɛ apam a ɛda okuafo ne adeɛtɔ kuo ntam ansa na bere no aba. Adeɛtɔ kuo no ka ho sɛ wɔbɛtɔ wo nnuaba boɔ a wɔaka akyi a wogye. Mfaaso ho ne: aguabasa a wɔadaa ho, adenneɛ a wɔde brɛ wo ka mu mmere bi, ne nnwuma boa.

candidates.question_en: What is Fairtrade certification and what are its benefits for farmers?
candidates.answer_en: Fairtrade certification guarantees farmers a minimum price for their produce that covers production costs plus a social premium that is invested in community development. Benefits include: stable income even when world prices drop, Fairtrade premium funds for schools, health, and infrastructure, access to pre-financing before harvest, better trading relationships, and marketing support. Fairtrade is common in Ghana for cocoa, coffee, and fresh fruit. Contact Fairtrade Africa for information.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Fairtrade kratafa yɛ na mfaaso bɛn na ɛwɔ ho ma okuafo?
candidates.answer_twi: Fairtrade kratafa hɔ kura sɛ okuafo nya boɔ a ɛdata wɔn nnuaba a ɛkata adwuma ho sika ne social premium a wɔde fa oman nkosuo mu. Mfaaso ho ne: sika a ɛda pɛ bere a amanaman boɔ tow, Fairtrade premium sika ma sukuu, yadeɛ, ne nkosuo adwuma, nya sika ansa na wogye nnuaba, adwuma ho apam a ɛyɛ pa, ne adwuma ho boa. Fairtrade pɛ wɔ Ghana ho ma kookoo, kɔfi, ne aba foforo. Ka kyerɛ Fairtrade Africa sɛ wunya nsɛm.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce post-harvest losses on my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Post-harvest losses in Ghana can be up to 40 percent of the harvest. Reduce losses by harvesting at the right maturity stage, handling produce gently to avoid bruising, drying produce properly before storage, using improved hermetic storage bags like GrainPro or metal silos for grains, building ventilated storage for roots and tubers, processing excess produce into value-added products, and connecting to buyers before harvest to reduce time between field and market.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ ho sɛ me nnuaba nhunu yi akyi?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba ahunu akyi yi Ghana bɛtumi akosi 40 percent. Sua ahunu de yi bere a ɛyɛ papa pa, dii wo nnuaba no yie sɛ ɛnsɔre, ma nnuaba no tew yie ansa na woguina mu, de improved hermetic storage bags te sɛ GrainPro anaa metal silos ma aba, tu ventilated storage ma nnɔho biara, de nnuaba a ɛboro so yɛ aduan a bo kɔ so, na ka buyers ho ansa na wuyi sɛ ɛhia bere ketewa wɔ afuom ne dwa ntam.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce post-harvest losses?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest at the right time, handle produce gently to avoid bruising, dry grains properly, store in appropriate conditions, transport in ventilated containers, and sell quickly for perishables. Post-harvest losses in Ghana can reach 30-40%.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi yɛ na m'aduan a megye no akyi anko mpoano?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye nnuaba bere a ɛsɛ, de nnuaba no a eye yie sɛ ɛnhow, yaw nnuaba a ayaw no yie, guina wɔ bae a ɛsɛ, de kɔ bae a mframa tumi pue mu, na tɔn ntɛm sɛ ɛyɛ aduan a ɛsɛe ntɛm. Ghana mu aduan a ɛko aseɛ wɔ gye akyi betumi kɔ 30-40%.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect stored food from rats and mice?
candidates.answer_en: Keep the storage area clean and free of food scraps. Seal all holes and cracks in walls. Use snap traps or approved rodenticides. Store bags on raised platforms away from walls. Cats are also effective.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora m'aduan a maguina fi ɔkra ne okusie ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora guina fie no horo na aduan asennua ntena mu. Popa tumtum ne ɛwɔwɔ nyinaa wɔ bɔ mu. Fa snap traps anaa dawuro a wɔagyei de kum ɔkra. Guina bags wɔ platform a ɛda sor tete akyi. Agyinamoa nso yɛ adwuma pa.

candidates.question_en: What time of day is best for harvesting vegetables?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest vegetables in the early morning when temperatures are cool. This helps produce stay fresh longer. Avoid harvesting in midday heat. For leafy vegetables, harvest with dew still present for crispness.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn wɔ da mu na ɛyɛ ɔkorɔ sɛ wogye nnuan?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye nnuan owia da ano bere a owia hye no ayɛ tirim. Eyi ma nnuan no tena pɛ sen ara. Bɔ hwɛ wɔ awia mu ahuhuro mu gye nnuan. Nhaban nnuan ho, gye won a nsuyiri da won so ara da no ho nkae.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce post-harvest losses in vegetables?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest vegetables early in the morning when cool, handle gently, sort out damaged ones immediately, store in cool ventilated areas, and sell quickly. For leafy vegetables, wrap in damp cloth to extend freshness. Avoid long transport in hot conditions.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi sua nnuan a megye wɔn akyi mpoano?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye nnuan owia da ano bere a ɛhuru, de wɔn pɛ, yi a wɔasɛe ntɛm ara, guina wɔ bae a ɛhuru na mframa pue mu, na tɔn ntɛm. Nhaban nnuan ho, de ntama nte de sɛɛ wɔn sɛ ɛma wɔn tena pɛ.

items.question_en: How can I control tilapia breeding and prevent overcrowding?
items.answer_en: To control tilapia breeding which causes overpopulation and stunted growth, use monosex culture by stocking only male tilapia. Males are identified by having one genital opening while females have two. Obtain male-only fingerlings from certified hatcheries that produce hormonally sex-reversed males. Alternatively introduce a predator species like Nile perch in small numbers to control fry, or use hapas to separate brood stock and collect fry for removal.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tilapia apataa kyerɛ wɔn phula sɛ wobɔ wɔn bɔhyɛ so?
items.answer_twi: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wobɔ tilapia bɔhyɛ so a ɛma nnipa pii ne nnoa hiana no so, de monosex culture to mu de mmarima tilapia pɛ si. Wɔahu mmarima no sɛ wɔwɔ genital ho baako na mmirikyi wɔ mmienu. Gye male-only fingerlings fi certified hatcheries a wɔyɛ hormonally sex-reversed males. Anaa de predator nhyiamu te sɛ Nile perch ketewa to mu sɛ wɔhwɛ fry so, anaa de hapas sɛ wɔkyerɛ brood stock ne pam fry ma wɔyi wɔn.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent overcrowding in a fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Stock according to the pond's capacity and monitor fish growth, water quality and available oxygen.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpataa dodo so wɔ pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa dodow a pond no tumi soa no gu mu na hwɛ mpataa nyin, nsuo quality ne oxygen a ɛwɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I construct a low-cost earthen fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with clay soil that holds water well, near a reliable water source. Mark out the pond area typically 20 by 25 metres. Dig to a depth of 1.5 to 2 metres with sloping sides for stability. Build an inlet pipe to bring water in and an outlet pipe at the deepest point to drain. Pack the dikes firmly to prevent leaks. Fill with water and leave for 2 weeks to cure and establish algae before stocking. The total cost including excavation for a 500 square metre pond is typically GHS 3,000 to 6,000.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ earthen apataa pond a bo sua?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ clay asase a ɛkora nsuo yie, bɛn nsuo kwan pa. Kyerɛ pond area a ɛtaa yɛ metres 20 ne 25. Boro kɔsi tia metres 1.5 kɔ 2 a ho mfimfini slopes wɔ gyinae ho. Tu inlet pipe sɛ nsuo aba mu na outlet pipe wɔ tia no so sɛ nsuo fa mu. Hyehye dikes no yie sɛ nsuo anyi. Ma nsuo kɔ mu na gyina nnansas mmienu sɛ ɛtena na algae ntua fɔw ansa na wode apataa to. Bo nyinaa a excavation ka ho ma pond a square metres 500 wɔ mu taa yɛ GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000.

candidates.question_en: When should I harvest tilapia?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest tilapia when they reach market size of 300 to 500 grams which typically takes 5 to 6 months from fingerling stage. Monitor growth by sampling fish monthly using a net. Harvest in the early morning when water temperature is cool to reduce fish stress. Partial harvesting at 4 months removes larger fish and allows smaller ones to grow. Sell fresh fish immediately or ice them for transport to market.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na meyiyɛ me tilapia apataa?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi tilapia bere a wɔkɔ si dwa kɛse a nnɔho 300 kɔ 500 gram a ɛtaa kyɛ mfee 5 kɔ 6 fi fingerling mu. Hwɛ sɛ apataa rebɛbo yie de sample apataa bere biara de net. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo berɛ dɛ sɛ apataa nhunu. Partial yi wɔ mfee nnan mu yi apataa kɛse na ma nketewa bo sɔ. Tɔ apataa fofor ntɛm anaa de ice ka ho ma akɔ dwa.

candidates.question_en: What is the best way to harvest fish from a pond?
candidates.answer_en: The best harvesting method depends on whether you are doing partial or complete harvest. For partial harvest use a seine net to selectively remove larger fish leaving smaller ones to grow. For complete harvest drain the pond partially then use nets to remove all fish. Harvest early morning when water is cool. Have containers ready with clean water or ice to keep fish alive or fresh. Weigh and record your harvest for business records. Never use chemicals or electricity to harvest as these are illegal and harmful.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛkwan bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ meyiyɛ apataa fi pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛkwan a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wuyiyɛ no kyɛ sɛ partial anaa complete harvest na woyɛ. Ma partial harvest de seine net yi apataa kɛse a wɔbɛ na ma nketewa tena so bo sɔ. Ma complete harvest sua nsuo ketewa fi pond mu afei de nets yi apataa nyinaa. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo dɛ. Ma containers a nsuo foforɔ anaa ice wɔ mu sɛ apataa aguina anaa tena foforɔ. Bu na kora wo harvest ho sɛ adwuma nsɛm. Mma wo mpo de chemicals anaa electricity yiyɛ efisɛ ɛnyɛ nea mmara gyina so na ɛyɛ bɔne.

candidates.question_en: How much does it cost to start a small fish farm in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Starting a small commercial fish farm in Ghana with two earthen ponds of 500 square metres each costs approximately GHS 15,000 to 25,000 including pond construction, fingerlings, feed for one cycle, and basic equipment. A plastic tank fish farm can be started for GHS 8,000 to 15,000. The main ongoing costs are fish feed which accounts for 60 to 70 percent of total production cost. With good management you can make a profit from the first cycle.
candidates.question_twi: Sika ahe na ɛyɛ papa sɛ mefi ase apataa adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apataa adwuma ketewa kɛse fi ase wɔ Ghana de earthen ponds mmienu a square metres 500 biara wɔ mu ho teetee GHS 15,000 kɔ 25,000 a pond yɛ, fingerlings, aduan wɔ cycle baako mu, ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ papa. Plastic tank apataa adwuma wobetumi de GHS 8,000 kɔ 15,000 fi ase. Nneɛma a ɛkyere daadaa a ɛkɔ so pii ne apataa aduan a ɛyɛ adwuma agyapade 60 kɔ 70 percent. Sɛ woyɛ adwuma pa a, wobetumi anya mfaso wɔ cycle a ɛdi kan mu.

candidates.question_en: What should I do if fish stop feeding suddenly?
candidates.answer_en: Check water quality, temperature, oxygen, recent weather, feed quality and signs of disease before increasing feed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ sɛ mpataa gyae di aduane ntɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsuo quality, ɔhyew, oxygen, weather a aba foforo, feed quality ne yare ho nsɛnkyerɛnne ansa na woama feed no so.

candidates.question_en: How should a fish farmer keep pond records?
candidates.answer_en: Record stocking date and number, feed used, mortalities, water-quality observations, treatments, harvest weight and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛw fish pond records?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw stocking da ne dodow, feed a wode dii dwuma, mpataa a awuwu, nsuo quality nsɛm, ayaresa, harvest duru ne tɔn.

items.question_en: What is the best way to plant cassava stems?
items.answer_en: Plant cassava stems at an angle of 45 degrees or vertically in the soil. Bury at least two to three nodes underground leaving three or more above ground. The spacing should be 1 metre by 1 metre for food production, or 0.8 by 1 metre for commercial production. Plant at the start of the rainy season when soil moisture is adequate. Planting upright gives higher yields but angled planting is easier to harvest.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛyɛ ɛkwan pa sɛ mede bankye abɔ to mu?
items.answer_twi: De bankye abɔ to mu wɔ angle 45 degrees anaa straight wɔ asase mu. Fa mu sɛ nodes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa bɛkɔ asase mu na nnua mmiɛnsa anaa saa kɔ so bɛsi asase so. Ahodɔ nni obi metre baako ne metre baako ho ma aduan na 0.8 ne metre baako ma adwuma kɛse. To mu nsuo berɛ akyirikyiri bere a asase mu nsuo ho hia. Straight to aba mu kyerɛ nnoa pii nanso angled nna hia adwuma pii bere a wuyi.

candidates.question_en: How do I select healthy cassava stems for planting?
candidates.answer_en: Select stems from healthy mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old. The stem should be firm, not shrivelled, about 2 to 3 cm thick and 20 to 30 cm long with at least 5 nodes. Avoid stems from diseased plants or those showing mosaic virus symptoms. Store cuttings in the shade for no more than 3 days before planting.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick bankye abɔ pa sɛ mede to mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi abɔ fi bankye nnuaba pa a wɔawo akyi mfee 8 kɔ 12. Abɔ no nni yie, mmaadwa gu ho, bɛyɛ sɛntimita 2 kɔ 3 tiawa na sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 tenten a ɛwɔ nodes 5 pɛ. Gye wo ho fi abɔ a ɛfi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho anaa a ɛkyerɛ mosaic virus ho nsono. Guina cutting no wɔ hare ha mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa pɛ ansa na wode to mu.

candidates.question_en: How does climate change affect farming in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Climate change in Ghana is causing more erratic rainfall, longer dry seasons, increased temperatures, more frequent flooding and drought. Adapt by using drought-tolerant varieties, adopting water harvesting techniques like half-moon pits and tied ridges, diversifying into drought-resistant crops like cowpea cassava and sorghum, using mulching to conserve soil moisture, agroforestry which involves planting trees with crops, joining early warning systems for weather forecasts, and timing planting to match current rainfall patterns rather than traditional calendars.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na climate change yɛ okuafo adwuma den wɔ Ghana na dɛn na menyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Climate change wɔ Ghana ma nsuo tɔ bere sesa daa, bone berɛ tenten, berɛhyɛ tɔ so, nsuo ne bone tɔ so. Siesie wo tiri ho de de drought-tolerant varieties to mu, de water harvesting nhyiamu te sɛ half-moon pits ne tied ridges, sesa kɔ drought-resistant nnuaba te sɛ bɔde, bankye ne sorghum, de mulching sɛ ɛkora asase nsuo, agroforestry a ɛkyerɛ to nnuaba ne nnuaba kaa bom, ka early warning systems ho ma berɛ nkra, na to aba bere sɛ nsuo a ɛtaa tɔ saa ara ho na gye traditional calendars.

candidates.question_en: How many acres of cassava do I need to make a meaningful profit?
candidates.answer_en: To make meaningful profit from cassava you need at least 2 to 5 acres. With improved varieties and good management, 5 acres can yield 40 to 75 tonnes of fresh cassava. At current market rates this translates to GHS 24,000 to 45,000 in revenue. After deducting costs of GHS 6,000 to 10,000 for a 5-acre farm, profit can be GHS 14,000 to 35,000 per season. Processing into gari or starch doubles or triples this profit.
candidates.question_twi: Asase ahe na mɛhia sɛ bankye adwuma ade sika ba?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛnya mfaso pa fi bankye mu a, wohia sɛ eka mmienu kɔ num pɛ. De improved varieties ne adwuma pa, eka num tumi de bankye foforɔ nnɔho 40 kɔ 75 tonne. Wɔ dwa bo a wɔwɔ saa ara, eyi bɛyɛ GHS 24,000 kɔ 45,000. Nnuaha wo costs GHS 6,000 kɔ 10,000 ma eka num afuom akyi, mfaso bɛtumi ayɛ GHS 14,000 kɔ 35,000 bere biara. De yɛ gari anaa starch a ɛde mfaso mmienu anaa mmiɛnsa ba.

candidates.question_en: What can I do with cassava peels and other cassava waste?
candidates.answer_en: Cassava peels can be dried and used as animal feed for goats, sheep and pigs, providing a valuable energy source. Fresh peels fermented for 3 to 4 days make good pig and poultry feed. Cassava peel compost improves soil fertility. The starchy water from gari processing can be fermented and used as a fermented cassava drink called pito or as a substrate for mushroom growing. Using cassava by-products reduces waste and adds extra income streams.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ bankye ho ne nsononko ho adwuma yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Bankye ho bɛtumi atew na de ma mmoa te sɛ birekyie, oguan ne prako aduan, de energy toɔ to. Bankye ho foforɔ a wɔde ferment adays mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan yɛ prako ne akoko aduan pa. Bankye ho compost boa asase aduan. Nsuo a starch wɔ mu fi gari yɛ ho bɛtumi aferment na de yɛ nsuo aduan a wɔfre no pito anaa de yɛ substrate ma mushroom noa. De bankye by-products de hyɛ nsono mu hia na ɛhia sika ahoma foforɔ.

candidates.question_en: How do I know when my crops need water?
candidates.answer_en: Push your finger 5cm deep into the soil — if dry, water is needed. Watch for early morning wilting as a sign of drought stress. Sandy soils need watering more often than clay soils. Tomatoes and vegetables need more frequent watering than cassava.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menim bere a m'nnuaba hia nsuo?
candidates.answer_twi: Hia wo nsateaa asase mu sɛntimita 5 — sɛ ɛyera a, hia nsuo. Hwɛ owia da ano nwonwon sɛ ɛkyerɛ nsuo hia. Asintiɛ asase hia nsuo pii sen amane asase. Ntomato ne nnuan hia nsuo pii sen bankye.

candidates.question_en: How should I harvest cassava properly?
candidates.answer_en: Cassava is usually harvested 9-18 months after planting. Cut the stem at 30-40 cm height then loosen the soil around the plant with a hoe and pull up the roots. Handle roots gently to avoid bruising.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye m'bankye yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Bankye taa gye wɔ abosome 9-18 akyi a wode to mu. Twa tibo no wɔ sɛntimita 30-40 so, afei de akɔde fa asase a ɛhyia nnua no ho na twe ntini no sor. De ntini no pɛ efisɛ sɛ ehow a ɛma ɛsɛe ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: How much money can I make from one acre of cassava?
candidates.answer_en: From one acre of cassava using improved varieties, you can harvest 8 to 15 tonnes of fresh roots. At a farm gate price of GHS 150 to 200 per bag, you can earn GHS 3,000 to 6,000 per acre after deducting input and labour costs of about GHS 800 to 1,200. Cassava farming is most profitable when you process it into gari, starch or fufu flour before selling.
candidates.question_twi: Mfa sika ahe bɛfata me wɔ bankye eka baako mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi bankye eka baako mu de varieties pa to mu a, wobetumi anya bankye fofor nnɔho 8 kɔ 15 tonne. Sɛ efie dwa kɛse bɛyɛ GHS 150 kɔ 200 biara bag ho a, wobetumi nya GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000 biara eka baako akyi a wogu inputs ne adwuma a ɛyɛ GHS 800 kɔ 1,200 ho. Bankye adwuma ho bo tɔ sen a wode ayɛ gari, starch anaa fufu flour ansa na wotɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can I add value to my farm produce to earn more money?
candidates.answer_en: Process raw produce into higher-value products: dry and package grains, make tomato paste, gari from cassava, or palm oil from palm fruits. Value addition reduces post-harvest losses and increases income.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mede boɔ ka m'afuo nnuaba ho sɛ menya sika dodo?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ aduan foforo no yɛ aduan a wɔtɔ boɔ kɛse: yaw na paka nnuaba a ayaw, yɛ ntomato paste, gari fi bankye, anaa ngo fi abe aba. Boɔ to so maa mpampa post-harvest mpoano ne ma sika dodo.

items.question_en: How do I choose crops that match my soil type?
items.answer_en: Match your crop to your soil type for best results. Sandy soils drain quickly and suit groundnut, cowpea, sweet potato and watermelon. Clay soils retain water and suit rice, taro cocoyam and some vegetables. Loam soils are the most versatile and suit almost all crops including maize, cassava, tomatoes and most vegetables. Get a simple soil test done at your nearest MOFA office or agricultural laboratory to know your soil pH and nutrient levels before choosing your crop.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick nnuaba pa ma me asase nhyiamu?
items.answer_twi: De wo nnuaba hyɛ wo asase nhyiamu mu ma nnoa pa. Sandy asase sua nsuo ntɛm na ɛbɛn groundnut, bɔde, sweet potato ne watermelon. Clay asase kora nsuo na ɛbɛn ɔmo, taro cocoyam ne nnuaba bi. Loam asase ne asase a ɛbɛn nnuaba bebree a aburoɔ, bankye, tomatoes ne nnuaba bebree ka ho. Gye wo asase hwɛ fi wo MOFA ofisi a ɛbɛn anaa agricultural laboratory ma wohunu wo asase pH ne ferefere levels ansa na wopick wo nnuaba.

candidates.question_en: How do I choose the best maize variety for my area?
candidates.answer_en: Choose your maize variety based on the rainfall pattern of your area, the soil type, and your market. For the forest zone with high rainfall, use medium to late maturing varieties like Abontem or Mamaba. For the savanna and transition zones, use drought-tolerant varieties like Obatanpa, Wari or Aburohemaa. For household consumption, choose floury white varieties. For animal feed, yellow varieties like Dobidi have higher energy content. Buy certified seed from licensed dealers.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick aburoɔ aba variety pa wɔ me ɛhɔ ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi wo aburoɔ variety sɛ nsuo a ɛtɔ bere wɔ wo hɔ, asase nhyiamu, na wo dwa so. Ma kwaeɛ zone a nsuo tɔ pii ho, de medium kɔ late maturing varieties te sɛ Abontem anaa Mamaba. Ma savanna ne ntam zones ho, de drought-tolerant varieties te sɛ Obatanpa, Wari anaa Aburohemaa. Ma efie didi, yi floury white varieties. Ma mmoa aduan, yellow varieties te sɛ Dobidi wɔ energy pii mu. Gye certified seed fi licensed dealers.

candidates.question_en: How can I make compost for my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Make compost by layering crop residues dry matter like maize stalks alternating with green matter like grass clippings and kitchen waste. Add a thin layer of soil or finished compost between layers to introduce decomposing organisms. Keep the pile moist but not waterlogged and turn it every 2 weeks. The compost is ready in 8 to 12 weeks when it is dark brown crumbly and earthy smelling. Apply 2 to 3 tonnes of compost per acre before planting to significantly improve soil fertility.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ compost ma me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ compost de layers a nnuaba a ato fɛw aba ntama a wɔatew te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ka ho ne nnuaba foforɔ te sɛ nhawan ne efie ho nneɛma. De asase ketewa anaa compost a ɛawie to ntam biara mu sɛ ɛde organisms a ɛhia kɔ. Ma pile no nsuo ho kakra nanso nsuo nni mu agyina na gyinaso mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas. Compost no atwa so nnansas nwɔtwe kɔ duonum mmienu mu bere a ɛyɛ dark brown, ɛpepee yie na ɛwɔ nhwirɛ pa. De compost tonnes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa to eka baako so ansa na wode aba to mu sɛ ɛboa asase aduan pii.

candidates.question_en: How can I start farming in Ghana with little money?
candidates.answer_en: Start small with crops that need minimal investment like vegetables, maize or cassava. Begin with what land you have access to. Use family labour initially to reduce costs. Join a farmer-based organisation for access to group inputs and credit. Apply for the government Planting for Food and Jobs programme which provides subsidized seeds and fertilizer. Reinvest your profits to gradually expand your farm each season.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana a sika ketewa wɔ me nkyɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi ase ketewa de nnuaba a sika ketewa na ɛhia te sɛ nnuaba, aburoɔ anaa bankye. Fi ase wɔ asase a wowɔ ho. De wo fie ho adwuma ansa na ɛhia sika. Ka okuafo kuo ho sɛ wɔde group inputs ne credit nya. Bisa aban Planting for Food and Jobs programme a wɔde subsidized aba ne ferefere to. De wo mfaso no to wo afuom no so bere biara ma ɛkɔ so kɛse tenten tenten.

candidates.question_en: What crop rotation plan is suitable for Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: A good crop rotation for Ghana is to plant legumes like cowpea or groundnut after cereals like maize or sorghum. Legumes fix nitrogen into the soil improving fertility naturally. A 3-year rotation could be maize in year one, cowpea in year two, and cassava or vegetables in year three. Avoid planting the same crop family in the same field two seasons in a row as this builds up pests and diseases specific to that crop.
candidates.question_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu pa wɔ Ghana ne de legumes te sɛ bɔde anaa groundnut to mu akyi cereals te sɛ aburoɔ anaa sorghum. Legumes de nitrogen ka asase mu a ɛboa asase aduan pa. Mfe mmiɛnsa rotation bɛtumi ayɛ: aburoɔ mfe a ɛdi kan mu, bɔde mfe mmienu mu, na bankye anaa nnuaba mfe mmiɛnsa mu. Gye wo ho fi de nnuaba nhyiamu koro to mu wɔ afuom koro mfe mmienu so kwa efisɛ eyi ma adwummaker ne yadeɛ a ɛfa nhyiamu no ho kɔ so.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare the soil before planting maize?
candidates.answer_en: Clear the land of weeds and old crop residues. Plough or dig to a depth of 20 to 30 cm to loosen the soil. If possible, apply compost or manure and incorporate it into the soil two weeks before planting. Level the seedbed to ensure even germination. Avoid burning crop residues as this destroys beneficial soil organisms.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ asase no so ansa na meto aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo ne nnuaba a ato fɛw fi asase no so. Boro asase no kosi sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 mu sɛ asase no atete yie. Sɛ wobetumi a, de compost anaa aguare to mu na fa ka ho mprɛnsa mmienu ansa na wode aba to mu. Siesie seedbed no so yie sɛ aba nyinaa retua fɔw yie. Mma nnuaba fidie anhye efisɛ eyi sɛe asase mu adwummaker pa.

candidates.question_en: Which crops are most resilient to climate change in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Drought-tolerant crops for Ghana's changing climate include improved NERICA rice, drought-tolerant maize varieties like Obatanpa and Omankwa, cowpea, sorghum, millet, and cassava. Contact CSIR-SARI or MOFA for the latest recommended varieties in your region.
candidates.question_twi: Nnuaba bɛn na ɛtumi wiase tebea sɛsae ase hyɛ yie wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase hyɛ wɔ Ghana tebea sɛsae mu ne NERICA ɔmɔ a wɔayɛ no foforo, aburow a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase te sɛ Obatanpa ne Omankwa, abɔdweɛ, ɔtɛ, ɔtɛ pa, ne bankye. Ka kyerɛ CSIR-SARI anaa MOFA sɛ wunya aba a wɔaka.

candidates.question_en: What do goats eat and how should I feed them?
candidates.answer_en: Goats are browsers that prefer leaves, shrubs and crop by-products over grass. Feed them a mixture of fresh grass and leaves, crop residues like maize stalks and groundnut haulms, hay, and concentrate feeds for pregnant or lactating does. Always provide clean water and mineral salt licks. Never feed moldy or rotten feed. Goats can also browse freely in managed areas to supplement their feeding.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na birekyie di na dɛn na mede ma wɔn yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Birekyie yɛ browsers a wɔpɛ nhaban, nhaban ketewa ne nnuaba a ato fɛw sen nhawan. Ma wɔn nhawan foforɔ ne nhaban ahohiana, nnuaba a ato fɛw te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ne groundnut saa, hay, na concentrate feeds ma mmirikyi a ɛwɔ aninso anaa a wɔwɔ nsuo mu. De nsuo pa ne mineral salt licks to mu bere nyinaa. Mma aduan a mold aba ho anaa a asɛe amma wɔn. Birekyie nso betumi abrowse wɔ baabi a wɔhwɛ so sɛ wɔkaa wɔn didi ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce feed costs in poultry farming?
candidates.answer_en: Reduce poultry feed costs by formulating your own feed using locally available ingredients like maize, soybean meal, fishmeal, rice bran and mineral premix. This can reduce feed cost by 20 to 30 percent compared to commercial feeds. Buy feed ingredients in bulk when prices are low. Use fermented feed to improve digestibility and reduce feed conversion ratio. Reduce waste by using appropriate feeders and filling them only two-thirds full. Grow fast-growing varieties and slaughter at the right age before feed efficiency declines.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me aduan bo sua wɔ akoko adwuma mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sua akoko aduan bo de yɛ wo ankasa aduan de nneɛma a ɛwɔ ho te sɛ aburoɔ, soybean meal, fishmeal, rice bran ne mineral premix. Eyi bɛtumi asua aduan bo 20 kɔ 30 percent tia commercial feeds. Gye aduan nneɛma pii bere a bo sua. De fermented feed ma digestibility kɔ so na sua feed conversion ratio. Hia adefoforo de feeders pa na ma wɔn mu mprɛnsa mmienu pɛ. To fast-growing varieties mu na kum bere a ɛyɛ papa ansa na feed efficiency huna.

items.question_en: How can I keep records on a cocoa farm?
items.answer_en: Record planting areas, labour, inputs, harvest quantities, sales, disease observations and major farm expenses so you can compare seasons.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akora nsɛm wɔ cocoa afuo ho?
items.answer_twi: Kyerɛw asase a wodua so, adwumayɛfo, nneɛma a wode di dwuma, aba dodow, tɔn, yare ho nsɛm ne sika a wode yɛɛ adwuma sɛnea wobɛtumi de akyerɛw seasons no toto ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I keep a cocoa plantation clean?
candidates.answer_en: Remove excessive weeds, dead material and diseased parts safely. Keep pathways accessible so trees can be inspected and harvested efficiently.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama cocoa afuo no ho atew?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nwura a ɛdɔɔso, nneɛma a awu ne afã a yare aka ho yiye. Ma akwan a wokɔ so yɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ nnua no na woagye aba.

candidates.question_en: How should cocoa pods be harvested?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest ripe pods carefully with appropriate tools and avoid damaging the flower cushions and stems of the tree.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn agye cocoa pod?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye cocoa pod a awie ase no wɔ ahwɛyiye mu, fa adwinnade a ɛfata di dwuma na bɔ ɔbea baabi a nhwiren fifi ne dua no ntini ho ban.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve survival of cocoa seedlings after planting?
candidates.answer_en: Harden seedlings before field planting, transplant during suitable moist conditions, protect them from excessive sun and water them when necessary.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama cocoa aba nketewa no atena ase yie bere a madu wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma aba nketewa no nya ahoɔden ansa na wode akɔ afuo mu, dua wɔn bere a asase wɔ nsuo, bɔ wɔn ho ban fi owia a ɛyɛ den ho na gu nsuo sɛ ɛhia.

candidates.question_en: Why is pruning important in cocoa?
candidates.answer_en: Pruning helps improve light and air movement, removes unwanted growth and makes it easier to inspect and harvest the trees.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na twitwa cocoa nnua ho hia?
candidates.answer_twi: Twitwa nnua no boa ma owia ne mframa kɔ mu yie, yi nnyinaso a ɛnsɛ na ɛma ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ nnua no na woagye aba.

candidates.question_en: Why is shade important for young cocoa?
candidates.answer_en: Young cocoa benefits from moderate shade because it reduces heat and water stress while the seedlings establish. Shade should be managed as the trees grow.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na sunsuma ho hia ma cocoa nketewa?
candidates.answer_twi: Cocoa nketewa nya mfasoɔ fi sunsuma a ɛnyɛ dodo mu efisɛ ɛtew ɔhyew ne nsuo a ɛyera so bere a aba no resiesie ne ho. Bere a nnua no nyin no, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhwɛ sunsuma no so.

candidates.question_en: How often should I inspect cocoa trees?
candidates.answer_en: Inspect regularly for pests, diseases, damaged branches, weeds and moisture stress. Early detection makes management easier.
candidates.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ cocoa nnua so?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ wɔn daa sɛ mmoawa, yare, nkorabata a asɛe, nwura anaa nsuo a ɛsua wɔ asase mu wɔ hɔ. Sɛ wohu ɔhaw ntɛm a, ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ so.

candidates.question_en: Why should cocoa beans be fermented?
candidates.answer_en: Proper fermentation develops the flavour and colour expected in good-quality cocoa beans. Poor fermentation can reduce quality and market value.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛyɛ cocoa aba fermentation?
candidates.answer_twi: Fermentation a wɔyɛ no yie ma cocoa nya hwene ne kɔla a wɔhwɛ kwan wɔ cocoa pa mu. Fermentation a ɛnyɛ yie tew ne quality ne boɔ so.

items.question_en: How can I grow ginger successfully?
items.answer_en: Ginger grows best in partially shaded humid conditions with rich well-drained soil. Plant rhizomes 5-7 cm deep spaced 20-30 cm apart. Keep soil moist and mulch heavily. Harvest after 8-10 months when leaves yellow and die back.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura kakaduro yie?
items.answer_twi: Kakaduro da sor pa wɔ beae a owia tra mu kakra na ɛwɔ huhu, asase a ɛwɔ aduan pa na nsuo pue mu yie. De rhizomes to asase mu sɛntimita 5-7 na gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 20-30. Kora asase nte na de mulch to so papaapa. Gye abosome 8-10 akyi a nhaban no dan sika na awu.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow cashew successfully?
candidates.answer_en: Cashew grows best in well-drained sandy or laterite soils in areas with a distinct dry season. Plant seeds directly 5 cm deep in the field or transplant seedlings. Space trees 8-10 meters apart. Apply fertilizer in the second year onward. Control collar rot disease, cashew stem and root borer insects, and anthracnose. Harvest nuts when the cashew apple turns yellow or red and the nut is dark grey. Cashew trees start producing at 3-5 years.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura cashew yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Cashew da sor pa wɔ asase a nsuo pue mu yie a ɛyɛ asintiɛ anaa laterite wɔ beae a ɔpɛ bere wɔ hɔ. To aba tɔtɔ wɔ asase mu sɛntimita 5 anaa si nnuaba mfoforo ananmu. Gyae nnua asukyerɛ mita 8-10. De ferefere to mfe a ɛto so abien ananmu. Kora collar rot yadeɛ, cashew tibo ne ntini adwummakers, ne anthracnose ase. Gye aba bere a cashew apple no dan hoho anaa kɔkɔɔ na aba no dan tuntum-brɔdwa. Cashew nnua da sor fi mfe 3-5 akyi.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow watermelon successfully?
candidates.answer_en: Watermelon needs well-drained sandy loam soil, warm temperatures, and plenty of sunlight. Space 1.5-2 m apart. Water deeply but infrequently. Apply potassium-rich fertilizer during fruiting. Harvest when the tendril near the fruit turns brown.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura watermelon yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Watermelon hia asintiɛ asase a nsuo pue mu yie, owia mu, na owia hye pa. Gyae asukyerɛ mita 1.5-2. De nsuo to asase mu yiye nanso mmere pii bi. De potassium ferefere to so bere a aba reba. Gye bere a ntini a ɛbɛn aba no dan ɛda.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow soybean commercially for profit?
candidates.answer_en: Soybeans are highly profitable legumes. Plant after rains are well established. Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium bacteria before planting (this fixes nitrogen and can triple yields). Space 30-45 cm within rows and 60 cm between rows. Apply phosphorus fertilizer at planting. Weed once at 3 weeks. Harvest when 95% of pods have turned yellow-brown. Dry to 12% moisture before storage. Soybeans have strong demand from oil processors and animal feed manufacturers.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura soya yɛ adwuma sɛ menya sika?
candidates.answer_twi: Soya yɛ abɔdweɛ a ɛde sika ba pa ara. To akyi a osu asi yie. De Bradyrhizobium bacteria ka aba ho ansa na woto (eyi fi nitrogen na ɛtumi ma nnuaba da sor mprɛ mmiɛnsa). Gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 30-45 wɔ ntam ne sɛntimita 60 wɔ nnua so ntam. De phosphorus ferefere to mu bere a wode to. Tia nhaban foforo bere a ɛto so mmiɛnsa no nnawotwe baako. Gye bere a 95% fidie no adan hoho bɔɔ. Yaw kosi 12% nsuku ansa na waguina. Soya hia yɛ kɛse wɔ ngo adwuma kuo ne mmoa aduan adwuma kuo ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow moringa and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Moringa is one of the most nutritious plants in the world and grows easily in Ghana. Plant seeds directly or use stem cuttings in well-drained soil. It tolerates drought and poor soils. Harvest leaves regularly to keep the tree short and productive. Moringa leaves can be eaten fresh, dried, and powdered. Benefits include: extremely high in iron, vitamins A and C, protein, and calcium. It is used medicinally and sold as a nutritional supplement at premium prices.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura moringa na mfaaso bɛn na ɛwɔ?
