candidates.answer_twi: Moringa yɛ nnua a ɛwɔ aduan ho nhwiren pa ara wɔ wiase mu na ɛda sor yie wɔ Ghana. To aba tɔtɔ anaa fa tibo cutting wɔ asase a nsuo pue mu yie. Ɛtumi nsuo pa ne asase a enni pa ase hyɛ. Gye nhaban pɛ sɛ ɛkora dua no tia ne adwuma mu. Moringa nhaban wobetumi di foforo, yaw na tutu. Mfaaso ho ne: iron, vitamins A ne C, protein, ne calcium ho yɛ dodo pa ara. Wɔde di dawuro adwuma na tɔn sɛ nutritional supplement wɔ boɔ kɛse.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow pineapple commercially?
candidates.answer_en: Commercial pineapple production: plant suckers or crowns from healthy plants, space 60x30 cm on raised beds in rows, apply NPK fertilizer 3 times per year, force flowering by applying ethephon or acetylene solution at 12-14 months to synchronize harvest, control mealy bugs and heart rot disease, harvest 15-18 months after planting. MD2 and Smooth Cayenne are popular export varieties. Ghana exports significant volumes of pineapple to Europe.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura aborɔfo wɔ adwuma mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Aborɔfo adwuma kura ho: to suckers anaa crowns fi nnua a wɔwɔ aho wɔ, gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 60x30 wɔ asase-sor afuo wɔ nnua so mu, de NPK ferefere to mprɛ mmiɛnsa bere biara, ma abode ba wɔ de ethephon anaa acetylene solution hyɛ wɔ bosome 12-14 akyi sɛ wogye bere koro, kora mealy bug ne heart rot yadeɛ ase, gye bosome 15-18 akyi a wode to mu. MD2 ne Smooth Cayenne yɛ export aba a wɔpɛ wɔn. Ghana de aborɔfo kɔ Yurop dodo.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare my land before planting?
candidates.answer_en: Clear the land of weeds and old crop residues. Plow or dig to loosen the soil to about 20-30 cm deep. Break up large clods and remove stones. Level the surface and apply basal fertilizer or compost before planting.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesiesie asase aba to mu ansa?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi sare ne nnua funu fi asase no so. Twa anaa hwe asase no mu kɔ sɛntimita 20- 30 mu. Bubu asase akɛse no na yi abo. Siesie fam no yiye na fa basal ferefere anaa compost gu so ansa na wode aba no agu fam.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm during drought?
candidates.answer_en: During drought, mulch heavily to conserve soil moisture, irrigate if possible, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and avoid adding nitrogen fertilizer which increases water demand. Harvest early-maturing varieties before drought peaks.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ m'afuo so bere a nsuo pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a nsuo pa no, de mulch to asase so yiye sɛ nsukuro wo mu, de nsuo to nnua so sɛ wonya tumi, paw nnuaba aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa so, na bɔ hwɛ de nitrogen ferefere to sɛ ɛma nnuaba hia nsuo dodo. Gye nnuaba a wɔware ntɛm ansa na nsuo pa yɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: What causes root rot and how can I prevent it?
candidates.answer_en: Root rot is caused by soil-borne fungi, mainly when soil stays waterlogged for too long. It causes roots to turn brown and mushy, plants to wilt even when soil is wet, and eventual plant death. Prevent by: improving soil drainage, avoiding overwatering, not planting in low-lying waterlogged areas, using raised beds, treating seeds with fungicide before planting, and rotating crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma ntini sɛe na ɛdeɛn na metumi kora ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Ntini sɛe fi asase fungus, titiriw bere a nsuo da asase mu tenten dodo. Ɛma ntini dan ɛda ne mmerɛ, nnuaba nwo bere a asase nte, na nnua wu. Kora ase wɔ: siesie asase nsuo pue anammɔn, bɔ hwɛ nsuo to dodo, mto nnuaba wɔ asase ase a nsuo hia mu, fa asase-sor afuo, de aba ka fungicide ho ansa na woto mu, na sesa nnuaba.

items.question_en: How do I apply for the Planting for Food and Jobs programme?
items.answer_en: To apply for the Planting for Food and Jobs programme, visit your nearest District Department of Agriculture office under the Ministry of Food and Agriculture. Bring your Ghana Card, proof of land ownership or land use agreement, and your farm location. Register as a beneficiary farmer. Subsidized inputs including seeds and fertilizers are then distributed through licensed agro-dealers in your district. The programme covers maize, rice, soybean, sorghum, vegetables and other crops.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mebisa Planting for Food and Jobs programme?
items.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛbisa Planting for Food and Jobs programme a, kɔ wo District Department of Agriculture ofisi a ɛbɛn wo wɔ Ministry of Food and Agriculture ase. De wo Ghana Card, asase ho evidence anaa asase de adi nhyiamu krataa, na wo afuom hɔ. Si ho sɛ beneficiary okuafo. Inputs a wɔde asua te sɛ aba ne ferefere na wɔde kyɛ wɔ licensed agro-dealers mu wɔ wo district mu. Programme no fa aburoɔ, ɔmo, soybean, sorghum, nnuaba ne nnuaba foforɔ ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I start farming in Ghana with little money?
candidates.answer_en: Start small with crops that need minimal investment like vegetables, maize or cassava. Begin with what land you have access to. Use family labour initially to reduce costs. Join a farmer-based organisation for access to group inputs and credit. Apply for the government Planting for Food and Jobs programme which provides subsidized seeds and fertilizer. Reinvest your profits to gradually expand your farm each season.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana a sika ketewa wɔ me nkyɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi ase ketewa de nnuaba a sika ketewa na ɛhia te sɛ nnuaba, aburoɔ anaa bankye. Fi ase wɔ asase a wowɔ ho. De wo fie ho adwuma ansa na ɛhia sika. Ka okuafo kuo ho sɛ wɔde group inputs ne credit nya. Bisa aban Planting for Food and Jobs programme a wɔde subsidized aba ne ferefere to. De wo mfaso no to wo afuom no so bere biara ma ɛkɔ so kɛse tenten tenten.

candidates.question_en: How do I choose the best maize variety for my area?
candidates.answer_en: Choose your maize variety based on the rainfall pattern of your area, the soil type, and your market. For the forest zone with high rainfall, use medium to late maturing varieties like Abontem or Mamaba. For the savanna and transition zones, use drought-tolerant varieties like Obatanpa, Wari or Aburohemaa. For household consumption, choose floury white varieties. For animal feed, yellow varieties like Dobidi have higher energy content. Buy certified seed from licensed dealers.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick aburoɔ aba variety pa wɔ me ɛhɔ ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi wo aburoɔ variety sɛ nsuo a ɛtɔ bere wɔ wo hɔ, asase nhyiamu, na wo dwa so. Ma kwaeɛ zone a nsuo tɔ pii ho, de medium kɔ late maturing varieties te sɛ Abontem anaa Mamaba. Ma savanna ne ntam zones ho, de drought-tolerant varieties te sɛ Obatanpa, Wari anaa Aburohemaa. Ma efie didi, yi floury white varieties. Ma mmoa aduan, yellow varieties te sɛ Dobidi wɔ energy pii mu. Gye certified seed fi licensed dealers.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare maize seed before planting?
candidates.answer_en: Treat maize seed with a fungicide and insecticide seed dressing before planting to protect against soil-borne diseases and early insect attack. Products like Apron Star or Gaucho are commonly used. Coat the seeds lightly, allow them to dry for 30 minutes and plant immediately. Buy certified seeds from reputable agro-input dealers to ensure good germination rates.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ aburoɔ aba ansa na meto mu?
candidates.answer_twi: De fungicide ne insecticide seed dressing to aburoɔ aba so ansa na wode to mu sɛ ɛhwɛ aba no so fi asase yadeɛ ne adwummaker atia a ɛdi kan. Nneɛma te sɛ Apron Star anaa Gaucho na wɔde taa yɛ. Kata aba no so kakra, ma no tew simma 30 na to mu ntɛm. Gye certified seeds fi agro-input dealers a wɔni gyinae so sɛ aba atua fɔw yie.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare the soil before planting maize?
candidates.answer_en: Clear the land of weeds and old crop residues. Plough or dig to a depth of 20 to 30 cm to loosen the soil. If possible, apply compost or manure and incorporate it into the soil two weeks before planting. Level the seedbed to ensure even germination. Avoid burning crop residues as this destroys beneficial soil organisms.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ asase no so ansa na meto aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo ne nnuaba a ato fɛw fi asase no so. Boro asase no kosi sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 mu sɛ asase no atete yie. Sɛ wobetumi a, de compost anaa aguare to mu na fa ka ho mprɛnsa mmienu ansa na wode aba to mu. Siesie seedbed no so yie sɛ aba nyinaa retua fɔw yie. Mma nnuaba fidie anhye efisɛ eyi sɛe asase mu adwummaker pa.

candidates.question_en: What is the Ghana Commodity Exchange and how can farmers use it?
candidates.answer_en: The Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) is a formal marketplace where farmers can sell their produce at transparent, standardized prices. To use it: register as a member through an accredited warehouse operator, store your certified grain in a GCX-accredited warehouse, receive a warehouse receipt that you can sell at the exchange or use as collateral for a bank loan. It is especially good for maize, soya, and sorghum.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Ghana Commodity Exchange yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) yɛ aguabasa a ɛwɔ ho yie a okuafo tumi tɔn wɔn nnuaba wɔ boɔ a wɔada adi ne a wɔasiesie. Sɛ wohwehwɛ fa di dwuma a, kyerɛw wo din wɔ accredited warehouse operator ho, guina wo nnuaba a wɔakyerɛw wɔ GCX-accredited warehouse mu, nya warehouse receipt a wobetumi tɔn wɔ exchange no mu anaa de kɔ ban ho sɛ collateral. Ɛyɛ adwuma yie pa ara ma aburow, soya, ne ɔtɛ.

candidates.question_en: How can I make compost for my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Make compost by layering crop residues dry matter like maize stalks alternating with green matter like grass clippings and kitchen waste. Add a thin layer of soil or finished compost between layers to introduce decomposing organisms. Keep the pile moist but not waterlogged and turn it every 2 weeks. The compost is ready in 8 to 12 weeks when it is dark brown crumbly and earthy smelling. Apply 2 to 3 tonnes of compost per acre before planting to significantly improve soil fertility.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ compost ma me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ compost de layers a nnuaba a ato fɛw aba ntama a wɔatew te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ka ho ne nnuaba foforɔ te sɛ nhawan ne efie ho nneɛma. De asase ketewa anaa compost a ɛawie to ntam biara mu sɛ ɛde organisms a ɛhia kɔ. Ma pile no nsuo ho kakra nanso nsuo nni mu agyina na gyinaso mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas. Compost no atwa so nnansas nwɔtwe kɔ duonum mmienu mu bere a ɛyɛ dark brown, ɛpepee yie na ɛwɔ nhwirɛ pa. De compost tonnes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa to eka baako so ansa na wode aba to mu sɛ ɛboa asase aduan pii.

candidates.question_en: What crop rotation plan is suitable for Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: A good crop rotation for Ghana is to plant legumes like cowpea or groundnut after cereals like maize or sorghum. Legumes fix nitrogen into the soil improving fertility naturally. A 3-year rotation could be maize in year one, cowpea in year two, and cassava or vegetables in year three. Avoid planting the same crop family in the same field two seasons in a row as this builds up pests and diseases specific to that crop.
candidates.question_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Adekuo nhyiamu pa wɔ Ghana ne de legumes te sɛ bɔde anaa groundnut to mu akyi cereals te sɛ aburoɔ anaa sorghum. Legumes de nitrogen ka asase mu a ɛboa asase aduan pa. Mfe mmiɛnsa rotation bɛtumi ayɛ: aburoɔ mfe a ɛdi kan mu, bɔde mfe mmienu mu, na bankye anaa nnuaba mfe mmiɛnsa mu. Gye wo ho fi de nnuaba nhyiamu koro to mu wɔ afuom koro mfe mmienu so kwa efisɛ eyi ma adwummaker ne yadeɛ a ɛfa nhyiamu no ho kɔ so.

candidates.question_en: What is intercropping and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Intercropping means growing two or more crops together on the same land. For example, maize with cowpea. Benefits include better land use, the legume adds nitrogen to the soil, reduced pest pressure, and income from two crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛyɛ intercropping na ɛboa?
candidates.answer_twi: Intercropping kyerɛ sɛ wokura nnuaba abien anaa dodo wɔ asase koro so. Nhwɛso so, aburow ne abɔdweɛ. Mfaaso ho ne: asase ho dwuma pa, abɔdweɛ de nitrogen ma asase, adwummakers hia sua, na nnuaba abien firi sika.

items.question_en: How much palm oil can one hectare produce in Ghana?
items.answer_en: Under traditional smallholder management, palm oil yield is 1 to 2 tonnes per hectare per year. With improved Tenera varieties and proper management including fertilization and pest control, yield increases to 4 to 6 tonnes of palm oil per hectare. A mature well-managed plantation of 10 hectares can produce 40 to 60 tonnes of palm oil annually worth GHS 200,000 to 300,000. Palm oil prices are relatively stable making it a reliable long-term investment.
items.question_twi: Abɛ ɔman ahe na ɛfiri hectare baako mu wɔ Ghana?
items.answer_twi: Wɔ traditional smallholder adwuma mu, abɛ ɔman aba yɛ tonnes baako kɔ mmienu biara hectare biara afe biara. De improved Tenera varieties ne adwuma pa a ferefere ne adwummaker hwɛ ka ho, nnoa kɔ tonnes 4 kɔ 6 abɛ ɔman biara hectare. Plantation a ɛatwa so na wohwɛ so yie a ɛtelɛ hectares 10 tumi de abɛ ɔman tonnes 40 kɔ 60 ba afe biara a ɛbɛyɛ GHS 200,000 kɔ 300,000. Abɛ ɔman bo yɛ so paa a ɛma ɛyɛ investment pa ma akyi.

candidates.question_en: How do I start a palm plantation in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with deep well-drained soils and rainfall above 1500 mm annually. Obtain certified tenera seedlings from CSIR-Oil Palm Research Institute at Kusi. Plant at 9 by 9 metres triangular spacing giving about 143 trees per hectare. Apply NPK fertilizer twice yearly. Palms begin producing after 3 to 4 years and remain productive for 25 to 30 years. Join the Ghana Oil Palm Development Company cooperative for support and guaranteed market.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase abɛ afuom wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ tia yie ne nsuo tew na nsuo a ɛtɔ biara afe hyɛ 1500 mm so. Gye certified tenera seedlings fi CSIR-Oil Palm Research Institute wɔ Kusi. De to mu wɔ 9 ne 9 metres triangular ahodɔ a ɛma nnuaba 143 wɔ hectare biara mu. De NPK ferefere to ho mprɛn mmienu biara afe. Abɛ fi ase wɔ aduane mfe mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan akyi na ɛgyina so wɔ mfe 25 kɔ 30. Ka Ghana Oil Palm Development Company kuo ho ma wɔboa wo ne dwa gyinae.

candidates.question_en: How should I grow coconut trees in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Coconut grows best along coastal areas and in areas with high rainfall. Plant whole mature coconuts or purchase nursery seedlings. Dig a hole 1 metre deep and wide, add compost to the base and plant the seedling. Space at 7 to 10 metres apart. Coconut begins bearing fruit after 6 to 10 years depending on variety. Dwarf varieties like Malayan Dwarf produce earlier at 3 to 4 years. Apply potassium-rich fertilizer for good fruit production.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ meto kuuku nnuaba wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Kuuku to yie wɔ mpoano ho ne hɔ a nsuo tɔ yie. De kuuku a ɛatwa so pɛpɛɛpɛ to mu anaa gye nursery seedlings. Boro awia a ɛtelɛ ne teaa metre baako, de compost to ase na to seedling. Fa ahodɔ 7 kɔ 10 metres. Kuuku fi ase de nsuo wɔ mfe 6 kɔ 10 akyi sɛ variety no so. Dwarf varieties te sɛ Malayan Dwarf de nsuo ntɛm wɔ mfe mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan. De ferefere a potassium wɔ mu to ho ma nsuo pa.

candidates.question_en: How can I process coconut into different products?
candidates.answer_en: Coconut can be processed into coconut oil by grating mature coconut extracting the milk and boiling until oil separates, coconut cream and milk for cooking, desiccated coconut from dried grated flesh, coconut shell charcoal and crafts, coconut fibre from the husk for mats and ropes, and coconut water which is a popular beverage. In coastal Ghana there is good market for fresh coconuts coconut oil and coconut water. Value addition significantly increases income from coconut farming.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ kuuku yɛ nneɛma ahorow ma sika?
candidates.answer_twi: Wobetumi de kuuku yɛ: kuuku ɔman de grate kuuku a ɛatwa so yi nsuo afei hyehye kosi sɛ ɔman pae fi, kuuku cream ne nsuo ma aduan, desiccated kuuku fi dried grated flesh, kuuku ano faako charcoal ne adwuma, kuuku saa fi husk ma dua mpaboa ne tow, na kuuku nsuo a ɛyɛ nsuo a wɔpɛ. Wɔ Ghana mpoano hɔ, dwa pa wɔ kuuku foforɔ, kuuku ɔman ne kuuku nsuo ho. Value addition ma sika a ɛfiri kuuku adwuma kɔ so pii.

candidates.question_en: How should I care for young coconut trees?
candidates.answer_en: Care for young coconut trees by watering deeply twice a week for the first 2 years especially during dry season. Apply NPK fertilizer with high potassium every 6 months. Keep the area around the base of the tree free from grass and weeds for 2 metres. Mulch around the base to retain moisture. Protect from cattle and goats which will eat young fronds. The rhinoceros beetle is a major pest that bores into the crown. Control it by removing dead palms from the vicinity and using a hooked tool to remove beetles from the crown.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ kuuku nnuaba a wɔ mmofra ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ kuuku nnuaba mmofra ho de quench tia mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas mfe mmienu a ɛdi kan mu a ɛhia pii bone berɛ. De NPK ferefere a potassium wɔ mu pii to ho mprɛnsa nsia biara. Kora baabi a ɛbɛn nnuaba no ase nhawan ne nhaban foforo fi ho sɛntimita mmienu. Mulch ho sɛ ɛkora nsuo. Hwɛ nnwan ne birekyie a wɔbɛdi mmofra nhaban ho. Rhinoceros beetle yɛ adwummaker kɛse a ɛbɔ kɔtɔ wɔ crown mu. Boa ho de yi nnuaba a awu wɔ ho fi ne de hooked tool yi beetles fi crown mu.

candidates.question_en: How do I know when palm fruits are ready to harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Palm fruits are ready when they turn reddish-orange and some fruits start falling naturally from the bunch. Use a long-handled chisel or harvesting sickle to cut the bunch from the tree. Collect fallen fruits from the ground too. Process within 24-48 hours of harvest to avoid free fatty acid buildup which reduces oil quality.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye abe aba yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Abe aba wie ase bere a wɔdan kɔkɔɔ-ɛda na aba bi firi bɔ afi ne ho pɛ. Fa long-handled chisel anaa harvesting sickle twa bɔ no fi dua no ho. Gye aba a atu gu asase so nso. Yɛ adwuma wɔ dafe 24-48 akyi a wogye sɛ free fatty acid nbi dodo a ɛsua ngo ho pa.

items.question_en: How should cocoa beans be dried?
items.answer_en: Dry beans gradually on a clean surface, turn them regularly and protect them from rain, smoke, dirt and animals.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ayow cocoa aba?
items.answer_twi: Yow aba no nkakrankakra wɔ beae a ɛho tew, dane wɔn daa na bɔ wɔn ho ban fi osu, wusi, fĩ ne mmoa ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve survival of cocoa seedlings after planting?
candidates.answer_en: Harden seedlings before field planting, transplant during suitable moist conditions, protect them from excessive sun and water them when necessary.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama cocoa aba nketewa no atena ase yie bere a madu wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma aba nketewa no nya ahoɔden ansa na wode akɔ afuo mu, dua wɔn bere a asase wɔ nsuo, bɔ wɔn ho ban fi owia a ɛyɛ den ho na gu nsuo sɛ ɛhia.

candidates.question_en: How should cocoa pods be harvested?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest ripe pods carefully with appropriate tools and avoid damaging the flower cushions and stems of the tree.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn agye cocoa pod?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye cocoa pod a awie ase no wɔ ahwɛyiye mu, fa adwinnade a ɛfata di dwuma na bɔ ɔbea baabi a nhwiren fifi ne dua no ntini ho ban.

candidates.question_en: Why should cocoa beans be fermented?
candidates.answer_en: Proper fermentation develops the flavour and colour expected in good-quality cocoa beans. Poor fermentation can reduce quality and market value.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛyɛ cocoa aba fermentation?
candidates.answer_twi: Fermentation a wɔyɛ no yie ma cocoa nya hwene ne kɔla a wɔhwɛ kwan wɔ cocoa pa mu. Fermentation a ɛnyɛ yie tew ne quality ne boɔ so.

candidates.question_en: How often should I inspect cocoa trees?
candidates.answer_en: Inspect regularly for pests, diseases, damaged branches, weeds and moisture stress. Early detection makes management easier.
candidates.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ cocoa nnua so?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ wɔn daa sɛ mmoawa, yare, nkorabata a asɛe, nwura anaa nsuo a ɛsua wɔ asase mu wɔ hɔ. Sɛ wohu ɔhaw ntɛm a, ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ so.

candidates.question_en: How can I keep a cocoa plantation clean?
candidates.answer_en: Remove excessive weeds, dead material and diseased parts safely. Keep pathways accessible so trees can be inspected and harvested efficiently.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama cocoa afuo no ho atew?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nwura a ɛdɔɔso, nneɛma a awu ne afã a yare aka ho yiye. Ma akwan a wokɔ so yɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ nnua no na woagye aba.

candidates.question_en: Why is shade important for young cocoa?
candidates.answer_en: Young cocoa benefits from moderate shade because it reduces heat and water stress while the seedlings establish. Shade should be managed as the trees grow.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na sunsuma ho hia ma cocoa nketewa?
candidates.answer_twi: Cocoa nketewa nya mfasoɔ fi sunsuma a ɛnyɛ dodo mu efisɛ ɛtew ɔhyew ne nsuo a ɛyera so bere a aba no resiesie ne ho. Bere a nnua no nyin no, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhwɛ sunsuma no so.

candidates.question_en: Why is pruning important in cocoa?
candidates.answer_en: Pruning helps improve light and air movement, removes unwanted growth and makes it easier to inspect and harvest the trees.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na twitwa cocoa nnua ho hia?
candidates.answer_twi: Twitwa nnua no boa ma owia ne mframa kɔ mu yie, yi nnyinaso a ɛnsɛ na ɛma ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ nnua no na woagye aba.

items.question_en: How can I process palm fruits into oil at home?
items.answer_en: To process palm oil at home: harvest fresh bunches and ferment for 3-5 days to loosen fruits, thresh fruits from the bunch, boil fruits for 30-60 minutes until soft, pound or press to separate oil from fiber, add water and boil the pulp again, skim oil from the surface, filter through cloth, boil the filtered oil to remove water (until bubbling stops), and cool before storing in sealed containers. Traditional palm press improves extraction efficiency.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meyɛ ngo wɔ fie?
items.answer_twi: Yɛ ngo wɔ fie eyi: gye bɔ foforo na ma wɔn da nnafoa 3-5 sɛ aba no pae yie, gye aba fi bɔ no ho, hyew aba no sɛntɔ 30-60 kosi sɛ wɔyɛ mmerɛ, tutu anaa pɛm sɛ yi ngo fi nsennua mu, de nsuo ka aba no ka ho na hyew bio, yi ngo fi so, hun wɔ ntama mu, hyew ngo a wɔahun no sɛ yi nsuo (kosi sɛ bubble ahwie), na ma ɛhuru ansa na waguina wɔ nkuku a apo so. Traditional palm press boa sɛ wunya ngo dodo.

candidates.question_en: How do I know when palm fruits are ready to harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Palm fruits are ready when they turn reddish-orange and some fruits start falling naturally from the bunch. Use a long-handled chisel or harvesting sickle to cut the bunch from the tree. Collect fallen fruits from the ground too. Process within 24-48 hours of harvest to avoid free fatty acid buildup which reduces oil quality.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye abe aba yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Abe aba wie ase bere a wɔdan kɔkɔɔ-ɛda na aba bi firi bɔ afi ne ho pɛ. Fa long-handled chisel anaa harvesting sickle twa bɔ no fi dua no ho. Gye aba a atu gu asase so nso. Yɛ adwuma wɔ dafe 24-48 akyi a wogye sɛ free fatty acid nbi dodo a ɛsua ngo ho pa.

candidates.question_en: How can I process coconut into different products?
candidates.answer_en: Coconut can be processed into coconut oil by grating mature coconut extracting the milk and boiling until oil separates, coconut cream and milk for cooking, desiccated coconut from dried grated flesh, coconut shell charcoal and crafts, coconut fibre from the husk for mats and ropes, and coconut water which is a popular beverage. In coastal Ghana there is good market for fresh coconuts coconut oil and coconut water. Value addition significantly increases income from coconut farming.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ kuuku yɛ nneɛma ahorow ma sika?
candidates.answer_twi: Wobetumi de kuuku yɛ: kuuku ɔman de grate kuuku a ɛatwa so yi nsuo afei hyehye kosi sɛ ɔman pae fi, kuuku cream ne nsuo ma aduan, desiccated kuuku fi dried grated flesh, kuuku ano faako charcoal ne adwuma, kuuku saa fi husk ma dua mpaboa ne tow, na kuuku nsuo a ɛyɛ nsuo a wɔpɛ. Wɔ Ghana mpoano hɔ, dwa pa wɔ kuuku foforɔ, kuuku ɔman ne kuuku nsuo ho. Value addition ma sika a ɛfiri kuuku adwuma kɔ so pii.

candidates.question_en: How do I start a palm plantation in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with deep well-drained soils and rainfall above 1500 mm annually. Obtain certified tenera seedlings from CSIR-Oil Palm Research Institute at Kusi. Plant at 9 by 9 metres triangular spacing giving about 143 trees per hectare. Apply NPK fertilizer twice yearly. Palms begin producing after 3 to 4 years and remain productive for 25 to 30 years. Join the Ghana Oil Palm Development Company cooperative for support and guaranteed market.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase abɛ afuom wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ tia yie ne nsuo tew na nsuo a ɛtɔ biara afe hyɛ 1500 mm so. Gye certified tenera seedlings fi CSIR-Oil Palm Research Institute wɔ Kusi. De to mu wɔ 9 ne 9 metres triangular ahodɔ a ɛma nnuaba 143 wɔ hectare biara mu. De NPK ferefere to ho mprɛn mmienu biara afe. Abɛ fi ase wɔ aduane mfe mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan akyi na ɛgyina so wɔ mfe 25 kɔ 30. Ka Ghana Oil Palm Development Company kuo ho ma wɔboa wo ne dwa gyinae.

candidates.question_en: How should I grow coconut trees in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Coconut grows best along coastal areas and in areas with high rainfall. Plant whole mature coconuts or purchase nursery seedlings. Dig a hole 1 metre deep and wide, add compost to the base and plant the seedling. Space at 7 to 10 metres apart. Coconut begins bearing fruit after 6 to 10 years depending on variety. Dwarf varieties like Malayan Dwarf produce earlier at 3 to 4 years. Apply potassium-rich fertilizer for good fruit production.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ meto kuuku nnuaba wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Kuuku to yie wɔ mpoano ho ne hɔ a nsuo tɔ yie. De kuuku a ɛatwa so pɛpɛɛpɛ to mu anaa gye nursery seedlings. Boro awia a ɛtelɛ ne teaa metre baako, de compost to ase na to seedling. Fa ahodɔ 7 kɔ 10 metres. Kuuku fi ase de nsuo wɔ mfe 6 kɔ 10 akyi sɛ variety no so. Dwarf varieties te sɛ Malayan Dwarf de nsuo ntɛm wɔ mfe mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan. De ferefere a potassium wɔ mu to ho ma nsuo pa.

candidates.question_en: How should I care for young coconut trees?
candidates.answer_en: Care for young coconut trees by watering deeply twice a week for the first 2 years especially during dry season. Apply NPK fertilizer with high potassium every 6 months. Keep the area around the base of the tree free from grass and weeds for 2 metres. Mulch around the base to retain moisture. Protect from cattle and goats which will eat young fronds. The rhinoceros beetle is a major pest that bores into the crown. Control it by removing dead palms from the vicinity and using a hooked tool to remove beetles from the crown.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ kuuku nnuaba a wɔ mmofra ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ kuuku nnuaba mmofra ho de quench tia mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas mfe mmienu a ɛdi kan mu a ɛhia pii bone berɛ. De NPK ferefere a potassium wɔ mu pii to ho mprɛnsa nsia biara. Kora baabi a ɛbɛn nnuaba no ase nhawan ne nhaban foforo fi ho sɛntimita mmienu. Mulch ho sɛ ɛkora nsuo. Hwɛ nnwan ne birekyie a wɔbɛdi mmofra nhaban ho. Rhinoceros beetle yɛ adwummaker kɛse a ɛbɔ kɔtɔ wɔ crown mu. Boa ho de yi nnuaba a awu wɔ ho fi ne de hooked tool yi beetles fi crown mu.

items.question_en: How can trees support a farm?
items.answer_en: Trees can provide shade, wind protection, organic matter and products such as fruit or timber, while suitable agroforestry can improve farm resilience.
items.question_twi: Sɛn na nnua betumi aboa afuo?
items.answer_twi: Nnua tumi ma sunsuma, bɔ mframa ho ban, ma organic matter na ma fruit anaa timber, na agroforestry a ɛfata tumi ma afuo no nya ahoɔden bere tenten.

candidates.question_en: How can mulch help during drought?
candidates.answer_en: Mulch reduces evaporation, protects the soil surface and can help conserve moisture around crop roots.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na mulch betumi aboa bere a ɔpɛ wɔ hɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Mulch tew nsuo a ɛyera so, bɔ asase anim ho ban na ɛboa ma nsuo tena nnɔbae ntini ho.

candidates.question_en: How can water harvesting support dry-season farming?
candidates.answer_en: Stored water can supplement irrigation during dry periods when designed and managed safely.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na nsuo a yɛboaboa ano betumi aboa ɔpɛ bere kuayɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsuo a wɔakora no tumi boa irrigation wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu sɛ wɔayɛ no yie na wɔhwɛ so wɔ ahobammɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: What is the benefit of planting windbreaks?
candidates.answer_en: Windbreaks can reduce wind speed, protect crops from wind damage and reduce moisture loss.
candidates.question_twi: Mfasoɔ bɛn na windbreak wɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Windbreak tew mframa ahoɔden so, bɔ nnɔbae ho ban fi mframa sɛe ho na tew nsuo yera so.

candidates.question_en: How can farmers prepare for floods?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid planting in high-risk low areas where possible, improve drainage, protect soil structure and have a plan for moving inputs and livestock to safer areas.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie m'afuo ama nsuyiri?
candidates.answer_twi: Mma wotɔ nnɔbae wɔ mmeae a nsuyiri taa ba sɛ wubetumi akwati, siesie drainage, bɔ asase structure ho ban na nya plan sɛnea wobɛfa nneɛma ne mmoa akɔ baabi a ahobammɔ wɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can farmers prepare for a late rainy season?
candidates.answer_en: Monitor local weather information, choose suitable planting dates and varieties, conserve soil moisture and avoid planting too early into dry soil.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn asiesie m'akuayɛ ma osu bere no akyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ local weather nsɛm, paw bere ne variety a ɛfata, kora nsuo wɔ asase mu na mma wofiri ase dua ntɛm wɔ asase a ɛda so yɛ kusuu mu.

candidates.question_en: Why should farmers maintain soil cover?
candidates.answer_en: Soil cover reduces erosion, limits moisture loss and protects soil from intense rainfall and heat.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ akuafoɔ ma asase no kata?
candidates.answer_twi: Asase a covered no tew erosion so, tew nsuo yera so na bɔ asase no ho ban fi osu den ne ɔhyew ho.

items.question_en: When should I harvest sorghum?
items.answer_en: Harvest sorghum when grain is hard, heads have turned their mature color, and moisture content is around 20-25%. Dry after harvest before storage. Harvest promptly to avoid bird damage.
items.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ megye ɔtɛ?
items.answer_twi: Gye ɔtɛ bere a aba no ayɛ den, aba no dinn adan wɔn rere na nsukuro yɛ bɛn 20-25%. Yaw akyi a wogye ansa na waguina. Gye ntɛm sɛ anomaa mfomso anba.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce post-harvest losses?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest at the right time, handle produce gently to avoid bruising, dry grains properly, store in appropriate conditions, transport in ventilated containers, and sell quickly for perishables. Post-harvest losses in Ghana can reach 30-40%.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi yɛ na m'aduan a megye no akyi anko mpoano?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye nnuaba bere a ɛsɛ, de nnuaba no a eye yie sɛ ɛnhow, yaw nnuaba a ayaw no yie, guina wɔ bae a ɛsɛ, de kɔ bae a mframa tumi pue mu, na tɔn ntɛm sɛ ɛyɛ aduan a ɛsɛe ntɛm. Ghana mu aduan a ɛko aseɛ wɔ gye akyi betumi kɔ 30-40%.

candidates.question_en: What time of day is best for harvesting vegetables?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest vegetables in the early morning when temperatures are cool. This helps produce stay fresh longer. Avoid harvesting in midday heat. For leafy vegetables, harvest with dew still present for crispness.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn wɔ da mu na ɛyɛ ɔkorɔ sɛ wogye nnuan?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye nnuan owia da ano bere a owia hye no ayɛ tirim. Eyi ma nnuan no tena pɛ sen ara. Bɔ hwɛ wɔ awia mu ahuhuro mu gye nnuan. Nhaban nnuan ho, gye won a nsuyiri da won so ara da no ho nkae.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce post-harvest losses on my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Post-harvest losses in Ghana can be up to 40 percent of the harvest. Reduce losses by harvesting at the right maturity stage, handling produce gently to avoid bruising, drying produce properly before storage, using improved hermetic storage bags like GrainPro or metal silos for grains, building ventilated storage for roots and tubers, processing excess produce into value-added products, and connecting to buyers before harvest to reduce time between field and market.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ ho sɛ me nnuaba nhunu yi akyi?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba ahunu akyi yi Ghana bɛtumi akosi 40 percent. Sua ahunu de yi bere a ɛyɛ papa pa, dii wo nnuaba no yie sɛ ɛnsɔre, ma nnuaba no tew yie ansa na woguina mu, de improved hermetic storage bags te sɛ GrainPro anaa metal silos ma aba, tu ventilated storage ma nnɔho biara, de nnuaba a ɛboro so yɛ aduan a bo kɔ so, na ka buyers ho ansa na wuyi sɛ ɛhia bere ketewa wɔ afuom ne dwa ntam.

candidates.question_en: What is contract farming and how does it benefit farmers?
candidates.answer_en: Contract farming is an agreement between a farmer and a buyer before the season starts. The buyer agrees to purchase your produce at a fixed price after harvest. Benefits include guaranteed market, sometimes free inputs on credit, and technical support.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na contract farming yɛ na ɛboa me sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Contract farming yɛ apam a ɛda okuafo ne adeɛtɔ kuo ntam ansa na bere no aba. Adeɛtɔ kuo no ka ho sɛ wɔbɛtɔ wo nnuaba boɔ a wɔaka akyi a wogye. Mfaaso ho ne: aguabasa a wɔadaa ho, adenneɛ a wɔde brɛ wo ka mu mmere bi, ne nnwuma boa.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce post-harvest losses in vegetables?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest vegetables early in the morning when cool, handle gently, sort out damaged ones immediately, store in cool ventilated areas, and sell quickly. For leafy vegetables, wrap in damp cloth to extend freshness. Avoid long transport in hot conditions.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi sua nnuan a megye wɔn akyi mpoano?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye nnuan owia da ano bere a ɛhuru, de wɔn pɛ, yi a wɔasɛe ntɛm ara, guina wɔ bae a ɛhuru na mframa pue mu, na tɔn ntɛm. Nhaban nnuan ho, de ntama nte de sɛɛ wɔn sɛ ɛma wɔn tena pɛ.

candidates.question_en: What is Fairtrade certification and what are its benefits for farmers?
candidates.answer_en: Fairtrade certification guarantees farmers a minimum price for their produce that covers production costs plus a social premium that is invested in community development. Benefits include: stable income even when world prices drop, Fairtrade premium funds for schools, health, and infrastructure, access to pre-financing before harvest, better trading relationships, and marketing support. Fairtrade is common in Ghana for cocoa, coffee, and fresh fruit. Contact Fairtrade Africa for information.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Fairtrade kratafa yɛ na mfaaso bɛn na ɛwɔ ho ma okuafo?
candidates.answer_twi: Fairtrade kratafa hɔ kura sɛ okuafo nya boɔ a ɛdata wɔn nnuaba a ɛkata adwuma ho sika ne social premium a wɔde fa oman nkosuo mu. Mfaaso ho ne: sika a ɛda pɛ bere a amanaman boɔ tow, Fairtrade premium sika ma sukuu, yadeɛ, ne nkosuo adwuma, nya sika ansa na wogye nnuaba, adwuma ho apam a ɛyɛ pa, ne adwuma ho boa. Fairtrade pɛ wɔ Ghana ho ma kookoo, kɔfi, ne aba foforo. Ka kyerɛ Fairtrade Africa sɛ wunya nsɛm.

candidates.question_en: What are the benefits of joining a farmer cooperative?
candidates.answer_en: Benefits of farmer cooperatives include: collective bargaining power for better input prices and higher selling prices, shared access to expensive equipment like tractors and storage facilities, group loans that may be easier to access than individual loans, collective learning and knowledge sharing, risk pooling among members, access to bulk markets that individual farmers cannot reach, and stronger political voice when advocating for farmer interests with government.
candidates.question_twi: Mfaaso bɛn na ɛwɔ ho wɔ si okuafo cooperative?
candidates.answer_twi: Okuafo cooperative mfaaso ho ne: kuo tumi kɛse ma adenneɛ boɔ sua ne tɔn boɔ kɛse, ka egyapade a wɔboɔ yɛ den te sɛ tractor ne guina fie ho bom, kuo ka a ɛtumi yɛ mmerɛ sɛ nya sen onipa ho ka, kuo suahu ne nyansam kyɛ, mfomso sesae wɔ kuo mu, nya aguabasa kɛse a okuafo baako nntumi nkɔ hɔ, ne kuo mu tumi kɛse bere a wɔka okuafo ho nsɛm kyerɛ ɔman.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect stored food from rats and mice?
candidates.answer_en: Keep the storage area clean and free of food scraps. Seal all holes and cracks in walls. Use snap traps or approved rodenticides. Store bags on raised platforms away from walls. Cats are also effective.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora m'aduan a maguina fi ɔkra ne okusie ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora guina fie no horo na aduan asennua ntena mu. Popa tumtum ne ɛwɔwɔ nyinaa wɔ bɔ mu. Fa snap traps anaa dawuro a wɔagyei de kum ɔkra. Guina bags wɔ platform a ɛda sor tete akyi. Agyinamoa nso yɛ adwuma pa.

items.question_en: How long can fresh cassava be stored after harvest?
items.answer_en: Fresh cassava deteriorates within 24-72 hours after harvest. For longer storage, process into dried chips, gari, or flour. Waxing the roots can extend fresh storage to about a week. Keep in cool, shaded areas.
items.question_twi: Bere ahe na metumi guina bankye a megye no akyi?
items.answer_twi: Bankye foforo sɛe wɔ dafe 24-72 akyi a wogye no. Sɛ wohwehwɛ guina bere tenten a, yɛ no bankye chips a ayaw, gari, anaa mfurow. Waxing bankye no de tumi ma no tena pɛ bere koro nnawotwe mu. Wura no wɔ bae a ɛhuru na owia ntra mu.

candidates.question_en: How should I harvest cassava properly?
candidates.answer_en: Cassava is usually harvested 9-18 months after planting. Cut the stem at 30-40 cm height then loosen the soil around the plant with a hoe and pull up the roots. Handle roots gently to avoid bruising.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na megye m'bankye yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Bankye taa gye wɔ abosome 9-18 akyi a wode to mu. Twa tibo no wɔ sɛntimita 30-40 so, afei de akɔde fa asase a ɛhyia nnua no ho na twe ntini no sor. De ntini no pɛ efisɛ sɛ ehow a ɛma ɛsɛe ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: How many acres of cassava do I need to make a meaningful profit?
candidates.answer_en: To make meaningful profit from cassava you need at least 2 to 5 acres. With improved varieties and good management, 5 acres can yield 40 to 75 tonnes of fresh cassava. At current market rates this translates to GHS 24,000 to 45,000 in revenue. After deducting costs of GHS 6,000 to 10,000 for a 5-acre farm, profit can be GHS 14,000 to 35,000 per season. Processing into gari or starch doubles or triples this profit.
candidates.question_twi: Asase ahe na mɛhia sɛ bankye adwuma ade sika ba?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛnya mfaso pa fi bankye mu a, wohia sɛ eka mmienu kɔ num pɛ. De improved varieties ne adwuma pa, eka num tumi de bankye foforɔ nnɔho 40 kɔ 75 tonne. Wɔ dwa bo a wɔwɔ saa ara, eyi bɛyɛ GHS 24,000 kɔ 45,000. Nnuaha wo costs GHS 6,000 kɔ 10,000 ma eka num afuom akyi, mfaso bɛtumi ayɛ GHS 14,000 kɔ 35,000 bere biara. De yɛ gari anaa starch a ɛde mfaso mmienu anaa mmiɛnsa ba.

candidates.question_en: How much money can I make from one acre of cassava?
candidates.answer_en: From one acre of cassava using improved varieties, you can harvest 8 to 15 tonnes of fresh roots. At a farm gate price of GHS 150 to 200 per bag, you can earn GHS 3,000 to 6,000 per acre after deducting input and labour costs of about GHS 800 to 1,200. Cassava farming is most profitable when you process it into gari, starch or fufu flour before selling.
candidates.question_twi: Mfa sika ahe bɛfata me wɔ bankye eka baako mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi bankye eka baako mu de varieties pa to mu a, wobetumi anya bankye fofor nnɔho 8 kɔ 15 tonne. Sɛ efie dwa kɛse bɛyɛ GHS 150 kɔ 200 biara bag ho a, wobetumi nya GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000 biara eka baako akyi a wogu inputs ne adwuma a ɛyɛ GHS 800 kɔ 1,200 ho. Bankye adwuma ho bo tɔ sen a wode ayɛ gari, starch anaa fufu flour ansa na wotɔ.

candidates.question_en: What can I do with cassava peels and other cassava waste?
candidates.answer_en: Cassava peels can be dried and used as animal feed for goats, sheep and pigs, providing a valuable energy source. Fresh peels fermented for 3 to 4 days make good pig and poultry feed. Cassava peel compost improves soil fertility. The starchy water from gari processing can be fermented and used as a fermented cassava drink called pito or as a substrate for mushroom growing. Using cassava by-products reduces waste and adds extra income streams.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ bankye ho ne nsononko ho adwuma yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Bankye ho bɛtumi atew na de ma mmoa te sɛ birekyie, oguan ne prako aduan, de energy toɔ to. Bankye ho foforɔ a wɔde ferment adays mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan yɛ prako ne akoko aduan pa. Bankye ho compost boa asase aduan. Nsuo a starch wɔ mu fi gari yɛ ho bɛtumi aferment na de yɛ nsuo aduan a wɔfre no pito anaa de yɛ substrate ma mushroom noa. De bankye by-products de hyɛ nsono mu hia na ɛhia sika ahoma foforɔ.

candidates.question_en: How do I select healthy cassava stems for planting?
candidates.answer_en: Select stems from healthy mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old. The stem should be firm, not shrivelled, about 2 to 3 cm thick and 20 to 30 cm long with at least 5 nodes. Avoid stems from diseased plants or those showing mosaic virus symptoms. Store cuttings in the shade for no more than 3 days before planting.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick bankye abɔ pa sɛ mede to mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi abɔ fi bankye nnuaba pa a wɔawo akyi mfee 8 kɔ 12. Abɔ no nni yie, mmaadwa gu ho, bɛyɛ sɛntimita 2 kɔ 3 tiawa na sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 tenten a ɛwɔ nodes 5 pɛ. Gye wo ho fi abɔ a ɛfi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho anaa a ɛkyerɛ mosaic virus ho nsono. Guina cutting no wɔ hare ha mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa pɛ ansa na wode to mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I add value to my farm produce to earn more money?
candidates.answer_en: Process raw produce into higher-value products: dry and package grains, make tomato paste, gari from cassava, or palm oil from palm fruits. Value addition reduces post-harvest losses and increases income.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mede boɔ ka m'afuo nnuaba ho sɛ menya sika dodo?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ aduan foforo no yɛ aduan a wɔtɔ boɔ kɛse: yaw na paka nnuaba a ayaw, yɛ ntomato paste, gari fi bankye, anaa ngo fi abe aba. Boɔ to so maa mpampa post-harvest mpoano ne ma sika dodo.

candidates.question_en: How does climate change affect farming in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Climate change in Ghana is causing more erratic rainfall, longer dry seasons, increased temperatures, more frequent flooding and drought. Adapt by using drought-tolerant varieties, adopting water harvesting techniques like half-moon pits and tied ridges, diversifying into drought-resistant crops like cowpea cassava and sorghum, using mulching to conserve soil moisture, agroforestry which involves planting trees with crops, joining early warning systems for weather forecasts, and timing planting to match current rainfall patterns rather than traditional calendars.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na climate change yɛ okuafo adwuma den wɔ Ghana na dɛn na menyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Climate change wɔ Ghana ma nsuo tɔ bere sesa daa, bone berɛ tenten, berɛhyɛ tɔ so, nsuo ne bone tɔ so. Siesie wo tiri ho de de drought-tolerant varieties to mu, de water harvesting nhyiamu te sɛ half-moon pits ne tied ridges, sesa kɔ drought-resistant nnuaba te sɛ bɔde, bankye ne sorghum, de mulching sɛ ɛkora asase nsuo, agroforestry a ɛkyerɛ to nnuaba ne nnuaba kaa bom, ka early warning systems ho ma berɛ nkra, na to aba bere sɛ nsuo a ɛtaa tɔ saa ara ho na gye traditional calendars.

candidates.question_en: What pests commonly attack cassava and how can I control them?
candidates.answer_en: Major cassava pests include cassava mealybug which causes wilting and stunted growth, cassava green mite causing leaf bronzing, and cassava whitefly which spreads mosaic virus. Control mealybug by releasing natural enemies like the parasitoid wasp Anagyrus lopezi. Remove affected plants and use clean planting material. Spray insecticidal soap or neem extract for mites and whitefly.
candidates.question_twi: Adwummaker bɛn na ɛtaa tu mako bankye na dɛn na menyɛ wɔn ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Adwummaker kɛse a ɛtaa tu bankye mako ne: cassava mealybug a ɛma nnuaba huru na nwa nni, cassava green mite a ɛma nhaban no yɛ bronze, na cassava whitefly a ɛpam mosaic virus. Boa mealybug ho de parasitoid wasp a wɔfre no Anagyrus lopezi guu. Yi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho na de planting material pa. De insecticidal soap anaa neem extract hware mites ne whitefly ho.

items.question_en: How can I grow cocoyam successfully in Ghana?
items.answer_en: Cocoyam grows best in moist fertile soils with partial shade. Plant corms or cormels at a depth of 5 to 10 cm and spacing of 60 by 60 cm. It performs well under banana or plantain canopies. Apply organic matter at planting. Cocoyam requires regular watering during dry periods and takes 7 to 12 months to mature depending on variety. Taro cocoyam and Tannia are the two main types grown in Ghana.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ meto kɔkɔnte yie wɔ Ghana?
items.answer_twi: Kɔkɔnte to yie wɔ asase a nsuo ho ne asase a ɛyɛ dɛ a ɛwɔ owia bi. De corms anaa cormels to mu wɔ tia 5 kɔ 10 sɛntimita na ahodɔ 60 ne 60 sɛntimita. Ɛbɛto yie wɔ kwadu anaa boɔde nnuaba ase. De organic matter to ho bere a wode to mu. Kɔkɔnte hia quench daadaa berɛ a nsuo annya so na ɛtwa so wɔ mfee 7 kɔ 12 mu sɛ variety no so. Taro cocoyam ne Tannia ne nhyiamu mmienu a wɔtaa to mu wɔ Ghana.

candidates.question_en: What types of pepper are commonly grown in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Common pepper types grown in Ghana include scotch bonnet which is the most popular hot pepper for local cooking and export, bird's eye pepper which is very hot and small, cayenne pepper used for spice, bell pepper for salads and fresh markets, and hot banana pepper. Scotch bonnet commands the best market price and is the most commonly grown commercially.
candidates.question_twi: Pepper nhyiamu bɛn na wɔtaa to mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Pepper nhyiamu a wɔtaa to mu wɔ Ghana ne scotch bonnet a ɛyɛ hot pepper a ɛtaa to mu sen wɔ aduan mu ne export, bird's eye pepper a ɛyɛ hyehyɛ paa na ɛketewa, cayenne pepper a wɔde yɛ spice, bell pepper ma salads ne fresh markets, na hot banana pepper. Scotch bonnet de dwa bo kɛse wɔ adwa mu na ɛyɛ adwuma kɛse pii.

candidates.question_en: How can I export my farm produce from Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: To export farm produce from Ghana register your business with GIPC if it involves foreign investment, obtain an export licence from the Ghana Export Promotion Authority, ensure your produce meets destination country phytosanitary standards by getting certificates from the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate under MOFA, have your produce inspected by Ghana Standards Authority, work with a licensed freight forwarder for logistics, and target markets with high demand for Ghanaian products like the EU for chilli and pineapple and the UK for yam and plantain.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mede me afuom nnuaba tɔ amansan foforɔ fi Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛde wo afuom nnuaba tɔ amansan foforɔ fi Ghana a, si wo adwuma ho wɔ GIPC sɛ obi fi amansan foforɔ wɔ mu, gye export licence fi Ghana Export Promotion Authority, hwɛ sɛ wo nnuaba to country a wɔde kɔ phytosanitary standards mu de certificates fi Plant Protection ne Regulatory Services Directorate wɔ MOFA ase, ma Ghana Standards Authority hwɛ wo nnuaba so, ka licensed freight forwarder ho ma logistics, na tia markets a wɔpɛ Ghana nneɛma pii te sɛ EU ma pepper ne pineapple ne UK ma bayerɛ ne boɔde.

candidates.question_en: What causes small plantain bunches and how can I increase their size?
candidates.answer_en: Small plantain bunches are caused by poor soil fertility, water stress during bunch formation, heavy pest or disease pressure especially black sigatoka, overcrowded suckers competing for nutrients, using inferior planting material, and not removing dead leaves promptly. Improve bunch size by applying NPK and potassium fertilizer regularly, irrigating during dry spells, controlling sigatoka with fungicide, desuckering to one sucker per stool, and using quality sword suckers for planting.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn ma boɔde ntama yɛ ketewa na dɛn na menyɛ sɛ ɛntɔ me?
candidates.answer_twi: Boɔde ntama nketewa ba efisɛ asase aduan hia, nsuo ahia bere a ntama reyɛ, adwummaker ne yadeɛ a ɛhia pii a black sigatoka ka ho, suckers pii a wɔdi ferefere ho brε, planting material mfa ho, na amma wo nhaban a ɛawu asiesie ntɛm. Boa ntama bo kɔ so de de NPK ne potassium ferefere to ho bere biara, quench bone berɛ mu, boa sigatoka ho de fungicide hware, desuckering kɔsi sucker baako biara stool, na de sword suckers pa to mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I control Black Sigatoka disease in plantain?
candidates.answer_en: Black sigatoka is a serious fungal disease causing black streaks on leaves that eventually kill them. Control it by removing and destroying affected leaves regularly, ensuring good drainage, maintaining adequate spacing for air circulation, and applying recommended fungicides like Mancozeb or Dithane every 2 to 3 weeks during wet seasons. Use resistant varieties like Apantu and FHIA-21 where available.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ black sigatoka yadeɛ ho wɔ boɔde ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Black sigatoka yɛ fungal yadeɛ kɛse a ɛma nhaban no yɛ black na ɛkum wɔn awiei pɛ. Boa ho de yi na sɛe nhaban a yadeɛ aba ho daadaa, hwɛ sɛ nsuo tew yie, kora ahodɔ pa sɛ mframa fa mu yie, na de fungicides a wɔagyae so te sɛ Mancozeb anaa Dithane hware mprɛnsa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa mu nsuo berɛ. De varieties a wɔagyae so te sɛ Apantu ne FHIA-21 fa to mu wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ.

candidates.question_en: How should I manage suckers in a plantain farm?
candidates.answer_en: Manage suckers by allowing only one follower sucker per stool at a time. Remove excess suckers using a sharp spade cutting them off at soil level. Choose the best positioned sword sucker as the follower. After harvest of the main bunch cut the harvested stem down to 1 metre and let it die naturally. A well-managed stool can produce continuously for 5 to 7 years. Fertilize each stool with 100 to 200 grams of NPK twice a year for sustained production.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ suckers sɛ me boɔde afuom ayɛ adwuma yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ suckers de ma sucker baako pɛ tena wɔ stool biara bere koro. Yi suckers a ɛboro so de spade akyer wɔ asase so. Yi sword sucker a ɛtete yie ma ɛyɛ follower. Ntama kɛse yi akyi twa abɔ a woyii no kɔsi metre baako na ma no wu ankasa. Stool a wohwɛ so yie tumi de nnuaba ba daadaa mfe 5 kɔ 7. De NPK gram 100 kɔ 200 to stool biara ho mprɛn mmienu biara afe ma nnoa tena so.

candidates.question_en: What is the difference between plantain farming and banana farming?
candidates.answer_en: Plantain and banana are closely related but differ in use and management. Plantain is starchier, larger and must be cooked before eating. Banana is sweeter, eaten raw and matures faster. Banana requires more water and is more sensitive to drought. Plantain is more tolerant of less fertile soils. Both need similar disease management. Commercial banana farming for export requires higher standards of pest and disease control.
candidates.question_twi: Nte sɛn bɛn na ɛwɔ boɔde adwuma ne kwadu adwuma ntam?
candidates.answer_twi: Boɔde ne kwadu yɛ bɔhyɛ bɔhyɛ nanso wɔyɛ so sɛ wɔde wɔn ho na wɔhwɛ wɔn so nte. Boɔde wɔ starch pii, ɛso sen, na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhyehye ansa na wɔbɛdi. Kwadu dɛ, na wɔdi atoa, na ɛtwa so ntɛm. Kwadu hia nsuo pii na ɛyɛ amrane wɔ bone ho. Boɔde tumi gyina asase a ferefere nni mu pii. Wɔn mmienu hia yadeɛ hwɛ koro. Kwadu kɛse adwuma ma export hia adwummaker ne yadeɛ hwɛ pa sen.

candidates.question_en: Which type of plantain sucker is best for planting?
candidates.answer_en: The best sucker for planting is the sword sucker which has narrow pointed leaves at the base and a large healthy corm. It grows faster and produces larger bunches than water suckers. The sword sucker should be 45 to 90 cm tall. Avoid planting peepers which are very small suckers, and water suckers which have broad leaves but small weak corms.
candidates.question_twi: Sucker bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ mede to mu wɔ boɔde afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Sucker a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wode to mu ne sword sucker a ɛwɔ nhaban aketewa pointɛd wɔ ase na ɛwɔ corm kɛse pa. Eba mu ntɛm na ede ntama kɛse guu sen water suckers. Sword sucker no nni yie sɛ 45 kɔ 90 sɛntimita tenten. Gye wo ho fi peepers a yɛ suckers nketewa a, na water suckers a ɛwɔ nhaban tenten nanso ɛwɔ corm kɛse mma.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce wind damage in plantain?
candidates.answer_en: Use suitable spacing, maintain healthy plants and consider wind protection where strong winds are common.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mframa sɛe so wɔ plantain mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa spacing a ɛfata, ma nnua no nyɛ ahoɔden na susuw wind protection ho wɔ mmeae a mframa den taa ba.

items.question_en: What minimum pond size is suitable for commercial fish farming?
items.answer_en: For commercial fish farming the minimum recommended pond size is 500 square metres. This size allows you to stock approximately 1,500 to 2,500 tilapia or 5,000 to 10,000 catfish fingerlings. Smaller ponds are possible but make it harder to achieve economies of scale and recover your investment. Ideally a commercial fish farm should have at least 2 to 3 ponds to allow rotation for pond maintenance and continuous production and staggered harvesting for regular income.
items.question_twi: Pond ketewa bɛn na ɛhia ma adwuma kɛse apataa?
items.answer_twi: Ma adwuma kɛse apataa, pond ketewa a wɔakyerɛw so ne square metres 500. Kɛse yi ma wubetumi ade tilapia bɛyɛ 1,500 kɔ 2,500 anaa catfish fingerlings 5,000 kɔ 10,000 to mu. Ponds nketewa yɛ bebiara nanso ɛyɛ den sɛ wonya mfaso yie na wonya wo sika bio. Bere biara, adwuma kɛse apataa afuom nini yie sɛ ponds mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa wɔ hɔ sɛ ɛboa pond hwɛ ne nnoaboa toa so pɛ ne yi aba bere biara ma owuo-teetee bere biara.

candidates.question_en: How much does it cost to start a small fish farm in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Starting a small commercial fish farm in Ghana with two earthen ponds of 500 square metres each costs approximately GHS 15,000 to 25,000 including pond construction, fingerlings, feed for one cycle, and basic equipment. A plastic tank fish farm can be started for GHS 8,000 to 15,000. The main ongoing costs are fish feed which accounts for 60 to 70 percent of total production cost. With good management you can make a profit from the first cycle.
candidates.question_twi: Sika ahe na ɛyɛ papa sɛ mefi ase apataa adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apataa adwuma ketewa kɛse fi ase wɔ Ghana de earthen ponds mmienu a square metres 500 biara wɔ mu ho teetee GHS 15,000 kɔ 25,000 a pond yɛ, fingerlings, aduan wɔ cycle baako mu, ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ papa. Plastic tank apataa adwuma wobetumi de GHS 8,000 kɔ 15,000 fi ase. Nneɛma a ɛkyere daadaa a ɛkɔ so pii ne apataa aduan a ɛyɛ adwuma agyapade 60 kɔ 70 percent. Sɛ woyɛ adwuma pa a, wobetumi anya mfaso wɔ cycle a ɛdi kan mu.

candidates.question_en: What is the best way to harvest fish from a pond?
candidates.answer_en: The best harvesting method depends on whether you are doing partial or complete harvest. For partial harvest use a seine net to selectively remove larger fish leaving smaller ones to grow. For complete harvest drain the pond partially then use nets to remove all fish. Harvest early morning when water is cool. Have containers ready with clean water or ice to keep fish alive or fresh. Weigh and record your harvest for business records. Never use chemicals or electricity to harvest as these are illegal and harmful.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛkwan bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ meyiyɛ apataa fi pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛkwan a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wuyiyɛ no kyɛ sɛ partial anaa complete harvest na woyɛ. Ma partial harvest de seine net yi apataa kɛse a wɔbɛ na ma nketewa tena so bo sɔ. Ma complete harvest sua nsuo ketewa fi pond mu afei de nets yi apataa nyinaa. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo dɛ. Ma containers a nsuo foforɔ anaa ice wɔ mu sɛ apataa aguina anaa tena foforɔ. Bu na kora wo harvest ho sɛ adwuma nsɛm. Mma wo mpo de chemicals anaa electricity yiyɛ efisɛ ɛnyɛ nea mmara gyina so na ɛyɛ bɔne.

candidates.question_en: When should I harvest tilapia?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest tilapia when they reach market size of 300 to 500 grams which typically takes 5 to 6 months from fingerling stage. Monitor growth by sampling fish monthly using a net. Harvest in the early morning when water temperature is cool to reduce fish stress. Partial harvesting at 4 months removes larger fish and allows smaller ones to grow. Sell fresh fish immediately or ice them for transport to market.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na meyiyɛ me tilapia apataa?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi tilapia bere a wɔkɔ si dwa kɛse a nnɔho 300 kɔ 500 gram a ɛtaa kyɛ mfee 5 kɔ 6 fi fingerling mu. Hwɛ sɛ apataa rebɛbo yie de sample apataa bere biara de net. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo berɛ dɛ sɛ apataa nhunu. Partial yi wɔ mfee nnan mu yi apataa kɛse na ma nketewa bo sɔ. Tɔ apataa fofor ntɛm anaa de ice ka ho ma akɔ dwa.

candidates.question_en: How can I construct a low-cost earthen fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with clay soil that holds water well, near a reliable water source. Mark out the pond area typically 20 by 25 metres. Dig to a depth of 1.5 to 2 metres with sloping sides for stability. Build an inlet pipe to bring water in and an outlet pipe at the deepest point to drain. Pack the dikes firmly to prevent leaks. Fill with water and leave for 2 weeks to cure and establish algae before stocking. The total cost including excavation for a 500 square metre pond is typically GHS 3,000 to 6,000.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ earthen apataa pond a bo sua?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ clay asase a ɛkora nsuo yie, bɛn nsuo kwan pa. Kyerɛ pond area a ɛtaa yɛ metres 20 ne 25. Boro kɔsi tia metres 1.5 kɔ 2 a ho mfimfini slopes wɔ gyinae ho. Tu inlet pipe sɛ nsuo aba mu na outlet pipe wɔ tia no so sɛ nsuo fa mu. Hyehye dikes no yie sɛ nsuo anyi. Ma nsuo kɔ mu na gyina nnansas mmienu sɛ ɛtena na algae ntua fɔw ansa na wode apataa to. Bo nyinaa a excavation ka ho ma pond a square metres 500 wɔ mu taa yɛ GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent overcrowding in a fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Stock according to the pond's capacity and monitor fish growth, water quality and available oxygen.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpataa dodo so wɔ pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa dodow a pond no tumi soa no gu mu na hwɛ mpataa nyin, nsuo quality ne oxygen a ɛwɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: What should I do if fish stop feeding suddenly?
candidates.answer_en: Check water quality, temperature, oxygen, recent weather, feed quality and signs of disease before increasing feed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ sɛ mpataa gyae di aduane ntɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsuo quality, ɔhyew, oxygen, weather a aba foforo, feed quality ne yare ho nsɛnkyerɛnne ansa na woama feed no so.

candidates.question_en: How should a fish farmer keep pond records?
candidates.answer_en: Record stocking date and number, feed used, mortalities, water-quality observations, treatments, harvest weight and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛw fish pond records?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw stocking da ne dodow, feed a wode dii dwuma, mpataa a awuwu, nsuo quality nsɛm, ayaresa, harvest duru ne tɔn.

items.question_en: How can rabbit production be made more profitable?
items.answer_en: Control feed costs, reduce mortality, maintain good breeding performance, keep records and target reliable markets.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama rabbit kuayɛ anya mfasoɔ pii?
items.answer_twi: Hwɛ aduane sika so, te owu so, ma breeding yɛ papa, kyerɛwtohɔ na nya gua a wobɛtumi anya ho ahotoso.

candidates.question_en: How do I start a small rabbit farm?
candidates.answer_en: Begin with healthy breeding stock, suitable housing, reliable feed and water, a cleaning routine and a simple production record system.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahyɛ rabbit kuayɛ ketewa ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi rabbits a wɔyɛ ahoɔden mu ase, nya dan a ɛfata, aduane ne nsuo a wɔde di dwuma daa, ahotew nhyehyɛe ne kyerɛwtohɔ ketewa.

candidates.question_en: How should rabbit manure be handled?
candidates.answer_en: Collect it regularly and compost or manage it appropriately before applying it to crops.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ rabbit dɔte?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye dɔte no daa na yɛ compost anaa hwɛ so yie ansa na wode agu nnɔbae so.

candidates.question_en: What records are useful in rabbit farming?
candidates.answer_en: Keep records of mating, kindling, litter size, growth, treatments, deaths and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛm bɛn na mfaso wɔ rabbit kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw mating, awo, litter size, nyin, ayaresa, owu ne tɔn.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce heat stress in rabbits?
candidates.answer_en: Provide shade, ventilation, clean water and protect cages from direct heat during hot periods.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate heat stress so wɔ rabbits mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma sunsuma, mframa kɔ mu, nsuo pa na bɔ cages no ho ban fi ɔhyew tee ho bere a ɛyɛ hyew.

candidates.question_en: Why should rabbits not be kept in dirty cages?
candidates.answer_en: Dirty housing increases odour, parasites and disease risks and can reduce animal performance.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔde rabbits tena cage a ɛho ntew?
candidates.answer_twi: Cage fĩ ma hua bɔne, parasites ne yare dɔɔso na ɛtumi tew mmoa no ahoɔden ne nyin so.

candidates.question_en: How do I identify a sick rabbit?
candidates.answer_en: Watch for reduced feeding, unusual behaviour, diarrhoea, breathing problems, discharge or sudden weight loss.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ rabbit bi ayare?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛ ɔnni aduane, ne suban asesa, ɔyɛ ahonhon, ne ho tumi pue nsuo, anaa ne duru resa ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: What makes a rabbit housing unit suitable?
candidates.answer_en: It should be dry, well ventilated, secure from predators and easy to clean.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma rabbit dan yɛ papa?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɛyɛ yera, mframa kɔ mu, ɛbɔ rabbits ho ban fi mmoa a wɔyɛ wɔn ayayade ho na ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wɔhohoro.

items.question_en: What are whiteflies and how can I remove them from my crops?
items.answer_en: Whiteflies are tiny white insects that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Control them by spraying insecticidal soap, neem oil, or imidacloprid. Yellow sticky traps also help. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer which attracts them.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn yi adwummakers fitaa fi m'nnɔbae so?
items.answer_twi: Whitefly yɛ adwummakers fitaa ketewa a wɔnom nnuaba mogya na wɔde yadeɛ brɛ. Kora wɔn ase wɔ adwummakers dawuro sabɔ, neem dawuro, anaa imidacloprid so. Yellow sticky traps nso boa. Bɔ hwɛ nitrogen ferefere dodo efisɛ ɛtwe wɔn.

candidates.question_en: What are whiteflies and how can I get rid of them?
candidates.answer_en: Whiteflies are tiny white insects that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Control them by spraying insecticidal soap, neem oil, or imidacloprid. Yellow sticky traps also help. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer which attracts them.
candidates.question_twi: Adwummakers fitaa a wɔwɔ m'nnuan so yɛ dɛn na metumi yi wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fitaa abowa yɛ adwummakers fitaa ketewa a wɔnom nnuaba mogya na wɔde yadeɛ brɛ. Kora wɔn ase wɔ adwummakers dawuro sabɔ, neem dawuro, anaa imidacloprid so. Yellow sticky traps nso boa. Bɔ hwɛ nitrogen ferefere dodo efisɛ ɛtwe wɔn.

candidates.question_en: Can too much fertilizer damage my crops?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, over-fertilizing can burn plant roots and leaves, cause excessive leafy growth with poor fruiting, pollute water sources, and waste money. Always follow the recommended rates on fertilizer bags or advice from your extension officer. Start with less and increase gradually based on crop response.
candidates.question_twi: Ferefere dodo tumi sɛe m'nnuaba anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, ferefere dodo tumi hyew nnuaba ntini ne nhaban, ma nnuaba nhaban da sor dodo na aba ba sua, ha nsuo mu, na seaa sika. Bue ferefere bag so krataa nhyɛso anaa fa wo extension officer nsɛm di. Fi ferefere sua na fa dodo so kakra kakra wɔ nnuaba tebea so.

candidates.question_en: What causes leaf-tip burn and how can I fix it?
candidates.answer_en: Leaf tip burn can be caused by: fertilizer burn from too much nitrogen or potassium, salt stress from poor quality irrigation water, calcium deficiency, water stress during hot weather, or wind damage. Check your fertilizer rates and water quality first. Apply calcium fertilizer and ensure consistent watering. The condition often improves once the cause is corrected.
candidates.question_twi: M'nnuaba nhaban ɔkyɛ yɛ sɛ wɔahyew. Dɛn na ɛhia?
candidates.answer_twi: Nhaban ɔkyɛ hyew betumi fi: ferefere burn fi nitrogen anaa potassium dodo, salt ɔkɔm fi nsuo a enni pa, calcium hia, nsuo hia wɔ ahuhuro mu, anaa mframa ɔkɔm. Hwɛ wo ferefere kɛse ne nsuo ho pa ansa. De calcium ferefere to so na kora nsuo to pɛ. Tebea no taa yɛ pa bere a wuyɛ dawuro.

candidates.question_en: What is GlobalGAP certification and how does it help farmers export produce?
candidates.answer_en: GlobalGAP (Good Agricultural Practices) is an international certification standard that verifies produce is grown safely and sustainably. It is required by most European supermarkets to import fresh produce. Getting certified opens doors to premium export markets. Requirements include: safe pesticide use with records, worker welfare, environmental protection, and food safety. In Ghana, groups like PFAG (Pesticide and Fertilizer Association of Ghana) can help farmers get certified.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na GlobalGAP kratafa yɛ na ɛboa okuafo sɛ wɔde nnuaba kɔ amanaman?
candidates.answer_twi: GlobalGAP (Good Agricultural Practices) yɛ amanaman kratafa nhyɛso a ɛkyerɛ sɛ nnuaba kura yie na ɛho tumi. Yurop supermarkets bebree hia sɛ na wɔde nnuaba foforo ba. Nya kratafa no bue aguabasa kɛse a wɔtɔn wɔn boɔ kɛse. Nhyɛso ho ne: adwummakers dawuro fa a ɛho tumi ne nsɛm kora, adwumafo ho hwɛ, ɛwim ho hwɛ, ne aduan ho tumi. Wɔ Ghana, kuo te sɛ PFAG (Pesticide and Fertilizer Association of Ghana) tumi boa okuafo nya kratafa.

candidates.question_en: How can I increase my cocoa yield?
candidates.answer_en: Prune cocoa trees regularly to remove dead wood and improve light. Apply recommended fertilizers. Control black pod disease by removing infected pods and spraying copper-based fungicides. Replace unproductive old trees with improved varieties.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi ma m'kookoo da sor dodo?
candidates.answer_twi: Twa kookoo nnua so pɛ sɛ yi dua kum ne nnua a wɔawu fi mu na ma owia hyɛ mu. De ferefere a wɔaka to so. Kora black pod yadeɛ ase wɔ yi pods a wɔayarɛ na de copper fungicide guare so. Si nnua kedee a wonnya bi fi wɔn ho na de aba foforɔ a ɛda sor wɔ wɔn beae.

candidates.question_en: What does NPK mean on a fertilizer bag?
candidates.answer_en: NPK stands for Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K) — the three main nutrients plants need. Nitrogen helps leafy growth, Phosphorus supports root development and flowering, and Potassium strengthens stems and improves fruit quality. The numbers like 15-15-15 show the percentage of each nutrient in the bag.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na NPK kyerɛ wɔ ferefere bag so?
candidates.answer_twi: NPK kyerɛ Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), ne Potassium (K) — aduan titiriw mmiɛnsa a nnuaba hia. Nitrogen boa nhaban da sor, Phosphorus boa ntini ne abode, na Potassium ma tibo yɛ den na aba yɛ pa. Nɔma te sɛ 15-15-15 no kyerɛ kɛse a aduan biara wɔ bag mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I use YouTube to learn better farming practices?
candidates.answer_en: YouTube has thousands of free farming tutorials. Search for: specific crop names plus 'farming Ghana', pest or disease names plus 'how to control', fertilizer application techniques, irrigation setup guides, and post-harvest handling. Subscribe to channels like IITA, CTA Agriculture, and local Ghanaian farming channels. Download videos on WiFi to watch offline when you are at the farm without internet access.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mefa YouTube di dwuma sɛ sua okuafo adwuma anammɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: YouTube wɔ okuafo adwuma nhyehyɛe ahorow a ɛyɛ daa. Hwehwɛ: nnuaba din ne 'farming Ghana', adwumakers anaa yadeɛ din ne 'how to control', ferefere to anammɔn, nsuo to nhyehyɛe, ne gye akyi hwɛ ase anammɔn. Kyerɛw wo din wɔ channels te sɛ IITA, CTA Agriculture, ne Ghana okuafo channels. Sii videos wɔ WiFi so sɛ wuhwɛ wɔn bere a wowɔ afuo so na internet nni hɔ.

candidates.question_en: What food-safety practices should farmers follow?
candidates.answer_en: Key food safety practices for farmers include: washing hands before handling produce, using clean water for irrigation especially on leafy vegetables, applying pesticides according to label instructions and respecting pre-harvest intervals, not using human waste as fertilizer, keeping animals away from vegetable gardens, using clean equipment and containers, and training farm workers on hygiene practices.
candidates.question_twi: Aduan ho tumi anammɔn bɛn na okuafo sɛ bu wɔn so?
candidates.answer_twi: Aduan ho tumi anammɔn a ɛhia ma okuafo ne: hohoro wo nsa ansa na wohwɛ nnuaba ho, fa nsuo horo sɛ to nnuaba so titiriw nhaban nnuan so, de adwummakers dawuro to wɔ krataa nhyɛso so na bu pre-harvest bere so, mfa onipa aguare yɛ ferefere, mma mmoa nnuaba afuo mu, fa egyapade ne nkuku horo, na kyerɛ afuo adwumafo aduan ho tumi anammɔn.

items.question_en: What is the difference between tilapia and catfish farming?
items.answer_en: Tilapia is easier to manage, tolerates lower water quality, feeds on plankton and algae as well as pellets, and is cheaper to produce. Catfish grows faster, commands a higher market price, tolerates very low oxygen levels but needs more protein in feed. Catfish farming gives higher profit per fish but requires more management. Many farmers in Ghana combine both species for diversified income.
items.question_twi: Nte sɛn bɛn na ɛwɔ tilapia ne catfish adwuma ntam?
items.answer_twi: Tilapia yɛ mmerɛw sɛ wohwɛ so, ɛtumi gyina nsuo a ɛnni yie, ɛdi plankton ne algae ne pellets nso, na bo wɔ to a ɛsua. Catfish bo sɔ ntɛm, dwa bo yɛ so sen, ɛtumi gyina oxygen nketewa a wɔ nsuo mu nanso ɛhia protein pii wɔ aduan mu. Catfish adwuma de mfaso kɛse ba ma apataa baako baako nanso ɛhia adwuma pii. Akuafo pii wɔ Ghana de nhyiamu mmienu kaa bom sɛ wɔnya owuo-teetee foforo.

candidates.question_en: What is the best way to harvest fish from a pond?
candidates.answer_en: The best harvesting method depends on whether you are doing partial or complete harvest. For partial harvest use a seine net to selectively remove larger fish leaving smaller ones to grow. For complete harvest drain the pond partially then use nets to remove all fish. Harvest early morning when water is cool. Have containers ready with clean water or ice to keep fish alive or fresh. Weigh and record your harvest for business records. Never use chemicals or electricity to harvest as these are illegal and harmful.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛkwan bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ meyiyɛ apataa fi pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛkwan a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wuyiyɛ no kyɛ sɛ partial anaa complete harvest na woyɛ. Ma partial harvest de seine net yi apataa kɛse a wɔbɛ na ma nketewa tena so bo sɔ. Ma complete harvest sua nsuo ketewa fi pond mu afei de nets yi apataa nyinaa. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo dɛ. Ma containers a nsuo foforɔ anaa ice wɔ mu sɛ apataa aguina anaa tena foforɔ. Bu na kora wo harvest ho sɛ adwuma nsɛm. Mma wo mpo de chemicals anaa electricity yiyɛ efisɛ ɛnyɛ nea mmara gyina so na ɛyɛ bɔne.

candidates.question_en: When should I harvest tilapia?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest tilapia when they reach market size of 300 to 500 grams which typically takes 5 to 6 months from fingerling stage. Monitor growth by sampling fish monthly using a net. Harvest in the early morning when water temperature is cool to reduce fish stress. Partial harvesting at 4 months removes larger fish and allows smaller ones to grow. Sell fresh fish immediately or ice them for transport to market.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na meyiyɛ me tilapia apataa?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi tilapia bere a wɔkɔ si dwa kɛse a nnɔho 300 kɔ 500 gram a ɛtaa kyɛ mfee 5 kɔ 6 fi fingerling mu. Hwɛ sɛ apataa rebɛbo yie de sample apataa bere biara de net. Yi anɔpa bere a nsuo berɛ dɛ sɛ apataa nhunu. Partial yi wɔ mfee nnan mu yi apataa kɛse na ma nketewa bo sɔ. Tɔ apataa fofor ntɛm anaa de ice ka ho ma akɔ dwa.

candidates.question_en: How much does it cost to start a small fish farm in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Starting a small commercial fish farm in Ghana with two earthen ponds of 500 square metres each costs approximately GHS 15,000 to 25,000 including pond construction, fingerlings, feed for one cycle, and basic equipment. A plastic tank fish farm can be started for GHS 8,000 to 15,000. The main ongoing costs are fish feed which accounts for 60 to 70 percent of total production cost. With good management you can make a profit from the first cycle.
candidates.question_twi: Sika ahe na ɛyɛ papa sɛ mefi ase apataa adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Apataa adwuma ketewa kɛse fi ase wɔ Ghana de earthen ponds mmienu a square metres 500 biara wɔ mu ho teetee GHS 15,000 kɔ 25,000 a pond yɛ, fingerlings, aduan wɔ cycle baako mu, ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ papa. Plastic tank apataa adwuma wobetumi de GHS 8,000 kɔ 15,000 fi ase. Nneɛma a ɛkyere daadaa a ɛkɔ so pii ne apataa aduan a ɛyɛ adwuma agyapade 60 kɔ 70 percent. Sɛ woyɛ adwuma pa a, wobetumi anya mfaso wɔ cycle a ɛdi kan mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I construct a low-cost earthen fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Select a site with clay soil that holds water well, near a reliable water source. Mark out the pond area typically 20 by 25 metres. Dig to a depth of 1.5 to 2 metres with sloping sides for stability. Build an inlet pipe to bring water in and an outlet pipe at the deepest point to drain. Pack the dikes firmly to prevent leaks. Fill with water and leave for 2 weeks to cure and establish algae before stocking. The total cost including excavation for a 500 square metre pond is typically GHS 3,000 to 6,000.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ earthen apataa pond a bo sua?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi asase a ɛwɔ clay asase a ɛkora nsuo yie, bɛn nsuo kwan pa. Kyerɛ pond area a ɛtaa yɛ metres 20 ne 25. Boro kɔsi tia metres 1.5 kɔ 2 a ho mfimfini slopes wɔ gyinae ho. Tu inlet pipe sɛ nsuo aba mu na outlet pipe wɔ tia no so sɛ nsuo fa mu. Hyehye dikes no yie sɛ nsuo anyi. Ma nsuo kɔ mu na gyina nnansas mmienu sɛ ɛtena na algae ntua fɔw ansa na wode apataa to. Bo nyinaa a excavation ka ho ma pond a square metres 500 wɔ mu taa yɛ GHS 3,000 kɔ 6,000.

candidates.question_en: What should I do if fish stop feeding suddenly?
candidates.answer_en: Check water quality, temperature, oxygen, recent weather, feed quality and signs of disease before increasing feed.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ sɛ mpataa gyae di aduane ntɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsuo quality, ɔhyew, oxygen, weather a aba foforo, feed quality ne yare ho nsɛnkyerɛnne ansa na woama feed no so.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent overcrowding in a fish pond?
candidates.answer_en: Stock according to the pond's capacity and monitor fish growth, water quality and available oxygen.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mpataa dodo so wɔ pond mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa dodow a pond no tumi soa no gu mu na hwɛ mpataa nyin, nsuo quality ne oxygen a ɛwɔ mu.

candidates.question_en: How should a fish farmer keep pond records?
candidates.answer_en: Record stocking date and number, feed used, mortalities, water-quality observations, treatments, harvest weight and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyerɛw fish pond records?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw stocking da ne dodow, feed a wode dii dwuma, mpataa a awuwu, nsuo quality nsɛm, ayaresa, harvest duru ne tɔn.

items.question_en: When should I deworm cattle and what should I use?
items.answer_en: Deworm cattle every 3 to 4 months using broad-spectrum anthelmintics like Ivermectin which controls both internal and external parasites, Albendazole or Levamisole. Deworm at the start of the rainy season when parasite burden peaks and again at the start of the dry season. Always weigh or estimate the body weight of each animal to administer the correct dose. Underdosing causes resistance. Rotate between dewormers annually. Calves need more frequent deworming every 6 to 8 weeks.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ nnwan mu adwummaker na bere bɛn?
items.answer_twi: Wia nnwan mu adwummaker mprɛnsa mmiɛnsa kɔ nnan de broad-spectrum anthelmintics te sɛ Ivermectin a ɛboa internal ne external parasites mmienu, Albendazole anaa Levamisole. Wia nsuo berɛ akyirikyiri bere a parasites taa pii ne bone berɛ akyirikyiri bio. Bu anaa hunu nnwan biara nnɔho sɛ wobɛma dose a ɛyɛ papa. Dose hiana ma resistance. Sesa dewormers afe biara. Calves hia deworming a ɛtaa sen nnansas nsia kɔ nwɔtwe.

candidates.question_en: Which fodder crops are suitable for cattle in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Good fodder crops for cattle in Ghana include Napier grass which produces high biomass and can be harvested every 6 to 8 weeks, Guinea grass, Stylosanthes guianensis which is a nutritious legume that fixes nitrogen, Centrosema which is a climbing legume, Leucaena trees which provide protein-rich pods and leaves, and Mucuna which is an excellent dry season fodder. Establish a fodder plot of at least 0.5 hectares per cow. Cut and carry feed to cattle rather than letting them graze uncontrolled to improve feed efficiency.
candidates.question_twi: Fodder nnuaba bɛn na mede ato mu sɛ mede ma me nnwan wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Fodder nnuaba pa ma nnwan wɔ Ghana ne Napier grass a ɛde biomass pii ba na wubetumi ayi bere biara nnansas nsia kɔ nwɔtwe, Guinea grass, Stylosanthes guianensis a ɛyɛ legume pa a ɛde nitrogen ka, Centrosema a ɛyɛ climbing legume, Leucaena nnuaba a ɛde pods ne nhaban a protein wɔ mu pii ba, na Mucuna a ɛyɛ bone berɛ fodder pa. Tu fodder plot a hectares 0.5 pɛ biara bɔ. Yi na de aduan kɔ nnwan nkyɛn na gye wo ho fi sɛ wɔnkɔ wɔ ho ho so sɛ ɛboa aduan de yie.

candidates.question_en: How do I start cattle farming in Ghana?
