candidates.answer_en: Cattle farming requires significant capital and land. Common breeds in Ghana include the West African Shorthorn, White Fulani and Red Fulani. Start with 5 to 10 cows and 1 bull. Secure adequate grazing land of at least 1 hectare per animal or have a crop and fodder production plan. Vaccinate against CBPP, FMDV and rinderpest. Deworm quarterly. Keep records of breeding, feeding and health. Consider joining the National Cattle Farmers Association for market access and support.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mefi ase nnwan adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnwan adwuma hia sika kɛse ne asase. Breeds a wɔpɛ wɔ Ghana ne West African Shorthorn, White Fulani ne Red Fulani. Fi ase de nnwankow 5 kɔ 10 ne ɔbarima baako. Hwɛ sɛ nhawan asase ho hia sɛ hectare baako biara nnwan anaa wɔ nnuaba ne fodder to mu plan. Hware so ma CBPP, FMDV ne rinderpest. Wia adwummaker mprɛnsa nnan. Kora nsɛm ho sɛ bɔhyɛ, aduan ne health. Twe wo adwene ho fi ase wɔ National Cattle Farmers Association ho ma dwa kɔ ho ne mmoa.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve the productivity of local cattle?
candidates.answer_en: Improve local cattle productivity by crossbreeding with improved exotic bulls like Friesian, Brown Swiss or Sahiwal through artificial insemination services available from CSIR-Animal Research Institute. Improve nutrition through fodder production of improved grasses like Panicum maximum and Stylosanthes, supplement with concentrate feed for breeding cows and calves, deworm and vaccinate regularly, and provide mineral supplements. Better management alone can increase productivity by 30 to 50 percent.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me local nnwan nnoa bo kɔ so?
candidates.answer_twi: Boa local nnwan nnoa ho de crossbreeding ne improved exotic bulls te sɛ Friesian, Brown Swiss anaa Sahiwal wɔ artificial insemination services a CSIR-Animal Research Institute de. Boa aduan ho de fodder to mu a improved grasses te sɛ Panicum maximum ne Stylosanthes, de concentrate feed ka ho ma breeding cows ne calves, wia adwummaker ne hware bere biara, na de mineral supplements ka ho. Adwuma pa pɛ tumi ma nnoa kɔ so 30 kɔ 50 percent.

candidates.question_en: What is green manure and how do I use it?
candidates.answer_en: Green manure means growing specific crops like legumes or grasses and then plowing them back into the soil while still green. This adds organic matter and nitrogen to the soil. Common green manure crops include cowpea, mucuna, and lablab. Plow them in at least 3 weeks before planting your main crop.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na nhwiren-tew ferefere yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Nhwiren-tew ferefere kyerɛ kura nnuaba bi te sɛ abɔdweɛ anaa atɛntɛnni na afei boro wɔn gu asase mu bere a wɔda koraa. Eyi de nhwiren foforo ne nitrogen ka asase ho. Nhwiren-tew ferefere nnuaba a wɔtaa di dwuma ne abɔdweɛ, mucuna, ne lablab. Boro wɔn gu asase mu wiemu 3 ansa na wokura wo nnuaba titiriw.

candidates.question_en: What vaccines do cattle need in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Essential vaccines for cattle in Ghana include CBPP (Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia) vaccine given annually, FMD (Foot and Mouth Disease) vaccine twice yearly in endemic areas, blackleg vaccine for calves and Lumpy Skin Disease vaccine. Contact your nearest Veterinary Services Directorate office under MOFA for the current vaccination programme and schedule. Government vaccination campaigns also take place periodically and are subsidized.
candidates.question_twi: Vaccines bɛn na nnwan hia wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Vaccines a nnwan hia wɔ Ghana ne CBPP (Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia) vaccine a wɔde to ho afe biara, FMD (Foot and Mouth Disease) vaccine mprɛn mmienu afe biara wɔ hɔ a yadeɛ wɔ, blackleg vaccine ma calves ne Lumpy Skin Disease vaccine. Ka Veterinary Services Directorate ofisi a ɛbɛn wo wɔ MOFA ase sɛ wɔde vaccination programme foforɔ ne schedule no bɛkyerɛ wo. Aban vaccination campaigns nso wɔ bere biara na wɔde nsua.

candidates.question_en: What is trypanosomiasis and how does it affect cattle in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Trypanosomiasis also called nagana or sleeping sickness in cattle is transmitted by the tsetse fly and is common in the forest and transition zones of Ghana. Affected cattle show weight loss, anaemia, enlarged lymph nodes, fever and eventually death. Control by treating affected animals with diminazene aceturate, managing tsetse fly through bush clearing and insecticide-treated traps, and keeping cattle in areas with low tsetse fly populations. N'Dama and West African Shorthorn breeds have natural tolerance.
candidates.question_twi: Trypanosomiasis yɛ dɛn na ɛyɛ nnwan den te sɛn wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Trypanosomiasis a wɔfre no nagana anaa sleeping sickness wɔ nnwan mu ne yadeɛ a tsetse fly de tete na ɛtaa ba wɔ Ghana kwaeɛ ne ntam zones. Nnwan a yadeɛ aba ho hunu nnɔho, wɔ mogya wɔn mu, lymph nodes a ɛso, oniwa ne owu awiei pɛ. Boa ho de hu nnwan a yadeɛ aba ho de diminazene aceturate, tsetse fly hwɛ de kuro tokuru ne insecticide-treated traps, na kora nnwan wɔ hɔ a tsetse fly nni so pii. N'Dama ne West African Shorthorn breeds wɔ tumi a ɛfa wɔn ankasa.

candidates.question_en: Why should cattle have access to shade and clean water?
candidates.answer_en: Shade reduces heat stress while clean, reliable water supports hydration, feed intake and normal body functions.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ anantwi nya sunsuma ne nsuo pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Sunsuma te heat stress so, na nsuo pa a wɔnya daa boa hydration, aduane di ne nipadua no nnwuma a ɛfata.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve the quantity and quality of cow milk?
candidates.answer_en: Improve cow milk quality and quantity by: feeding balanced rations including good pasture, silage, hay, and concentrate feed; providing clean water always; milking at the same time every day; maintaining good hygiene during milking; treating and preventing mastitis (udder inflammation) promptly; providing shade and reducing stress; and selecting productive dairy breeds or crossing local cattle with improved breeds.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi ma m'boo nufuo pa ara?
candidates.answer_twi: Siesie boo nufuo ho pa ne kɛse wɔ: ma aduan a ɛpɛ wɔn ho yie a mu wɔ atɛntɛnni pa, silage, hay, ne concentrate aduan; de nsuo horo ma wɔn daa; nom wɔn nufuo bere koro da biara; kora ho tumi bere a wonuom nufuo; yɛ dawuro ma na kora mastitis (nufuo mu yadeɛ) ntɛm; ma ewim brɛ wɔn na mma wɔn nhaw; na paw boo a wɔn nufuo yɛ pa anaa ka beae boo ne boo foforɔ a ɛda sor bom.

items.question_en: What can snails eat on a farm?
items.answer_en: Provide suitable fresh plant materials and balanced supplementary feed appropriate for the farming system.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na snails tumi di wɔ afuo mu?
items.answer_twi: Ma wɔn nhaban ne nnɔbae a ɛyɛ foforo a ɛfata ne supplementary feed a ɛkari pɛ sɛ system no hia.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect snails from predators?
candidates.answer_en: Use secure housing, mesh or barriers and check regularly for ants, rodents, birds and other predators.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn abɔ snails ho ban fi mmoa a wɔdi wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa housing a ɛyɛ den, mesh anaa barriers na hwɛ afuo no daa sɛ ants, okusie, anomaa ne mmoa foforo nnya wɔn.

candidates.question_en: How do I reduce snail mortality?
candidates.answer_en: Maintain suitable moisture, hygiene, feed quality and protection while monitoring the snails regularly.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate snail owu so?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma moisture yɛ pɛ, ma ahotew, feed quality ne protection yɛ papa na hwɛ snails no daa.

candidates.question_en: Why does humidity matter in snail farming?
candidates.answer_en: Snails need a moist environment to remain active and feed properly, but excessive standing water should be avoided.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na humidity ho hia wɔ snail kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Snails hia tebea a ɛyɛ nwini sɛ wɔbɛtena ase na wɔadidi yie, nanso mma nsuo nnyina hɔ dodo.

candidates.question_en: How should harvested snails be handled?
candidates.answer_en: Handle them carefully, keep them clean and use hygienic storage and transport practices.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ snails a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa ahwɛyiye, ma wɔn ho tew na fa akwan a ɛho tew di dwuma wɔ guina ne transport mu.

candidates.question_en: Can snail farming be done on a small scale?
candidates.answer_en: Yes. It can begin on a small scale if housing, moisture, feeding and predator control can be managed.
candidates.question_twi: Snail kuayɛ tumi yɛ ketewa anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane. Wobetumi afi ase ketewa sɛ wubetumi ahwɛ housing, nsuo, aduane ne mmoa a wɔdi snails no so.

candidates.question_en: Why should snail pens be kept shaded?
candidates.answer_en: Shade helps prevent overheating and excessive drying of the environment.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ snail pen nya sunsuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Sunsuma boa ma ɔhyew nnya mmoa no na ɛmma beae no nnyɛ yera dodo.

candidates.question_en: How do I choose a site for snail farming?
candidates.answer_en: Choose a cool, shaded, humid and secure site with good drainage and protection from direct sunlight.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw beae ama snail kuayɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw beae a ɛnwɔ ɔhyew dodo, ɛwɔ sunsuma, nsuo wɔ mu kakra, ɛbɔ mmoa no ho ban na nsuo tumi firi mu yie.

items.question_en: How can I tell whether snails are growing well?
items.answer_en: Monitor shell development, body size, feeding activity and survival over time.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ snails renyin yie?
items.answer_twi: Hwɛ wɔn shell development, nipadua kɛse, sɛnea wɔdi ne wɔn survival bere nyinaa.

candidates.answer_en: Snails need a moist environment to remain active and feed properly, but excessive standing water should be avoided.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na humidity ho hia wɔ snail kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Snails hia tebea a ɛyɛ nwini sɛ wɔbɛtena ase na wɔadidi yie, nanso mma nsuo nnyina hɔ dodo.

items.question_en: Why are farmer field demonstrations useful?
items.answer_en: Demonstrations allow farmers to see a practice under local conditions and compare results with familiar methods.
items.question_twi: Adɛn nti na farmer field demonstration wɔ mfasoɔ?
items.answer_twi: Ɛma akuafoɔ hu kuayɛ kwan bi wɔ wɔn mpɔtam ankasa mu na wɔtumi toto ne nea wɔnim dedaw no ho.

candidates.question_en: Why should I record planting dates?
candidates.answer_en: Planting dates help you track crop duration, compare seasons and plan future farm activities.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mekyerɛw planting dates?
candidates.answer_twi: Planting dates boa ma wohu nna a nnɔbae no de nyin, toto seasons ho na siesie farm adwuma a ɛbɛba no.

candidates.question_en: How can farmer groups help with information sharing?
candidates.answer_en: Groups can share market information, labour, equipment, experiences, training opportunities and links to extension services.
candidates.question_twi: Sɛn na farmer groups betumi aboa wɔ nsɛm kyɛmu mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kuo tumi kyɛ market nsɛm, adwumayɛfo, equipment, osuahu, training opportunities ne kwan a wɔbɛfa so anya extension services.

candidates.question_en: Why should I record crop failures?
candidates.answer_en: Recording failures helps identify repeated problems such as pests, poor timing, drought, disease or unsuitable varieties.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mekyerɛw nnɔbae a wɔsɛe?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛboa ma wohu ɔhaw a ɛsan ba bio te sɛ mmoawa, bere a woplant no, ɔpɛ, yare anaa variety a ɛnsɛ.

candidates.question_en: How can a farmer calculate yield per acre?
candidates.answer_en: Divide the total marketable harvest from the plot by the plot area measured in acres, using consistent units.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn abu yield wɔ acre baako so?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyɛ harvest a wotɔn no nyinaa wɔ plot no so mu acre dodow a plot no yɛ, na fa unit koro di dwuma bere nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: What farm records should a beginner start with?
candidates.answer_en: Start with crop area, planting date, seed used, major inputs, labour, harvest quantity, sales and major expenses.
candidates.question_twi: Farm records bɛn na beginner okuafoɔ ɛsɛ sɛ ofi ase de?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi crop area, da a wotɔɔ, aba a wode dii dwuma, inputs titiriw, adwumayɛfo, harvest dodow, tɔn ne sika a wode yɛ adwuma ase.

candidates.question_en: How can I use last season's farm records to plan the next season?
candidates.answer_en: Update them as activities happen rather than waiting until the end of the season. Frequent records are more accurate and useful.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn de last season farm records asiesie season foforo?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw records no bere a adwuma no rekɔ so, na mma ntwɛn season no awie. Records a wɔkyerɛw daa yɛ nokware na wɔboa paa.

items.question_en: How should breeding rabbits be selected?
items.answer_en: Choose healthy animals with good body condition, sound feet and a history of good growth or reproduction.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw rabbits a mɛde ayɛ breeding?
items.answer_twi: Paw mmoa a wɔyɛ ahoɔden, wɔn nipadua tebea yɛ pa, wɔn nan yɛ den na wɔn nyin anaa reproduction ho abakɔsɛm yɛ papa sɛ ɛwɔ hɔ.

candidates.question_en: How should rabbit manure be handled?
candidates.answer_en: Collect it regularly and compost or manage it appropriately before applying it to crops.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ rabbit dɔte?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye dɔte no daa na yɛ compost anaa hwɛ so yie ansa na wode agu nnɔbae so.

candidates.question_en: How do I start a small rabbit farm?
candidates.answer_en: Begin with healthy breeding stock, suitable housing, reliable feed and water, a cleaning routine and a simple production record system.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahyɛ rabbit kuayɛ ketewa ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Fi rabbits a wɔyɛ ahoɔden mu ase, nya dan a ɛfata, aduane ne nsuo a wɔde di dwuma daa, ahotew nhyehyɛe ne kyerɛwtohɔ ketewa.

candidates.question_en: What makes a rabbit housing unit suitable?
candidates.answer_en: It should be dry, well ventilated, secure from predators and easy to clean.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma rabbit dan yɛ papa?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɛyɛ yera, mframa kɔ mu, ɛbɔ rabbits ho ban fi mmoa a wɔyɛ wɔn ayayade ho na ɛyɛ mmerɛ sɛ wɔhohoro.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce heat stress in rabbits?
candidates.answer_en: Provide shade, ventilation, clean water and protect cages from direct heat during hot periods.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate heat stress so wɔ rabbits mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma sunsuma, mframa kɔ mu, nsuo pa na bɔ cages no ho ban fi ɔhyew tee ho bere a ɛyɛ hyew.

candidates.question_en: Why should rabbits not be kept in dirty cages?
candidates.answer_en: Dirty housing increases odour, parasites and disease risks and can reduce animal performance.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔde rabbits tena cage a ɛho ntew?
candidates.answer_twi: Cage fĩ ma hua bɔne, parasites ne yare dɔɔso na ɛtumi tew mmoa no ahoɔden ne nyin so.

candidates.question_en: How do I identify a sick rabbit?
candidates.answer_en: Watch for reduced feeding, unusual behaviour, diarrhoea, breathing problems, discharge or sudden weight loss.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ rabbit bi ayare?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛ ɔnni aduane, ne suban asesa, ɔyɛ ahonhon, ne ho tumi pue nsuo, anaa ne duru resa ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: What records are useful in rabbit farming?
candidates.answer_en: Keep records of mating, kindling, litter size, growth, treatments, deaths and sales.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛm bɛn na mfaso wɔ rabbit kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw mating, awo, litter size, nyin, ayaresa, owu ne tɔn.

items.question_en: How do I set up a brooder for day-old chicks?
items.answer_en: A brooder provides warmth for day-old chicks in the first 2 to 3 weeks. Use a heat lamp or electric bulb hung 45 cm above the floor in a circular guard made from cardboard or wire. Maintain temperature at 35 degrees Celsius in week one reducing by 3 degrees each week. Spread wood shavings as litter 5 to 7 cm deep. Provide water in chick-sized drinkers and starter feed in shallow trays. Watch chick behaviour to adjust temperature correctly.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ brooder ketewa ma day-old chicks?
items.answer_twi: Brooder de berɛhyɛ ma day-old chicks wɔ nnansas mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa a ɛdi kan mu. De heat lamp anaa electric bulb a wɔde a so sɛntimita 45 fi asase so wɔ circular guard a wɔde cardboard anaa waya yɛ mu. Kora berɛ wɔ degrees 35 Celsius nnansa baako mu a ɛkɔ sua degrees mmiɛnsa bere biara. Terɛ wood shavings yɛ litter sɛntimita 5 kɔ 7 tia. De nsuo wɔ chick-sized drinkers na starter feed wɔ trays tete. Hwɛ chicks ahyɛso sɛ wobɛtua berɛ no ho yie.

candidates.question_en: How do I prepare a simple farm budget?
candidates.answer_en: A simple farm budget lists all expected income and all expected costs for one season. Income includes expected yield multiplied by expected price. Costs include land preparation, seeds, fertilizer, pesticides, labour for planting weeding and harvesting, transport and packaging. Subtract total costs from total income to get expected profit. Always add a 10 to 15 percent buffer for unexpected costs. Review your actual results against the budget after each season to improve planning for the next season.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ afuom budget ketewa?
candidates.answer_twi: Afuom budget ketewa kyerɛ owuo-teetee a wohwia ne costs nyinaa ma bere baako. Owuo-teetee ka ho nnoa a wohwia a wɔde dwa bo a wohwia bu. Costs ka ho asase siesie, aba, ferefere, pesticides, adwuma ma to mu, nhaban foforo yi ne yi, transport ne packaging. Gui costs nyinaa fi owuo-teetee nyinaa mu sɛ wohunu mfaso a wohwia. De 10 kɔ 15 percent buffer ka ho ma costs a onhwia. Hwɛ wo actual results tia budget akyi bere biara sɛ ɛboa wo siesie adwuma pa ma bere a ɛdi hɔ.

candidates.question_en: How can I get land for farming in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Access farming land in Ghana through several ways including purchasing outright if you have capital, sharecropping where you farm another person's land and share the harvest usually 50 50, leasing land through a written agreement typically 5 to 20 years in peri-urban areas, accessing communal lands through the chief or family head in rural areas, and government land allocations for special farming zones. Always secure a written land use agreement even for sharecropping arrangements to protect your investment.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ menya asase ma okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Nya asase ma okuafo adwuma wɔ Ghana de akwan ahorow a ɛka ho de gye to sɛ wo wɔ sika, sharecropping a woto obi asase so na fa nnoa twa mmienu pɛ taa yɛ 50 50, lease asase de nhyiam krataa taa bɛyɛ mfe 5 kɔ 20 wɔ dɔn ho, nya communal asase wɔ ohene anaa abusua panyin nkyɛn wɔ kurow ho, na aban asase kyɛ ma okuafo adwuma zones a wɔayɛ. Hwɛ sɛ wotwerɛ asase de nhyiam krataa bere biara naaso sharecropping nhyiamu ma wo sɛ ɛhwɛ wo sika so.

candidates.question_en: How can I grow soybean commercially for profit?
candidates.answer_en: Soybeans are highly profitable legumes. Plant after rains are well established. Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium bacteria before planting (this fixes nitrogen and can triple yields). Space 30-45 cm within rows and 60 cm between rows. Apply phosphorus fertilizer at planting. Weed once at 3 weeks. Harvest when 95% of pods have turned yellow-brown. Dry to 12% moisture before storage. Soybeans have strong demand from oil processors and animal feed manufacturers.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura soya yɛ adwuma sɛ menya sika?
candidates.answer_twi: Soya yɛ abɔdweɛ a ɛde sika ba pa ara. To akyi a osu asi yie. De Bradyrhizobium bacteria ka aba ho ansa na woto (eyi fi nitrogen na ɛtumi ma nnuaba da sor mprɛ mmiɛnsa). Gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 30-45 wɔ ntam ne sɛntimita 60 wɔ nnua so ntam. De phosphorus ferefere to mu bere a wode to. Tia nhaban foforo bere a ɛto so mmiɛnsa no nnawotwe baako. Gye bere a 95% fidie no adan hoho bɔɔ. Yaw kosi 12% nsuku ansa na waguina. Soya hia yɛ kɛse wɔ ngo adwuma kuo ne mmoa aduan adwuma kuo ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm from flooding and waterlogging?
candidates.answer_en: Protect your farm from flooding and waterlogging by planting on raised beds or ridges especially for vegetables and root crops, digging drainage channels around the field perimeter to direct excess water away, avoiding farming in flood-prone low-lying areas during heavy rain seasons, choosing flood-tolerant varieties where possible, using cover crops and mulching to reduce runoff, and planting trees or grass strips along slopes to slow water flow and reduce erosion.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me afuom annya nsuo tia?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye wo afuom fi nsuo ho de to mu wɔ beds a ɛtele anaa ridges a ɛhia pii ma nnuaba ne nnɔho, boro drainage channels fa afuom no ho nyinaa sɛ ɛde nsuo a ɛboro so kɔ ho, gye wo ho fi okuafo adwuma wɔ hɔ a nsuo taa tia wɔ nsuo berɛ kɛse mu, yi flood-tolerant varieties wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ, de cover crops ne mulching sua runoff, na to nnuaba anaa nhawan strips wɔ mmepɔ ho sɛ ɛhia nsuo kwan na sua erosion.

candidates.question_en: How can I manage irrigation efficiently and reduce water waste?
candidates.answer_en: Manage irrigation efficiently by irrigating in the early morning or evening to reduce evaporation losses, using drip irrigation which delivers water directly to the root zone reducing waste by up to 50 percent compared to overhead sprinkler systems, mulching to retain soil moisture, monitoring soil moisture before irrigating rather than watering on a fixed schedule, levelling fields to ensure even water distribution, and fixing leaks in pipes and channels promptly.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mede quench pa yie sɛ me nsa nsuo?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ quench yie de quench wɔ anɔpa anaana anaa awia ansanaan sɛ ɛhia evaporation suas, de drip quench a ɛde nsuo kɔ nnɔho asase mu nsɛm sua nsa suas kɔ 50 percent tia overhead sprinkler systems tia, mulch sɛ asase nsuo agua, hwɛ asase nsuo ansa na woquench na gye wo ho fi quench schedule a ɛte so, siesie fields sɛ nsuo kɔ yie, na sa nsuo kwan mu holes ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: What is vermicomposting and how do I start it?
candidates.answer_en: Vermicomposting uses earthworms to break down organic waste into very high-quality compost called vermicompost or worm castings. To start: get a container or build a wooden box, add bedding of moist shredded newspaper or cardboard, add earthworms (red wigglers are best), feed with fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, and eggshells. Avoid meat, dairy, and oily food. Harvest the rich compost from the bottom every 2-3 months.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na vermicomposting yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mesi ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Vermicomposting fa asase nwirɛntwi di dwuma sɛ pɛ nhwiren foforo asennua yɛ compost a ɛwɔ aduan pa pa ara a wɔfre vermicompost anaa worm castings. Sɛ wohwehwɛ si ase: nya nkuku anaa yɛ dua box, de krataa anaa cardboard a wɔatwa twa na wɔapo mu de yɛ mpa, de asase nwirɛntwi hyɛ (red wiggler yɛ pa pa ara), de nnuan ne aba asennua, coffee, ne kosua nkuku hyɛ. Bɔ hwɛ nam, nkyene aduan, ne ngo aduan. Gye compost a ɛwɔ ase hɔ no abosome 2-3 biara.

candidates.question_en: What are nematodes and how do they affect crops?
candidates.answer_en: Nematodes are microscopic worms that live in soil. Some are harmful to crops — they attack roots causing galls (swellings), stunted growth, and yellowing. They are common in sandy soils and warm climates. Control by rotating crops, using resistant varieties, adding organic matter to soil, and solarizing soil (covering with clear plastic to heat it and kill nematodes during the dry season).
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na nematode yɛ na ɛyɛ m'nnuaba dɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Nematode yɛ nwirɛntwi a wɔte asase mu a wɔhunu da. Bi yɛ nnuaba ɔkɔm — wɔtwe ntini ho ma ɛyɛ kɛse, nnuaba nni sor yie, na nhaban hoho. Wɔtaa wɔ asintiɛ asase ne ahuhuro mu. Kora ase wɔ sesa nnuaba, fa aba a ɛtumi hyɛ ase, de nhwiren foforo ka asase ho, na solarize asase (fa plastik fitaa sɛɛ so sɛ ɛhye mu na kum nematode wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu).

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce the cost of organic farming inputs?
candidates.answer_en: Reduce input costs through organic farming by making your own compost from crop residues and animal manure, using biological pest controls like neem leaf extract and predatory insects instead of chemical pesticides, planting legumes in rotation to fix nitrogen naturally reducing need for nitrogen fertilizer, using intercropping to suppress weeds naturally, collecting and saving open-pollinated seeds rather than buying hybrid seeds each season, and building soil health over time to reduce fertilizer dependence.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ organic farming sɛ ɛhia inputs sika sua?
candidates.answer_twi: Sua inputs sika de organic farming de yɛ wo ankasa compost fi nnuaba a ato fɛw ne mmoa aguare, de biological pest controls te sɛ neem nhaban extract ne predatory insects na gye wo ho fi chemical pesticides, to legumes mu wɔ rotation sɛ ɛde nitrogen ka asase mu ankasa a ɛhia nitrogen ferefere sua, de intercropping hia nhaban foforo ankasa, pam na guina open-pollinated aba na gye wo ho fi gye hybrid aba bere biara, na tu asase ho bere biara sɛ ferefere nhia nansen.

items.question_en: How can I protect my farm from theft?
items.answer_en: Protect your farm by: building proper fencing with thorny hedges or wire fencing, using watchdogs especially at harvest time, forming community vigilance groups with neighboring farmers, harvesting promptly when crops are ready to minimize field time after ripening, installing basic alarm systems if affordable, registering your farm to establish legal ownership, and developing good relationships with neighboring community members.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora m'afuo fi korɔmfo ho?
items.answer_twi: Kora wo afuo wɔ: si fense yie wɔ nkyerɛ nhwiren anaa wire, fa ɔkraman kora titiriw bere a wogye nnuaba, si kuo ne okuafo a wɔbɛn wo sɛ wɔhwɛ so, gye nnuaba ntɛm bere a ɛawie ase sɛ afuo mu bere sua akyi a nnuaba awi, si basic alarm sɛ sika wɔ ho, kyerɛw wo afuo din sɛ wunya asase krataa yie, na yɛ abakɔsɛm yie ne oman mu nnipa a wɔbɛn wo.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm from flooding and waterlogging?
candidates.answer_en: Protect your farm from flooding and waterlogging by planting on raised beds or ridges especially for vegetables and root crops, digging drainage channels around the field perimeter to direct excess water away, avoiding farming in flood-prone low-lying areas during heavy rain seasons, choosing flood-tolerant varieties where possible, using cover crops and mulching to reduce runoff, and planting trees or grass strips along slopes to slow water flow and reduce erosion.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me afuom annya nsuo tia?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye wo afuom fi nsuo ho de to mu wɔ beds a ɛtele anaa ridges a ɛhia pii ma nnuaba ne nnɔho, boro drainage channels fa afuom no ho nyinaa sɛ ɛde nsuo a ɛboro so kɔ ho, gye wo ho fi okuafo adwuma wɔ hɔ a nsuo taa tia wɔ nsuo berɛ kɛse mu, yi flood-tolerant varieties wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ, de cover crops ne mulching sua runoff, na to nnuaba anaa nhawan strips wɔ mmepɔ ho sɛ ɛhia nsuo kwan na sua erosion.

candidates.question_en: How should I keep records for my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Keep a simple farm diary or notebook. Record planting dates, inputs purchased and costs, labor hired and paid, crop activities, harvest quantities, and sales. Simple mobile apps or voice memos on your phone can help record activities easily.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora m'afuo nsɛm?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora afuo krataa anaa nsɛmpoma ketewa. Kora aba to da, adenneɛ a wotɔ ne won boɔ, dwumadie a wohwɛ ne sika a wode twaa, afuo adwuma, nnuaba a wogye, ne tɔn nsɛm. Mobile apps ketewa anaa kasa nkrataa wɔ wo fɔn no tumi boa wo kora nsɛm yie.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm during drought?
candidates.answer_en: During drought, mulch heavily to conserve soil moisture, irrigate if possible, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and avoid adding nitrogen fertilizer which increases water demand. Harvest early-maturing varieties before drought peaks.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ m'afuo so bere a nsuo pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a nsuo pa no, de mulch to asase so yiye sɛ nsukuro wo mu, de nsuo to nnua so sɛ wonya tumi, paw nnuaba aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa so, na bɔ hwɛ de nitrogen ferefere to sɛ ɛma nnuaba hia nsuo dodo. Gye nnuaba a wɔware ntɛm ansa na nsuo pa yɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: Should I register my farm with the government?
candidates.answer_en: Registering your farm with MOFA gives you access to government subsidies, training, extension services, credit, and market linkages. Visit your local MOFA office or District Assembly with your ID and land documents. Registration is free and very beneficial.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mede m'afuo nkyerɛw?
candidates.answer_twi: Wo afuo nkyerɛw wɔ MOFA de tumi ma wo sɛ wunya ɔman ho boa, nyansapɔ, extension nnwuma, ka, ne aguabasa ho kyɛfa. Kɔ wo MOFA ofisi anaa District Assembly a ɛbɛn wo wɔ wo nkyerɛwsɛm ne asase krataa. Nkyerɛw yɛ daa na ɛboa pa ara.

candidates.question_en: How do I calculate the profit from my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Profit equals Total Sales Revenue minus Total Costs. Track all expenses including seeds, fertilizer, labor, transport, and chemicals and all income from sales. Keep a simple notebook or use your phone to record daily expenses.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na melem m'afuo ho mfaaso?
candidates.answer_twi: Mfaaso yɛ sika nyinaa a wogye fi tɔn no minus sika nyinaa a wode. Kora sika nyinaa a wode ka ho te sɛ aba, ferefere, dwumadie, kwan so sika, dawuro, ne sika nyinaa a wogye fi tɔn. Kora krataa ketewa anaa fa wo fɔn de kora da biara ho sika.

candidates.question_en: How can I conserve water on my farm during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Conserve water by mulching heavily around plants to reduce evaporation, watering early morning or evening only, using drip irrigation which reduces water use by up to 60%, growing drought-tolerant crops, making windbreaks to reduce drying winds, and collecting and storing rainwater during wet season.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora nsuo wɔ m'afuo mu wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora nsuo wɔ de mulch to nnuaba ho papaapa sɛ nsukyerɛ ba sua, de nsuo to owia da ano anaa anwummere pɛ, fa nsuo tete-tete kyɛ a ɛsua nsuo kɔ 60%, kura nnuaba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase, si windbreaks sɛ mframa a ɛma asase yera nkɔ, na gye ne guina osu nsuo wɔ osu bere mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I prepare my farm for unpredictable weather?
candidates.answer_en: To prepare for unpredictable weather: grow more than one crop to spread risk, keep records of past planting dates and yields to understand your local patterns, store enough food and seed reserves, install or improve water harvesting systems, use drought and flood-tolerant varieties, maintain healthy soil with high organic matter which buffers both drought and flooding, and join farmer groups that share weather information.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesiesie m'afuo ama ɛwim tebea a ɛntumi nnim?
candidates.answer_twi: Siesie ama ɛwim tebea a ɛntumi nnim: kura nnuaba dodo sɛ mfomso antete, kora aba to bere ne nnuaba a wogye ho nsɛm sɛ wuhu wo beae tebea, guina aduan ne aba ahwɛso, si anaa siesie nsuo guina systɛm, fa aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ne nsuo tenten ase hyɛ, kora asase a enni aho yie ne nhwiren foforo dodo a ɛboa wɔ nsuo pa ne nsuo tenten bere, na ba okuafo kuo a wɔkyɛ ɛwim amanneɛ.

candidates.question_en: What are the major risks in farming and how can I manage them?
candidates.answer_en: Main farming risks include weather risks from drought or flooding, pest and disease outbreaks, price volatility at harvest time, input price increases, land tenure insecurity, and lack of market access. Manage these risks by diversifying crops so one failure does not ruin you entirely, using drought-resistant varieties, taking out crop insurance where available, joining farmer groups for collective bargaining, storing produce to sell when prices improve, securing formal land documents, and building relationships with multiple buyers.
candidates.question_twi: Aho yɛ den bɛn na ɛwɔ okuafo adwuma mu na dɛn na menyɛ wɔn ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Aho yɛ den kɛse a ɛwɔ okuafo adwuma mu ne: berɛ ho aho yɛ den fi bone anaa nsuo, adwummaker ne yadeɛ ba ntɛm, dwa bo sesa bere a wuyiyɛ, inputs bo kɔ so, asase ho gyinae ankyɛ, na dwa kɔ ho hia. Boa ho de nnuaba ahorow to sɛ baako a atua ho nhia wo a ennye wo ho nyinaa, de drought-resistant varieties to mu, gye crop insurance wɔ hɔ a ɛwɔ, ka okuafo kuo ho ma wobɔ bo kaa bom, guina nnuaba sɛ wotɔ bere a bo yɛ yie, hwɛ sɛ asase ho krataa pa wɔ wo nkyɛn, na kora wo adwene ho buyers kuo mmerantee ho.

items.question_en: What is Fall Armyworm and how can I control it?
items.answer_en: Fall Armyworm is a highly destructive caterpillar that mainly attacks maize. It can destroy an entire field within days. Control with insecticides like emamectin benzoate, apply early morning, and target the whorls where larvae hide.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na Aborɔnoma Adwummaker Kɛse ne ɛyɛ ɔkɔmm bɛn?
items.answer_twi: Aborɔnoma Adwummaker Kɛse yɛ aborɔnoma adwummaker a ɔsɛe dodo na ɔtaa kɔ aburow so. Ɔtumi seaa afuo koro nyinaa wɔ nnafoa mu. Kora ase wɔ adwummakers dawuro te sɛ emamectin benzoate, de to owia da ano, na hyɛ nhaban mu a adwummakers no kɔfa ho.

candidates.question_en: What is Fall Armyworm and what does it do to maize?
candidates.answer_en: Fall Armyworm is a highly destructive caterpillar that mainly attacks maize. It can destroy an entire field within days. Control with insecticides like emamectin benzoate, apply early morning, and target the whorls where larvae hide.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Fall Armyworm ne ɛyɛ ɔkɔmm bɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fall Armyworm yɛ aborɔnoma adwummaker a ɔsɛe dodo na ɔtaa kɔ aburow so. Ɔtumi seaa afuo koro nyinaa wɔ nnafoa mu. Kora ase wɔ adwummakers dawuro te sɛ emamectin benzoate, de to owia da ano, na hyɛ nhaban mu a adwummakers no kɔfa ho.

candidates.question_en: My maize leaves have dark areas and insects are eating them. What should I do?
candidates.answer_en: This is likely the Fall Armyworm. Look inside the whorl for worms. Apply insecticides like emamectin benzoate early morning or late evening. Sand mixed with ash applied into the whorl also helps as an organic option.
candidates.question_twi: M'aburow nhaban wɔ tumtum na wɔredidi won. Dɛn na meyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Eyi tumi yɛ Aborɔnoma Adwummaker Kɛse adwummaker. Hwɛ nhaban mu sɛ wɔhwehwɛ adwummakers anaa wɔ ho ntama. De adwummakers dawuro te sɛ emamectin benzoate guare owia da ano anaa nnɔnhwerew mu. Asintiɛ a waka nkamfo ka ho no tumi de gu nhaban mu sɛ nhwiren dawuro.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds on my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Control weeds by timely hand weeding in the first 3-4 weeks after planting, using mulch to suppress weeds, and applying pre-emergence herbicides at planting. The first weeding must be done within 2-3 weeks after crop emergence.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ nhaban a ɛntia asɛm yie a mennya sika koraa?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nhaban foforo ase wɔ nnafoa 3-4 a aburow pue akyi no mu, fa mulch kora nhaban foforo ase, na de herbicide to ansa na nnuaba pue. Nhaban foforo tia a ɛdi ɛkan no yɛ wɔ nnafoa 2-3 mu a nnuaba pue akyi.

candidates.question_en: What is maize streak virus and how can I manage it?
candidates.answer_en: Maize streak virus causes yellow streaks running along the leaf veins giving leaves a striped appearance. It is transmitted by the leafhopper insect. There is no cure once a plant is infected. Control by planting resistant varieties like Obatanpa and Mamaba from CSIR, destroying infected plants early, and controlling leafhoppers with appropriate insecticides. Avoid late planting as late-planted fields suffer more leafhopper attacks.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛkyerɛ maize streak virus na dɛn na menyɛ ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Maize streak virus ma nhaban ho yɛ yellow streaks a ɛkɔ wɔ nhaban abɔ ho na ɛma nhaban no yɛ stripes. Leafhopper adwummaker de tete. Yadeɛ no nni dawuro bere a nnuaba nya mu. Boa ho de resistant varieties te sɛ Obatanpa ne Mamaba fi CSIR to mu, yi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na de insecticides hware leafhoppers so. Gye wo ho fi late to mu efisɛ afuom a wɔde to mu akyi sen no nya leafhopper atia sen.

candidates.question_en: How can I identify Fall Armyworm in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Look for ragged holes in leaves with fine sawdust-like droppings inside the funnel of the plant. The worm itself is greenish-brown with stripes along the body and a distinctive Y-shaped marking on the head. Affected plants will have leaves with irregular feeding damage. Check your field early morning when the worms are most active on the surface.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛkyerɛ sɛ fall armyworm atu mako wɔ me aburoɔ afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ afifide a wɔatwa mu ne akyɛkyɛɛ teketeke a ɛte sɛ sawdust wɔ nnuaba funnel mu. Adwummaker no ankasa yɛ green-brown na ɛwɔ lines wɔ ne ho so na ɛwɔ nsono a ɛte sɛ Y wɔ ne ti so. Nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho wɔ nsono a wɔatwa mu te ɛnte. Hwɛ wo afuom anɔpa anaana bere a adwummaker no wɔ asase so pefee.

candidates.question_en: What is aflatoxin in maize and how can I prevent it?
candidates.answer_en: Aflatoxin is a deadly poison produced by Aspergillus fungi that grows on improperly dried or stored maize. It causes liver cancer and can kill animals and humans. Prevent aflatoxin by drying maize properly to below 13 percent moisture before storage, using hermetic storage bags or metal silos, inspecting stored grain regularly and discarding mouldy grain, using aflasafe biocontrol product, and never feeding visibly mouldy grain to animals.
candidates.question_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ dɛn wɔ aburoɔ mu na dɛn na menyɛ sɛ ɛnnya?
candidates.answer_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ poisons a ɛyɛ den a Aspergillus fungi a ɛso wɔ aburoɔ a wonma no tew yie anaa a wonguina yie ho de ba. Ɛma akokoaa yareɛ na etumi kum mmoa ne nnipa. Gye aflatoxin fi ho de ma aburoɔ no tew yie kɔ 13 percent nsuo ase ansa na woguina, de hermetic storage bags anaa metal silos, hwɛ aba a woguina bere biara na yi aba a mold aba ho, de aflasafe biocontrol de, na mma aba a mold aba ho amma mmoa.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Weed at 2 to 3 weeks and again at 6 to 8 weeks after planting. These two weeding operations are critical because early weeds compete directly with young maize for nutrients and water. You can use hand weeding with a hoe or apply pre-emergence herbicides like atrazine before the maize germinates. Mulching between rows also suppresses weeds.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ nhaban foforo a wɔ me aburoɔ afuom mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo nnansa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa akyi na bio wɔ nnansa nsia kɔ nwɔtwe akyi a wode aba to mu. Adwuma nhaban foforo yi mmienu no ho hia pa ara efisɛ nhaban foforo a ɛdi kan no di aburoɔ foforo bere a ɛwɔ ho ferefere ne nsuo ho brε. Wobetumi de nsa ne atia yam yi nhaban foforo anaa de herbicides a wɔfre no atrazine to ho ansa na aburoɔ aba atua fɔw. Mulching nsɛm ntam mu nso boa nhaban foforo ho.

candidates.question_en: What is the Ghana Commodity Exchange and how can farmers use it?
candidates.answer_en: The Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) is a formal marketplace where farmers can sell their produce at transparent, standardized prices. To use it: register as a member through an accredited warehouse operator, store your certified grain in a GCX-accredited warehouse, receive a warehouse receipt that you can sell at the exchange or use as collateral for a bank loan. It is especially good for maize, soya, and sorghum.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Ghana Commodity Exchange yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) yɛ aguabasa a ɛwɔ ho yie a okuafo tumi tɔn wɔn nnuaba wɔ boɔ a wɔada adi ne a wɔasiesie. Sɛ wohwehwɛ fa di dwuma a, kyerɛw wo din wɔ accredited warehouse operator ho, guina wo nnuaba a wɔakyerɛw wɔ GCX-accredited warehouse mu, nya warehouse receipt a wobetumi tɔn wɔ exchange no mu anaa de kɔ ban ho sɛ collateral. Ɛyɛ adwuma yie pa ara ma aburow, soya, ne ɔtɛ.

items.question_en: How can I control Panama disease in plantain and banana?
items.answer_en: Panama disease is a fatal fungal soil disease. Use certified disease-free planting material, avoid planting in previously infected soil, practice strict hygiene by cleaning tools before moving between farms, and plant resistant varieties like Cardaba or FHIA hybrids. There is no chemical cure.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na metumi kora Panama yadeɛ ase wɔ borɔdɔ ne kwadu mu?
items.answer_twi: Panama yadeɛ yɛ fungal asase yadeɛ a ɛkum. De aba a wɔakyerɛw wɔ ho a enni yadeɛ to mu, bɔ hwɛ to wɔ asase a yadeɛ aka ho ansa, yɛ ho tumi yie wɔ hohoro adeɛ ansa na wosesa afuo, na to aba a ɛtumi hyɛ ase te sɛ Cardaba anaa FHIA.

candidates.question_en: How can I control Black Sigatoka disease in plantain?
candidates.answer_en: Black sigatoka is a serious fungal disease causing black streaks on leaves that eventually kill them. Control it by removing and destroying affected leaves regularly, ensuring good drainage, maintaining adequate spacing for air circulation, and applying recommended fungicides like Mancozeb or Dithane every 2 to 3 weeks during wet seasons. Use resistant varieties like Apantu and FHIA-21 where available.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ black sigatoka yadeɛ ho wɔ boɔde ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Black sigatoka yɛ fungal yadeɛ kɛse a ɛma nhaban no yɛ black na ɛkum wɔn awiei pɛ. Boa ho de yi na sɛe nhaban a yadeɛ aba ho daadaa, hwɛ sɛ nsuo tew yie, kora ahodɔ pa sɛ mframa fa mu yie, na de fungicides a wɔagyae so te sɛ Mancozeb anaa Dithane hware mprɛnsa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa mu nsuo berɛ. De varieties a wɔagyae so te sɛ Apantu ne FHIA-21 fa to mu wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ.

candidates.question_en: What is the difference between plantain farming and banana farming?
candidates.answer_en: Plantain and banana are closely related but differ in use and management. Plantain is starchier, larger and must be cooked before eating. Banana is sweeter, eaten raw and matures faster. Banana requires more water and is more sensitive to drought. Plantain is more tolerant of less fertile soils. Both need similar disease management. Commercial banana farming for export requires higher standards of pest and disease control.
candidates.question_twi: Nte sɛn bɛn na ɛwɔ boɔde adwuma ne kwadu adwuma ntam?
candidates.answer_twi: Boɔde ne kwadu yɛ bɔhyɛ bɔhyɛ nanso wɔyɛ so sɛ wɔde wɔn ho na wɔhwɛ wɔn so nte. Boɔde wɔ starch pii, ɛso sen, na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhyehye ansa na wɔbɛdi. Kwadu dɛ, na wɔdi atoa, na ɛtwa so ntɛm. Kwadu hia nsuo pii na ɛyɛ amrane wɔ bone ho. Boɔde tumi gyina asase a ferefere nni mu pii. Wɔn mmienu hia yadeɛ hwɛ koro. Kwadu kɛse adwuma ma export hia adwummaker ne yadeɛ hwɛ pa sen.

candidates.question_en: How can I select healthy plantain suckers?
candidates.answer_en: Choose vigorous, disease-free planting material from healthy mother plants and avoid suckers showing unusual damage or weakness.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw plantain suckers a wɔyɛ ahoɔden?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw planting material a ɛyɛ ahoɔden na yare nni ho, na ɛfiri mother plants a ɛyɛ sehat. Mfa suckers a asɛe anaa ayɛ mmerɛ.

candidates.question_en: What causes small plantain bunches and how can I increase their size?
candidates.answer_en: Small plantain bunches are caused by poor soil fertility, water stress during bunch formation, heavy pest or disease pressure especially black sigatoka, overcrowded suckers competing for nutrients, using inferior planting material, and not removing dead leaves promptly. Improve bunch size by applying NPK and potassium fertilizer regularly, irrigating during dry spells, controlling sigatoka with fungicide, desuckering to one sucker per stool, and using quality sword suckers for planting.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn ma boɔde ntama yɛ ketewa na dɛn na menyɛ sɛ ɛntɔ me?
candidates.answer_twi: Boɔde ntama nketewa ba efisɛ asase aduan hia, nsuo ahia bere a ntama reyɛ, adwummaker ne yadeɛ a ɛhia pii a black sigatoka ka ho, suckers pii a wɔdi ferefere ho brε, planting material mfa ho, na amma wo nhaban a ɛawu asiesie ntɛm. Boa ntama bo kɔ so de de NPK ne potassium ferefere to ho bere biara, quench bone berɛ mu, boa sigatoka ho de fungicide hware, desuckering kɔsi sucker baako biara stool, na de sword suckers pa to mu.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce wind damage in plantain?
candidates.answer_en: Use suitable spacing, maintain healthy plants and consider wind protection where strong winds are common.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate mframa sɛe so wɔ plantain mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa spacing a ɛfata, ma nnua no nyɛ ahoɔden na susuw wind protection ho wɔ mmeae a mframa den taa ba.

candidates.question_en: How should I manage suckers in a plantain farm?
candidates.answer_en: Manage suckers by allowing only one follower sucker per stool at a time. Remove excess suckers using a sharp spade cutting them off at soil level. Choose the best positioned sword sucker as the follower. After harvest of the main bunch cut the harvested stem down to 1 metre and let it die naturally. A well-managed stool can produce continuously for 5 to 7 years. Fertilize each stool with 100 to 200 grams of NPK twice a year for sustained production.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ suckers sɛ me boɔde afuom ayɛ adwuma yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ suckers de ma sucker baako pɛ tena wɔ stool biara bere koro. Yi suckers a ɛboro so de spade akyer wɔ asase so. Yi sword sucker a ɛtete yie ma ɛyɛ follower. Ntama kɛse yi akyi twa abɔ a woyii no kɔsi metre baako na ma no wu ankasa. Stool a wohwɛ so yie tumi de nnuaba ba daadaa mfe 5 kɔ 7. De NPK gram 100 kɔ 200 to stool biara ho mprɛn mmienu biara afe ma nnoa tena so.

candidates.question_en: Which type of plantain sucker is best for planting?
candidates.answer_en: The best sucker for planting is the sword sucker which has narrow pointed leaves at the base and a large healthy corm. It grows faster and produces larger bunches than water suckers. The sword sucker should be 45 to 90 cm tall. Avoid planting peepers which are very small suckers, and water suckers which have broad leaves but small weak corms.
candidates.question_twi: Sucker bɛn na ɛhia pa ara sɛ mede to mu wɔ boɔde afuom?
candidates.answer_twi: Sucker a ɛhia pa ara sɛ wode to mu ne sword sucker a ɛwɔ nhaban aketewa pointɛd wɔ ase na ɛwɔ corm kɛse pa. Eba mu ntɛm na ede ntama kɛse guu sen water suckers. Sword sucker no nni yie sɛ 45 kɔ 90 sɛntimita tenten. Gye wo ho fi peepers a yɛ suckers nketewa a, na water suckers a ɛwɔ nhaban tenten nanso ɛwɔ corm kɛse mma.

candidates.question_en: How can I export my farm produce from Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: To export farm produce from Ghana register your business with GIPC if it involves foreign investment, obtain an export licence from the Ghana Export Promotion Authority, ensure your produce meets destination country phytosanitary standards by getting certificates from the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate under MOFA, have your produce inspected by Ghana Standards Authority, work with a licensed freight forwarder for logistics, and target markets with high demand for Ghanaian products like the EU for chilli and pineapple and the UK for yam and plantain.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mede me afuom nnuaba tɔ amansan foforɔ fi Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛde wo afuom nnuaba tɔ amansan foforɔ fi Ghana a, si wo adwuma ho wɔ GIPC sɛ obi fi amansan foforɔ wɔ mu, gye export licence fi Ghana Export Promotion Authority, hwɛ sɛ wo nnuaba to country a wɔde kɔ phytosanitary standards mu de certificates fi Plant Protection ne Regulatory Services Directorate wɔ MOFA ase, ma Ghana Standards Authority hwɛ wo nnuaba so, ka licensed freight forwarder ho ma logistics, na tia markets a wɔpɛ Ghana nneɛma pii te sɛ EU ma pepper ne pineapple ne UK ma bayerɛ ne boɔde.

items.question_en: What should I do if my farm becomes waterlogged?
items.answer_en: If your farm floods regularly, take these steps: dig drainage channels around and through the field to direct water away, create raised beds to keep plant roots above waterline, plant flood-tolerant crop varieties, install water pumps to remove standing water quickly, build earthen bunds around the field perimeter, and consider planting floating rice varieties if flooding is very severe and frequent.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na mɛyɛ sɛ nsuo hyɛ m'afuo mu dodo?
items.answer_twi: Sɛ nsuo taa hye wo afuo mu a, yɛ eyi: hu mmɔnkyemmonkyem twa ne wɔ afuo mu de nsuo no kɔ, yɛ raised beds sɛ nnuaba ntini atena sor nsuo soronko, to aba a ɛtumi nsuo tenten ase hyɛ, si nsuo pumps sɛ yi nsuo a ɛda hɔ ntɛm, yɛ asase bɔ twa afuo no ho, na hwɛ fa floating rice aba sɛ nsuo tenten taa ba na ɛyɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm from flooding and waterlogging?
candidates.answer_en: Protect your farm from flooding and waterlogging by planting on raised beds or ridges especially for vegetables and root crops, digging drainage channels around the field perimeter to direct excess water away, avoiding farming in flood-prone low-lying areas during heavy rain seasons, choosing flood-tolerant varieties where possible, using cover crops and mulching to reduce runoff, and planting trees or grass strips along slopes to slow water flow and reduce erosion.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me afuom annya nsuo tia?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye wo afuom fi nsuo ho de to mu wɔ beds a ɛtele anaa ridges a ɛhia pii ma nnuaba ne nnɔho, boro drainage channels fa afuom no ho nyinaa sɛ ɛde nsuo a ɛboro so kɔ ho, gye wo ho fi okuafo adwuma wɔ hɔ a nsuo taa tia wɔ nsuo berɛ kɛse mu, yi flood-tolerant varieties wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ, de cover crops ne mulching sua runoff, na to nnuaba anaa nhawan strips wɔ mmepɔ ho sɛ ɛhia nsuo kwan na sua erosion.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm during drought?
candidates.answer_en: During drought, mulch heavily to conserve soil moisture, irrigate if possible, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and avoid adding nitrogen fertilizer which increases water demand. Harvest early-maturing varieties before drought peaks.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mehwɛ m'afuo so bere a nsuo pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a nsuo pa no, de mulch to asase so yiye sɛ nsukuro wo mu, de nsuo to nnua so sɛ wonya tumi, paw nnuaba aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa so, na bɔ hwɛ de nitrogen ferefere to sɛ ɛma nnuaba hia nsuo dodo. Gye nnuaba a wɔware ntɛm ansa na nsuo pa yɛ dodo.

candidates.question_en: How can I prepare my farm for unpredictable weather?
candidates.answer_en: To prepare for unpredictable weather: grow more than one crop to spread risk, keep records of past planting dates and yields to understand your local patterns, store enough food and seed reserves, install or improve water harvesting systems, use drought and flood-tolerant varieties, maintain healthy soil with high organic matter which buffers both drought and flooding, and join farmer groups that share weather information.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mesiesie m'afuo ama ɛwim tebea a ɛntumi nnim?
candidates.answer_twi: Siesie ama ɛwim tebea a ɛntumi nnim: kura nnuaba dodo sɛ mfomso antete, kora aba to bere ne nnuaba a wogye ho nsɛm sɛ wuhu wo beae tebea, guina aduan ne aba ahwɛso, si anaa siesie nsuo guina systɛm, fa aba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ne nsuo tenten ase hyɛ, kora asase a enni aho yie ne nhwiren foforo dodo a ɛboa wɔ nsuo pa ne nsuo tenten bere, na ba okuafo kuo a wɔkyɛ ɛwim amanneɛ.

candidates.question_en: How can I conserve water on my farm during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Conserve water by mulching heavily around plants to reduce evaporation, watering early morning or evening only, using drip irrigation which reduces water use by up to 60%, growing drought-tolerant crops, making windbreaks to reduce drying winds, and collecting and storing rainwater during wet season.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekora nsuo wɔ m'afuo mu wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora nsuo wɔ de mulch to nnuaba ho papaapa sɛ nsukyerɛ ba sua, de nsuo to owia da ano anaa anwummere pɛ, fa nsuo tete-tete kyɛ a ɛsua nsuo kɔ 60%, kura nnuaba a ɛtumi nsuo pa ase, si windbreaks sɛ mframa a ɛma asase yera nkɔ, na gye ne guina osu nsuo wɔ osu bere mu.

candidates.question_en: How do I know if my seeds have germinated properly?
candidates.answer_en: Check germination 5-10 days after planting depending on the crop. Good germination means at least 80% of planted seeds have sprouted uniformly. If germination is poor, check if seeds were planted too deep, soil was too dry or waterlogged, temperature was too extreme, or seeds were old. Replant gaps with fresh seeds immediately.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menim sɛ m'aba apue yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛ aba no afifi nna 5-10 akyi a wode agu fam5. Sɛ aba no fifi yiye a, ɛkyerɛ sɛ aba a wode agu fam no 80% pɛ afifi pɛpɛɛpɛ80. Sɛ aba no mfifi yiye a, hwɛ sɛ wode agu fam dodo, asase no yɛ kusuu anaa nsuo dɔɔso wɔ mu, ewim yɛ hye anaa nwunu dodo, anaa aba no dedaw. Fa aba foforo gu mmeae a ɛda hɔ no ntɛm ara.

candidates.question_en: How do I know if my fertilizer is working?
candidates.answer_en: Signs that fertilizer is working include: darker green leaves, faster plant growth, larger leaves, and higher yield compared to unfertilized plots. If plants remain yellowish and grow slowly after 2-3 weeks of fertilizer application, the fertilizer may not have been applied correctly or the soil may have other problems.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menim sɛ m'ferefere yɛ adwuma?
candidates.answer_twi: Ahohyenam sɛ ferefere yɛ adwuma ne: nhaban a wɔyɛ tuntum-akyen pa ara, nnuaba a wɔda sor ntɛm, nhaban kɛse, ne nnuaba a wɔda sor dodo sen beae a wɔanto ferefere. Sɛ nnuaba da hoho na wɔda sor brɛ akyi a ferefere to so wiemu 2-3 a, ferefere no beɛ to so yie anaa asase no wɔ nsɛm foforɔ.

candidates.question_en: What causes root rot and how can I prevent it?
candidates.answer_en: Root rot is caused by soil-borne fungi, mainly when soil stays waterlogged for too long. It causes roots to turn brown and mushy, plants to wilt even when soil is wet, and eventual plant death. Prevent by: improving soil drainage, avoiding overwatering, not planting in low-lying waterlogged areas, using raised beds, treating seeds with fungicide before planting, and rotating crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma ntini sɛe na ɛdeɛn na metumi kora ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Ntini sɛe fi asase fungus, titiriw bere a nsuo da asase mu tenten dodo. Ɛma ntini dan ɛda ne mmerɛ, nnuaba nwo bere a asase nte, na nnua wu. Kora ase wɔ: siesie asase nsuo pue anammɔn, bɔ hwɛ nsuo to dodo, mto nnuaba wɔ asase ase a nsuo hia mu, fa asase-sor afuo, de aba ka fungicide ho ansa na woto mu, na sesa nnuaba.

candidates.question_en: How should I plant crops on slopes to prevent water erosion?
candidates.answer_en: On slopes, always plant across the slope (contour planting) rather than up and down. Make ridges along contour lines to hold water. Plant cover crops or grasses on the steepest parts. Use tied ridges (ridges with cross-ties every few meters) to capture rainwater. Mulch heavily to protect soil between plants.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn dua nnɔbae wɔ mmepɔw so na nsuo rentwa asase?
candidates.answer_twi: Wɔ kwantempon so, to aba twa kwantempon so daa (contour planting) na mmom kɔ sor na gu ase. Yɛ ntwaho wɔ contour lines no ho na ama nsuo akora. To cover crops anaa atɛntɛnni wɔ beae a ɛkwan pa ara. Fa tied ridges (ntwaho a wɔne kyɛ ɛtɔ so baako biara) sɛ ɛgye osu nsuo. De mulch to so papaapa sɛ ɛkora asase nnuaba ntam.

items.question_en: What equipment do I need to start a small farm?
items.answer_en: Essential tools for smallholder farming include a hoe and cutlass for land preparation and weeding, a watering can for irrigation, a knapsack sprayer for pesticide application, a measuring tape, storage bags including hermetic bags for grain, and a simple scale.
items.question_twi: Adeɛ bɛn na mehia sɛ mesi afuo ketewa?
items.answer_twi: Adeɛ a ɛhia wɔ afuo ketewa mu ne akɔde ne sekan ma asase siesie ne nhaban tia, nsuo kyɛ ma nsuo to, knapsack sprayer ma dawuro guare, susudua, guina bags a hermetic bags ka ho ma nnuaba, ne scale ketewa ma nnuaba sus.

candidates.question_en: What documents do I need to qualify for an agricultural loan?
candidates.answer_en: To qualify for agricultural loans, banks and microfinance institutions typically require: farm records showing area farmed and crops grown, sales records for at least one season, input purchase receipts, a farm business plan, MOFA registration certificate, land ownership or lease documents, a valid ID, and sometimes a guarantor. Start keeping records now even if you are not currently seeking a loan — it takes time to build a credible financial history that banks trust.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛm bɛn na ɛsɛ mekora sɛ menya okuafo adwuma ka?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wohwehwɛ nya okuafo adwuma ka a, ban ne microfinance institutions taa hia: afuo nsɛm a ɛkyerɛ asase asukyerɛ ne nnuaba a wokura, tɔn nsɛm ma bere baako pɛ pɛ, adenneɛ tɔn krataa, afuo adwuma dwumadie plan, MOFA kyerɛwsɛm kratafa, asase wura anaa asɛ krataa, ID a ɛtia, na mmere bi obi a ɔbɛka ho. Fi kora nsɛm saa ara bere a wonhwehwɛ ka da — ɛhia bere sɛ si sika ho nsɛm a wɔgye di a ban tumi gye di.

candidates.question_en: How do I prepare a simple farm budget?
candidates.answer_en: A simple farm budget lists all expected income and all expected costs for one season. Income includes expected yield multiplied by expected price. Costs include land preparation, seeds, fertilizer, pesticides, labour for planting weeding and harvesting, transport and packaging. Subtract total costs from total income to get expected profit. Always add a 10 to 15 percent buffer for unexpected costs. Review your actual results against the budget after each season to improve planning for the next season.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ afuom budget ketewa?
candidates.answer_twi: Afuom budget ketewa kyerɛ owuo-teetee a wohwia ne costs nyinaa ma bere baako. Owuo-teetee ka ho nnoa a wohwia a wɔde dwa bo a wohwia bu. Costs ka ho asase siesie, aba, ferefere, pesticides, adwuma ma to mu, nhaban foforo yi ne yi, transport ne packaging. Gui costs nyinaa fi owuo-teetee nyinaa mu sɛ wohunu mfaso a wohwia. De 10 kɔ 15 percent buffer ka ho ma costs a onhwia. Hwɛ wo actual results tia budget akyi bere biara sɛ ɛboa wo siesie adwuma pa ma bere a ɛdi hɔ.

candidates.question_en: How do I prepare a simple farm business plan?
candidates.answer_en: A simple farm business plan includes what you will grow and how much, land available, inputs needed and their costs, expected yield and selling price, total expected income, total costs, and expected profit. Also include risks and how you will manage them.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meyɛ afuo adwuma dwumadie plan ketewa?
candidates.answer_twi: Afuo adwuma dwumadie plan ketewa mu wɔ: dea wobɛkura ne sɛn, asase a wowɔ, adenneɛ a hia ne wɔn boɔ, nnuaba a wobɛnya ne tɔn boɔ, sika nyinaa a wobɛnya, sika nyinaa a wode, ne mfaaso a wobɛnya. Ka nsɔhwɛ ne ɛdeɛn na wobɛyɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ won ase.

candidates.question_en: How does mulching help my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Mulching covers soil with dry grass, straw, leaves, or plastic and conserves soil moisture reducing watering by 50%, regulates soil temperature, suppresses weed growth, and adds organic matter as it decomposes. Apply 5-10cm thick around plants.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mulching boa m'afuo?
candidates.answer_twi: Mulching sɛɛ asase wɔ atɛntɛnni kraen, tow, nhaban, anaa plastik na ɛkora nsukuro wɔ asase mu ma nsuo to sua 50%, siesie asase osu, kora nhaban foforo ase, na de nhwiren foforo ka ho bere a ɛadwo. De sɛntimita 5-10 to nnuaba ho.

candidates.question_en: What is agroforestry and how can it benefit my farm?
candidates.answer_en: Agroforestry is growing trees alongside crops or livestock on the same land. Benefits include: trees provide shade that reduces water stress, tree roots hold soil and prevent erosion, fallen leaves add organic matter, some trees fix nitrogen improving soil fertility, trees provide fruit or timber as additional income, and trees help store carbon reducing climate change impact. Recommended trees include Moringa, Leucaena, and Acacia.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na agroforestry yɛ na ɛboa m'afuo sɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Agroforestry yɛ kura nnua wɔ nnuaba anaa mmoa ho wɔ asase koro so. Mfaaso ho ne: nnua de ewim brɛ ma ɛma nsuo hia nkɔm, nnua ntini kora asase na ɛmma asase nhuru, nhaban a atu de nhwiren foforo ka ho, nnua bi fi nitrogen ma asase ho nhwiren da sor, nnua de aba anaa dua bi ka ho sɛ sika foforɔ, na nnua boa guina carbon na ɛsua katawere mu sɛsae ho ɔkɔm. Nnua a wɔka wɔn ho ne Moringa, Leucaena, ne Acacia.

candidates.question_en: What is precision farming and can a small farmer use it?
candidates.answer_en: Precision farming means using data and technology to apply exactly the right amount of inputs at the right time and place. Smallholders can practice basic precision farming by: soil testing different parts of the field and applying fertilizer based on results, using mobile apps to track crop growth, monitoring pest and disease hotspots and targeting treatment, and keeping detailed farm records to identify what works best.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na precision farming yɛ na okuafo ketewa tumi yɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Precision farming kyerɛ fa data ne technology di dwuma sɛ de adenneɛ a ɛfata to bere a ɛsɛ na beae a ɛsɛ. Okuafo ketewa tumi yɛ basic precision farming wɔ: hwɛ asase ahorow afuo mu na de ferefere to wɔ adwuma ho, fa mobile apps di dwuma sɛ kora nnuaba da sor, hwɛ adwumakers ne yadeɛ beae na hyɛ dawuro hɔ pɛ, na kora afuo nsɛm mu yiye sɛ wuhu dea yɛ adwuma pa.

candidates.question_en: What should I include in a simple farm business plan?
candidates.answer_en: A simple farm business plan should include your farm description and location, the crops or animals you plan to produce, how much land you have, your production costs for inputs seeds fertilizer labour and equipment, expected yields and prices, how you plan to sell your produce, and your profit projection. Keep it simple and realistic. You can get a template from MOFA extension offices or agricultural NGOs like GSMA or Agric-Ahaban.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ meyɛ me afuom adwuma plan ketewa?
candidates.answer_twi: Afuom adwuma plan ketewa nni yie sɛ ɛwɔ wo afuom ho nsɛm ne ɛhɔ a ɛwɔ, nnuaba anaa mmoa a wopɛ sɛ woto mu, asase a wowɔ, wo adwuma agyapade ho sika sɛ inputs, aba, ferefere, adwuma ne nneɛma, nnoa a wohwia ne bo a wohwia, ɛkwan a wopɛ sɛ wode wo nnuaba tɔ, na sika a wohwia sɛ wobɛnya. Ma no yɛ mmerɛw na ɛteɛ. Wobetumi anya template fi MOFA extension offices anaa NGOs te sɛ GSMA anaa Agric-Ahaban.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect my farm from flooding and waterlogging?
candidates.answer_en: Protect your farm from flooding and waterlogging by planting on raised beds or ridges especially for vegetables and root crops, digging drainage channels around the field perimeter to direct excess water away, avoiding farming in flood-prone low-lying areas during heavy rain seasons, choosing flood-tolerant varieties where possible, using cover crops and mulching to reduce runoff, and planting trees or grass strips along slopes to slow water flow and reduce erosion.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ me afuom annya nsuo tia?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye wo afuom fi nsuo ho de to mu wɔ beds a ɛtele anaa ridges a ɛhia pii ma nnuaba ne nnɔho, boro drainage channels fa afuom no ho nyinaa sɛ ɛde nsuo a ɛboro so kɔ ho, gye wo ho fi okuafo adwuma wɔ hɔ a nsuo taa tia wɔ nsuo berɛ kɛse mu, yi flood-tolerant varieties wɔ hɔ a wɔwɔ, de cover crops ne mulching sua runoff, na to nnuaba anaa nhawan strips wɔ mmepɔ ho sɛ ɛhia nsuo kwan na sua erosion.

items.question_en: Why should cucumber farmers avoid planting the crop repeatedly in the same spot?
items.answer_en: Rotation reduces the buildup of pests and diseases that remain in the soil and helps maintain better field health.
items.question_twi: Adɛn nti na cucumber okuafoɔ nni sɛ wɔdua no mpɛn pii wɔ beae koro?
items.answer_twi: Nsesae nnɔbae no ma mmoawa ne yare a ɛtena asase mu no ntumi nhyia dodo na ɛboa asase ne afuo no ma ɛyɛ yie.

candidates.question_en: Why do cucumber vines need support?
candidates.answer_en: Supporting vines can improve air circulation, keep fruits cleaner and make harvesting easier.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛma cucumber vines nya biribi kura wɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Ɛboa ma mframa fa mu yie, ma aba no ntra dɔte mu na ɛma gyeɛ yɛ mmerɛ.

candidates.question_en: What kind of site is suitable for cucumber?
candidates.answer_en: Choose a sunny site with fertile, well-drained soil and access to reliable water.
candidates.question_twi: Beae bɛn na ɛfata ma cucumber?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw beae a owia wɔ, asase no yɛ pa na nsuo firi mu yie, na nsuo wɔ hɔ daa.

candidates.question_en: How often should cucumber be picked?
candidates.answer_en: Pick frequently during the production period so mature fruits do not remain on the vines and slow further production.
candidates.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ megye cucumber?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye wɔn daa wɔ bere a wɔrebɔ aba mu sɛnea aba a awie ase renka dua no so na ɛrenkum aba foforo.

candidates.question_en: How can I protect cucumber flowers?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid unnecessary disturbance during flowering, maintain adequate moisture and manage pests that attack flowers and young fruits.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn abɔ cucumber nhwiren ho ban?
candidates.answer_twi: Mma nhwiren no ho nnyɛ basabasa bere a ɛrehuru, ma nsuo a ɛfata na hwɛ mmoawa a wɔtow nhwiren ne aba nketewa no so.

candidates.question_en: Can cucumber be grown in containers?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, but use a sufficiently large container, good drainage, fertile growing media and support for the vines.
candidates.question_twi: Cucumber tumi nyin wɔ nkuku mu anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, nanso fa kuku a ɛso kɛse, nsuo tumi firi mu, asase pa ne adeɛ a ɛbɛkura vines no.

candidates.question_en: When should cucumber be harvested?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest when fruits have reached the market size and are still firm and tender. Delayed harvesting can reduce quality.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ megye cucumber?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye bere a aba no anya kɛse a gua hia na ɛda so yɛ den na ɛyɛ mmerɛ. Sɛ wotwentwɛn a quality betumi resa.

candidates.question_en: How should cucumbers be handled after harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Handle them gently, keep them shaded and avoid excessive heat to preserve freshness and reduce bruising.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ cucumber akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa ahwɛyiye, kora wɔn wɔ sunsuma na mma ɔhyew den nka wɔn sɛnea fresh no bɛtena hɔ na wɔmpirapira.

candidates.question_en: What causes bitter cucumber fruits?
candidates.answer_en: Stress such as uneven watering, extreme temperatures or variety-specific factors can contribute to bitterness.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛma cucumber yɛ nwene?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsuo a ɛnyɛ pɛ, ɔhyew a ɛdɔɔso anaa ɛsua, ne nneɛma a ɛfa variety ho tumi ma cucumber yɛ nwene.

items.question_en: How deep should I plant maize seeds?
items.answer_en: Plant maize seeds 3-5 cm deep. If the soil is dry, plant slightly deeper to reach moisture. Space seeds 25-30 cm apart within rows and 75-90 cm between rows.
items.question_twi: Ɛsukyerɛ bɛn na mede aburow aba to asase mu?
items.answer_twi: De aburow aba to asase mu sɛntimita 3-5. Sɛ asase no yera a, to mu kakra dodo na wo nsa adu nsukuro ho. Gyae asukyerɛ 25-30 sɛntimita wɔ aba biara ntam na 75-90 sɛntimita wɔ nnua so ntam.

candidates.question_en: What spacing should I use when planting maize?
candidates.answer_en: Use a spacing of 75 cm between rows and 40 cm between plants within the row. Plant 2 seeds per hole at a depth of 3 to 5 cm. After germination, thin to one strong plant per stand. This spacing allows each plant enough space, sunlight and nutrients to grow well.
candidates.question_twi: Ahodɔ bɛn na mede aba to mu bere a meto aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: De ahodɔ 75 sɛntimita fa nsɛm ho na 40 sɛntimita fa nnuaba ho wɔ nsɛm mu. De aba mmienu to mu fa ho biara wɔ uɛ 3 kɔ 5 mu. Aba tua fɔw akyi, yi nnuaba kosi nnuaba kronkron baako wɔ fa biara. Ahodɔ yi ma nnuaba biara nya ahorow, owia na ferefere a ɛyɛ papa.

candidates.question_en: When is the best time to plant maize in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: In Ghana, the best time to plant maize is at the beginning of the rainy season — March to April in the south, and May to June in the north. Plant when you have received at least 2-3 good rains so the soil is well moistened.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛyɛ ɔkorɔ sɛ wode aburow to mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Wɔ Ghana, bere pa ara sɛ wode aburow to mu ne nsuo bere mfiase — Ɛbɔ kwan so Oforisuo wɔ apuei fam, na Ayɛwohomumo kwan so Mumu wɔ atifi fam. To aba mu bere a wanya nsu mmɛn 2-3 yie na asase no atenante yie.

candidates.question_en: What fertilizer should I apply to maize and when?
candidates.answer_en: Apply NPK 15-15-15 at planting rate of 2 bags per acre mixed into the soil near the seed. At 4 to 6 weeks after planting when the maize is knee high, apply urea (top dressing) at 1 bag per acre. Place urea 5 to 7 cm from the stem and cover lightly with soil to prevent loss through evaporation.
candidates.question_twi: Ferefere bɛn na mede to aburoɔ ho na bere bɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: De NPK 15-15-15 to mu bere a wode aba to mu, bags mmienu biara eka baako mu, na fa ka ho asase a ɛbɛn aba no ho. Nnansa 4 kɔ 6 akyi a aburoɔ aba mu rebɛ kɔsi ntam, de urea (top dressing) to ho, bag baako biara eka baako mu. De urea sie sɛntimita 5 kɔ 7 fi aburoɔ no ho na kata so kakra asase mu sɛ ɛrenyi fi.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare the soil before planting maize?
candidates.answer_en: Clear the land of weeds and old crop residues. Plough or dig to a depth of 20 to 30 cm to loosen the soil. If possible, apply compost or manure and incorporate it into the soil two weeks before planting. Level the seedbed to ensure even germination. Avoid burning crop residues as this destroys beneficial soil organisms.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ asase no so ansa na meto aburoɔ?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo ne nnuaba a ato fɛw fi asase no so. Boro asase no kosi sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 mu sɛ asase no atete yie. Sɛ wobetumi a, de compost anaa aguare to mu na fa ka ho mprɛnsa mmienu ansa na wode aba to mu. Siesie seedbed no so yie sɛ aba nyinaa retua fɔw yie. Mma nnuaba fidie anhye efisɛ eyi sɛe asase mu adwummaker pa.

candidates.question_en: How should I prepare maize seed before planting?
candidates.answer_en: Treat maize seed with a fungicide and insecticide seed dressing before planting to protect against soil-borne diseases and early insect attack. Products like Apron Star or Gaucho are commonly used. Coat the seeds lightly, allow them to dry for 30 minutes and plant immediately. Buy certified seeds from reputable agro-input dealers to ensure good germination rates.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ aburoɔ aba ansa na meto mu?
candidates.answer_twi: De fungicide ne insecticide seed dressing to aburoɔ aba so ansa na wode to mu sɛ ɛhwɛ aba no so fi asase yadeɛ ne adwummaker atia a ɛdi kan. Nneɛma te sɛ Apron Star anaa Gaucho na wɔde taa yɛ. Kata aba no so kakra, ma no tew simma 30 na to mu ntɛm. Gye certified seeds fi agro-input dealers a wɔni gyinae so sɛ aba atua fɔw yie.

candidates.question_en: When is maize ready to harvest and what signs should I look for?
candidates.answer_en: Maize is ready to harvest 90 to 120 days after planting depending on the variety. Signs of maturity include dry brown silks on the cob, a hard black layer at the base of the kernel when you remove it, and husks that have turned dry and papery. The grain moisture at harvest should be around 25 to 30 percent. For dry storage, allow the cobs to dry further until moisture drops to 13 percent.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na aburoɔ atwa so sɛ wɔbɛ yi na dɛn na ɛkyerɛ saa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aburoɔ atwa so sɛ wɔbɛ yi adays 90 kɔ 120 akyi a wode aba to mu, sɛ variety no so. Nsono a ɛkyerɛ sɛ ɛatwa so ne: silks brown ne wɔ afahye a atew, nsono tuntum kɛse wɔ aba no ase bere a wuyi mu, na husks no atew sɛ ntama. Nsuo a ɛwɔ aba mu bere a wuyi ne bɛyɛ 25 kɔ 30 percent. Ma no tew bio kɔsi sɛ nsuo besi 13 percent ansa na woguina mu.

candidates.question_en: How do I know when my maize is ready to harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Maize is ready when the husks turn brown and dry, the silks are dark brown/black, and the kernels are hard. This is usually 90-120 days after planting depending on the variety.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na menim sɛ m'aburow awie ase na ɛyɛ a megye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Aburow awie ase bere a ntwaho no dan ɛda na ayera, nhwiren no adan ɛda kɔkɔɔ/tuntum, na aba no ayɛ den. Eyi taa ba nnafoa 90-120 a wode aba to mu no akyi wɔ aba no ahodoɔ so.

candidates.question_en: What is crop rotation and why is it important?
candidates.answer_en: Crop rotation means growing different crops on the same land each season. For example, grow maize in season 1, then cowpea in season 2. This breaks pest cycles, improves soil fertility, and increases yields.
candidates.question_twi: Dea ɛyɛ sɛ wosesa nnuaba gu asase mu na adɛn na ɛyɛ papa?
candidates.answer_twi: Nnuaba sesae kyerɛ sɛ wokura ahorow nnuaba wɔ asase koro so bere biara. Nhwɛso so, kura aburow bere 1 mu, afei kura abɔdweɛ wɔ bere 2 mu. Eyi bubu adwummakers ntam, yɛ asase mu aduan ho nhwiren na ɛma nnuaba da sor dodo.

items.question_en: Can watermelon be grown with other crops?
items.answer_en: It can be intercropped in suitable systems, but the vines require adequate space and should not be overcrowded.
items.question_twi: Watermelon tumi nyin ne nnɔbae foforo bom anaa?
items.answer_twi: Aane, wobetumi adua no bom wɔ nhyehyɛe a ɛfata mu, nanso vines no hia beae a ɛdɔɔso na ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔhyɛ no ma dodo.

candidates.question_en: How do I select land for watermelon?
candidates.answer_en: Choose warm, sunny, well-drained land with fertile soil and enough space for vines to spread.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn apaw asase ma watermelon?
candidates.answer_twi: Paw asase a ɛyɛ hyew, owia wɔ, nsuo firi mu yie na ɛyɛ pa, na beae no yɛ kɛse ma vines no trɛw.

candidates.question_en: How can I know when watermelon is mature?
candidates.answer_en: Use several maturity signs together, such as changes in the tendril near the fruit, ground spot colour and the fruit's overall appearance.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ watermelon awie ase?
candidates.answer_twi: Hwɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne pii bom, te sɛ tendril a ɛbɛn aba no, kɔla a asase fã a aba no da so wɔ no yɛ, ne sɛnea fruit no tebea te nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How should watermelon be graded before sale?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest at the right maturity, handle fruits carefully and transport them in a way that prevents crushing and excessive heat.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyekyɛ watermelon ansa na matɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye aba a maturity yɛ yie, fa ahwɛyiye na de no kɔ gua so wɔ kwan a ɛremma ɛmpira anaa ɔhyew nka no dodo.

candidates.question_en: How can I improve watermelon fruit size?
candidates.answer_en: Use good seed, maintain balanced nutrition, provide adequate water and manage weeds and pests from early growth.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama watermelon aba no yɛ kɛse?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa aba pa, ma nutrients yɛ pɛ, ma nsuo a ɛfata na hwɛ nwura ne mmoawa so fi ase.

candidates.question_en: How should watermelon be handled at harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Cut fruits carefully, avoid dropping them and keep them protected from excessive heat and physical damage.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ watermelon bere a meregye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Twa aba no yie, mma ɛntɔ fam na kora no fi ɔhyew den ne mpirapira ho.

candidates.question_en: Why does watermelon need good drainage?
candidates.answer_en: Its roots perform poorly in prolonged waterlogged soil, which can increase root disease and reduce growth.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na watermelon hia asase a nsuo firi mu yie?
candidates.answer_twi: Ne ntini yɛ adwuma bɔne wɔ asase a nsuo gyina mu kyɛ dodo, na ɛtumi ma root yare dɔɔso na nyin tew.

candidates.question_en: When should I reduce irrigation before harvest?
candidates.answer_en: Once fruits are approaching maturity, excessive watering can dilute quality and increase cracking risk. Adjust watering according to soil and crop condition.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mete nsuo so ansa na megye watermelon?
candidates.answer_twi: Bere a watermelon rebɛwie ase no, nsuo dodo tumi tew quality so na ɛma aba no paapae. Yɛ nsuo no sɛnea asase ne nnɔbae no tebea te.

candidates.question_en: Why are watermelon fruits cracking?
candidates.answer_en: Sudden changes in water availability, heavy rain after dry conditions and other stress can contribute to cracking.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na watermelon aba paapae?
candidates.answer_twi: Nsuo a ɛsakra ntɛm, osu den akyi ɔpɛ ne ɔhaw foforo bi betumi ama watermelon aba paapae.

items.question_en: What is the push-pull farming system?
items.answer_en: Push-pull is a clever intercropping system developed in Africa that controls stemborers (the most destructive maize pest) without chemicals. Plant Desmodium grass between maize rows (it repels/pushes stemborers away) and Napier grass or Brachiaria around the field border (it attracts/pulls stemborers and traps them). Desmodium also fixes nitrogen and suppresses Striga weed. This system is free to maintain once established.
items.question_twi: Dɛn na push-pull farming systɛm yɛ?
items.answer_twi: Push-pull yɛ intercropping anammɔn ahorow a wɔyɛ wɔ Afrika a ɛkora stemborer (aburow adwummaker a ɛsɛe pa ara) ase a wɔmfa chemicals. To Desmodium atɛntɛnni wɔ aburow nnua ntam (ɛkora/push stemborer kɔ) na Napier atɛntɛnni anaa Brachiaria twa afuo no ho (ɛtwe/pull stemborer na gye wɔn). Desmodium nso fi nitrogen na kora Striga nhaban foforo ase. Anammɔn no yɛ daa akyi a wɔasi no yie.

candidates.question_en: What is the Ghana Commodity Exchange and how can farmers use it?
candidates.answer_en: The Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) is a formal marketplace where farmers can sell their produce at transparent, standardized prices. To use it: register as a member through an accredited warehouse operator, store your certified grain in a GCX-accredited warehouse, receive a warehouse receipt that you can sell at the exchange or use as collateral for a bank loan. It is especially good for maize, soya, and sorghum.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Ghana Commodity Exchange yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?
