candidates.answer_twi: Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) yɛ aguabasa a ɛwɔ ho yie a okuafo tumi tɔn wɔn nnuaba wɔ boɔ a wɔada adi ne a wɔasiesie. Sɛ wohwehwɛ fa di dwuma a, kyerɛw wo din wɔ accredited warehouse operator ho, guina wo nnuaba a wɔakyerɛw wɔ GCX-accredited warehouse mu, nya warehouse receipt a wobetumi tɔn wɔ exchange no mu anaa de kɔ ban ho sɛ collateral. Ɛyɛ adwuma yie pa ara ma aburow, soya, ne ɔtɛ.

candidates.question_en: What is contract farming and how can it help farmers in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Contract farming is an agreement between a farmer and a buyer where the buyer agrees to purchase your produce at a pre-agreed price before you plant. In Ghana, companies like Masara N'Arziki for maize, Biase Plantations for sugarcane, various cocoa buying companies and export vegetable companies offer contract farming arrangements. Benefits include guaranteed market, access to inputs on credit, technical support and stable income. The main risk is being locked into a price that may be lower than the open market if prices rise.
candidates.question_twi: Contract farming yɛ dɛn na ɛbɛtumi aboa me wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Contract farming ne nhyiam a ɛwɔ okuafo ne buyer ntam a buyer gyina so sɛ ɔbɛgye wo nnuaba bo a wɔako ka ansa na wode aba to mu. Wɔ Ghana, companies te sɛ Masara N'Arziki ma aburoɔ, Biase Plantations ma sugarcane, cocoa gye companies bebree ne export vegetable companies de contract farming nhyiam to. Mfaaso ne: dwa gyinae, access kɔ inputs wɔ credit so, technical mmoa ne owuo-teetee foforo so. Aho yɛ den kɛse ne sɛ wobɔ bo a ɛtumi yɛ sua sen open market sɛ bo kɔ so.

candidates.question_en: What is Fall Armyworm and what does it do to maize?
candidates.answer_en: Fall Armyworm is a highly destructive caterpillar that mainly attacks maize. It can destroy an entire field within days. Control with insecticides like emamectin benzoate, apply early morning, and target the whorls where larvae hide.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na Fall Armyworm ne ɛyɛ ɔkɔmm bɛn?
candidates.answer_twi: Fall Armyworm yɛ aborɔnoma adwummaker a ɔsɛe dodo na ɔtaa kɔ aburow so. Ɔtumi seaa afuo koro nyinaa wɔ nnafoa mu. Kora ase wɔ adwummakers dawuro te sɛ emamectin benzoate, de to owia da ano, na hyɛ nhaban mu a adwummakers no kɔfa ho.

candidates.question_en: How can I control weeds in my maize farm?
candidates.answer_en: Weed at 2 to 3 weeks and again at 6 to 8 weeks after planting. These two weeding operations are critical because early weeds compete directly with young maize for nutrients and water. You can use hand weeding with a hoe or apply pre-emergence herbicides like atrazine before the maize germinates. Mulching between rows also suppresses weeds.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ nhaban foforo a wɔ me aburoɔ afuom mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Yi nhaban foforo nnansa mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa akyi na bio wɔ nnansa nsia kɔ nwɔtwe akyi a wode aba to mu. Adwuma nhaban foforo yi mmienu no ho hia pa ara efisɛ nhaban foforo a ɛdi kan no di aburoɔ foforo bere a ɛwɔ ho ferefere ne nsuo ho brε. Wobetumi de nsa ne atia yam yi nhaban foforo anaa de herbicides a wɔfre no atrazine to ho ansa na aburoɔ aba atua fɔw. Mulching nsɛm ntam mu nso boa nhaban foforo ho.

candidates.question_en: What is intercropping and what are its benefits?
candidates.answer_en: Intercropping means growing two or more crops together on the same land. For example, maize with cowpea. Benefits include better land use, the legume adds nitrogen to the soil, reduced pest pressure, and income from two crops.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛyɛ intercropping na ɛboa?
candidates.answer_twi: Intercropping kyerɛ sɛ wokura nnuaba abien anaa dodo wɔ asase koro so. Nhwɛso so, aburow ne abɔdweɛ. Mfaaso ho ne: asase ho dwuma pa, abɔdweɛ de nitrogen ma asase, adwummakers hia sua, na nnuaba abien firi sika.

candidates.question_en: What is maize streak virus and how can I manage it?
candidates.answer_en: Maize streak virus causes yellow streaks running along the leaf veins giving leaves a striped appearance. It is transmitted by the leafhopper insect. There is no cure once a plant is infected. Control by planting resistant varieties like Obatanpa and Mamaba from CSIR, destroying infected plants early, and controlling leafhoppers with appropriate insecticides. Avoid late planting as late-planted fields suffer more leafhopper attacks.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na ɛkyerɛ maize streak virus na dɛn na menyɛ ho?
candidates.answer_twi: Maize streak virus ma nhaban ho yɛ yellow streaks a ɛkɔ wɔ nhaban abɔ ho na ɛma nhaban no yɛ stripes. Leafhopper adwummaker de tete. Yadeɛ no nni dawuro bere a nnuaba nya mu. Boa ho de resistant varieties te sɛ Obatanpa ne Mamaba fi CSIR to mu, yi nnuaba a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na de insecticides hware leafhoppers so. Gye wo ho fi late to mu efisɛ afuom a wɔde to mu akyi sen no nya leafhopper atia sen.

candidates.question_en: When is the best time to plant maize in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: In Ghana, the best time to plant maize is at the beginning of the rainy season — March to April in the south, and May to June in the north. Plant when you have received at least 2-3 good rains so the soil is well moistened.
candidates.question_twi: Bere bɛn na ɛyɛ ɔkorɔ sɛ wode aburow to mu wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Wɔ Ghana, bere pa ara sɛ wode aburow to mu ne nsuo bere mfiase — Ɛbɔ kwan so Oforisuo wɔ apuei fam, na Ayɛwohomumo kwan so Mumu wɔ atifi fam. To aba mu bere a wanya nsu mmɛn 2-3 yie na asase no atenante yie.

candidates.question_en: What is aflatoxin in maize and how can I prevent it?
candidates.answer_en: Aflatoxin is a deadly poison produced by Aspergillus fungi that grows on improperly dried or stored maize. It causes liver cancer and can kill animals and humans. Prevent aflatoxin by drying maize properly to below 13 percent moisture before storage, using hermetic storage bags or metal silos, inspecting stored grain regularly and discarding mouldy grain, using aflasafe biocontrol product, and never feeding visibly mouldy grain to animals.
candidates.question_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ dɛn wɔ aburoɔ mu na dɛn na menyɛ sɛ ɛnnya?
candidates.answer_twi: Aflatoxin yɛ poisons a ɛyɛ den a Aspergillus fungi a ɛso wɔ aburoɔ a wonma no tew yie anaa a wonguina yie ho de ba. Ɛma akokoaa yareɛ na etumi kum mmoa ne nnipa. Gye aflatoxin fi ho de ma aburoɔ no tew yie kɔ 13 percent nsuo ase ansa na woguina, de hermetic storage bags anaa metal silos, hwɛ aba a woguina bere biara na yi aba a mold aba ho, de aflasafe biocontrol de, na mma aba a mold aba ho amma mmoa.

items.question_en: How can I grow crops in containers if I do not have enough land?
items.answer_en: Growing in containers is called container gardening. Use large buckets, old tires, plastic bags, or purpose-made pots. Fill with a mix of soil, compost, and sand for good drainage. Good container crops include tomatoes, peppers, leafy vegetables, herbs, and onions. Place in a sunny spot and water frequently as containers dry out faster than ground soil.
items.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na mekura nnuaba wɔ nkuku anaa pots mu sɛ menni asase?
items.answer_twi: Kura wɔ nkuku mu sɛ container gardening. Fa bucket kɛse, tayɛ kedee, plastik bags, anaa nkuku a wɔyɛ wɔn ho. Hye asase, compost, ne asintiɛ bom mu sɛ nsuo pue mu yie. Nnuaba a wɔda sor yie wɔ nkuku mu ne ntomato, mako, nhaban nnuan, nduaba aduan, ne gyene. Si wɔn wɔ beae a owia hye na de nsuo to pɛ efisɛ nkuku yera ntɛm sen asase.

candidates.question_en: Can I grow vegetables during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, you can grow vegetables in the dry season with irrigation. Crops like tomatoes, pepper, onions, leafy vegetables, and cucumbers grow well in dry season with proper watering.
candidates.question_twi: Metumi adua nnɔbae wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, wobetumi kura nnuan wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu sɛ wode nsuo gu so. Nnɔbae te sɛ ntomate, mako, gyeene, nhaban nnɔbae, ne cucumber nyini yiye wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu sɛ wode nsuo gu so yiye a.

candidates.question_en: How can I make tomato farming profitable?
candidates.answer_en: To make profit from tomatoes, time your production to sell when prices are high which is usually the dry season from November to February. Use drip irrigation for dry season production. Produce in bulk to negotiate better prices, form a farmer group to collectively market your tomatoes, and consider simple processing like tomato paste or puree to add value and extend shelf life. Keep detailed records of all costs.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ menyɛ sika wɔ tomatoes adwuma mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Sɛ wobɛfa sika wɔ tomatoes mu a, siesie wo to aba bere sɛ bɛtɔ bere a bo wɔ so wɔ yiye a ɛyɛ daadaa bone berɛ fi Ɔbenem kɔ Ɔpepon. De drip irrigation ma bone berɛ to aba. To pii sɛ wobɛtumi aho bo mu yie, fa okuafo kuo sɛ wɔde tomatoes bɛtɔ kaa bom, na twe wo adwene ho processing ketewa te sɛ tomato paste anaa puree sɛ ɛbɛde bo kɔso na ɛma ɛtena mu akyi. Kora wo adwuma sika ho nsɛm nyinaa.

candidates.question_en: How should I store tomatoes without using a refrigerator?
candidates.answer_en: Store tomatoes at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Do not stack heavily. Keep them stem-side down. Tomatoes last 1-2 weeks this way. For longer preservation, dry, can, or make tomato paste. Never refrigerate unripe tomatoes.
candidates.question_twi: Ɛdeɛn na meguina m'ntomato a menhyɛ wɔn fridge mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Guina ntomato wɔ fie mu osu a ɛyɛ pɛ sɛ owia ntra wɔn so tɔtɔ. Mfa wɔn si so dodo. De wɔn si wɔn tibo fam. Ntomato tumi tena nnawotwe 1-2 eyi ho. Sɛ wohwehwɛ tena bere tenten a, yaw, kanta, anaa yɛ ntomato paste.

candidates.question_en: My harvested tomatoes are spoiling quickly. What can I do?
candidates.answer_en: Avoid harvesting during wet conditions. Handle gently to prevent bruising. Store in cool shaded well-ventilated areas on raised surfaces. Remove and separate any rotting fruits immediately. Consider making tomato paste or drying to reduce losses. Transport in ventilated crates not plastic bags.
candidates.question_twi: M'ntomato a megye wɔn resɛe ntɛm. Dɛn na metumi yɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Bɔ hwɛ gye bere a nsuo wɔ hɔ. De wɔn pɛ sɛ wɔnhow. Guina wɔ bae a ɛhuru, owia ntra mu, mframa pue mu na ɛda sor. Yi na twa ntomato a resɛe ntɛm ara. Fa tomato paste yɛ anaa yaw sɛ mpampa sika kɔ mpoano.

candidates.question_en: How can I prevent tomato late blight?
candidates.answer_en: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans is the most destructive tomato disease. Prevent it by using resistant varieties, avoiding overhead irrigation, ensuring good spacing for air circulation, removing and destroying infected plant material immediately, and applying copper-based fungicides like Ridomil or Champion preventively especially during wet humid weather.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ tomato late blight annya me nnuaba?
candidates.answer_twi: Late blight a Phytophthora infestans ma ɛba ne tomatoes yadeɛ a ɛsɛe paa. Gye wo ho fi mu de varieties a wɔagyae so, gye wo ho fi nsuo wɔ atifi ho quench, hwɛ sɛ ahodɔ pa wɔ hɔ sɛ mframa fa mu, yi na sɛe plant material a yadeɛ aba ho ntɛm, na de copper-based fungicides te sɛ Ridomil anaa Champion hware ansa bere a nsuo ne ahuhuruw wɔ.

candidates.question_en: What irrigation method is best for tomatoes in Ghana?
candidates.answer_en: Drip irrigation is the best method for tomatoes in Ghana. It delivers water directly to the root zone reducing disease incidence from leaf wetness, improving water use efficiency, allowing fertigation where fertilizer is applied through the drip system, and reducing weed growth. Furrow irrigation is also acceptable for flat land. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation for tomatoes as wet foliage encourages fungal diseases like late blight. Irrigate in the morning to allow foliage to dry before evening.
candidates.question_twi: Quench nhyiamu bɛn na ɛhia pa ara ma tomatoes wɔ Ghana?
candidates.answer_twi: Drip quench ne nhyiamu pa ara ma tomatoes wɔ Ghana. Ɛde nsuo kɔ nnɔho asase mu nsɛm a ɛhia yadeɛ a ɛba efisɛ nhaban nsuo, ɛboa nsuo de pa, ɛma fertigation a wɔde ferefere fa wɔ drip system mu to, na ɛhia nhaban foforo. Furrow quench nso yɛ yie ma asase a ɛtee. Gye wo ho fi overhead sprinkler quench ma tomatoes efisɛ nhaban nsuo boa fungal yadeɛ te sɛ late blight. Quench anɔpa sɛ nhaban tew ansa na anwumere aba.

candidates.question_en: How should I stake tomato plants?
candidates.answer_en: Staking tomatoes keeps the plant upright reducing soil contact and disease. Use bamboo stakes or wooden sticks about 1.5 metres tall. Insert the stake 15 cm into the soil beside the plant without damaging roots. Tie the plant loosely to the stake using soft twine in a figure-8 pattern at every 20 to 30 cm of growth. Begin staking when plants are 20 to 30 cm tall. Indeterminate varieties need continuous staking as they grow while determinate varieties need staking only once.
candidates.question_twi: Dɛn na menyɛ tomatoes stake pa?
candidates.answer_twi: Tomatoes stake ma nnuaba gyina straight na ɛhia asase ne yadeɛ nka ho. De bamboo stakes anaa dua bio a ɛtelɛ sɛ metres 1.5. De stake si sɛntimita 15 asase mu bɛn nnuaba no ho a nnɔho nsɔre. Kyekyere nnuaba no de twine mmerɛw wɔ stake no ho wɔ figure-8 nhyiamu wɔ bere biara a nnuaba rekɔ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 so. Fi ase de stake bere a nnuaba bɛyɛ sɛntimita 20 kɔ 30 tenten. Indeterminate varieties hia stake bere nyinaa a wɔreba mu na determinate varieties hia stake mprɛn baako pɛ.

candidates.question_en: When should I transplant tomato seedlings?
candidates.answer_en: Transplant tomato seedlings when they are 4-6 weeks old, have 4-6 true leaves, are 15-20 cm tall, and have a sturdy stem. Seedlings that are too young may not survive transplanting shock. Seedlings that are too old (over 8 weeks) become root-bound and may not establish well in the field.
candidates.question_twi: Mfeɛ bɛn na ɛfata sɛ mesi ntomato nnuaba mfoforo ananmu?
candidates.answer_twi: Si ntomato nnuaba mfoforo ananmu bere a wɔdin nnawotwe 4-6, wɔwɔ nhaban 4-6, wɔn soroɔ yɛ sɛntimita 15-20, na wɔwɔ tibo den. Nnuaba mfoforo a wɔkum dodo betumi ankyɛ si ananmu no ɔkɔm. Nnuaba mfoforo a wɔadin dodo (nnawotwe 8 kenkan) yɛ root-bound na betumi ansi yie wɔ afuo mu.

items.question_en: How do I know if okra needs water?
items.answer_en: Look for dry soil, drooping leaves and slow growth. Water the crop when soil moisture is becoming insufficient.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ okra hia nsuo?
items.answer_twi: Hwɛ sɛ asase no ayera, nhaban asɛe anaasɛ nyin no akɔ brɛoo. Gu nsuo bere a nsuo a ɛwɔ asase mu resa.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce weed competition in okra?
candidates.answer_en: Keep the field weed-free during early growth through timely weeding and appropriate cultural practices.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ate nwura ne okra akyinnyɛ so?
candidates.answer_twi: Ma afuo no ho tew fi nwura ho bere a okra no refi ase, na yɛ nwura yiyie ne akwan a ɛfata wɔ afuo mu.

candidates.question_en: Can okra be grown during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, where a reliable water source is available and irrigation is managed well.
candidates.question_twi: Okra tumi nyin wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, sɛ nsuo a wode bɛgu so wɔ hɔ daa na wobɛhwɛ irrigation no yie a.

candidates.question_en: How should okra be graded for sale?
candidates.answer_en: Separate pods by size, freshness and visible quality. Remove damaged or over-mature pods and use clean packaging.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn akyekyɛ okra ma atɔn?
candidates.answer_twi: Yɛ no gu nkyekyɛmu sɛnea ne kɛse, ne fresh ne sɛnea ɛho tew te. Yi nea apira anaa ahyɛ den dodo na fa packaging a ɛho tew di dwuma.

candidates.question_en: What is a good harvesting practice for okra?
candidates.answer_en: Use clean hands or suitable tools, avoid damaging the plant and collect pods into clean containers.
candidates.question_twi: Kwan bɛn na ɛyɛ papa sɛ wɔde gye okra?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa nsa a ɛho tew anaa adwinnade a ɛfata di dwuma, bɔ dua no ho ban na fa aba no gu ade a ɛho tew mu.

candidates.question_en: Why are my okra pods becoming hard?
candidates.answer_en: Pods become hard when they stay on the plant too long. Harvest them while they are still young and tender.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na me okra aba reyɛ den?
candidates.answer_twi: Okra aba yɛ den bere a ɛtena dua no so kyɛ dodo. Gye no bere a ɛyɛ baabi a ɛda so yɛ ketewa na ɛyɛ mmerɛ.

candidates.question_en: How can I extend the freshness of harvested okra?
candidates.answer_en: Keep harvested pods shaded and cool, handle them gently and market them quickly because okra loses quality fast.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama okra a magye no ayɛ fresh akyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora okra a magye no wɔ sunsuma ne baabi a ɛyɛ nwunu, fa ahwɛyiye di wɔn ho dwuma na tɔn ntɛm efisɛ okra yera ne quality ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: Why does okra produce poorly after strong rain?
candidates.answer_en: Heavy rain can cause waterlogging, nutrient loss, flower damage or disease pressure. Good drainage and balanced management can reduce these problems.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na okra tɔ wɔ aba so yie wɔ osu den akyi?
candidates.answer_twi: Osu den tumi ma nsuo gyina, ma nutrients yera, sɛe nhwiren anaa ma yare dɔɔso. Nsuo firi mu yie ne afuo nhwɛsoɔ pa tumi tew ɔhaw yi so.

candidates.question_en: How often should okra pods be harvested?
candidates.answer_en: Harvest tender pods frequently so they do not become fibrous. Regular picking also encourages continued production.
candidates.question_twi: Mpɛn ahe na ɛsɛ sɛ megye okra aba?
candidates.answer_twi: Gye okra aba a ɛyɛ mmerɛ no mpɛn pii sɛnea ɛrenyɛ den na ɛrenyɛ fiber. Gyeɛ daa nso hyɛ nnua no nkuran ma ɛtoa aba so.

items.question_en: How do I start an okra farm?
items.answer_en: Choose fertile, well-drained soil, obtain good seed, prepare the land, plant at suitable spacing and plan for regular weeding and harvesting.
items.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahyɛ okra afuo ase?
items.answer_twi: Paw asase pa a nsuo firi mu, nya aba pa, siesie asase, dua wɔ ntam a ɛfata na yɛ nhwɛso nwura ne gyeɛ daa.

candidates.question_en: How can I reduce weed competition in okra?
candidates.answer_en: Keep the field weed-free during early growth through timely weeding and appropriate cultural practices.

candidates.answer_twi: Gye okra aba a ɛyɛ mmerɛ no mpɛn pii sɛnea ɛrenyɛ den na ɛrenyɛ fiber. Gyeɛ daa nso hyɛ nnua no nkuran ma ɛtoa aba so.

candidates.question_en: How can I extend the freshness of harvested okra?
candidates.answer_en: Keep harvested pods shaded and cool, handle them gently and market them quickly because okra loses quality fast.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ama okra a magye no ayɛ fresh akyɛ?
candidates.answer_twi: Kora okra a magye no wɔ sunsuma ne baabi a ɛyɛ nwunu, fa ahwɛyiye di wɔn ho dwuma na tɔn ntɛm efisɛ okra yera ne quality ntɛm.

candidates.question_en: Can okra be grown during the dry season?
candidates.answer_en: Yes, where a reliable water source is available and irrigation is managed well.
candidates.question_twi: Okra tumi nyin wɔ ɔpɛ bere mu anaa?
candidates.answer_twi: Aane, sɛ nsuo a wode bɛgu so wɔ hɔ daa na wobɛhwɛ irrigation no yie a.

candidates.question_en: Why are my okra pods becoming hard?
candidates.answer_en: Pods become hard when they stay on the plant too long. Harvest them while they are still young and tender.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na me okra aba reyɛ den?
candidates.answer_twi: Okra aba yɛ den bere a ɛtena dua no so kyɛ dodo. Gye no bere a ɛyɛ baabi a ɛda so yɛ ketewa na ɛyɛ mmerɛ.

items.question_en: Why is ventilation important in a mushroom room?
items.answer_en: Ventilation helps control humidity, temperature and carbon dioxide and can support healthy fruiting.
items.question_twi: Adɛn nti na mframa ho hia wɔ mushroom dan mu?
items.answer_twi: Mframa a ɛkɔ mu boa ma humidity, ɔhyew ne carbon dioxide yɛ pɛ na ɛboa mushrooms ma wɔbɔ aba yie.

candidates.question_en: Why is hygiene important in mushroom production?
candidates.answer_en: Clean equipment and growing areas reduce contamination by unwanted organisms that can compete with the mushrooms.
candidates.question_twi: Adɛn nti na ahotew ho hia wɔ mushroom kuayɛ mu?
candidates.answer_twi: Adwinnade ne beae a wɔyɛ no ho tew ma nneɛma foforo a ɛho nhia no ntumi nko mushrooms no na ɛtew contamination so.

candidates.question_en: What basic conditions do mushrooms need to grow?
candidates.answer_en: Mushrooms need a suitable growing substrate, moisture, appropriate temperature, cleanliness and adequate ventilation for the chosen species.
candidates.question_twi: Tebea bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mushrooms nya na wɔnyin?
candidates.answer_twi: Mushroom hia growing material a ɛfata, nsuo, ɔhyew a ɛfata, ahotew ne mframa a ɛkɔ mu sɛnea species no hia.

candidates.question_en: What records should a mushroom farmer keep?
candidates.answer_en: Record substrate quantities, production dates, contamination, harvest weight, sales, losses and operating costs.
candidates.question_twi: Nsɛm bɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mushroom okuafoɔ kyerɛw?
candidates.answer_twi: Kyerɛw substrate dodow, da a wofii ase, contamination, aba no duru, tɔn, asɛe ne sika a wode yɛ adwuma.

candidates.question_en: How do I know mushroom substrate is contaminated?
candidates.answer_en: Unusual colours, foul smells or rapid growth of unwanted mould can indicate contamination.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu sɛ mushroom substrate no ayɛ contamination?
candidates.answer_twi: Kɔla a ɛnsɛ, hua bɔne anaa mould a ɛnyin ntɛm betumi akyerɛ sɛ contamination aba.

candidates.question_en: How should harvested mushrooms be handled?
candidates.answer_en: Handle them gently, keep them clean and cool, and move them to market or appropriate storage quickly.
candidates.question_twi: Mɛyɛ dɛn ahwɛ mushrooms akyi a magye no?
candidates.answer_twi: Fa ahwɛyiye, ma ɛho tew na ɛyɛ nwunu, na de no kɔ gua anaa guina a ɛfata ntɛm.
